Logic step redesign: developer handoff

Funnel step 3, and the Logic view the main builder shares with it · 2026-09-22 · code refs are origin/main (b4aa278, 2026-09-16) unless marked mock

This is one screen with two styles, switched by its title, and both are in scope equally. Filter Results + Rules: one question picks the result, other questions narrow it, and rules add exceptions. Rules only: every result comes from a rule, written as a row of sentences under the header with a recommendations strip beneath. Each style has an Edit view and a Table view with Export and Import, a rule window, an Add recommendations window, the Questions step's Add a question dialog and its question types, inline text editing with a save pill, and delete with Undo everywhere.

Rules only is its own way of deciding results, not a different view of the same thing: the style is saved on the quiz and the engine follows it. Read the Decisions section first, then Engine semantics, then the screen sections.

  • Sizing reference (Filter Results + Rules)

D1 · Rules only: UI lens or real engine mode Settled

DECIDED 2026-09-21 (owner). Settled · build option B. Option B. Rules only is a real engine mode, not a UI lens: it is its own method of deciding results. The logic style is kept on the quiz through publish (a decider-gated, .optional() doc field, never .default()); when it is 'rules' the engine ignores question roles and answer mappings and the FIRST matching rule's recommendations are the result (the no-base path already in recommendDecider). Filter Results + Rules keeps today's engine: the picking question gives the base, filter questions narrow it, rules act on top. Nothing to decide here; this is implementation work.

History, not a choice: the question and the options this was chosen from

Question. Should 'Rules only' become a real, published engine mode (every result comes from a rule; the hidden picking question and filter roles stop applying), or stay today's UI-only lens over a doc that still needs one fully mapped picking question?

  • A. Keep UI-only: logic_style stays in build_session (stripped at publish). V1/V2/V3/V4 and the publish untargeted gate still block without a mapped picking question; the hidden mapping stays the base; Show rules append to it; filter roles still narrow. The Rules-only screen then needs a visible way to fix those blocks, and its copy ('Every outcome is a rule you write', 'nothing shows until you create one') must change.
  • B. Make it real with a fallback: a decider-gated optional doc field (e.g. Quiz.logic_style) that publish keeps; in 'rules' the engine ignores the decides mapping and filter roles, so a matching rule's targets are the result (the existing no-base path, recommendDecider.ts:279-283); validation swaps V1–V4, the V2 bypass and the untargeted gate for Rules-only checks; unmatched shoppers get the fallback chain (runtime change).
  • B-lite. Same as B, but unmatched shoppers keep today's 'We couldn't find a perfect match…' text (no app/components/runtime/** change).

Reasoning at the time, superseded by the ruling above. B, shipped as B-lite first if the owner wants to avoid a runtime edit in the same release; the fallback follows with the Results-step fallback settings.

Why. The approved Rules-only screen (rules row + recommendations strip, no questions) can't be honest or unblockable under A: blocks would point at a question the screen hides, and Show rules would sit invisibly behind the hidden mapping (probe-verified). The engine delta for B is small because resolveTarget already treats show/prioritize as the result when there is no base, and gating on a new optional field keeps legacy docs byte-identical and existing decider docs unchanged.

D2 · Show: engine append vs the 'these become the results' hint (PARTLY DECIDED 2026-09-21) Part settled

PART DECIDED 2026-09-21 (owner). Settled for Rules only · open for Filter Results + Rules. Rules only: Show is the whole result, so the hint 'these become the results' is true there, and Pin and Hide are meaningless under first-match-wins. Build the rule window with Show only when the style is 'rules'; keep Show / Pin / Hide in Filter Results + Rules. STILL OPEN: in Filter Results + Rules, Show appends after the base pool and is often cut off by the results cap while its hint promises 'these become the results'. The owner must choose: change the engine so Show puts its products first, or change the hint to describe appending. The reference mock now implements the settled half: in Rules only its rule window offers Show alone.

The question and the options, and what is still open

Question. Show appends the rule's products after the answer's results, so with the default hero + 3 grid they are invisible whenever the mapped recommendation already has 4 sellable products (and always on a product-shaped base). The mock and the live rule window promise 'these become the results'. Change the engine, the copy, or both? And should Rules only still offer Pin, which behaves exactly like Show when there is no mapping?

  • A. Copy only: keep the engine; the Filter hint says what happens (e.g. 'added after the answer's results'); under D1-B Rules only keeps 'these become the results'.
  • B. Engine: Show puts its products first (prepend, dedupe) on decider docs, hint 'these show first'; Pin stays reorder-only. Non-default hero/grid sorting can still re-sort them, as it does Pin today.
  • C. Engine: Show replaces the results (the legacy action-less behaviour) in both styles; the hint stays.
  • D. The rethink proposal: two verbs (Show = put first; Pin folds into Show).

Reasoning. Still open for Filter Results + Rules only: the owner picks either the engine change (B, Show puts its products first) or hint wording that describes appending (A). Nothing else in D2 is open. The Rules-only half is settled: Show is the whole result there, so the rule window offers Show alone and neither Pin nor Hide is offered, which is what the engine semantics, data model, rule window and Rules-only sections all build.

Why. Append is invisible in the default configuration, so Show rarely does anything a merchant can see; prepending keeps the mapped products below and makes the verb match its label without deleting the answer's results (C would). It changes behaviour for every published decider quiz with Show rules (pre-production posture, no legacy impact) and must follow the runtime procedure. In Rules only, Pin is indistinguishable from Show.

D3 · What blocks Continue in each style Settled

DECIDED 2026-09-22 (owner). Settled · build option B. Option B. One style-aware Tier-1 report drives the CTA, the check popover and publish. Filter Results + Rules keeps today's blocks and adds the route bypass and broken or impossible rules, plus warnings for a recommendation nothing can show, a rule that never runs, and an impossible all-of. Rules only blocks on: no rules, no rule that can show anything, and any rule missing its answers or its recommendations; it skips the picking-question checks (no decider, unmapped answers, decider bypass, filter values). 'Fix N issues' counts blocking findings only; the popover groups them per question or per rule. The report must never read safer than the publish gate.

History, not a choice: the question and the options this was chosen from

Question. What blocks Continue in each style, what only warns, and how is N in 'Fix N issues' counted?

  • A. Keep the live Tier-1 report as is: style-agnostic, V1/V4 also in Rules only, one count per finding.
  • B. One style-aware Tier-1 report: Filter keeps today's blocks plus the route bypass (B17) and broken or impossible rules (B8, B14), and adds warnings (never recommended, never runs, impossible all-of); Rules only blocks on no rules, no rule that can show anything, and rules without answers or recommendations; N counts blocking findings and the popover groups them per question or rule.
  • C. The mock's literal checks (blocks only on no picking question or unmapped answers, or zero rules).

Reasoning at the time, superseded by the ruling above. B

Why. One memoized report already drives the CTA, pill and modal, so style awareness belongs there. The mock's checks are too thin (confirmed B11, B14, B17) and the live ones are wrong for Rules only. The report must never read safer than the publish gate.

D4 · Where Diagnostics, Test a path and the AI review go Parked

PARKED 2026-09-22 (owner). Parked · build later. Parked by the owner on 2026-09-22: diagnostics come later. For this work: the check popover shows findings and opens from the CTA; do not rebuild 'Check my logic', the Diagnose modal, Test a path or the AI review into the step, and do not add the 'N to review' affordance yet. Leave the shipped PathTester and usePathQuality in place and unreferenced from the new step. When diagnostics are built, they hang off this popover's footer (option B of the original question).

History, not a choice: the question and the options this was chosen from

Question. With the top section and '✓ Check my logic' removed (decided Sep-17), Diagnostics, 'Test a path' and the Tier-2 AI review are reachable only when something blocks. Does the mock's anchored check popover replace the 'Diagnose & preview' modal, where do Test a path and the AI review live, and does the funnel-bar health pill stay?

  • A. The popover replaces the modal in the funnel; Test a path and the AI review leave step 3 (the builder keeps HealthPopover).
  • B. The popover shows findings and is always openable (the blocked CTA, plus a quiet 'N to review' affordance when only warnings exist), with footer links 'Test a path' and 'AI review' that open the existing modal tabs; the funnel-bar health pill is removed so the CTA is the one door.
  • C. Keep the modal as the only surface, opened from the CTA.

Reasoning at the time, superseded by the ruling above. B

Why. Keeps the shipped PathTester and usePathQuality without restoring removed chrome, makes warnings reachable (B11), and drops the duplicate pill the mock doesn't have. The 'N to review' affordance is new UI, so it needs the owner's OK.

D5 · First entry: style chooser or direct landing Settled

DECIDED 2026-09-22 (owner). Settled · build option A. Option A. No first-entry chooser. Resolve the style as: the saved style, else inference (any filter role means Filter Results + Rules; any rule and no filter role means Rules only), else default to Filter Results + Rules. Nothing is written to the quiz on page load; the style is only written when the merchant switches it. Delete the chooser screen and its inert 'Point based' row.

History, not a choice: the question and the options this was chosen from

Question. Keep the first-entry LogicStyleChooser ('How should this quiz pick results?', with an inert Point based row), or land directly in the workspace with the title switch? If landing directly, which style shows when none is saved?

  • A. No chooser; resolve persisted style > inference (any filter role → Filter Results + Rules; any rule → Rules only) > default Filter Results + Rules; nothing is written on page load.
  • A2. No chooser; default Rules only (the mock's opening state).
  • A3. No chooser; default from recommendEngine's catalogue heuristic.
  • B. Keep the chooser before the workspace.

Reasoning at the time, superseded by the ruling above. A

Why. The Sep-17/18 design puts the style behind the title switch and has no chooser. Funnel builds already auto-map a picking question (deciderMapping), so Filter Results + Rules works on first view while Rules only starts empty and blocked. The inert Point based row is ghost functionality.

D6 · Builder parity and where the style lives Parked

PARKED 2026-09-22 (owner). Parked · reference for the main builder work. Parked by the owner on 2026-09-22: the main builder is being rebuilt, so builder parity is not part of this work. Consequences for this build: the style still lives on the quiz doc (D1), so it survives graduation and the new builder can read it; build the funnel step 3 surface now; do not gate the new UI behind ruleFlow === 'onboarding' in a way that makes it unreachable later. Known gap while parked: a Rules-only quiz opens in today's builder as Filter Results + Rules, and today's builder Logic view still writes rules. The main-builder work picks this section up and builds the same two-style screen there.

History, not a choice: the question and the options this was chosen from

Question. Should the main builder's Logic view (the same LogicTabCard) show the chosen style, the title switch, Edit | Table, Import | Export, the Rules-only screen and the funnel's 'Your recommendations' rule-window band? Where does the style live so both surfaces can read and switch it? Does the field save pill also show in the builder, which already has a top-bar save status?

  • A. Full parity: the builder passes logicStyle and the onboarding band; the style is a decider-gated doc field written by autosave (works on both routes); the field pill shows on both surfaces.
  • B. Read-only parity: the builder renders the right style; switching stays funnel-only (build_session intent).
  • C. Funnel-only: gate all new UI on ruleFlow === 'onboarding'; the builder stays as is.

Reasoning at the time, superseded by the ruling above. A, using the doc field from D1-B. If D1 stays A, choose B and copy the style somewhere the builder can read at graduation.

Why. Today the style is dropped at graduation and a Rules-only quiz opens in the builder as Attributes + Rules, so the merchant sees a different logic model from the one they built. The card is shared by design, and the builder's PUT writes build_session wholesale, so a style kept only in build_session can be clobbered.

D7 · How Undo is built Settled

DECIDED 2026-09-22 (owner). Settled · build option A. Option A. Extend the shared toast with one optional action (plus duration, a live region and keyboard reach) and record the dated owner exception against the design-system rule that toasts carry no actions; add the missing toast providers so Undo is never silently unavailable. Undo is implemented as inverse mutations against the latest document (restore a rule at its index by its id; several deletes in a row accumulate into one Undo), never a whole-document snapshot, so it cannot undo unrelated edits made while the toast is up.

History, not a choice: the question and the options this was chosen from

Question. Every delete, reorder and import shows an Undo toast with no confirm (decided Sep-18). The design-system toast is message-only by rule ('Not clickable, no actions: if an action is needed, it isn't a toast', DS-V2 §7.5), and the embedded routes have no toast provider. How is Undo built?

  • A. Extend QzToast with one optional action (plus duration, live region and keyboard reach) and amend the §7.5 rule with the dated owner exception; add providers to the embedded routes.
  • B. A separate Undo bar component used only by the Logic workspace.
  • C. No toast Undo: rely on the builder's ⌘Z stack (the funnel has none).

Reasoning at the time, superseded by the ruling above. A, with Undo implemented as inverse mutations against the latest doc (restore a rule at its index by id; several deletes accumulate into one Undo), never a whole-doc snapshot.

Why. One toast system keeps queue-of-one behaviour and styling consistent. Inverse mutations avoid undoing unrelated edits made while the toast is up (debounced autosave, other panes) and keep ⌘Z working in the builder.

D9 · Moving 'Picks results' clears mappings Settled

DECIDED 2026-09-22 (owner). Settled · build option A. Option A. Moving 'Picks results' to another question keeps clearing both questions' answer mappings, but it is announced: a toast names what was cleared (for example 'Q1's 6 recommendations were removed') and its Undo restores the role and every target. One path serves the role menu, the Table and Import. No confirm dialog.

History, not a choice: the question and the options this was chosen from

Question. Moving 'Picks results' to another question (role menu, Table, Import) runs moveDecider, which silently clears both questions' answer mappings. Confirm first, announce with Undo, or park the mappings and restore them on switch-back?

  • A. Keep the clearing; a toast names what was cleared (e.g. 'Q1's 6 recommendations were removed') with an Undo that restores the role and all targets.
  • B. A confirm dialog before clearing.
  • C. Park: stop clearing on move so switching back restores the old mappings (changes a locked mutation rule).

Reasoning at the time, superseded by the ruling above. A

Why. Matches the Sep-18 no-confirm + Undo pattern, fixes B6 without touching moveDecider's stale-target rule, and one path serves the role menu, the Table and Import (B24).

D10 · What type changes do to answers and rules Open

STILL OPEN. Not yet ruled on. What a question-type change does to answers and rules (scale conversions dropping answers, five-point trimming to five points, and the rules that referenced the dropped answers). The mock currently trims and tells the merchant; the recommendation is to keep that with an Undo, in the same pattern as D9.

The question and the options, and what is still open

Question. When a question's type changes, do its answers change? The live Questions step keeps answers on Five-point (a unit test pins it); the mock trims or pads to exactly 5 and prunes rule conditions. Should leaving multi-select convert that question's all-of rules to any-of, and what happens to rules when points are removed?

  • A. Live TypeChipSelector semantics: Five-point stamps scale_config {min:1,max:5} and keeps answers; only the points stepper adds or removes answers; leaving multi-select converts all-of rules to any-of with a toast; removed points leave affected rules flagged, with Undo.
  • B. Mock semantics: Five-point trims or pads to 5 answers and prunes rule conditions.
  • C. Converting to a scale replaces answers with numbered points after a confirmation.

Reasoning. A

Why. The owner asked for types 'matched to the live Questions step' (Sep-18). A keeps one behaviour across steps 2 and 3, keeps the pinned test, and never silently deletes mappings (B7, B45).

D12 · 'is not' combined with 'all of' Settled

DECIDED 2026-09-22 (owner). Settled · build option A. Option A. 'is not' and 'all of' cannot be combined. On an 'is not' row the any/all toggle is hidden and the row means none of these answers; sentences read 'not (A or B)'; Import rejects 'NOT (A AND B)' with a named reason. No new storage is added.

History, not a choice: the question and the options this was chosen from

Question. The mock lets an 'is not' row be 'all of' and reads it 'not (A and B)'. The engine can't store that: is_not always means none of the answers, and the live window silently saves none-of. Remove the combination or add storage?

  • A. Remove it: on 'is not' rows the any/all toggle is hidden; the row means none of these; sentences read 'not (A or B)'; import rejects 'NOT (A AND B)'.
  • B. Add optional storage (e.g. DecisionRule.not_all_of?: string[] of question ids) plus engine, analyzer and runtime support.

Reasoning at the time, superseded by the ruling above. A

Why. It keeps the engine predicate unchanged, the combination is rare, and the live UI already misrepresents it.

D16 · Import/Export file contract and library Settled

DECIDED 2026-09-22 (owner). Settled · build option B. Option B, with the Rules sheet staying all-or-nothing. The file carries identity as well as text: every 'When they answer' cell reads 'Qn = answer', the Answers sheet gains a trailing do-not-edit 'Answer ID' column and the Rules sheet a 'Rule ID' column. The Answers sheet updates answers in place and never adds or deletes them; the Recommendations sheet is read-only and any edits to it are reported as ignored. A missing column means 'leave unchanged', never 'clear'. Reasoning at the time, superseded by the ruling above. B, keeping the Rules sheet all-or-nothing (the Sep-18 design) with SheetJS CE 0.20.3 loaded as a lazy chunk.

Why. Text-only matching can't survive repeated answer texts or row edits, and ids make round trips exact. SheetJS matches the mock's API and is smaller; the npm 0.18.5 build has published CVEs (CVE-2023-30533, CVE-2024-22363), and Import parses merchant files.

Scope, sources and ground rules

Read this section first. It fixes what you build, where it renders, which sources you trust and in what order, and the rules every change follows. Terms such as recommendation, Picks results, Keeps everything and never runs are defined in the glossary.

The owner has ruled on every decision this section used to leave open except three. What follows is written in the indicative: it is the thing to build, not a menu. A parenthesised decision id, "(D7)", points at the reasoning in Owner decisions; it is not a signal that anything is still being weighed. The three genuinely open items are gathered under Still open, and parked and marked again wherever they touch a build step.

What ships

One Logic workspace in two styles: "Filter Results + Rules" (logic_style "attributes") and "Rules only" (logic_style "rules"). Both are real engine modes. Rules only is not a view of the other style and not a simplified lens on it: it is its own method of deciding a result, and it decides results for published quizzes (D1). Write the copy, the checks and the tests for two first-class modes.

The style lives on the quiz document as a new top-level Quiz.logic_style field, decider-gated and .optional(), and survives publish into publishedJson so the runtime can read it (D1). Today it lives only in build_session.logic_style (quizSchema.ts:1698-1708), which publish strips (quizPublish.ts:789, 804-807), so a style kept there can never reach the engine. Data model has the field, its migration and its mutation.

Each style has an Edit view and a Table view, switched by "Edit | Table" (mock ACT.vw). The header actions differ by style and view (mock headRight(), confirmed by running the file):

  • Rules only · Edit: a "Paste rules" link and a "Create a rule" primary button. "Paste rules" opens the live PasteRulesModal (mock ACT.stub with the message "Opens the existing Paste rules window"; PasteRulesModal.tsx, mounted by LogicTabCard.tsx:23, 559). Its cross-question "or" output is split into adjacent rules before it is committed (D13, Engine semantics).
  • Filter Results + Rules · Edit: the description gets "More ▾" / "Less ▾" (mock hintHTML(), STYLE_HINT, ACT.hint, remembered in localStorage lg-hint); the Rules-only description has one sentence and no "More". The rules column carries "+ Add" in its head (.rcol-h) and "Paste rules" in its foot (.rcol-f), both written by renderFilter(). The column sits on the right of the workspace (D22).
  • Table view (either style): "Import" and, once the downloads capability resolves (mock DL), "Export" of quiz-logic.xlsx. Neither renders in an Edit view. Export doubles as the import template (D16-template).

Around the workspace sit the rule window ("Create a rule" / "Edit rule"), the "Add recommendations" window, the live "Add a question" dialog, and inline editing of question and answer text with a save pill at the edited field (D8).

Five consequences worth reading before you start

  • The style field has to be top-level, not in build_session. Publish strips build_session out of publishedJson (quizPublish.ts:789, 804-807), so a style stored there is invisible to /q and to /q/:id.json. A top-level key is carried through publish untouched, and stripPublicJsonPayload drops only review_enrichment_sources and translations (quizPublish.ts:49-50), so the public JSON carries it too.
  • A top-level field needs no intent. The funnel's autosave keeps the server's build_session and writes every other field of the client doc (funnelIntents.server.ts:124-131), and the builder's PUT writes the whole document (quizEditorIO.server.ts:341-359). So Quiz.logic_style is written by a pure mutation through useQuizDraft's commit on both surfaces. The set-logic-style intent (funnelIntents.server.ts:1461-1481) loses its only caller when the chooser goes; leave the intent and the build_session.logic_style field in place, parsed forever, and stop writing them.
  • The publish gate blocks a Rules-only quiz until it is style-aware. quizPublish.ts:408-414 throws PublishError on any validateQuiz issue, and validateQuiz emits missing_decider when no question carries role: "decides" (quizValidation.ts:128). A Rules-only quiz has no such question by definition, so validateQuiz gets the same style awareness as the report in the same change, or nothing built in Rules only can ever be published. The report must never read safer than the gate; that invariant is already encoded at pathReport.ts:124-136.
  • The safety net is a real runtime change. Today a decider doc whose target does not resolve renders a bare card containing the localized no_results_match string and nothing else (QuizRuntime.tsx:1713-1721). The named fallbacks run only for a target that resolved and turned out empty (recommendDecider.ts:522-538), and the comment at recommendDecider.ts:520-521 says the unresolved case is "deliberately not handled here". This work handles it, for both styles, which means the runtime proof rules apply in full (Repo rules).
  • D12 costs no storage. The schema already says an is_not group requires none of its listed answers and that any_of relaxes only "is" groups (quizSchema.ts:1725-1730). The work is the UI (hide the any/all toggle on an "is not" row), the sentence grammar, the Import reason, and never putting a question that carries is_not conditions into any_of.

Still open, and parked

Three items are still open. Do not pick them.

D2, Filter Results + Rules only. In that style "Show" appends after the base pool and is often cut off by the results cap, while its hint promises "these become the results" (recommendDecider.ts:261-275 for the action path; Engine semantics step 8 for the cap). The owner chooses between changing the engine so Show puts its products first, and changing the hint to describe appending. Blocks: the Filter rule window's Show hint copy, any engine change to Show ordering, and the Filter-side test that pins what Show does. Does not block: anything in Rules only, where D2 is settled (Show is the whole result and the rule window offers Show only), or the Show / Pin / Hide verbs themselves, which stay in Filter Results + Rules.

D10, question-type changes. What a type change does to answers and to the rules that referenced them (scale conversions dropping answers, five-point trimming to five, and the rules pointing at the dropped answers). Blocks: the type-change path behind the question pane's type chips and the "Add a question" dialog's type switch. Meanwhile: the mock trims and tells the merchant; build nothing that depends on a different answer, and do not ship a silent trim.

D14, second half. Whether used recommendations also move to the end of the tray, and how the armed state reads on the builder's editor surface, which re-points the accent colour. Blocks: tray ordering and the builder's armed styling only. Does not block: the colours, which are settled (green = placed on no answer, black = placed, violet = armed), or the one-row "+N more" layout.

When a step needs one of these, stop, ask the owner and name the waiting step in your report. Never pick an option silently.

Two areas are parked. Build neither now.

D4, diagnostics. The check popover shows findings and opens from the CTA. Do not rebuild "Check my logic", the Diagnose modal, "Test a path" or the AI review into this step, and do not add the "N to review" affordance. Leave the shipped PathTester (three importers on origin/main, all of which render it: LogicView.tsx:16 at :246 and :248, DiagnoseModal.tsx:9 at :80, ContextPanel.tsx:27 at :657; BuilderSettings.tsx:23 and RecPageDiagram.tsx:110 only mention it in comments) and usePathQuality (one importer, HealthPopover.tsx:7, called at :62) in place and unreferenced from the new step; they are not dead code and they are not yours to delete. When diagnostics are built later they hang off this popover's footer.

D6, builder parity. The main builder is being rebuilt, so this work ships the funnel step 3 surface only. The style still lives on the document (D1), so the new builder can read it. Two things follow. First, name the gap in your report and hand it to the main-builder project: a Rules-only quiz opens in today's builder as Filter Results + Rules, because BuilderLogicView passes no logicStyle prop (BuilderSettings.tsx:67-79; the prop at LogicTabCard.tsx:105 and rulesOnly = logicStyle === "rules" at :112), and today's builder Logic view still writes rules. Second, do not gate the new UI on ruleFlow === "onboarding" or on anything else that would make it unreusable there; build it so the main-builder work can mount the same two-style screen.

The reference mock, and how to read it

  • Follow https://claude.ai/artifact/4qJdbPyszvZe34AEm9yvWS. Source: /Users/chase/code/quizocalypse-builder/docs/design/logic-tab/rules-row/index.html, untracked in git. The source is being edited in place as the confirmed mock defects are fixed (Fixed in mock items), and the artifact is republished from it; the last republish was 2026-09-21. On 2026-09-21 the file is about 1,200 lines; the 1,067-line copy that was reviewed for the defect list is kept at scratchpad/review/rules-row.before-fixes.html. Because the file moves, this handoff cites mock code by identifier (a function, handler, constant or stylesheet rule), never by line number; search the file for the name.
  • Both styles are in it, and both are first-class. It opens on Rules only (const S, initial style:"rules"; S has no view key until ACT.vw or ACT.reset sets one, and an absent view renders as Edit). The title ▾ (the .stitle button in statusHead(), data-act="stylemenu", title "Change how this quiz decides") opens the "Logic style" popover (styleMenu() via ACT.stylemenu) with "Filter Results + Rules" and "Rules only". ACT.setstyle changes the style and sets the view to Edit when the pick differs from the current style, and leaves the view alone on a re-pick; confirmed by running the file: switching from Table lands on Edit, re-picking the current style from Table stays on Table. Nothing in the mock or in this handoff ranks one style above the other.
  • Sizes: build at 100%. Owner decision D20, 2026-09-20: the mock's sizes are the spec. In the stylesheet: .work max-width 1256px (padding 22px 16px 40px), .stage min-width 1200px, .grid3 columns 262px minmax(0,1fr) 304px (computed 262 / 656 / 304 at a 1440px viewport). docs/design/logic-tab/logic-step-sizes/index.html (artifact Gsj46uCPJka9H6831htWxb) is a ×1.3 scaled copy and is not the spec. Layout and sizing has every measurement.
  • Ignore docs/design/logic-tab/logic-step-layouts/index.html (artifact S7Nhkh6t5Z9cWd6F8NpjGQ) for its Rules only screen: that is the older three-column layout. Its Filter Results + Rules sizing CSS is identical to rules-row's, and it is the file the 2026-09-20 sizing decision names, so it is only the Rules only screen you ignore.
  • Product versus harness. The product is the .work card that renderInner() writes into #stage (Rules only: statusHead() plus rulesBand() and vizRecs(), or tableHTML() in Table view; Filter Results + Rules: renderFilter()) and the overlay roots after the stage: #pop (popovers), #modal (rule window), #aqm (Add a question), #addrec (Add recommendations), #toast, #svb (save pill), #svlive (the screen-reader live region svStart() writes "Saved" into) and the hidden #impfile file input that ACT.imp clicks for Import. fbar(), which renderInner() also puts inside #stage (logo, the step rail "✓ Recommendations · ✓ Questions · 03 Logic · 04 Results", a stubbed "‹" Back and "Continue →"), is a stand-in for the live funnel chrome (Step1Funnel's bar and Continue bridge, Step1Funnel.tsx:99-117; funnelChrome.tsx:43 useFunnelBar), not part of LogicTabCard; its only real content is the "Fix N issues to continue" gate (Checks and Continue). Its "N to review" is not built: D4 parks the diagnostics affordance. The builder renders the card without it. The .shell bar above the stage (h1 "Logic step · Rules only", the "10 answers on Q5" and "30 recommendations" checkboxes #stress / #stress30, "Reset" ACT.reset, "Show it empty" ACT.wipe) and the #pitch line (text set per style in renderInner()) are a test harness; the h1 never changes with the style (Mock stand-ins).
  • Where behaviour lives. const S is the doc-like workspace state: sel, style, view, armed, uid, qs, rules. Overlay drafts and transient state are separate globals: M (rule-window draft), AQ (Add a question), AR (Add recommendations), VP (value-picker draft), pop (the open popover), UNDO and IMP_UNDO (undo snapshots), SV (save pill), RECS (the recommendation catalogue, mutated by ACT.arAdd and the 30-recommendations toggle), hintOpen (More / Less) and DL (downloads capability), plus the popover search strings PKQ, MRQ, TRQ. Workspace actions change S and call render(), which runs renderInner(), fitRows(), svPlace() and then placePop() (or drawPop() while the check popover is open); overlay actions call drawModal, drawAQ, drawAR, drawVP or drawPop instead. One document click listener closes a stale popover and dispatches ACT[el.dataset.act](el) for the nearest [data-act]; the const ACT table holds every handler. The document keydown listener owns the Esc order (popover, then Add a question, then Add recommendations, then the rule window, then the armed chip) and Enter / Space on div[data-act] and tr[data-act]. The remaining listeners, by target: the search inputs #vp-q, #pk-q, #mr-q, #tr-q (input); the inline editors [data-edit] (focusin, input, keydown, focusout, paste, driving svStart / svPlace); the .aqgrip keydown that reorders Add-a-question rows with ArrowUp / ArrowDown; #impfile change → importFile; dragstart / dragover / drop / dragend on .rr[data-ri] (rule reorder); mouseover on .rpill[data-r] (strip hover); #stress and #stress30 change (harness); window resize → markMore, fitRows, placeToast, placePop, svPlace; capture-phase document scroll → placePop and svPlace. To learn what a control does, read its data-act, then ACT[that name].
  • Dead code in it. The "How this works" and "How rules work" popover builders (const HOW, const HOWR, ACT.how, ACT.howrules) have no trigger in either style (zero data-act="how" / "howrules" elements render). The top section is removed (D23); do not port them.
  • Where a ruling overrides the mock. The mock is the design reference, not the final word: where a ruling and the mock disagree, the ruling wins and the mock is still being edited towards it. Four disagreements you will hit. Show / Pin / Hide in Rules only: the mock still draws all three; build Show only there (D2). "is not" plus "all of": the mock renders mnot and mall on the same row, with an overMax warning for the combination; hide the any/all toggle on an "is not" row instead (D12). Duplicate: the mock has no Duplicate control anywhere; put it in the rule window's top row next to "Delete rule" (D11). Undo: the mock's UNDO / snap / ACT.undo restores S.rules wholesale through fitRule, which is a snapshot; build inverse mutations against the latest document instead (D7).
  • It specifies behaviour, not implementation. Its data are stand-ins, its checks, coverage and shadow logic are simplifications, and its save pill runs on timers. Mock stand-ins says what replaces each.
The defect list is 63 confirmed reports numbered B1 to B68; B33, B39, B42, B44 and B46 were rejected, so those numbers are gaps. Their CODE lines quote line numbers of the reviewed 1,067-line copy (scratchpad/review/rules-row.before-fixes.html); on the current file, search for the identifier or the quoted copy.

Where code truth lives

  • origin/main at b4aa278 (2026-09-16) is the only code truth. Read it through git: 
    git -C /Users/chase/code/quizocalypse-builder show origin/main:app/components/studio/logicTab/LogicTabCard.tsx
git -C /Users/chase/code/quizocalypse-builder grep -n "logic_style" origin/main -- app
git -C /Users/chase/code/quizocalypse-builder ls-tree -r --name-only origin/main app/components/studio/logicTab
  • The working tree is stale. Branch builder sits at cb25601 (2026-08-11), 163 commits behind origin/main. Its app/components/studio/logicTab/ has 7 of origin/main's 16 files: it lacks the seven modules LogicQuestionWidget, ValuePickerPopover, PasteRulesModal, CoverageSidebar, createRuleBand, AttributePickerDialog and RulesSetupScaffold (plus the ValuePickerPopover and createRuleBand test files), and its Step3Shell has no style chooser. Never read Logic code, docs or line numbers from it.
  • Build on origin/main. Don't check out, reset, clean or stash over the builder tree: it holds the owner's uncommitted work (modified files and untracked folders such as app/components/integrations/) and the untracked mocks, and the stash stack is shared by every worktree. A separate worktree created from origin/main (git worktree add <dir> origin/main) leaves all of that untouched.
  • Ref convention. Every path:line in this document is on origin/main (b4aa278) unless marked mock; mock references are identifiers, not lines. If origin/main has moved past b4aa278 after your git fetch, run git log b4aa278..origin/main -- <path> before relying on a line. If a ref and the code disagree, the code wins; tell the owner.

CLAUDE.md's architecture map predates the Logic step. The funnel has four visible steps, Recommendations, Questions, Logic and Results (funnelStages.ts:19-33), not the five CLAUDE.md lists (CLAUDE.md:43-49); logic_model sits at quizSchema.ts:1992, not :1331 (CLAUDE.md:37); and the legacy points-model folder is app/components/onboarding/questionsLogic/, not the app/components/questionsLogic/ CLAUDE.md:112 names (no such folder exists on origin/main). Its rules still apply.

The decider-only invariant

  • Legacy docs never reach the new UI. QuestionBuilderStage renders Step3Shell only when logic_model === "decider"; legacy docs get QuestionsLogicLayout and their Continue skips Logic (QuestionBuilderStage.tsx:76, 87-93, 204-255). BuilderLogicView sends legacy docs to LogicView (BuilderSettings.tsx:52-65; LogicTabCard.tsx:49-50).
  • Gate everything new on logic_model === "decider": every mutation, engine branch, validation branch and loader field. A mutation called on a legacy doc returns it unchanged, as setQuestionRole does (deciderMutations.ts:22-24).
  • The style field and the engine branch are inside that gate. Quiz.logic_style is only ever written on a decider doc, and resolveTarget's Rules-only branch sits inside the logic_model === "decider" arm that recommendationEngine.ts:392 already enters. A legacy doc's resolution path does not change by a single line.
  • The safety net is decider-gated too. Build it inside the decider arm of QuizRuntime (the branch at QuizRuntime.tsx:1713-1721 and the fallback computation at :1584-1595). The legacy result path at :1722 onwards, including its own globalFallback prop, is untouched.
  • Legacy docs stay byte-identical (CLAUDE.md:36-39); the byte pin checks it. A new top-level .optional() key never appears on a legacy doc, so the pinned quiz's JSON is unchanged; prove it, do not assume it.
  • New schema fields are .optional(), never .default(): a default rewrites every legacy doc on its next parse-save round trip (CLAUDE.md:40-41). Follow BuildSession.logic_style, which is absent until set and round-trips absent (quizSchema.ts:1698-1708), and DecisionRule.match / any_of, whose comments spell out the same discipline (quizSchema.ts:1733-1734, 1746-1749).

Precedence: the newest owner ruling wins

Owner rulings are dated, and the newest wins over older rulings, code comments and design docs. For this screen the newest are the 2026-09-21 and 2026-09-22 rulings recorded in Owner decisions, which sit above the 2026-09-17/18 mock rounds and the 2026-09-20 sizing decision; an owner ruling dated after this handoff beats it too. When you change code that sits under a comment recording an older ruling, follow this handoff and rewrite the comment with the new ruling and its date. Edit design docs (DECISIONS.md, the logic-tab README) only with the owner's OK.

The safety net has no merchant control on a decider quiz, and you are not building one. The chain the net reuses reads global_fallback, then rec_page_settings.global.emptyFallbackCol, then safetyNetCol (QuizRuntime.tsx:1584-1595; recommendDecider.ts:522-538), and publish already fetches and bakes both collections for decider docs (quizPublish.ts:443-447). But the only UI that writes those two fields is RecPageV2Panel.tsx:472-488, and Step1Funnel mounts RecommendationStage (which contains it) only for legacy docs; decider docs get ResultsGuided instead (Step1Funnel.tsx:326-340), and ResultsGuided deliberately dropped its own fallback chooser (ResultsGuided.tsx:513-515). On a decider doc the writers are the build-time seed (onboardingBuild.server.ts:399-404) and the decider-conversion seed (proposeDeciderConversion.ts:221). So a decider quiz can reach publish with no net configured, and the net then resolves nothing and the shopper sees the same bare no_results_match card as today. Build the net over the chain as it stands, do not invent a control for it, and raise the gap with the owner in your report.

Copy and styling rules

  • No em dashes in merchant-facing copy (owner, 2026-09-07; LogicQuestionWidget.tsx:57). No lint or check-tokens catches them, so before you hand back run 
    git -C /Users/chase/code/quizocalypse-builder grep -n $'\xe2\x80\x94' origin/main -- app/components/studio/logicTab app/components/studio/AddQuestionDialog.tsx app/components/onboarding/questionsLogicV3/Step3Shell.tsx
    over your branch as well, and reword every string a merchant can read (comments may keep them). On origin/main the merchant-facing ones are: AddQuestionDialog.tsx:173 (the "Five point" note), :182-183 (the answer grip's title and aria-label); AttributePickerDialog.tsx:191; CreateRuleModal.tsx:615, 619 (save-failure toasts), 746, 775, 864, 896 ("+N more, type to narrow"), 786, 882, 798, 1104 (the legacy-rule note); Explainers.tsx:259, 309, 336, 475, 494 (mounted by LogicTabCard); LogicTabCard.tsx:219, 235, 286, 309, 453; LogicTabMenus.tsx:374, 609; PasteRulesModal.tsx:126-127; QuestionWindow.tsx:212, 504, 508, 624, 717, 790; ValuePickerPopover.tsx:352; logicTabFields.ts:576-577 (the narrow-by toasts); Step3Shell.tsx:440 and :487 (both inside the top section that D23 removes). Every new string this work adds is subject to the same rule: the D9 clear toast, the D12 Import reason, the D16 sheet headers and the example row's placeholder cells, and the D3 finding messages. In the mock the same rule applies to the typeBtn template's title ("Change the question type ..."), the .aqnote sentence in aqHTML() ("Five point generates the answers itself ...") and the .aqgrip title and aria-label in aqHTML() ("Reorder ..."). The lone dash glyph that marks an empty cell (LogicQuestionWidget.tsx:395, 978; LogicTabCard.tsx:306; QuestionWindow.tsx:950; the mock's .dash and .dim2 spans in Info cells and "Shown by rules") is a placeholder, not copy.
  • Locked vocabulary, enforced through one module. Never surface decider, bucket, branch, boost, weight or score (HANDOFF.md:46-47). D18 makes this checkable: the merchant-facing names live in one shared constants module that every surface imports, the builder's Rules inspector and the pinned tests included. The renames are "Attributes + Rules" → "Filter Results + Rules", "Asked only" → "Info only", "Recommendations from step 1" → "Recommendations", "+ Add rule" → "Create a rule" / "+ Add", and the empty Picks cell and its picker both read "Choose a result". The live sites to move: LogicQuestionWidget.tsx:59 (trayLabel), :70-75 and :794-817 (the "Tag buckets" filter and group heading, which break the locked vocabulary today), :352 (the role labels); LogicTabMenus.tsx:452, 460; Explainers.tsx:173; logicTabFields.ts:596; ContextPanel.tsx:932 (the builder's Rules inspector) with its pinned assertions at ContextPanel.rules.test.tsx:99, 108; and the comments at quizSchema.ts:362 and :1702. QuestionSection.tsx:427 carries the same literal but the component is unmounted, so it is not a blocker; if you touch the file, take the constant.
  • Rule sentences have one grammar (D17): verb-first and answers-only ("Show dryness when ..."), parentheses around multi-answer groups, bold joins, "not (...)" for a negated group, full-text tooltips on truncated answers, and a question label only when the same answer text exists on another question. The Table and the export never use that form: they always read "Q7 = Yes" (D16, D17). Mock sentence() is the reference for the prose form.
  • Two colour vocabularies, two surfaces. D14's decided colours govern the Picks-results tray and the picker: .tchip.fresh (green text, --ok-line border) = placed on no answer of this question, .tchip.used (the base .tchip ink; there is no separate .used rule) = placed, .tchip.armed (accent border and wash) = armed. The Rules-only "Your recommendations" strip uses a different signal in the mock: an .rpill with an amber .sd dot (--warn-dot) and, on the "+ Create a rule" pills, the dashed --warn-line border of .rpill.none = no rule yet; a green .sd.on dot = has a rule. Do not apply green / black to the strip or amber dots to the tray. Whether used recommendations also move to the end of the tray is the open half of D14; build the colours, leave the order as the mock has it and say so in your report.
  • No hex colours and no px box-shadow literals in .tsx under app/components or app/routes; check-tokens fails on any new offender (scripts/check-tokens.mjs:4-13). Map the mock's :root values to tokens. Most equal Quartz tokens, for example --accent #5B45D6 = --qz-accent, --ink #201C2E = --qz-ink, --ground #F5F4F8 = --qz-cream-2, --ok-wash #E7F3ED = --qz-live-wash (quizocalypse.css:59-101). The rest have close counterparts in the Logic-step token set --qz-ls-* (line2, ok-line, warn-wash, warn-line, crit-wash, crit-line, cell-bg) or none at all (the blue result-chip family --res, --res-wash, --res-line, and --warn-dot). Two things to know before you extend that set: the Quartz sheet defines --qz-ls-* twice, at quizocalypse.css:173-182 (inside the shape group, "Scoped to the Logic step surfaces", which also defines --qz-on-accent) and again at :226-236 ("Used ONLY by the .qz-lm-* Logic-step modal section"); the later block wins with identical values, so collapse them into one block and widen the comment when you add tokens rather than inlining hex. And the mock's neighbours differ from the tokens by a shade (--ok-line #BFE0CF vs --qz-ls-ok-line #BEDCCC; --warn-wash #FBF1E0 vs #FBF3E4; --warn-line #EDD3A4 vs #E9D9B5; --crit-wash #FBEDEC vs #FBECEA; --crit-line #EFCBC7 vs #E8C4C0; --line2 #CFCADC vs #CFCADD): the token values win, not the mock's hex. Shadows use --qz-lift-* (quizocalypse.css:197-199).
  • Desktop only, at 100%. The Wiskr admin is desktop-only (owner, 2026-09-16): build for 1280 to 1440px wide and draw no phone layout for this screen. Build at the mock's sizes (D20, 2026-09-20): card max 1256px, stage min 1200px, columns 262 / 1fr / 304; below 1200px the page scrolls sideways, it never reflows. The shopper-facing /q runtime still has to work on phones, and the safety net renders there, so its no-match and fallback states get a phone screenshot as well as a desktop one.

How to use the Owner decisions list

  • Every ruling in The rulings, as build instructions is built as written. That list is the whole of the settled scope: D1 with its safety net, D2's Rules-only half, D3, D5, D7, D8, D9, D11, D12, D13, D14's colours, D15, D16 with the template, D17, D18, D19, D20, D21, D22, D23 and D24. An item's old "recommendation" text in the decisions list is history now, not a proposal to weigh; read it only for the reasoning.
  • Also decided, and specified in the sections rather than the list: choosing the other style always lands on Edit, even from Table, and re-choosing the current style keeps the view (mock ACT.setstyle); deleting a rule asks no confirmation and shows "Rule N deleted" with an "Undo" button. In the mock, while that toast is up, further deletes, drops in the rule drag ("Moved to position N") and "Show it empty" (ACT.wipe) join the same Undo entry, so the toast reads "2 rules deleted" and the button becomes "Undo both" or "Undo all N" when deletes mix with moves; that accumulation is the behaviour to build, but build it out of inverse mutations that accumulate, not out of the mock's whole-state snap (D7). The live baseline already deletes without a confirm: LogicTabCard.tsx:467-470 commits removeDecisionRule(doc, rule.id) and toasts "Rule deleted", so there is no rule-delete confirm to remove; window.confirm survives only in the unmounted RuleRow.tsx:67 and in Step3Shell.tsx:277 (question and content-page delete). "+ Add question" opens the live AddQuestionDialog (owner ruling 2026-09-16, AddQuestionDialog.tsx:5-11); the pane's question types follow the live Questions step's TypeChipSelector.
  • The three open items block only the steps the implementation plan ties to them (Implementation plan): D2's Filter half, D10's type-change path, D14's tray ordering and builder armed styling. Build everything else. When a step needs one of them, stop, ask the owner, and name the waiting step in your report. Never pick an option silently.
  • The two parked areas are not gaps to fill. D4 (diagnostics) and D6 (builder parity) are deliberate omissions with a later home. Do not build them, do not work around them, and do not delete the code they will use. Name the D6 gap in your report and hand it to the main-builder project.

What ships today and what this change keeps, replaces, removes or adds

This section is the delta against origin/main (b4aa278). It describes shipped behaviour only where this change touches it, and each row points to the section that specifies the new behaviour. Tags: Exists keep it as it is (restyle only); Partial keep the code, change its behaviour or copy; New build it; Conflict a shipped surface the design removes or replaces; Fixed in mock a defect the review confirmed that the current mock file no longer has. "Dn" refers to the Owner decisions list; a "(Dn)" pointer in a row is there so a reader can find the reasoning, not because the row is still a choice.

The owner has ruled. Build this, do not re-open it.

Settled and specified below as built behaviour: D1 (Rules only is a real engine mode, the style lives on the doc) and its safety net, the Rules-only half of D2, D3 (one style-aware Tier-1 report), D5 (no first-entry chooser), D7 (toast with one action, Undo as inverse mutations), D8 (save pill at the edited field), D9 (announced mapping clear with Undo), D11 (row controls on hover and focus, Duplicate in the window), D12 ("is not" never combines with "all of"), D13 (Paste rules splits a cross-question "or"), the colour half of D14, D15 ("+ Add recommendations" writes through ensure-targets with a group kind), D16 and its template addition (the identity-carrying spreadsheet), D17 (verb-first answers-only sentences), D18 (rename everywhere through shared constants), D19 (keep the live surfaces the mock does not draw), D20 (the mock's 100% sizes: .work max 1256px, stage min 1200px, columns 262px / 1fr / 304px), D21 (embedded toast provider only), D22 (rules column on the right), D23 (top section removed) and D24 (rule window layout).

Parked, do not build now: D4 diagnostics and D6 builder parity. Each is named at the rows it touches, with what to do meanwhile.

Still open, do not pick: the Filter half of D2, D10, and the second half of D14. See the callout below.

Three open questions touch this section. Flag them, do not decide them.
  • D2, the Filter Results + Rules half. In Filter Results + Rules, "Show" appends its recommendations after the base pool and is then cut off by the results cap, while the rule window's hint promises "these become the results". The owner must choose: change the engine so Show puts its products first, or change the hint to describe appending. Blocks: the Show hint copy in the Filter rule window, and whether applyRuleAction's show branch keeps appending (recommendDecider.ts:294-300, the show branch of applyRuleAction). Build the Filter window with Show / Pin / Hide exactly as today and leave the hint string in one place so a copy change is a one-line edit. Nothing about Rules only waits on this: there Show is the whole result and the window offers Show only.
  • D10. What a question-type change does to answers and to the rules that referenced them (scale conversions dropping answers, a five-point trim, rules left pointing at answers that no longer exist). Blocks: the pane's type line and the "Question type" popover, the Table's Type column, and whether the loss carries an Undo in the D9 pattern. Build the type line and the popover so the conversion path is a single function the ruling can later fill in; do not ship a conversion that silently drops answers before it is ruled on.
  • D14, the second half. Whether recommendations already used still move to the end of the tray, and how the armed state reads on the builder's editor surface (which re-points the accent colour). Blocks: the tray's sort order and the accent token, and retargeting logic-widget-verify.mjs:99,151, which pin today's grey-and-slide-last cards. The colours are settled (green not placed, black placed, violet armed); build those and keep the sort behind one comparator.
Mock references. "Mock" means docs/design/logic-tab/rules-row/index.html as it stands on 2026-09-21 14:40 (1,200 lines). It was edited after the Sep-19 inventories and the Sep-20 fix records were captured, so this section cites it by function or handler name, never by line. Things the current file has that the earlier inputs do not: the bar's "N to review" link and ACT.review, the cached deadCalc/deadWhy with three "never runs" reasons, lossMsg/lossToast after answer or recommendation removals, undoLive() gating a run of deletes into one Undo, rule ids from rid(), the coverage helpers showsRecs/recMapped/recCovered, and the empty Filter column's "No question picks the result yet" branch in ruleRows(). Two of those are deliberately not ported: the "N to review" link and ACT.review are diagnostics, which D4 parks, and the mock's loadXLSX() script tag pulls a library D16 rules out.

This work ships funnel step 3 only. D6 parks builder parity because the main builder is being rebuilt; the style still lives on the quiz doc so the new builder can read it, and nothing in the new UI may be written in a way that makes it unreusable there.

Acceptance for this delta

These are the checks that prove the delta itself landed. Per-surface acceptance lives in the sections each row links to; the full gate chain and probe list are in tests-and-probes.

The dual-model invariant, first and last

  1. The gate chain runs unpiped and clean before every commit: npm run typecheck && npm test -- --run && npm run build && npm run lint && node scripts/check-tokens.mjs (CLAUDE.md, origin/main lines 50-53).
  2. The byte pin holds after every deploy: curl -sS https://quizocalypse-studio.fly.dev/q/cmqqcb0ao004mqvkwjug7t0ya.json | shasum -a 256 starts c02ccaec98a0fe9e. That quiz is a published legacy doc; never republish it.
  3. A legacy doc (logic_model absent) parsed and re-serialized through the new schema is byte-identical. The new style field is .optional() and decider-gated, so a legacy round trip adds no key.
  4. A published decider doc that predates this change and has no style field resolves exactly as it does today, through the Filter Results + Rules engine. Prove it on a deploy fixture by diffing normalized outerHTML of the same /q/:id render before and after.

The runtime change (D1 and the safety net)

  1. Unit: with the style "rules", resolveTarget returns the first matching rule's recommendations and reads no role and no answer mapping; the same doc with the style absent resolves through the picking question.
  2. Unit: with the style "rules" and no rule matching, the result is the safety net chain (global_fallback, then emptyFallbackCol, then safetyNetCol), and emptyFallback: "hide" still wins as an explicit choice.
  3. Unit: in Filter Results + Rules, a resolution with an empty pool takes the same chain, unchanged from today.
  4. Full e2e plus screenshot review of /q, per CLAUDE.md origin/main lines 77-80: app/components/runtime/** and the engine libs it imports are the highest-risk edit class. Decompose, do not rewrite.
  5. The public JSON of a newly published Rules-only quiz carries the style field, and of a newly published Filter quiz carries it too; neither carries build_session.

The step

  1. Opening step 3 writes nothing to the quiz. Confirm with a network trace: no autosave PUT and no intent fires on load, on either style (D5).
  2. A quiz with a filter role and no saved style opens on Filter Results + Rules; a quiz with a rule, no filter role and no saved style opens on Rules only; a quiz with neither opens on Filter Results + Rules. No chooser renders in any case.
  3. A quiz whose only style is build_session.logic_style opens on that style and writes nothing until the merchant switches.
  4. Switching the style writes the doc field once, lands on Edit, and survives Back then Continue.
  5. Deleting a rule toasts "Rule N deleted · Undo"; Undo restores that rule at its index with its id. An unrelated edit made while the toast is up is still present after Undo. Two deletes in a row produce one "2 rules deleted · Undo".
  6. Reordering by ↑ or ↓ with the keyboard alone works in the Filter column and the Rules-only row; the drop line and the landing index agree for both directions.
  7. Moving "Picks results" to another question toasts what was cleared, and Undo restores both questions' roles and every cleared target. The role menu, the Table and Import all produce the same toast.
  8. An "is not" row shows no any/all toggle; its sentence reads "not (A or B)"; the same rule exported and re-imported round-trips, and a hand-written "NOT (A AND B)" import is rejected with a named reason.
  9. Pasting a rule whose questions are joined by "or" produces adjacent rules, one per question group, with the same verb and the same recommendations, and no stored match: "any". An existing rule with match: "any" still renders correctly and keeps it after an edit.
  10. Export on a quiz with no rules produces a file with both sheets, their headers, the id columns and one example row, which imports back without error.
  11. Import of a file whose Rules sheet has one bad row changes nothing and names the row. Import of a file missing a column leaves that column's data unchanged. An edited Recommendations sheet reports the edits as ignored.
  12. "+ Add recommendations" creates rows through /api/categories/ensure-targets in batches of at most 12, is idempotent on a repeat, and its rows are still there after a Step-1 re-group.
  13. In Rules only the rule window offers Show only; in Filter Results + Rules it offers Show, Pin and Hide.
  14. The blocked CTA opens the check popover; the popover's question findings select the question and its rule findings open the rule. No other control in the step opens diagnostics.
  15. The Tier-1 report in Rules only reports no picking-question findings, and blocks on zero rules, on no rule that can show anything, and on a rule missing answers or recommendations. The report never reads safer than the publish gate.
  16. No internal word (decider, bucket, branch, boost, weight, score, "Tag buckets") appears in the rendered step, the builder's Rules inspector, the Table or the export. Grep the shared constants module, then the rendered DOM.
  17. On /app/onboarding/:quizId a delete toast renders and its Undo works (D21).

Layout and sizing

Build at the size of the reference mock, unscaled (D20). The owner confirmed the sizing on Filter Results + Rules (artifact S7Nhkh6t) on 2026-09-20, and the reference mock 4qJdbPys carries the same stylesheet: every sizing rule quoted below is byte-identical in the two files (.work, .stage, .grid3, .rail, .arow, .rcol, .mrow and .bk all match character for character), so measure whichever file you have open and you get the same numbers. The size study at Gsj46uCP (the same widget at 130%) is not the spec. Every value below is read from the mock's stylesheet; in the app they come from Quartz --qz-* tokens, not hex or px literals (scripts/check-tokens.mjs:4-13 fails on a new hex colour or px box-shadow literal in any .tsx under app/components or app/routes).

How to read this section. Sizes are CSS px at 100%. "Padding" is top right bottom left. Type is size / weight / line-height in the Figtree stack ("Figtree", -apple-system, "Segoe UI", "Helvetica Neue", sans-serif); the base is 400 14px / 1.45. Wiskr admin is desktop-only: nothing here has a phone layout. Mock code is cited by identifier (a function, handler or stylesheet rule), never by line number, because the mock file is still being edited; deployed code is cited as path:line on origin/main (b4aa278).
The two styles are equals. "Rules only" is a saved engine mode, not a view of "Filter Results + Rules" (D1): the style lives on the quiz document and survives publish, and in "rules" the engine ignores question roles and answer mappings, so the first matching rule's recommendations are the result. Every measurement below therefore exists twice over: the Rules-only screen is complete on its own, not a trimmed version of the other. Nothing in this section may render Rules only as a degraded or partial layout.

Still open, and what it blocks here

Three owner decisions are still open. Do not pick any of them.
  • D2, the Filter Results + Rules half only. In "attributes", "Show" appends after the base pool and the results cap can cut it off, while its hint reads "these become the results" (mock VERBS). The owner chooses either an engine change or new hint wording. Blocks: the final string of the .vhint line in the rule window's "What happens" row when the style is "attributes", and nothing else. Build the row at the sizes below and read the hint from the copy constant so the string can change without touching layout. For Rules only D2 is settled: "Show" is the whole result, the hint is true there, and the rule window offers "Show" alone.
  • D10. What a question-type change does to answers and to the rules that referenced them. Blocks: no measurement. The answer row grid and the 58px scale-point buckets are built either way; D10 decides whether rows disappear under the merchant and what the announcement says, which lands in the question-pane and toast specs, not in these numbers.
  • D14, second half. Whether used recommendations also move to the end of the tray, and how the armed state reads on the builder's editor surface, which re-points the accent tokens (quizocalypse.css:250-257). Blocks: the chip order inside .tray-c and the armed chip's colour when this card is later mounted in the builder. Build the decided colours now (green, black, violet) in source order; leave the ordering comparator in one place so the answer is a one-line change.
Parked, with something to do meanwhile. D4 (diagnostics) is parked: the check popover shows findings and opens from the blocked CTA only. Do not lay out "Check my logic", the Diagnose modal, "Test a path", the AI review, or the "N to review" chip (mock .fbar .rev); leave the shipped PathTester and usePathQuality untouched and unreferenced. D6 (builder parity) is parked: build the funnel step 3 surface only. Meanwhile, keep every new rule scoped to the card's own class, never to .qz-s3-logicview or to the funnel page, so the main-builder project can mount the same card. Name the gap in your handover: a Rules-only quiz opens in today's builder as Filter Results + Rules.

The mock nests the card in a harness: .stagewrap (overflow-x auto) wraps .stage (min-width 1200, min-height 760), which holds .work (max-width 1256, padding 22 16 40) and then .card. In the app the funnel page plays the part of the stage, and today it is too narrow for the D20 sizes.

Widening the two wrappers is a required part of this work, not a nicety: at 1208 the three columns compute to 262 / 640 / 304 instead of 262 / 656 / 304, and the rule window's 676-wide answer strip stops matching the centre column it was measured against.

  • Sideways scroll below 1200 is a new wrapper. The mock gets it from .stagewrap. .qz-page is width: 100% with no overflow handling (quizocalypse.css:666, :812), so add one overflow-x: auto element around the card and set min-width: 1200px on the element inside it. The page scrolls sideways below 1200; it never reflows, and no column collapses.
  • Scope the new CSS to the card. Put every rule under the card's own class. .qz-s3-logicview is the funnel's wrapper; the builder mounts the card without it (D6), and a rule that only works inside the funnel wrapper has to be rewritten when the main builder picks this up.
  • The chooser's page rule goes with the chooser. Delete .qz-lsc* (quizocalypse.css:5652-5720) and the page override .qz-page.is-funnel:has(.qz-lsc) (:11768) with it. Nothing replaces them: the workspace renders on first entry, at the width above.
  • Minimum height. The mock's stage is min-height 760 and the questions rail is min-height 480, so a one-question quiz still fills the card. Keep both; an empty Rules-only quiz otherwise collapses to a header and a dashed box.

The "Answer ID" column exists only where the Answers sheet does, which is Filter Results + Rules. A Rules-only workbook carries Rules and Recommendations, so its "Qn = answer" cells have no id column to resolve against. That is a contract detail for the Table view section to state, not an open owner decision; flag it there rather than inventing a fourth sheet here.

Menus and popovers

All popovers share one surface: white, radius 8, --pop shadow, padding 10, 13px type; a 12 / 700 title with padding 4 8 8; items 13.5px, padding 7 8, radius 6, --ground on hover and --accent-wash in --accent-ink when on, with a right-aligned 11.5px hint in --ink4; checkboxes 15×15, radius 3, 1px --line2, filled --accent when on; search fields 13px, padding 6 9, 1px --rule-strong, radius 6; scrolling lists cap at 300 tall; footers 12.5px with a 1px --rule2 top rule. A popover opens 6px below its trigger, is capped at the viewport width minus 16, and clamps to an 8px side margin (mock placePop); it must also flip above the trigger, or cap its height and scroll, when it would run off the bottom (defect B27). Use the shared QzPopover and QzMenu primitives, widened where a menu needs more than their default.

Toast, Undo, save pill and the live region

Undo is the reason several rulings touch one small component, so build it once. D7 extends the shared toast; D9 and D11 and D13 and D16 all speak through it.

Colour tokens the mock uses

Map each to its Quartz counterpart rather than copying the hex: ink #201C2E, ink3 #4E4860, ink4 #645E78, ink25 #B4AFC4; rule #E4E1EC, rule2 #EFEDF4, line2 #CFCADC, rule-strong #948EA6; paper #FFFFFF, ground #F5F4F8, cell #FAF9FC; accent #5B45D6, accent-ink #4A36B8, accent-wash #EFECFD, accent-line #D5CDF8; ok #0F6B45 / #E7F3ED / #BFE0CF; warn #8A5300 / #FBF1E0 / #EDD3A4 with dot #C98A1B; crit #A5241C / #FBEDEC / #EFCBC7; result-chip blue #1D4F91 / #EAF2FE / #C9DCFB (new: recommendations in rule sentences are blue so they read differently from answers); scrim ink at 45%. Two things to know before you extend the token set: the Quartz sheet defines --qz-ls-* twice, at quizocalypse.css:173-182 and again at :226-236, with identical values, so collapse them into one block and widen its comment rather than inlining hex; and the mock's neighbours differ from the tokens by a shade, in which case the token value wins.

The builder wraps its views in an editor surface that re-points the accent family at the ink ladder ([data-qz-surface="editor"], quizocalypse.css:250-257), so a violet armed chip goes neutral there. The armed state must stay visibly distinct on that surface. How it reads there is the open half of D14, and D6 hands the builder work to the main-builder project; build the funnel surface now and keep the armed styling in one rule so the builder answer is a single override.

What not to port

  • Dead CSS in the mock. .mhead (a rule-window title bar, removed by D24), .rband-h (a heading row the Rules-only band never renders) and .relse have stylesheet rules and no renderer. Leave all three out.
  • The mock's spreadsheet loader. loadXLSX pulls xlsx 0.18.5 from cdnjs. D16 forbids it; use SheetJS CE 0.20.3 from the official SheetJS CDN tarball as a lazy chunk.
  • The explainer popovers. HOW and HOWR have no trigger in either style; the top section is gone (D23).
  • The "N to review" chip. .fbar .rev and the second check-popover trigger wait for D4.
  • The style chooser. .qz-lsc* (quizocalypse.css:5652-5720) and its page override (:11768) go with LogicStyleChooser (D5).
  • The harness. The .shell bar, the stress checkboxes, "Reset", "Show it empty" and the #pitch line are the artifact's test rig, and the mock's fbar is a stand-in for the live funnel chrome.
  • The 130% study. Gsj46uCP is a scaled copy, not a spec.

Acceptance criteria

  1. At a 1440px viewport the card measures 1224 wide and the three columns measure 262 / 656 / 304. At 1280px the card is 1224 and the page does not reflow. At 1100px the page scrolls sideways and the columns keep their widths.
  2. The funnel page and the logic wrapper are wide enough that .work binds at 1256: measure the wrapper's content box and assert it is at least 1256.
  3. Both styles render their own complete screen. Switching styles from Table lands on Edit; re-picking the current style keeps the view.
  4. Every rule row shows "↑", "↓" and the trash on hover and on keyboard focus, and the sentence does not move by a pixel when they appear. "↑" is disabled on the first row and "↓" on the last. There is no "✎" and no "⧉" on the row; "Duplicate" is in the rule window's top row beside "Delete rule".
  5. In Rules only the rule window offers "Show" alone, and the row keeps the same height as the Filter window's segment row. In Filter Results + Rules all three verbs render.
  6. Flipping a question row to "is not" removes the any/all button and changes neither the row's height nor the 44px column's width.
  7. A rule sentence with two answers on one question reads verb first, answers only, with parentheses around the group and the join in bold; a negated group reads "not (...)"; an answer longer than 30 characters is cut with an ellipsis and carries the full text as a tooltip.
  8. Deleting a rule shows a toast with a working "Undo" in the standalone funnel and in the embedded twin. With a rule window open the toast sits above its footer with 8px of clearance and covers neither the live sentence nor the primary button. The action is reachable by Tab, and the toast is announced.
  9. Undoing after an unrelated edit keeps that edit.
  10. Export on a quiz with no rules produces a file with every header, both id columns and one example row; importing that file back changes nothing. The Table view renders before the spreadsheet library is loaded.
  11. node scripts/check-tokens.mjs passes: no new hex colour and no px box-shadow literal in any new .tsx.
  12. Screenshots prove the interactive states, because a 200 and DOM markers do not: row hover and focus, the armed tray chip, the drag indicator, the save pill, a toast with its action, and each popover at a viewport where it has to flip or scroll.

Screen shell: funnel bar, title switch, description, view controls and overlay rules Draft · not yet fact-checked

This section covers everything above the workspace body that both styles and both views share. That is the funnel bar and the status header at the top of the card (title switch, description, actions, Edit | Table). It also covers how the style is switched, stored, published and resolved, the box sizes, and the overlay and keyboard rules that every popover, menu and window on the screen follows. The bodies under the header are specified in sections filter-edit-view, rules-only-edit-view and table-view-import-export. What the check popover contains is specified in checks-and-continue.

Both styles are equal. Filter Results + Rules and Rules only are two ways a quiz decides, not a screen and a view of it (D1, settled 2026-09-21). The shell is the same shell for both: the same header, the same title switch, the same view control, the same overlay rules. Nothing in this section may render Rules only as a reduced, preview or fallback state of the other.
How this section cites the mock. The reference mock is docs/design/logic-tab/rules-row/index.html, one file carrying both styles. It is still being edited, so it is cited by function, handler or class name (statusHead(), ACT.setstyle, .stitle), never by line number. Deployed code is cited as path:line on origin/main (b4aa278). The mock's shell bar above the stage ('Logic step · Rules only', '10 answers on Q5', '30 recommendations', 'Reset', 'Show it empty'; the .shell block and #pitch) is test harness. Do not build it.

The bar override contract. Stages publish through useFunnelBar. The override object must be memoized on real state and every handler inside it must be referentially stable. Otherwise each publish re-renders the parent, which builds a new object and publishes again, forever (funnelChrome.tsx:11-14, 43-50). Every new field goes into the existing useMemo (Step3Shell.tsx:321-346): isAiPaused, the popover content, its open flag and the Logic look. Keep the callbacks stable with useCallback, state setters or the fetcher-ref pattern (QuestionBuilderStage.tsx:85-101).
Leaving and going back. 'Leave the builder?' promises that everything is saved (Step1Funnel.tsx:184-187). But 'Leave →' is a plain Link (Step1Funnel.tsx:179), and an edit can still be waiting in the 700 ms autosave debounce (useQuizDraft.ts:58-68). Back and the stepper fire goto-stage, which rewrites the whole doc it loaded (funnelIntents.server.ts:1510-1513): the same race to-rec-page has. This now matters more, because the logic style rides on the doc (D1) and is therefore in the debounce with every other edit. Either apply the flush-and-wait and the build_session-only write from section checks-and-continue to all three, or prove with a probe that the pending PUT still lands. The dialog body and the StepNav tooltips contain em dashes (Step1Funnel.tsx:185; StepNav.tsx:38-43). They are shared funnel chrome outside this change, so leave them unless the owner extends the 2026-09-07 rule (LogicQuestionWidget.tsx:57) to existing copy.

Status header

Decided (owner, 2026-09-17/18; D23). The whole top section goes: the h1, 'How this works', CatalogStrip, and the style bar with 'Switch to …' and '✓ Check my logic' (Step3Shell.tsx:434-512). The card opens with one header row instead. It holds a clickable title with ▾ that switches the style, the one-line description with More beside it on the same baseline, the actions, and Edit | Table last.

Build the header once, as a new LogicHeader in app/components/studio/logicTab/. LogicTabCard renders it as the card's first child (mock statusHead(), called from renderFilter() and the Rules-only render), so the funnel (Step3Shell.tsx:520-532) and the builder (BuilderSettings.tsx:67-79) get the same markup from one component. The card root keeps data-testid="logic-tab-card" (LogicTabCard.tsx:511), because probes and deep links query it (UnifiedWorkspace.tsx:612; Step3Shell.tsx:192-199). Contract:

// app/components/studio/logicTab/LogicHeader.tsx (new)
type LogicStyle = "attributes" | "rules";
type LogicView = "edit" | "table";
type LogicHeaderProps = {
  style: LogicStyle;           // always resolved; there is no null / chooser state (D5)
  onStyleChange?: (style: LogicStyle) => void; // absent: static title, no ▾ (read-only card,
                               // and the builder host until the main-builder work wires it, D6)
  view: LogicView;
  onViewChange: (view: LogicView) => void;
  onPasteRules?: () => void;   // shown in Rules only + Edit
  onCreateRule?: () => void;   // shown in Rules only + Edit
  onImport?: () => void;       // shown in Table
  onExport?: () => void;       // shown in Table
  exporting?: boolean;         // keeps Export disabled across re-renders (B37)
};

The component takes the style and the switch as props and reads nothing from a host. That is what keeps it reusable when the main builder is rebuilt (D6): the builder work wires the two callbacks, it does not fork the component.
