Title switch and the Logic style menu

  • The title is a button labelled with the current style and the caret: 'Filter Results + Rules ▾' (logic_style 'attributes') or 'Rules only ▾' ('rules') (mock styleName()). Its tooltip reads 'Change how this quiz decides'. It needs aria-haspopup="menu" and aria-expanded. The mock has the first and not the second (B29).
  • Wrap the button in the page heading. Once the h1 'What should each answer do?' goes (Step3Shell.tsx:434), the title is the only heading left on the funnel step.
  • A click opens the 'Logic style' menu, left-aligned to the title (mock ACT.stylemenu opening styleMenu() at 330px). It has the heading 'Logic style' and two items, each a name plus a hint: 'Filter Results + Rules' with 'answers map, rules add exceptions', and 'Rules only' with 'every outcome is a rule you write'. Both items read as first-class choices; neither is marked recommended, default or advanced. The current item is marked: role="menuitemradio" with aria-checked="true", drawn with the accent wash.
  • At 330px the one-line item wraps both texts, which need about 345px (B29). Either stack the hint under the name, as the role menu's two-line items do, or widen the menu to about 400px. The name never wraps.
  • A second click on the title, a click outside or Esc closes the menu. Esc and a choice both return focus to the title.
  • Keyboard: Enter, Space or ArrowDown on the title opens the menu with focus on the checked item. ArrowUp and ArrowDown move and wrap, and Home and End jump. Enter or Space chooses. Tab closes the menu and moves on.
  • Build it on QzMenu (qz-overlays.tsx:442-490). Today QzMenu renders role="menu" with plain menuitem buttons inside a QzPopover. That popover labels its trigger aria-haspopup="dialog" and its box role="dialog" (qz-overlays.tsx:405-424), and has no arrow keys or focus handling. Extend QzMenu with a checked-item variant, a hint line, arrow keys, focus in and back, and aria-haspopup="menu", so the role and route menus can share the code.

Switching style

Decided (owner, 2026-09-18). Choosing the other style sets it and lands on Edit, even from Table. Choosing the current style keeps the current view. Any choice disarms the tray and closes the menu (mock ACT.setstyle). Switching loses nothing: roles, answer mappings, filter values and rules are untouched on the doc.
  • The header calls onStyleChange(style), which the host supplies. In the funnel that is Step3Shell's pickLogicStyle (Step3Shell.tsx:156-162), rewired to the doc write below. LogicTabCard then sets its view to Edit if the style changed, clears the armed recommendation and closes any open popover. Focus returns to the title button, and its new name announces the change (B30).
  • No confirmation dialog. The switch is lossless on the doc: it writes one field and deletes nothing. 'Lossless by construction' is the property the shipped intent already promises (funnelIntents.server.ts:1461-1467), and the doc field keeps it.
  • The switch does change what shoppers get after the next publish. In 'rules' the engine ignores question roles and answer mappings and the first matching rule's recommendations are the result; in 'attributes' the picking question gives the base, Narrows questions filter it and rules act on top (D1). The mappings stay on the doc either way, so flipping back restores the old behaviour exactly.
  • The CTA and the check popover recount at once from the one style-aware Tier-1 report (D3, section checks-and-continue). Rules only blocks on no rules, on no rule that can show anything, and on a rule missing its answers or its recommendations; it skips the picking-question checks. Filter Results + Rules keeps today's blocks and adds route bypass and broken or impossible rules. The report reads the style the engine will read, never the screen's guess (see First entry).
  • Both styles share one no-match behaviour: a shopper no rule matches gets the Results step's safety net, and the same net covers an empty result in Filter Results + Rules (D1 safety net). The shell shows nothing for this; it is named here so the style switch is not described as changing the empty-result story. The code sites are in section engine-semantics: Rules only resolves through the existing no-base path (recommendDecider.ts:276-283), an unmatched shopper falls out of resolveTarget as null (recommendDecider.ts:278, 286), and the net is global_fallback then deciderFallbackProducts (QuizRuntime.tsx:1583-1595; recommendDecider.ts:522-538).
The safety net is a runtime change, so it carries the runtime proof rules. app/components/runtime/** is the highest-risk edit class in this repo. Legacy (non-decider) docs must stay byte-identical, the full e2e suite runs, the screenshot review runs on /q, and the byte pin must hold after deploy (sha256 of /q/cmqqcb0ao004mqvkwjug7t0ya.json starts c02ccaec98a0fe9e). Nothing in this shell section ships a runtime change; do not let the shell work and the runtime work land in one commit.

Where the style is stored

The style lives on the quiz document and survives publish (D1). Today it lives in the funnel's draft-only scratch: pickLogicStyle sets a local override and posts set-logic-style on the shared stage fetcher (Step3Shell.tsx:140-162; QuestionBuilderStage.tsx:94-101), the server writes build_session.logic_style (funnelIntents.server.ts:1468-1481), and publish strips the whole build_session (quizPublish.ts:789-810), so nothing about the style reaches a shopper. That is exactly what D1 changes.

TopicBuild
Field NewQuiz.logic_style: z.enum(["rules","attributes"]).optional(), top level, beside the other Logic v2 fields. Decider-gated and never .default(): a default would rewrite every legacy doc on the next parse-save round trip. Absent means today's engine, so every doc published before this change keeps its behaviour byte for byte. Follow the pattern of the existing optional session field (quizSchema.ts:1698-1708).
Writecommit() through useQuizDraft, on whichever surface hosts the card. The funnel PUT stores the doc content and keeps the server's build_session (funnelIntents.server.ts:114-134); the builder PUT stores the whole doc (quizEditorIO.server.ts:342-359). One write path, no intent.
Read order (screen only)resolveLogicStyle(doc): doc.logic_style, then build_session.logic_style (migration only), then inference, then Filter Results + Rules (D5). One pure helper, exported and unit-tested, and it decides which screen opens and nothing else. The Tier-1 report, the 'Fix N' count and the publish gate read engineLogicStyle(doc) instead. Today the order is private to Step3Shell (Step3Shell.tsx:142-155).
PublishquizPublish.ts keeps logic_style on publishedJson when it is present, and writes nothing when it is absent. It is not draft-only state, so it must not join the strip list at quizPublish.ts:804-807. Pin this with a test that publishes a doc with the field, a doc without it, and a legacy doc, and asserts the field's presence and absence byte for byte.
Migration from build_sessionA quiz whose style was picked in the funnel before this change carries it only in build_session.logic_style. The resolver reads it, so the screen opens correctly. The doc field is written the first time the merchant chooses in the title menu; from then on the doc field wins and the session copy is ignored. Nothing migrates on load (D5), so no merchant's published quiz changes behaviour without a click. Read the caveat in First entry: until the doc field exists, the engine runs the Filter path.
The set-logic-style intent ExistsThe new UI never calls it. Its only caller is submitLogicStyle in QuestionBuilderStage (QuestionBuilderStage.tsx:94-101), reached only from the deleted chooser and the deleted style bar. Delete the caller with them. Leave the server branch in place for one release so an in-flight client cannot 400, then remove it with its schema comment (funnelIntents.server.ts:1461-1481; quizSchema.ts:1698-1707). Keep the BuildSession.logic_style field parsed forever: legacy schema fields stay parsed in this repo.
When the write failsThe local doc is the source of truth, so nothing reverts and no style-specific error copy is needed. A failed save shows 'Not saved · Retry' in the bar (funnelChrome.tsx:96-109), which is the same failure every other edit has.
Why the doc field also fixes Back, then Continue. QuestionBuilderStage stays mounted across Questions and Logic (Step1Funnel.tsx:298-316; QuestionBuilderStage.tsx:180-234). Its useQuizDraft never re-reads initialDoc (useQuizDraft.ts:28), so the client doc keeps the build_session it first loaded, while Step3Shell remounts on every entry and drops its local pick (Step3Shell.tsx:140-155). Today that loses the style on re-entry. With the style in the doc it survives by construction: the client doc is the one the autosave owns. Do not add a second in-session override; the local localStyle state goes with the intent.
Whole-doc writes still race. set-logic-style and the navigation intents rewrite the whole doc they read at the start of the request (funnelIntents.server.ts:1476-1479, 1510-1513), so they can undo an autosave PUT that lands between their read and their write. With the style in the doc, a style switch is now one of the edits that can be lost this way. Make goto-stage and to-rec-page patch only build_session on a freshly read draft, the fix section checks-and-continue asks for, and flush the autosave before navigating.

First entry

Decided (owner, 2026-09-22; D5, option A). There is no first-entry chooser. The step opens straight into the workspace with the title switch. Delete LogicStyleChooser and the inert 'Point based' row with it.
  • The style resolves in this order, in one pure helper:
    1. doc.logic_style.
    2. build_session.logic_style (quizzes that picked a style before this change).
    3. Inference: any question with the filter role means Filter Results + Rules; otherwise any rule means Rules only (Step3Shell.tsx:151-154).
    4. Filter Results + Rules.
    Keep that order exactly. Do not add a mapped-picking-answer test before the rules test: D5 fixes the order.
  • Nothing is written on page load. Resolving the style never fires an intent and never marks the doc dirty. The style is written when the merchant chooses in the title menu.
  • Because the resolver can no longer return null, the header's style prop is not nullable and the card has no chooser branch. Delete Step3Shell's logicStyle === null branch (Step3Shell.tsx:422-428).
  • Deletions: app/components/onboarding/questionsLogicV3/logic/LogicStyleChooser.tsx (233 lines; its only importer is Step3Shell.tsx:32-35), LogicStyleChooser.test.ts, the chooserScan memo (Step3Shell.tsx:170-173) unless CatalogStrip's replacement still needs buildChooserScan, and the chooser's CSS including the 1000px page cap (quizocalypse.css:11766-11768). recommendEngine goes with the chooser: the resolver never guesses from the catalogue.
  • The page always opens on Edit.
Inference does not change the engine, and the checks must say so. Inference only chooses which screen opens. The engine reads the published field, and an absent field means today's Filter Results + Rules engine. So a decider quiz with rules, no Narrows question and no saved style opens on Rules only (that is already what ships today, Step3Shell.tsx:151-154) while its shoppers still get the picking question's mapping. Two requirements follow. First, the Tier-1 report, the 'Fix N' count and the publish gate all read engineLogicStyle(doc) = doc.logic_style ?? "attributes", the style the engine will run, so the report can never read safer than the gate (D3). Second, choosing the style already shown in the title menu writes it when nothing is saved, so one click makes an inferred style real; today's mock ignores a same-style choice (ACT.setstyle returns early when S.style is unchanged) and must not. State the difference in the check popover's copy when it blocks, not in a banner.

The toast contract (D7, option A)

  • Extend QzToastProvider so show() takes an optional action ({ label, onAction }) and an optional duration. Keep the queue of one. The toast stays role="status" with aria-live="polite", and the action is a real focusable <button>, so pointer-events: none can no longer sit on the whole pill (quizocalypse.css:4406-4415): move it to the text, or drop it and let the action take the press.
  • Reach the action from the keyboard. An Undo the merchant cannot reach is not an Undo. Give the action a focus stop while the toast is up, and a shortcut is not a substitute for it.
  • Record the exception. The design-system rule in qz-toast.tsx:13-17 says a toast is never clickable and carries no actions. The owner granted a dated exception on 2026-09-22 (D7). Write that into the file's comment with the date and the decision id, so the next reader does not "fix" it back.
  • Undo is inverse mutations, never a snapshot. Undo applies the inverse of what was done to the latest document (restore a rule at its index by its id; restore a role and its targets), so an unrelated edit made while the toast is up survives. Several deletes in a row accumulate into one Undo. Do not port the mock's snap() / UNDO, which stores JSON.stringify(S.rules) and replays it wholesale; that is the root cause of mock defect B1.
  • The announced clear (D9): moving 'Picks results' to another question still clears both questions' answer mappings, and a toast names what was cleared, for example 'Q1's 6 recommendations were removed', with an Undo that restores the role and every target. One code path serves the role menu, the Table and Import. No confirm dialog. The shell's part is only that the toast can carry that action at all.
  • The providers. QzToastProvider is mounted on the studio routes (studio.tsx:31-39; studio_.$id.tsx:117-121; studio_.onboarding_.$quizId.tsx:38-40) and on neither embedded twin, so useQzToast resolves to the context's no-op default (qz-toast.tsx:31) and every toast is silent there. Add the provider to app/routes/app.onboarding_.$quizId.tsx:39-46 and app/routes/app.quizzes.$id_.studio.tsx:45-53. That is the whole of the embedded work in this build (D21): the hardcoded /studio links and giving embedded decider quizzes the new Logic view are separate tasks.
Reach. Ten files import QzPopover, including HealthPill, FlowRail, DesignAiButton, BuilderFlowTab, the logicTab pickers and menus, and studio.quizzes. Two files import QzMenu and 14 import QzModal; useQzToast has more callers still. Changes to these primitives change the whole admin, so run the screenshot pass on those consumers too. Also extend qz-overlays.test.tsx, which today pins QzModal's Esc and × behaviour (qz-overlays.test.tsx:30-66), and pin the toast's new action and duration against nextToastState (qz-toast.tsx:23-29). The z-index ladder stays as it is: popovers sit just above modals at calc(var(--qz-z-modal) + 10), and toasts sit on top at --qz-z-toast (quizocalypse.css:223-224, 4394, 4408).

Accessibility checklist for the shell

  • Tab order follows the visual order: title, More / Less, the actions, Edit, Table. The reviewed mock's page order tested as logical; keep it.
  • The title is a button inside the heading, with aria-haspopup="menu" and aria-expanded. Its accessible name is the style name, so returning focus to it after a switch announces the new style (B29, B30).
  • The style menu is a role="menu" labelled 'Logic style', with role="menuitemradio" items that carry aria-checked. Focus starts on the checked item. Arrow keys wrap, and Home and End jump. Enter and Space choose. Esc and Tab close it. Focus returns to the title (B29).
  • Edit | Table is a role="group" labelled 'View', with aria-pressed on each button. Focus stays on the chosen button. When a style switch forces Edit, focus goes to the title (B30).
  • More / Less has aria-expanded and aria-controls. Its label changes and focus stays on it.
  • The blocked CTA keeps aria-haspopup="dialog" (Step1Funnel.tsx:125) and gains aria-expanded. Focus moves into the check popover when it opens and back to the CTA on Esc.
  • A toast with an action is reachable by keyboard while it is up, and its message is announced by the live region without stealing focus (D7).
  • Every control that a row reveals on hover is also revealed on keyboard focus, including the rule rows' ↑/↓ and trash (D11).
  • No action in the shell leaves focus on <body>.

Filter Results + Rules · Edit: rail, question pane and rules column Draft · not yet fact-checked

This is the Edit view of Filter Results + Rules, one of the step's two logic styles. The other, Rules only, is a different way of deciding results with its own screen (section rules-only-edit-view) and its own engine branch, not a view of this one. Both are in scope equally; neither is a fallback for the other. In this style one question picks the result, other questions narrow it by product values, and rules run on top as exceptions.

How the screen knows which style it is in (D5). The style is resolved, never asked for. One shared helper (resolveLogicStyle, section data-model-and-mutations) reads, in order: the saved doc.logic_style; then build_session.logic_style, for drafts that picked a style before the doc field existed (quizSchema.ts:1708, written only by the set-logic-style intent, funnelIntents.server.ts:1468-1481); then inference, where a question with role filter means Filter Results + Rules and a rule with no filter role means Rules only (the live inference, Step3Shell.tsx:151-154); then the default, Filter Results + Rules. Nothing is written to the quiz on load. The style is written only when the merchant switches it, through the title switch in the header (section header-and-shell). There is no first-entry chooser: LogicStyleChooser and its inert 'Point based' row are deleted, and Step3Shell's logicStyle === null branch (Step3Shell.tsx:422-437) goes with them.

Where it renders. LogicTabCard renders this screen whenever the resolved style is not 'rules' (LogicTabCard.tsx:104-112). It mounts in funnel step 3 (Step3Shell.tsx:520-532, which passes the resolved style and ruleFlow="onboarding") and in the main builder's Logic view, which mounts the same card with neither prop (BuilderSettings.tsx:67-79). Under the status header (section header-and-shell) the card is one grid of three columns: the question rail (262px), the question pane (minmax(0,1fr)) and the rules column (304px) on the right (mock .grid3 and renderFilter; sizes per D20, rules column on the right per D22).

How to read the tables. Build is the spec: it is what ships, in the indicative. Writes names the pure mutation and the stored field it changes. Live today is what origin/main does now, so it says what to keep, change or delete in LogicTabCard, LogicQuestionWidget, LogicTabMenus and ValuePickerPopover. Code refs are path:line on origin/main (b4aa278). Mock references name the function, handler or class (railItems, pane, ruleRows, sentence(), the ACT handlers) and never a line number, because the mock is still being edited.

Settled for this screen. Build it as written, not as a choice.

  • D1 the logic style is a real engine mode saved on the quiz through publish, so this screen's style is a stored fact, not a local view state. Filter Results + Rules keeps today's engine exactly: the picking question gives the base, filter questions narrow it, the first matching rule acts on top.
  • D1 safety net a shopper who ends this quiz with nothing to show gets the Results step's safety net. That is a shopper-facing runtime change and carries the full runtime proof (see "What a shopper sees when this screen produces nothing").
  • D3 one style-aware Tier-1 report drives the CTA, the check popover and publish. In this style it keeps today's blocks and adds the route bypass and broken or impossible rules, with warnings for a recommendation nothing can show, a rule that never runs and an impossible all-of.
  • D5 no chooser, resolution order as above, nothing written on load.
  • D7 the shared toast takes one optional action, a duration and keyboard reach; Undo is inverse mutations against the latest document, never a whole-document snapshot.
  • D8 the save pill shows at the edited field only; the ambient autosave chrome stays silent when healthy.
  • D9 moving 'Picks results' still clears both questions' mappings, and a toast names what was cleared with an Undo that restores the role and every target.
  • D11 rule rows: click the row to edit, a trash icon, and ↑/↓ revealed on hover and on keyboard focus. Duplicate moves into the rule window's top row.
  • D12 'is not' and 'all of' never combine: on an 'is not' row the any/all toggle is hidden and the row means none of these answers.
  • D13 Paste rules splits a cross-question 'or' into adjacent rules; rules already carrying match: "any" still render faithfully with 'or' between questions.
  • D14 colours green = the recommendation is not placed on any answer, black = placed, violet = armed.
  • D15 new recommendations are written through ensure-targets with a group kind, always quiz-scoped, so they appear in this screen's tray and pickers at once.
  • D17 rule sentences are verb-first and answers-only, with parentheses around multi-answer groups, bold joins, 'not (...)' and full-text tooltips.
  • D18 the renames land everywhere through shared constants; internal words never reach the merchant.
  • D19 the live surfaces the mock does not draw stay: the attribute picker on the Narrows flip, every rule-flag reason in the mock's tag style, product-count popovers, the picker's kind filters and drill-in. The "won't work as written" banner is dropped; 'Explore every path' stays builder-only.
  • D20 / D22 / D23 / D24 mock sizes at 100%, rules column on the right, no top section, rule window layout as specified.
  • D21 the embedded twins get the missing toast provider, so Undo is never invisible there.

Parked, and what to do meanwhile.

D4, diagnostics. The check popover shows the findings and opens from the CTA (section checks-and-continue). Do not rebuild 'Check my logic', the Diagnose modal, Test a path or the AI review into this step, and do not add an 'N to review' affordance. D6, builder parity. The main builder is being rebuilt, so this work ships the funnel step 3 surface only. Three consequences for this screen. (1) The style lives on the quiz document (D1), so it survives graduation and the new builder can read it. (2) Do not gate the new UI behind ruleFlow === "onboarding" in a way that makes it unreachable from the builder later; keep the card's props the seam. (3) Known gap while parked: the builder mounts LogicTabCard with no logicStyle (BuilderSettings.tsx:67-79), so rulesOnly is false and a Rules-only quiz opens in today's builder as Filter Results + Rules, where the builder's Logic view still writes rules against the old chrome. Name that gap in the handoff to the main-builder project; do not paper over it here.

Rules every column follows

  • The style is read, never stored locally. The card takes the resolved style as a prop and treats it as data. It never writes it, never infers it a second time, and never caches it in component state; switching styles is the header's job. A card that gets no style behaves as Filter Results + Rules, which is what the builder mount relies on today (LogicTabCard.tsx:104-112).
  • Selection is settable from outside. Today the selected question is internal state in LogicTabCard (LogicTabCard.tsx:133) passed down as selectedId / onSelect (LogicTabCard.tsx:501-502). Step3Shell's health links and the builder's 'Open in Logic →' only scroll to a data-node-id (Step3Shell.tsx:192-199, 289-307; UnifiedWorkspace.tsx:598-624), so they never select anything; the check popover's rows (section checks-and-continue) need the same. Add a controlled pair (for example selectedQuestionId + onSelectQuestion, uncontrolled by default) and have every jump set it. An unknown id falls back to the first question (LogicQuestionWidget.tsx:149).
  • Test hooks stay. Keep data-testid="logic-tab-card" on the wrapper and data-node-id on every rail row and on the pane (LogicTabCard.tsx:511; LogicQuestionWidget.tsx:213, 355). Give each rule row a stable data-rule-id so rule jumps land on the row.
  • Toasts and Undo (D7). Every action on this screen that removes or clears something the merchant authored toasts, and that toast carries one action. The shared toast is extended once, in app/components/qz-toast.tsx: an optional { label, onAction }, an optional duration (the DS default of 2400 ms is too short to reach an Undo, qz-toast.tsx:19), a live region the action lives inside (the portal already renders role="status" aria-live="polite", qz-toast.tsx:68) and keyboard reach, so the action is focusable and Esc dismisses. Record the dated owner exception beside the rule it bends, the DS-V2 §7.5 comment at qz-toast.tsx:13-17 ("Not clickable, no actions"), naming the date and D7. Undo is always inverse mutations against the latest document (docRef.current, the seam LogicTabCard already keeps at LogicTabCard.tsx:128-129), never a snapshot of the whole doc: a snapshot would silently revert edits the merchant made while the toast was up. The mock does exactly what the build must not do, replacing the whole rules array from a deep copy (mock snap() and ACT.undo); copy its wording and its run-joining, not its mechanism. Several deletes inside one toast window accumulate into one Undo.
  • Popovers. Every popover on this screen is a QzPopover (qz-overlays.tsx:294-440): one open at a time, closed by an outside click, Esc or a second click on its trigger, flipped or height-clamped near the viewport edge (qz-overlays.tsx:332-403). What it lacks: it positions only when it opens, aligns only to the trigger's left edge (qz-overlays.tsx:352), stamps aria-haspopup="dialog" on every trigger (qz-overlays.tsx:411-417), and never moves focus in or back. Phase 3 adds re-anchoring on resize, scroll and content change (B28), a right-align option (role menu, route menu, '+N more' list), menu roles with arrow keys and focus in and back (B29). Popover titles wrap long unbroken words (B60).
  • Read-only. When LogicTabCard gets no commit (previews, tests) every control here is inert, as the widget already does (LogicQuestionWidget.tsx:360-375, 1078-1095, 1215-1226). That includes the type line and the inline text.
  • Text. Question, answer and recommendation text is rendered as React text everywhere, including title attributes and popover titles (B21). No em dashes in any new copy, per the rule the widget already carries (LogicQuestionWidget.tsx:57).
  • Words (D18). The renames land in shared constants, not per surface: ROLE_JOBS / ROLE_FOOT (logicTabFields.ts:593-601) carry 'Picks the result', 'Narrows' and 'Info only' (was 'Asked only', logicTabFields.ts:596), and the private copy this screen holds (COPY, LogicQuestionWidget.tsx:58-67, and REC_SOURCES, LogicQuestionWidget.tsx:70-77) moves into the same module so the pane, the Table, the rule window, the Rules inspector and the pinned tests read one source. The tray label becomes 'Recommendations' (was 'Recommendations from step 1', LogicQuestionWidget.tsx:59 and the group aria-label at :775); the picker's 'Tag buckets' kind becomes 'Tags' (LogicQuestionWidget.tsx:70-75); '+ Add rule' becomes 'Create a rule' in the window and '+ Add' on the column header (LogicTabCard.tsx:273); the empty Picks cell and its picker both read 'Choose a result' (already the live constant, LogicQuestionWidget.tsx:60, and already the mock's copy in pane). Internal words never reach the merchant: decider, bucket, branch, boost, weight, score. Two other surfaces carry the same strings and change with them: the builder's Rules inspector (ContextPanel.tsx:932) and the older funnel question section (QuestionSection.tsx:427); the pinned test that asserts 'Asked only' (ContextPanel.rules.test.tsx:99, 108) is updated in the same commit. The legacy branch-node editor's own '+ Add rule' (app.quizzes.$id.tsx:3337) writes conditional_rules and is a different feature; leave it alone.
  • Colour tokens. Violet = --qz-accent, --qz-accent-wash, --qz-accent-ink, --qz-accent-line; green = --qz-ok text on a --qz-ls-ok-line border; black = --qz-ink (quizocalypse.css:84-89, 97, 177). In the builder, [data-qz-surface="editor"] re-points the whole accent family to ink (quizocalypse.css:249-276, set at UnifiedWorkspace.tsx:1804), so armed and selected states turn ink there; how that should read is the open half of D14.
  • Disarming. The armed recommendation clears on selecting another question (live, LogicQuestionWidget.tsx:174-176) and, new, on Esc when no popover or window is open, on any role change and on any style change (mock ACT.sel, ACT.setrole, ACT.setstyle and the Esc handler).

What a shopper sees when this screen produces nothing (D1 safety net)

This screen can produce a shopper who reaches the results with nothing: an answer that maps to no recommendation, a route that skips the picking question, stacked Narrows answers whose intersection is empty, or a Hide rule that empties the pool. Settled: that shopper gets the Results step's safety net, and the same net covers an empty result in Rules only. One behaviour for both styles.

Two different code paths reach that state today, and only one of them already lands on the net.

  • A target resolves but the pool is empty (narrowing intersects to nothing, a Hide rule removes everything, the target's products are all unsellable). The engine still returns its decider block, so the runtime's fallback chain runs: global_fallback first when it resolves products, then emptyFallbackCol, then safetyNetCol (QuizRuntime.tsx:1579-1595; deciderFallbackProducts, recommendDecider.ts:522-538). An explicit emptyFallback: "hide" still means show nothing, and the net does not override it (recommendDecider.ts:514-517). Nothing to change here.
  • Nothing resolves at all (no rule matched and no base mapping applied). resolveTarget returns null and the engine returns early with no decider key at all (recommendationEngine.ts:392-397), so explained.decider is falsy and the runtime never reaches the fallback chain. The comment on the fallback function says this case "is prevented at build time by V1/V2 and is deliberately not handled here" (recommendDecider.ts:520-521). That is the change D1 asks for: the null resolution must reach the same fallback layer, so the miss lands on the net instead of an empty page.

This is a change in the shopper-facing runtime, so it carries the full proof the repo demands (CLAUDE.md): legacy docs byte-identical (the change sits inside the logic_model === "decider" branch, so no legacy quiz reaches it), the full e2e suite, screenshot review of the /q result page in both the net and the no-net cases, and the byte pin after deploy. Add unit coverage in recommendDecider.test.ts for the null resolution in both styles, and keep the decision in one place: the fallback layer, not two call sites.

On this screen the merchant sees the cause, not the net: the answer-level 'X of Y' count on Narrows cells (LogicQuestionWidget.tsx:1159-1174), the 'never runs' and 'fires for everyone' tags on rules, and the check popover's findings. The net's own configuration lives on the Results step; this step never writes global_fallback.

Keyboard on this screen

  • Tab order: rail rows and '+ Add question' → title → type line → role button → tray chips and '+N more' → per answer row: answer text, cell (and its chip buttons), route button → rules column: '+ Add', each rule row, its ↑, ↓ and trash → 'Paste rules'.
  • Enter or Space activates rail rows, cells, rule rows and every button. Opening any popover moves focus into it; closing returns focus to its trigger (B29).
  • Rule rows reorder from the keyboard: the ↑/↓ buttons appear on focus, not only on hover, and focus stays on the moved row's button (D11, B19).
  • Esc closes the innermost thing first (popover, then window, then the armed chip); inside an inline edit it only reverts the text. A toast that carries an Undo is reachable by Tab while it is up and dismissed by Esc (D7).
  • After any action focus stays on the control used, or on its re-rendered twin; it never falls to <body> (B30).

Done means

Acceptance for this screen, beyond the per-row behaviour above. The full probe list is in section tests-and-probes; these are the ones this screen owns.

  1. Style. A decider quiz with logic_style: "attributes" opens on this screen; one with no field and a filter role opens here too; one with no field, no filter role and at least one rule opens on Rules only; one with none of it opens here. Loading any of them writes nothing: the saved document is byte-identical after a load and a reload. A legacy (non-decider) document never gains the key.
  2. Publish. The style survives publish: publishedJson.logic_style equals the draft's, and the byte-pinned legacy quiz's /q/:id.json sha256 still starts c02ccaec98a0fe9e.
  3. Undo. Delete a rule, edit a different question's title while the toast is up, then press Undo: the rule comes back at its old index and the title edit survives. Two deletes inside one toast window undo together. Undo is reachable by Tab and announced.
  4. Announced clearing. Moving 'Picks results' from a mapped question toasts the count of removed recommendations, and Undo restores both questions' roles, every target and the required flag. The same helper runs when the Table view or an Import moves the role.
  5. Row controls. With no mouse: Tab to a rule row, reveal ↑/↓, reorder, and land back on the same button. Duplicate is not on the row and is in the rule window.
  6. Sentences. A rule with two answers on one question reads with parentheses; an 'is not' row reads 'not (A or B)' and offers no any/all toggle; a stored match: "any" rule reads 'or' between its questions and still does after an edit; a truncated chip shows its full text on hover and on focus.
  7. Flags. All five reasons render in the tag style at full contrast, in this column and in the Table, and they agree with the check popover: nothing is flagged here that the report calls clean, and nothing the report blocks on is unflagged here.
  8. Safety net. A published quiz in this style where the shopper's path resolves nothing renders the net, not an empty page; a quiz whose merchant chose 'hide' still renders nothing. Both covered by unit tests and by the e2e run, with screenshots.
  9. Embedded. The same delete in the embedded twin shows the toast and its Undo (D21).
  10. Interactive states are proved by screenshot, not by DOM markers: armed tray, drop look, each open picker, the type popover left open during a stepper change, and the save pill beside the role button.
Pieces this screen needs beyond the data-model list. (1) setLogicStyle and resolveLogicStyle, so the card reads one resolved style (D1, D5). (2) The announced decider move: one helper that runs moveDecider, counts what it cleared, toasts it and returns an inverse that restores both questions' roles, their target_id / target_ids and the required flag the promote sets (deciderMutations.ts:194-236); the role menu, the Table and Import all call it (D9). (3) restoreDecisionRule(doc, rule, index), and an inverse for a reorder (D7, D11). (4) An inverse for setScalePoints removals that re-inserts the removed answers (same ids, handles, targets and values) and their handle edges at their old positions (B7), landing with D10. (5) The toast action API in app/components/qz-toast.tsx, plus the provider in the two embedded routes that lack it: app.onboarding_.$quizId.tsx:41-46 and app.quizzes.$id_.studio.tsx:51-55 (the studio twins already wrap it, studio_.onboarding_.$quizId.tsx:38-40, studio_.$id.tsx:117-121) (D7, D21). (6) The controlled selection prop on LogicTabCard. (7) A data-rule-id hook on rule rows. (8) Grouping and 'not (...)' in describeRuleConditions (ruleSummary.ts:11-29), so one describer serves the row, the Table, the export and the AI copy (D17). Each new mutation is pure, starts with if (doc.logic_model !== "decider") return doc, imports concrete mutation modules rather than the quizMutations barrel, and is unit-tested.
Shared-surface risk. LogicTabCard, LogicQuestionWidget, LogicTabMenus and ValuePickerPopover also make up the builder's Logic view (BuilderSettings.tsx:67-79), and TypeChipSelector and AddQuestionDialog also serve the Questions step, so every change here lands on those surfaces. D6 parks builder parity but does not isolate the code: decide per change whether the builder gets it now or is left as it is, and record it, rather than discovering it in a screenshot. The D18 renames deliberately do land everywhere, including the builder's Rules inspector (ContextPanel.tsx:932) and the tests that pin the old words (ContextPanel.rules.test.tsx:99, 108). The probes that pin today's widget (logic-widget-verify.mjs: tray thumbnails, grey and slide-last, 'Recommendations from step 1') change in the same work (section tests-and-probes). Prove the interactive states with screenshots, not DOM markers.

Rules only · Edit: the rules row and the Your recommendations strip

This is the screen a merchant sees when the quiz's logic style is Rules only and the view is Edit. Rules only is one of the two ways this product decides a result, and it is a complete method in its own right (D1): the merchant writes rules, the first rule that matches a shopper wins, and that rule's recommendations are the result. It is not a view of Filter Results + Rules and it is not a simplified mode. The two styles share this handoff's vocabulary, its components and its checks; they differ in which engine path runs and in what the screen puts in front of the merchant.

Under the shared status header the screen has two bands: the rules, as one full-width numbered list, and a tinted "Your recommendations" strip that shows which recommendations a rule can actually show. It renders inside the shared LogicTabCard when the host passes logicStyle="rules". Today only the funnel passes a style (Step3Shell.tsx:520-532); the builder renders LogicTabCard without the prop (BuilderSettings.tsx:69-75), which is the parked D6 gap named in section 10. In the mock this screen is rulesBand() and vizRecs(), the strip popover stripMoreHTML(), the one-row fit fitRow(), the delete path delRule() and snap(), and the flag text deadWhy() / deadTag().

Every code reference below is path:line on origin/main (b4aa278) and was read there; the working tree is stale and was not used. The mock is cited by function name only, because it is still being edited.

What is settled for this screen. Rules only is a real engine mode and the style lives on the quiz document through publish (D1). Shoppers no rule matches get the Results step's safety net, and the same net covers an empty result in Filter Results + Rules (D1 safety net). One style-aware Tier-1 report drives the CTA, the check popover and publish (D3). There is no first-entry chooser (D5). The shared toast gains one optional action and Undo is built from inverse mutations (D7). Moving "Picks results" announces what it cleared and offers Undo (D9). Rule rows carry click-to-edit, trash and ↑/↓ on hover and keyboard focus, and Duplicate moves into the rule window (D11). "is not" and "all of" cannot combine (D12). Paste rules splits a cross-question "or" into adjacent rules (D13). "+ Add recommendations" writes through ensure-targets with a "group" kind (D15). The spreadsheet carries identity and Export doubles as the template (D16). Sentences are verb-first and answers-only (D17). Names come from shared constants (D18). The live surfaces the mock does not draw are kept (D19). The embedded twins get the missing toast provider (D21). The step's top section is gone (D23). Build all of it.
Still open, and what each one blocks. Three questions are not ruled on. Do not pick them; build around them and mark the seam.
  • D2, the Filter Results + Rules half. Settled for Rules only: Show is the whole result, the hint "these become the results" is true, and the rule window offers Show alone there. Open for Filter Results + Rules: Show appends after the base pool and the results cap often cuts it off, while the same hint promises it becomes the result. The owner chooses an engine change or new hint wording. Blocks: the final Show hint text in the Filter style's rule window, and whether the coverage helper's Filter branch may count a Show rule as coverage at all (section 3.1). It blocks nothing in Rules only.
  • D10. What a question-type change does to answers and to the rules that referenced them. Blocks: the wording and the Undo of the flags a type change leaves on rows (section 2.2). Build the flags; the type-change path itself waits.
  • D14, second half. Whether recommendations that are already used move to the end of the tray, and how the armed state reads on the builder's editor surface, which re-points the accent colour. Blocks: nothing on this screen's pill order, which is settled (uncovered first, then covered), but it blocks the lit-row colour on the builder surface (section 3.3).

2.2 Flags on rows

One tag per row: blocking reasons first, then reasons the rule cannot fire, then the rest. D19 keeps every live reason, rendered in the mock's tag style; the "won't work as written" banner is dropped. Compute the flags with the same analyzer functions the Tier-1 report uses, once per document change, the way ruleFlags is memoized today (LogicTabCard.tsx:206-225). The extended shadow check is not cheap (B12 measured about 131 ms at 40 rules that each name up to 10 answers), so it must never run per row or per render. Fixed in mock The mock now memoizes on a fingerprint of the rules and the questions (deadWhy() over dwFp() and the DW cache); copy that shape.

2.3 Delete and Undo

  • Trash (click, Enter or Space) commits removeDecisionRule(doc, rule.id) at once (deciderMutations.ts:256-261). No confirm. Toast: "Rule N deleted · Undo", where N is the row's number before the delete (mock delRule()).
  • The shared toast gains one optional action (D7). QzToastProvider ships as message-only, auto-dismisses after 2,400 ms and keeps a queue of one (app/components/qz-toast.tsx:13-19, 23-29, 58). Extend it with: an optional action: {label, onAction}, an optional duration (this screen passes 6,000 ms, the mock's toastU() hold), and a hold so the timer does not expire while the toast is hovered or holds focus (B32). The provider already renders role="status" aria-live="polite" (qz-toast.tsx:68), which the mock's bare <div id="toast" hidden> does not; keep it and make the action a real <button> inside the live region so it is reachable by keyboard from the row that was just deleted.
  • Record the exception. The design-system comment at qz-toast.tsx:13-17 says a toast is "Not clickable, no actions: if an action is needed, it isn't a toast." Replace that comment with the dated owner exception (D7, 2026-09-22): one optional action is allowed, and only one. Update the design-system reference in the same change so the next reader does not "fix" it back.
  • Undo is an inverse mutation against the latest document, never a snapshot (D7). Add a pure restoreDecisionRule(doc, rule, index) beside its neighbours in app/lib/mutations/deciderMutations.ts: it re-inserts the same rule object, with the same id, at its old index, clamped to the array length, and returns its input unchanged when that id already exists. It opens with the same doc.logic_model !== "decider" guard as removeDecisionRule (deciderMutations.ts:257) and moveDecisionRule (:265), and gets unit tests including the legacy no-op and the duplicate-id no-op. No restore mutation exists today; removeDecisionRule only filters. A whole-document snapshot would roll back edits made while the toast was up, including rules saved from the rule window, which is exactly what D7 rejects.
  • Deletes inside one toast's lifetime join one entry: "2 rules deleted · Undo" brings all of them back in their original order (B35). Fixed in mock snap() and delRule() accumulate, and a run that mixes deletes with moves labels the button "Undo both" or "Undo all N" (toastU()). A later plain toast replaces the Undo toast, as the mock allows; that is the queue-of-one behaviour the provider already has, and it is accepted.
  • A restored rule whose answers or recommendations were removed in the meantime comes back with its missing parts flagged ("answer deleted", "recommendation deleted"), never trimmed and never crashing (B1; DECISIONS.md:42-45). Rules reference answer ids and Category ids, so this follows once every lookup tolerates a miss. Fixed in mock the mock fixes B1 by trimming (fitRule()); do not copy that part.
  • Deleting the last rule shows the empty state (2.5).
  • Focus after a delete: the row that took its place, else the new last row, else "Create your first rule"; never <body> (B30).
  • Undo must never corrupt an open rule window (B2). With restore by id this holds by construction: the window stays bound to its own rule id (LogicTabCard.tsx:545-547). Toasts sit above the rule window (--qz-z-toast 200 against --qz-z-modal 120, quizocalypse.css:223-224; the window uses .qz-modal-scrim, CreateRuleModal.tsx:979, quizocalypse.css:4286-4288), so the Undo stays clickable while the window is open. The mock's placeToast() also lifts it above an open window's footer (B34); the rule window section owns that placement and the case where the edited rule disappears.
  • Every host needs a provider (D21). QzToastProvider wraps studio.tsx:31, studio_.$id.tsx:117 and studio_.onboarding_.$quizId.tsx:38. The embedded funnel route has none (app/routes/app.onboarding_.$quizId.tsx:39-46 renders <TitleBar> and <Step1Funnel> with nothing around them), so today an embedded delete is unrecoverable and silent. Add the provider there. Nothing else in the embedded twins changes in this work (section 10).
  • In the builder the Undo commit goes through the same commit, so the 50-snapshot ⌘Z history stays coherent (UnifiedWorkspace.tsx:162, 196, 216-227).

2.4 Reorder

Order is priority. The engine evaluates rules top to bottom and stops at the first rule that has at least one condition and matches, whatever its action (recommendDecider.ts:226-239). Both reorder paths write moveDecisionRule(doc, ruleId, toIndex), which removes the rule and re-inserts it at toIndex, clamped to the last index (deciderMutations.ts:264-273). toIndex is therefore the rule's final index.

  • Drag. The whole row is the drag source; the dragged row drops to 40% opacity. A 2px accent line shows where the rule will land, and the line and the drop index come from one calculation (B18). Moving down, the rule lands below the hovered row, so the line sits on that row's bottom edge; moving up, on its top edge. A top-half/bottom-half rule is fine as long as one function yields both. The line clears when the pointer leaves the list; a drop on the row itself or outside the list does nothing.
  • Conflict Live has the same mismatch as the mock: .qz-lw-rcard.is-drop-target always draws the line on the top edge (quizocalypse.css:10194), while the drop commits moveDecisionRule(doc, dragRuleId, i) (LogicTabCard.tsx:357), which lands one row lower on a downward drag.
  • Keyboard (D11). ↑ and ↓ move the rule one place. The handlers exist (LogicTabCard.tsx:404-421); what changes is that the buttons are visible on hover and on focus rather than only when focused, and that their labels name the rule number. Focus stays on the same button of the moved row; when the move disables that button (the rule reached the top or the bottom), focus goes to the other arrow (B30).
  • Feedback, for drag and ↑/↓ alike. Toast "Moved to position N · Undo", N being the final 1-based position. Undo moves that rule id back to its previous index, as an inverse mutation like every other Undo here (D7). Each reorder is one commit.
  • New rules from the rule window, from a pill or from Paste land at the bottom, lowest priority (createDecisionRule, deciderMutations.ts:347-371). The merchant moves them up; a broad rule placed low shows "never runs" at once.
  • A reorder changes outcomes, but the AI review's staleness hash sorts the rules and their shapes and never sees their order or their action (pathReportHash, pathReportMeta.ts:37-48); the engine section owns that fix.

2.5 Empty state (zero rules)

  • A dashed box (1px dashed line, 8px radius, centred, padding 22px 16px, 13.5px): "No rules yet. In Rules only every result comes from a rule, so nothing shows until you create one." with a primary "Create your first rule" that opens a blank rule window (mock rulesBand()'s .rempty2). Under D1 that sentence describes the shipped engine exactly: with no rule to match, every shopper falls to the safety net (section 4).
  • The strip still renders, every pill amber, "0/M have a rule".
  • The funnel CTA reads "Fix 1 issue to continue" and the check popover lists "Rules only needs at least one rule to show anything." (mock findings()). The Tier-1 report has no rule-count check today (pathReport.ts:383-408); it arrives with D3 (section 6).
  • It replaces RulesSetupScaffold (LogicTabCard.tsx:290-303), which writes one action: "show" rule per answer of a chosen question. Delete that component.
  • The empty state points at the template (D16). A merchant who would rather build in a spreadsheet can switch to Table and use "Export", which on a quiz with no rules still writes every sheet with its headers, its do-not-edit id columns and one example row, ready to fill in and import back. Put that as a secondary line under the primary button: "Or build them in a spreadsheet. Table, then Export, gives you the template." No dash and no arrow: the copy rule (owner, 2026-09-07) bans em dashes in merchant-facing strings, and it covers every new string this work adds. There is no second file format and no separate "Download template" affordance (section 9).

3. The Your recommendations strip

3.1 Header and the coverage count

Header: the kicker "Your recommendations" (10px, uppercase, 700, letter-spacing .07em) and "N/M have a rule" (12px, the fraction in ink with tabular figures). M is the number of pills; N is how many of them a rule can actually show. Copy as in the mock (vizRecs()); the label "Recommendations" is the D18 name for a Category row, and the internal words (bucket, target, category, tag bucket) never appear here.

One shared pure helper decides "has a rule". A rule covers a recommendation only when all of these hold:

  • it lists the recommendation (ruleTargets, recommendDecider.ts:63-72);
  • it can fire: at least one condition, at least one recommendation, not "never runs", not "can never match", no broken reference;
  • its action puts products in front of a shopper, which is style-dependent and follows the engine exactly:
    • Rules only: anything but Hide. With no base mapping, both Show and Pin degrade to the rule's own targets (recommendDecider.ts:275-285), and a legacy action-less rule replaces the result outright (recommendDecider.ts:230-237). A Hide resolves to no target (recommendDecider.ts:278), so it shows nothing and never covers.
    • Filter Results + Rules: Show only. Pin never covers, because prioritize only reorders products already in the pool (recommendDecider.ts:308-312), and Hide removes them (:307).

Fixed in mock The mock now implements exactly this split in showsRecs() (style === "rules" ? verb !== "hide" : verb === "show", combined with deadWhy()), and rulesShowing() / ruleCount() read through it. That is B10's fix; port it rather than the old count.

The helper returns, per Category id, the numbers of the rules that can show it. The same output feeds the strip (dot, order, fraction, pill names), the strip's "+N more" list, the rule window's band (which calls the raw count today, CreateRuleModal.tsx:493), the Table's "Shown by rules" and "Status" columns, and the Filter style's "never recommended" warning, which also counts answer mappings (mock recCovered() = recMapped() or ruleShows()). It is recommendationCoverage in the new file app/lib/recommendationCoverage.ts, the one home set in Data model, persistence and the mutations to add. Build it on top of the extended analyzer and give it the style as an argument. It replaces ruleCoverage (createRuleBand.ts:25-33), which today counts every rule of any action; that function is deleted and its callers re-pointed, and its unit test counts zero-condition rules as coverage (createRuleBand.test.ts:35-57), so those cases move in the same change.

  • Conflict CREATE-RULE-HANDOFF.md:208-215 (origin/main) defines coverage as a count of the rules whose target_ids contain the group. B10 supersedes the counting. Its "readout, not a gate" rule still holds for the count itself: the fraction never blocks Continue on its own. What does block is D3's list (section 6), which in Rules only includes "no rule that can show anything" — and that finding is computed from this same helper, so the two can never disagree.
  • Naming, settled: app/lib/ruleCoverage.ts already exists and means answer coverage (buildRuleCoverage, which rules read each question; imported only by CoverageSidebar.tsx:4), so recommendation coverage does not go in it under either name. It goes in the new app/lib/recommendationCoverage.ts, and ruleCoverage.ts is deleted with CoverageSidebar.
  • D2's open half touches only the Filter branch. If the owner changes the engine so Show puts its products first, the Filter branch stays "Show only" and becomes honest. If instead the hint is reworded to describe appending, the Filter branch may need a second condition (a Show rule whose products the results cap can reach) before it counts as coverage. Write the helper so the Filter branch is one clearly-marked predicate that can take that extra condition without touching the Rules-only branch.

Mock: vizRecs(), CSS .recrow and .rpill. One row, no wrap, gap 6px. Order: stable, uncovered first, then covered, each half in Category order; splitRecommendationGroups already makes that split (createRuleBand.ts:38-48).

How "+ Add recommendations" writes (D15). It posts to the existing POST /api/categories/ensure-targets, which is additive and idempotent: a row with the same (quizId, source, sourceRef) is reused, never duplicated, and nothing is deleted (app/routes/api.categories.ensure-targets.tsx:18-24). Four things change:

  • The kind enum gains "group" beside "tag" | "collection" | "product" | "metafield" (ensure-targets.tsx:29), for a shop-global Category row (quizId null) copied into the quiz the way Step 1 copies one. The copy carries the source row's membership and resolved productIds; the original is untouched.

  • Rows are always created quiz-scoped (quizId set), never shop-global, so they get a pill and so re-grouping the quiz does not orphan them.
  • Calls are batched at no more than 12 resources, which is already the endpoint's cap (resources: z.array(ResourceSchema).min(1).max(12), ensure-targets.tsx:37). A larger selection sends several calls and the toast counts the total.

  • Base order comes from the loader and differs by surface: the funnel sorts the quiz's rows by createdAt ascending (funnelLoader.server.ts:59-73), the builder by name ascending (quizEditorIO.server.ts:126-131). Align them, or a row added in the builder jumps when the loader revalidates.
  • Long names: the mock's names are short and nothing caps a pill. Real collection names can be long; cap the label with an ellipsis and the full name as a tooltip, and show it in the owner's screenshot review.
  • A quiz with no quiz-scoped rows is not drawn in the mock: show "+ Add recommendations" alone, without "0/0", and flag it in the screenshot review.

3.3 Lighting rules from a pill

  • While a pill, covered or uncovered, is under the pointer or has keyboard focus, every rule row whose ruleTargets include that Category id gets the accent wash, whatever its verb or flags (mock .rr.lit). An amber pill that lights a Hide rule or a "never runs" rule shows the merchant why it is not covered.
  • Derive the lit rows from state (one lit Category id) at render time; never cache DOM classes. The mock's version goes stale after a re-render and stays lit when the pointer leaves the window (B49). Clear it on pointer leave, on blur, when the pointer leaves the document, and when the Category or the rule list changes.
  • The builder surface (D14, second half, open). [data-qz-surface="editor"] re-points --qz-accent-wash to --qz-cream-2 and the accent to ink (quizocalypse.css:250-257, applied at UnifiedWorkspace.tsx:1804 and :2178), so on the builder the lit wash and the violet verb chip both go neutral. The colour meanings are settled — green is a recommendation not placed on any answer, black is placed, violet is armed — but how the armed and lit states read on that re-pointed surface is not. Build the lit state from the accent token so it inherits whatever that question is answered with; do not hard-code a second colour here. On the funnel surface, where this work ships, the wash is violet and correct.

  • The strip never wraps. On overflow, pills are hidden from the end (so covered ones go first) and "+N more" shows the hidden count; "+ Add recommendations" is never hidden (mock fitRow()). Refit on render, on container resize and on document.fonts.ready. Covered rows are inert, with the green dot, the name and "has a rule".

That covers B27 for this list (the mock opened it with 2 of its 349px visible). Focus moves into the list on open and back to "+N more" on close (B29), and the popover re-anchors or closes when the strip re-renders under it (B28). Fixed in mock for B28: the mock re-anchors popovers from their anchor, closes them on any outside click and locks page scroll behind windows.
  • The strip's list has no search, unlike the tray's and the rule window's "more" lists, which the mock now gives a search field. Adding one here needs the owner's OK; without it the list is capped by the number of quiz-scoped rows, which Step 1 keeps small.

4. What the engine does in Rules only

This is the behaviour the screen's copy describes, and it is the behaviour to build (D1). Both styles run the same first-match-wins loop over decision_rules; they differ in what happens around it.

4.1 The rule loop, shared by both styles

resolveTarget (recommendDecider.ts:217-292) walks decision_rules in array order, skips any rule with zero conditions (:228, the half-built case V9 warns about), and stops at the first rule whose conditions match. Only one rule ever applies to a shopper, whatever its action — which is why "never runs" ignores the verb. An action-less legacy rule replaces the target outright and returns immediately (:230-237); a rule with an action is held as actionRule and the engine then looks for a base.

4.2 The Rules-only branch

When logic_style is "rules", the engine ignores the deciding question and the filter questions entirely:

  • Skip the role === "decides" lookup in resolveTarget (recommendDecider.ts:241-262) so baseTargets is empty and baseTargetId is null. The existing no-base path then does exactly what D1 describes: Show and Pin both fall back to the rule's own targets (:275-285), and a Hide returns null (:278). That path is shipped code — it is unreachable today only because publish demands a mapped picking question.
  • Skip the filter stage in recommendForResult: hasFilters (recommendationEngine.ts:420) must read false in this style, so narrowIdsByFilters (filterMatching.ts:172) never runs and filterQuestions (filterMatching.ts:146-151) is not consulted. Stored filter values stay on the document, untouched and unread.
  • settingsForTarget still resolves the rec-page config from the rule's own target (recommendDecider.ts:189), so per-recommendation overrides keep working.
  • Both skips are gated on the new doc field and on logic_model === "decider". A legacy document has neither and takes the walkLadder path verbatim (recommendationEngine.ts:392). A decider document without the field behaves exactly as it does today.
What the screen saysWhat the engine does in Rules onlyWhat the engine does in Filter Results + Rules

There is no base mapping and no narrowing; with no rule, or no matching rule, the shopper reaches the safety net (4.3).Not the claim made there. The picking question's mapping is the base, filter questions narrow it, rules act on top.

It is flagged on the row and never counts as coverage (2.2, 3.1).Offered. Removes the rule's products from the pool (recommendDecider.ts:307).

4.3 The safety net, for both styles (D1 safety net)

One behaviour serves both styles: a shopper the logic cannot resolve gets the Results step's safety net rather than a bare apology.

  • What exists. The named fallback chain is shipped: deciderFallbackProducts tries emptyFallbackCol (unless the merchant explicitly chose "hide", which is respected) and then safetyNetCol, taking in-stock products from the baked product_index (recommendDecider.ts:505-537; the fields at quizSchema.ts:1836-1842). The runtime prefers the logic-build chooser's global_fallback when it resolves products, and runs the chain when an empty resolved result comes back, gated on cfg.fallbackOn !== false (QuizRuntime.tsx:1582-1594; quizSchema.ts:1815-1818). So in Filter Results + Rules an empty result already reaches the net today.
  • What is missing. When nothing resolves at all, resolveTarget returns null, recommendForResult returns early with no products and no decider block (recommendationEngine.ts:392-397), and the runtime falls into the else if (isDecider) branch and renders one line of muted text — "We couldn't find a perfect match for your answers. Try retaking the quiz with different choices." (QuizRuntime.tsx:1713-1721; app/components/runtime/chromeStrings.ts:48). The fallback chain is never consulted on that path. The schema comment says so in as many words: the no-target-resolved case "is prevented at BUILD time by Step-3 V1/V2 — deliberately no runtime handler" (quizSchema.ts:1838-1840). Rules only makes that path reachable, so it now needs a handler.
  • What to build. On the unresolved path, resolve the global rec-page config with resolveRecPageGlobal(quiz.rec_page_settings) (recommendDecider.ts:181-185) — settingsForTarget needs a target id and there is none — then run the same preference order the empty case uses: global_fallback first when it resolves products, else deciderFallbackProducts, all of it behind fallbackOn !== false. Render the same fallback block the resolved-but-empty case renders, so the two look identical to a shopper. When the chain also comes back empty, keep today's no_results_match line exactly as it is.
  • Proof, because this is a runtime change. app/components/runtime/** is the repository's highest-risk edit class. Decompose rather than rewrite. Prove legacy documents byte-identical (a legacy quiz never has logic_model === "decider" and so never reaches any of this). Render the same document on the local build and on the pre-change deploy and diff normalized outerHTML. Run the full e2e suite and the screenshot review for /q. Re-run the byte pin after the deploy: the first 16 characters of sha256 over /q/cmqqcb0ao004mqvkwjug7t0ya.json must still be c02ccaec98a0fe9e. New tests: a decider quiz in Rules only with no matching rule renders the fallback block; the same quiz with fallbackOn: false renders the no_results_match line; a Filter quiz whose resolved target is empty is unchanged; a legacy quiz is unchanged.

5. Data, state and writes

5.1 The style is a document field

Today logic_style lives on build_session (quizSchema.ts:1699-1708), which publish strips before it writes publishedJson (quizPublish.ts:789-810), and nothing in the engine or validation reads it: its only reader is Step3Shell (Step3Shell.tsx:141) and its only writer the set-logic-style intent (funnelIntents.server.ts:1468-1480). Under D1 the style must survive publish, so it moves onto the document.

  • Schema. Add logic_style: z.enum(["rules", "attributes"]).optional() to Quiz, beside logic_model (quizSchema.ts:1983-1995). Never .default(): a default adds the key to every legacy document on its next parse-and-save round trip, which is the dual-model invariant this repository checks with the byte pin.
  • Migration from the draft field. One pure read helper, resolveLogicStyle(doc), checks doc.logic_style, then doc.build_session?.logic_style for drafts that picked a style before the field existed, then the D5 inference, then the default. It never writes. The draft field is read forever and never deleted, in the same spirit as the other legacy fields this repository keeps parsing. The first time a merchant switches the style on such a draft, the write lands on the document field and the draft field simply stops being consulted.
  • Write. setLogicStyle(doc, style) in app/lib/mutations/deciderMutations.ts, with the same logic_model !== "decider" guard as its neighbours (deciderMutations.ts:257, 265), returning its input when nothing changes, committed through useQuizDraft on both surfaces. A failed save then shows in the funnel's "Not saved · Retry" chip instead of failing silently.
  • Publish keeps it. publishedJson is the document minus a strip list (quizPublish.ts:803-810); do not add logic_style to that list. The engine and validation read it from publishedJson.
  • The intent. set-logic-style (funnelIntents.server.ts:1468-1480) stops being the client's writer, and that is the whole of it: the client stops sending it, the server branch stays in place and parsed, nothing is deleted, and the probe asserts that no set-logic-style request is made. Nothing may read build_session.logic_style ahead of the document field.
  • Legacy documents never gain the key, because only the gated mutation writes it.

5.3 The announced mapping clear (D9)

This screen hides roles, so it never triggers the clear itself — but it shares the path, and the path lives in the mutation layer both styles call. Moving "Picks results" to another question still clears both questions' answer mappings; what changes is that it is announced. One code path serves the role menu, the Table and Import: it computes what was cleared, commits the move, then raises the toast "Q1's 6 recommendations were removed · Undo", whose Undo restores the role and every target as inverse mutations against the latest document (D7). No confirm dialog. The mock already computes the loss message (lossMsg()); that shape is the right one. The Filter Results + Rules section owns the menu; this section owns the rule half of the consequence: rules that referenced a cleared answer are never rewritten by the move, and any that now point at a missing answer render flagged (2.2).

6. Checks, the CTA and publish (D3)

One style-aware Tier-1 report drives all three. buildTier1Report (pathReport.ts:93) takes the style and emits one list; the funnel CTA, the check popover and the publish gate all read it, and the report must never read safer than publish. "Fix N issues to continue" counts blocking findings only; warnings never appear in N. The popover groups findings per question or per rule, and rule findings already carry {kind: "rule", ruleId} links (pathReport.ts:34-40) which this screen resolves to a row through data-rule-id (2.1).

7. Keyboard and focus

  • Tab order after the header: for each rule the row body, ↑, ↓ and trash; "Create your first rule" when the list is empty; then each pill, "+N more" and "+ Add recommendations". Duplicate is not in this order — it lives in the rule window (D11).
  • The ↑/↓ and trash are revealed by :focus-within as well as hover, so a keyboard user sees what they are about to press (D11). The visually-hidden treatment at quizocalypse.css:7445-7455 is replaced.
  • The rule window opens with focus inside and Tab trapped (useFocusTrap, CreateRuleModal.tsx:256; qz-overlays.tsx:33); B31 also wants the page behind it inert, which the mock does. On close, focus returns to the opener. useFocusTrap refocuses whatever had focus when the trap started, so when that opener is gone — an uncovered pill that turned green and moved, or collapsed into "+N more" — focus the new rule's row instead.
  • After a delete: the next row, else the new last row, else "Create your first rule". After a move: the same button of the moved row. After Undo: the restored row's body. Never <body> (B30).
  • Screen readers get the list's name, each row body's full-sentence name, the pill names from 3.2, and toasts through the provider's polite live region, with the Undo button inside it (2.3).

8. Words on this screen

8.1 Sentence grammar (D17)

Rule sentences are verb-first and answers-only: "Show Dryness when (Oily or Combination) and not (Fragrance-free)".

  • Verb chip first, then the recommendation chips, then " when ", then the answer groups.
  • Parentheses around any group of more than one answer; the joining words ("or", "and", "not") in bold.
  • A negated group reads not (A or B) — never "is not A and is not B" (D12; see 8.2).
  • A question label appears only when the same answer text exists on another question ("Yes" on two questions), in which case the group is prefixed "Q7 ". Otherwise the answer text stands alone.
  • Answers truncated at the mock's 28 characters show their full text on hover and on focus (B20); chips never break across lines (B47).
  • The Table view and the spreadsheet export always use the machine form, "Q7 = Yes", never this prose (D16, D17).
  • Build it once, from describeRuleConditions (ruleSummary.ts:11-29) extended to return tokens. That function already carries the rule's own join words: "or" inside an any_of column, "and" inside an all-of column, and the rule's match join across questions (:21-28). The prose surface and the machine surface take the same tokens and render them differently.

8.2 "is not" never combines with "all of" (D12)

  • On an "is not" row the any/all toggle is hidden. The row means none of these answers, which is what the engine has always done for an is_not group (quizSchema.ts:1724-1726).
  • Sentences read "not (A or B)".
  • Import rejects "NOT (A AND B)" with a named reason rather than guessing.
  • No new storage. Nothing is added to DecisionRule; the constraint is enforced in the rule window, in the sentence renderer and in the importer. A rule written before this build that somehow carries an is_not question in any_of still parses and still renders.
  • Consequence for 2.2: the "impossible all-of" check reads "is" groups only.

8.3 Cross-question "or" (D13)

  • Paste rules stops creating cross-question "or" rules. When the parser reports an across-question OR, the commit splits it into adjacent rules with the same verb and the same recommendations, which behaves identically under first-match-wins.
  • The paste parser stays frozen. rulePaste.ts keeps emitting match: "any" on the parsed line (rulePaste.ts:326-327); the split happens in the commit loop, which already calls createDecisionRule once per parsed line and forwards match (PasteRulesModal.tsx:115-123). That is the one place to change.
  • Rules that already carry a cross-question "or" render faithfully — the sentence reads "or" between question groups (describeRuleConditions, ruleSummary.ts:22) — and keep it when edited. Only new paste output is split.
  • A rule with an is_not-only group and match: "any" keeps its "fires for everyone" flag (2.2). Splitting removes the cause for new rules; the flag stays for old ones.

8.4 Renames (D18)

Rename everywhere, through the shared constants, in one change. Internal words — decider, bucket, branch, boost, weight, score, "Tag buckets" — never reach a merchant.

Also the builder's Rules inspector (ContextPanel.tsx:932), the legacy select option (QuestionSection.tsx:427), the explainer label (Explainers.tsx:173) and the pinned tests (ContextPanel.rules.test.tsx:99, 108).

9. The spreadsheet round trip, as it touches this screen

The Table view and Import/Export section owns the contract; three parts of it change what this screen can promise (D16, D16-template).

  • The file carries identity, not just text. Every "When they answer" cell reads "Qn = answer"; the Answers sheet gains a trailing do-not-edit "Answer ID" column and the Rules sheet a "Rule ID" column. That is what lets a merchant round-trip a rule without the importer guessing, and it is why an imported rule can land back on the same row in this list.
  • What Import may do. The Rules sheet stays all-or-nothing. The Answers sheet updates answers in place and never adds or deletes one. The Recommendations sheet is read-only, and any edit to it is reported as ignored rather than silently dropped. A missing column means "leave unchanged", never "clear". An imported rule that references a deleted answer arrives flagged on this screen (2.2), never trimmed.
  • Export is the template. Export downloads the current logic in exactly the format Import accepts, so the affordance must read as both. On a quiz with no rules Export still writes every sheet with its headers, the id columns and one example row marked EXAMPLE in the do-not-edit Rule ID column, so a merchant can fill it in and import it back. There is no second format and no separate template download. The empty state links to it (2.5).
  • The library. Use SheetJS CE 0.20.3 from the official SheetJS CDN tarball, loaded as a lazy chunk so it never enters the admin bundle. Never npm xlsx 0.18.5, which has published CVEs — and Import parses files a merchant supplies, so this is a parser on untrusted input. There is no xlsx dependency on origin/main today (package.json lists papaparse 5.5.4 and nothing else for this), and the mock's loadXLSX() pulls 0.18.5 from cdnjs: that is a mock stand-in, not the spec.
