12. Acceptance for this screen

The screen is done when all of these hold. Run the gate chain unpiped before every commit: npm run typecheck && npm test -- --run && npm run build && npm run lint && node scripts/check-tokens.mjs.

  1. Style. Quiz.logic_style exists, is .optional(), is written only by the gated setLogicStyle, survives publish, and a legacy document parsed and saved is byte-identical. Opening the Logic step writes nothing: a network trace on load shows no PUT and no intent. The chooser and its "Point based" row are gone.
  2. Engine. A decider quiz with logic_style: "rules" resolves the first matching rule's recommendations as the result, with no base mapping and no filter narrowing. The same quiz with the field absent behaves exactly as it does today. A unit test pins each of Show, Pin, Hide and an action-less rule on the no-base path.
  3. Safety net. A shopper who matches no rule sees the fallback block, in both styles, and the bare no_results_match line only when the chain is empty or fallbackOn is false. Proven with the full runtime procedure: DOM diff against the pre-change deploy, full e2e, screenshot review, and the byte pin reading c02ccaec98a0fe9e.
  4. Checks. "Fix N issues to continue" counts blocking findings only and matches what publish refuses, in both styles, on a fixture per row of the section 6 table. A Rules-only quiz with no rules blocks; the same quiz with one Hide-only rule blocks; a Rules-only quiz with no picking question publishes.
  5. Rows. Click to edit, trash, and ↑/↓ visible on hover and on :focus-within; Duplicate is in the rule window and nowhere on the row; the drop line and the drop index agree in both directions; the number renumbers after every move and delete.
  6. Undo. Deleting a rule raises a toast with a keyboard-reachable Undo that survives 6 s and does not expire while hovered or focused; Undo restores the rule at its index by id; two deletes share one Undo; an edit saved from the rule window while the toast is up is not rolled back. The embedded funnel route shows the same toast.
  7. Strip. The fraction and the dots agree with the engine on every fixture in section 3.1; the row never wraps and refits on resize and on fonts.ready; "+N more" opens at 1280 × 720 near the bottom edge without clipping; "+ Add recommendations" creates quiz-scoped rows through ensure-targets with the "group" kind and they appear at once as amber pills.
  8. Words. No merchant-facing string contains decider, bucket, branch, boost, weight, score or "Tag buckets"; the renames in 8.4 are applied through the shared constants and the pinned tests updated; sentences match the 8.1 grammar including "not (...)".
  9. Screenshots (funnel only while D6 is parked): rows at rest, on hover, with keyboard focus and lit; a drag in each direction showing where the line sits; each flag tag; the empty state with its template line; the strip with and without overflow; "+N more" opened near the bottom edge at 1280 × 720; an Undo toast after one delete and after two; the toast over an open rule window.

The rule window (Create a rule / Edit rule) Draft · not yet fact-checked

One dialog creates and edits every rule, in both logic styles. It is the live CreateRuleModal (app/components/studio/logicTab/CreateRuleModal.tsx) rebuilt to the layout the owner decided on 2026-09-17/18 (D24). The save path, the focus trap, the draft-safe scrim and the stored fields stay. The layout, the recommendations band, the footer, deleting, duplicating, prefilled creates and the way the window is bound to its rule change. This work ships the window on the funnel's step 3 surface; the main builder is being rebuilt separately and picks the same component up (D6, see Parked below), so nothing here may be gated in a way that makes it unreachable there. Code refs are origin/main (b4aa278). The mock is docs/design/logic-tab/rules-row/index.html, cited by function and handler name because it is still being edited.

The layout (D24, owner 2026-09-17/18). No title row: the aria-label carries the name. The × and "Delete rule" sit at the right of the "What happens" row. Order: "What happens", then "Your recommendations", then "When they answer". One scrolling body with only the footer pinned. Text-only recommendation chips (no thumbnails), two rows plus "See N more". The live rule sentence sits in the footer. This supersedes docs/design/logic-tab/CREATE-RULE-HANDOFF.md's 36px title bar (line 68), the 1,330px shell (lines 51, 65), the questions-first order, and "no read-back sentence" (lines 49, 226). e2e/create-rule-verify.mjs pins the old shell (1,330px width at line 90, the 36px title bar at 91, 130×62 buckets at 102, the 124px operator column at 109, "N selected" at 224 and 288, "+ Add something else" at 200) and is rewritten in the same change.
What the rulings change in this window.
  • The logic style becomes a field on the quiz doc that survives publish, and the engine gets a real Rules only branch (D1). The window reads the style from the doc, not from build_session.
  • Shoppers no rule matches land on the Results step's "Fallback" in both styles (D1 safety net). This is a shopper-facing runtime change and carries the runtime proof rules.
  • In Rules only the verb switch offers "Show" only, because the first matching rule's recommendations are the whole result (D2, settled for this style).
  • "Duplicate" moves out of the rule row and into the window's top row, next to "Delete rule" (D11).
  • "is not" and "all of" can no longer combine: the join toggle is hidden on an "is not" row and the row means none of these answers (D12).
  • Deleting from the window shows a toast that carries a working "Undo", built from inverse mutations, never a whole-doc snapshot (D7). The embedded /app twins gain the toast provider so that Undo is never invisible (D21).
  • The footer sentence is verb-first and answers-only, with parentheses around multi-answer groups and "not (…)" for negated ones (D17).
  • "+ Add recommendations" writes through ensure-targets, extended with a "group" kind and capped at 12 per call (D15).
  • Every label in the window comes from the shared rename constants, and no internal word reaches the merchant (D18).
  • The live surfaces the mock does not draw survive: rule-flag reasons, product-count popovers, the picker's kind filters and drill-in (D19). The "won't work as written" banner goes.

What this window is built on

Four settled decisions sit under this window. They are specified in full in Data model and Engine semantics; what the window depends on is here, because the verbs, the hints, the coverage readout and the save gate all change with them.

The style lives on the doc (D1)

Today the style is build_session.logic_style (app/lib/quizSchema.ts:1708), written by the set-logic-style intent (app/lib/funnelIntents.server.ts:1468-1481). build_session is stripped at publish (app/lib/quizPublish.ts:804), so that field cannot reach the runtime. Add a doc-level logic_style: z.enum(["rules","attributes"]).optional() beside logic_model (quizSchema.ts:1992), decider-gated, optional, never .default(), so an absent field round-trips absent and every legacy doc stays byte-identical. Name it logic_style at the doc root; it is a different field from build_session.logic_style and only one of them is ever written by a given surface.

  • Read order (one helper, used by the window, the step, the checks, publish and the engine): the doc field, else build_session.logic_style, else inference (any question with role === "filter" means Filter Results + Rules; any rule and no filter role means Rules only), else Filter Results + Rules (D5).
  • Migration: nothing is written on load. The first write is the merchant's own switch, which writes the doc field through the ordinary commit seam and leaves the build_session copy alone; the copy is harmless because it is read last and stripped at publish. A doc that never gets switched keeps resolving through inference, which is what it resolves to today (app/components/onboarding/questionsLogicV3/Step3Shell.tsx:141-155).
  • Publish bakes the field into publishedJson like any other decider field. No legacy doc gains it.

The engine branch (D1)

Rules only is its own method of deciding a result, not a view of the other one. resolveTarget (app/lib/recommendDecider.ts:217) widens its Pick<QuizDoc> from "nodes" | "decision_rules" to include "logic_style". Every caller already passes a whole doc (QuizRuntime.tsx:513, pathEnumeration.ts:140, recommendationEngine.ts:393, q.$id.rec-copy.tsx:128), so no call site changes. When the style is "rules":

  • The deciding-question lookup is skipped (recommendDecider.ts:242-259), so a decides role left on the doc from before a switch cannot contribute a base. Roles and answer mappings are ignored, not deleted: switching styles stays lossless.
  • The first matching rule's recommendations are the result, through the no-base path already in the function (recommendDecider.ts:276-283). A rule with no action (the legacy replace form) already returns its targets at recommendDecider.ts:230-236 and reaches the same answer.
  • A matching rule stored as "Hide" returns null (recommendDecider.ts:278), which is why "Hide" is not offered here (D2).
  • No rule matches: recommendDecider.ts:286 returns null, and the safety net below takes over.

Filter Results + Rules keeps today's engine exactly: the picking question gives the base, filter questions narrow it, rules act on top.

The safety net, for both styles (D1 safety net)

When resolveTarget returns null, explainDecider returns { products: [], rungUsed: null, … } with no decider key (app/lib/recommendationEngine.ts:394-398). QuizRuntime gates the whole Logic v2 reveal on that key (app/components/runtime/QuizRuntime.tsx:1579), so a no-match shopper drops to the classic result view, whose fallback renders only when global_fallback.enabled is true (QuizRuntime.tsx:1758-1766; resolveGlobalFallbackProducts returns an empty list otherwise, recommendationEngine.ts:551), and that flag is false by default (quizSchema.ts:1340). The default outcome today is an empty page on a different layout.

Build one behaviour for both styles: a null target still renders the decider reveal, and the Results step's "Fallback" fills it, through the same chain the reveal already uses when the product list comes back empty (QuizRuntime.tsx:1583-1594: global_fallback first, then deciderFallbackProducts). There is no merchant control to point at. On a decider quiz no reachable UI writes global_fallback, rec_page_settings.global.emptyFallbackCol or safetyNetCol: FallbackSection is imported only by LogicScroll, which has no importer on origin/main (app/components/onboarding/questionsLogicV3/logic/LogicScroll.tsx:24,398), and ResultsGuided records that the chooser left the Results step (app/components/onboarding/resultsGuided/ResultsGuided.tsx:513-515, owner 2026-08-18). The only writers on a decider doc are the build-time seed (app/lib/onboardingBuild.server.ts:399-404) and the decider-conversion seed (app/lib/proposeDeciderConversion.ts:221), so a decider quiz can reach publish with nothing configured and the shopper sees the same bare no_results_match card as today. Build the net over the chain as it stands, do not invent a control for it, and raise the gap in your report; Scope, sources and ground rules states it in the same words.

Read the code, not the schema comment, on this one. quizSchema.ts:2187-2190 still says global_fallback is "Parsed for back-compat only … intentionally never resolved or rendered — no builder control and no runtime fallback grid". That comment is stale: QZY-1 gave the field a mode chooser (quizSchema.ts:1342-1348), a Results-step control that is no longer mounted (FallbackSection.tsx:63-108; see above) and a builder control (ResultSettingsPanel.tsx:133-135), and the runtime resolves it in three places (QuizRuntime.tsx:1077-1078, 1583-1588, 1762-1763). Correct the comment in the same change, or the next reader will conclude the safety net does not exist.

This is a runtime change, so it carries the runtime proof rules. app/components/runtime/** is the highest-risk edit class: decompose, do not rewrite. Prove legacy docs byte-identical by rendering the same doc on the local build and the pre-change deploy and diffing normalized outerHTML. Run the full e2e and the screenshot review for /q. Re-check the byte pin after the deploy: curl -sS https://quizocalypse-studio.fly.dev/q/cmqqcb0ao004mqvkwjug7t0ya.json | shasum -a 256 must still start c02ccaec98a0fe9e. The gate for touching the reveal is a decider doc whose target resolves normally producing byte-identical HTML before and after.

One style-aware report, and no first-entry chooser (D3, D5)

  • The window's save gate and the step's Tier-1 report come from the same predicates. Rules only blocks on no rules, no rule that can show anything, and any rule missing its answers or its recommendations, and skips the picking-question checks. Filter Results + Rules keeps today's blocks and adds route bypass and broken or impossible rules. "Fix N issues" counts blocking findings only. The window's gate must never be looser than the report, and the report must never read safer than the publish gate (D3; see Checks and Continue).
  • There is no chooser screen. Delete LogicStyleChooser and its inert "Point based" row (app/components/onboarding/questionsLogicV3/logic/LogicStyleChooser.tsx:88-89, 169-170), and drop the logicStyle === null branch in Step3Shell.tsx:422. The window therefore always has a style (D5).

Entry points

Every entry closes any open popover first (mock ACT.addrule, ACT.editrule, ACT.createFor). While the window is open the page behind it is inert, so no second entry can fire underneath it (see Keyboard, focus and overlays below).

Host state. LogicTabCard holds two pieces of state today, createOpen and editRuleId (LogicTabCard.tsx:116-119), and passes the rule it finds by id (LogicTabCard.tsx:545-547). Replace them with one discriminated state, plus a reference to the element that opened the window (used for focus return):

type RuleWindow =

  | { kind: "edit"; ruleId: string };               // bound by id, never by list position

The two styles in this window

Both styles are first-class. The window is the same window; what differs is what a rule means, and therefore which verbs exist and what the hints promise.

Filter Results + RulesRules only
What a rule doesAn exception on top of the mapping. The picking question gives the base, filter questions narrow it, the first matching rule acts on the result.The whole decision. The first matching rule's recommendations are the result (D1). Roles and answer mappings are ignored by the engine.
Verbs offered"Show", "Pin", "Hide""Show" only (D2). Under first-match-wins with no base there is nothing to move to the top and nothing to remove, so "Pin" and "Hide" have no meaning here.
"Show" hintPer the open half of D2 (see Still open below). Today the engine appends a Show rule's products after the base pool (applyRuleAction, recommendDecider.ts:313-316), so "these become the results" is not accurate here and must not ship unchanged."these become the results" is accurate and ships as written, because there is no base pool (recommendDecider.ts:276-283).
A rule already stored with another verbOpens on its stored verb.Opens on its stored verb too. A doc can carry a prioritize or hide rule here because switching styles is lossless. Build requirement The switch renders "Show" plus, only when the bound rule's stored action is one of the others, that one option, selected. The window never misrepresents a stored rule and never rewrites a verb the merchant did not touch (the stored-state rule, DECISIONS.md:42-45). Say what a stored "Hide" does here: it sends every shopper it matches to the Results step's "Fallback" (recommendDecider.ts:278).

Layout

  • No title row. The box is role="dialog", aria-modal="true", aria-label "Create a rule" or "Edit rule" (mock modalHTML, .mbox). Live already sets these attributes (CreateRuleModal.tsx:983-985) but also renders an h2 title bar with the × (CreateRuleModal.tsx:987-992); remove the bar.
  • One scrolling body, in this order: the "What happens" row, the "Your recommendations" band, then the "When they answer" label and the question rows (mock modalHTML). Only the footer is pinned (.mscroll is flex:1 with its own scroll; .mfoot is flex:none). The "What happens" row, the × and "Delete rule" scroll away with the questions on purpose: the report asking to pin them (B33) was rejected as the owner-approved design. The mock's .mhead and .mhead h2 rules are dead CSS, as is the comment above them describing the rejected pinned header; port neither.
  • Width. The box hugs its widest question row (.mbox: width:fit-content, min-width:min(680px,100%)), and each answer strip is capped at 676px (.mans), which fits six 104px buckets. Measured in headless Chromium at 100%: 992px with the sample quiz, 1,000px with 10 answers on one question. Live is a fixed min(1330px, 96vw) (quizocalypse.css:11890).
  • Sideways scroll. A question with more than six answers scrolls sideways inside its own row, with a 44px fade at the right edge while more than 4px is left to scroll (.manswrap.more::after; markMore).
  • Height. Never taller than the viewport: the scrim has 16px padding plus the safe-area insets and the box is max-height:100% (#modal, .mbox). Measured: 733px tall at 1440×900; at 1280×720 it stops at 688px and the body scrolls by 45px. Live caps the box at 88vh (quizocalypse.css:11884-11889).
  • New drafts start at the top (B51): body scrollTop 0 and every answer strip scrollLeft 0, for "… & add another" and for prefilled creates; a redraw of the same draft keeps its scroll. Fixed in mock (drawModal(fresh) keeps .mscroll and per-row scrollLeft only when fresh is falsy). Live resets only the body (CreateRuleModal.tsx:689). In React, key the scroll body on a draft id that changes only when a new draft starts. Picks never re-key anything: "A pick must never move the merchant" still holds (CREATE-RULE-HANDOFF.md:233-241).
  • Sizes at 100% (mock): 22px padding each side of the question rows (.mq); question row grid 22px | 184px | 44px | answers with a 10px gap (.mrow); buckets 104×68 (.bk); scale points 58px wide with a 16px bold numeral (.bk.pt, .ptn); footer 65px tall (measured). Build them on size tokens (D20: the mock's 100% sizes are the spec, the 130% study is not).
  • The mock's ≤720px reflow is not needed: the Wiskr admin is desktop-only.
  • Builder accent. The window portals to document.body (CreateRuleModal.tsx:976-1148), outside the builder's data-qz-surface="editor" wrapper (UnifiedWorkspace.tsx:1800-1804), so the builder's ink stand-down does not reach it and its violet states stay violet. The second half of D14 is still open on how the armed state reads on that surface (see Still open below); nothing in this window is blocked on it, because this work ships the funnel surface.

The "Your recommendations" band

This band replaces the live onboarding band (CreateRuleModal.tsx:824-974), which had 248px thumbnail cards with a product peek on the count (CreateRuleModal.tsx:160-203), labelled "Needs a rule · N" / "Has rules · N" sections past six groups (CreateRuleModal.tsx:922-942), a "+ Add something else" catalogue (CreateRuleModal.tsx:912-920) and an "N selected" footer count (CreateRuleModal.tsx:1116-1120). The funnel surface uses the new band. The builder keeps its "What the quiz shows" band (CreateRuleModal.tsx:726-822) in the same slot until the main-builder work adopts this screen (D6), and everything else in the window stays shared: keeping the whole old window in the builder would fork the component, which the handoff warns against (CREATE-RULE-HANDOFF.md:278). Keep the band behind the existing flow prop rather than a new one, so the builder can switch to it with a prop value and no rewrite.

"+ Add recommendations" writes through ensure-targets (D15)

  • The write goes to POST /api/categories/ensure-targets (app/routes/api.categories.ensure-targets.tsx), extended with a "group" kind alongside tag, collection, product and metafield (the enum at api.categories.ensure-targets.tsx:26-31). A group is copied into the quiz the way Step 1 does.
  • Tag keys are normalized to the Step-1 slugs before the call, so a tag added here and the same tag added in Step 1 resolve to one row.
  • Rows are always created quiz-scoped. The route already prefers a quiz-scoped row over a shop-global one when reusing (api.categories.ensure-targets.tsx:78-95).
  • Batched at no more than 12 resources per call, which is the route's own cap (api.categories.ensure-targets.tsx:36). It is additive and idempotent, so a retry reuses rather than duplicates, and the rows survive re-grouping.
  • The same endpoint serves the funnel now and the builder later, which is what keeps D6's parked work cheap.

Validation and warnings

  • Save gate. Both save buttons stay disabled until at least one answer and at least one recommendation are picked, no impossible all-of remains, and no save is in flight. Live checks picks, recommendations and busy (canCreate, CreateRuleModal.tsx:590); the mock now checks all three conditions (modalHTML's ok, which includes !impossible(M)). Fixed in mock. The first two conditions match createDecisionRule's own refusal (deciderMutations.ts:359).
  • Impossible all-of blocks saving (B14). A multi-select "is" row set to "all of" with more picks than max_selections can never match: the shopper's Next button stays disabled above the maximum (app/components/runtime/views/QuestionView.tsx:356, 413, 421). Show the warning and block the save. That follows DECISIONS.md:14 (G3), where a combination that can never fire is blocked, not warned about. Use one shared predicate with the analyzer's "can never match" reason (see Engine semantics), so the window's gate and the Tier-1 report agree by construction (D3).
  • No impossible warning on "is not" rows: under D12 an "is not" row has no join, and none-of can always be satisfied.
  • The gate is never looser than the report (D3). Rules only blocks publish on a rule missing its answers or its recommendations, which is the same pair the window blocks on, so a rule that saves here can never be a blocking finding for those two reasons. If a new block is added to the report, add it here in the same change.
  • Nothing else blocks the save. Coverage stays a readout (CREATE-RULE-HANDOFF.md:214-216). "never runs", "half-built", "target deleted" and "fires for everyone" appear as rule-flag reasons in the rule lists after saving, in the mock's tag style (D19), not in the window.

The sentence grammar (D17)

  • Verb-first and answers-only. "Show dryness when (Shiny or Blotchy) and (Forehead and Cheeks) and not (One or two)". No "Q7 is" prefixes in the sentence.
  • Parentheses around multi-answer groups, with the join in bold between them. A single-answer group has no parentheses. Partial The mock's whenHTML already does the parentheses and bold joins; the footer's sentence(M, true) does not yet, so the footer builder needs the same grammar.
  • Negated groups read "not (…)", which is the D12 meaning made readable.
  • Full-text tooltips. The mock truncates at 30 characters (short) without a title; add the full text as title on every shortened chip (B20).
  • A question label appears only when it is needed, that is when the same answer text exists on another question in the quiz. Otherwise the answer text stands alone.
  • The Table and the export always use the machine form, "Q7 = Yes" (mock whenText, sheets). Two forms, one describer, chosen by a mode flag: never two implementations.

Toasts. Success: "Rule created" (create) and "Rule saved" (edit), the same for the "… & add another" variants (mock ACT.msave). They replace the live "✓ Rule created", "✓ Rule updated" and "✓ Rule saved" (CreateRuleModal.tsx:671, 687). A toast shown while the window stays open must not cover its footer (B34): the design-system toast is fixed 28px above the bottom of the viewport (quizocalypse.css:4406-4415), which lands on the footer of a full-height window. Raise it above the open window's footer. Fixed in mock (placeToast lifts the toast above the topmost open window's footer).

The toast with an action, and Undo (D7, D9, D21)

The shipped toast is a queue of one, auto-dismissing at 2,400ms, explicitly non-interactive: "Not clickable, no actions: if an action is needed, it isn't a toast" (app/components/qz-toast.tsx:13-17), and the CSS sets pointer-events: none (quizocalypse.css:4414). D7 amends that rule rather than inventing a fifth surface.

  • Extend the shared toast, once. useQzToast returns (message: string) => void today (qz-toast.tsx:33-35). Widen it to take one optional action { label, onAction } and an optional duration. One action, never two. Restore pointer-events only when an action is present, so an actionless toast stays exactly as it is.
  • Record the exception. Write the dated owner exception into the design-system contract comment in qz-toast.tsx:13-17, the way the overlay contract records its own amendments (qz-overlays.tsx:16-25). Without it the next reader deletes the action as a contract violation.
  • Announcement and keyboard reach. The toast already renders role="status" aria-live="polite" (qz-toast.tsx:68), which announces the message but leaves the action unreachable: an assistive-technology user hears "Rule 3 deleted" and has no way to act. Keep the message in the live region, make the action a real focusable button, give it a longer duration than 2,400ms when an action is present, and make it reachable from the keyboard without hunting (B32). Pause the dismiss timer while the action has focus or the pointer is over the toast.
  • Undo is inverse mutations, never a snapshot. A delete's Undo re-inserts the same rule at its index through a new pure restoreDecisionRule(doc, rule, index), which is a no-op when the id already exists (see Data model). It is built against getLatestDoc() at the moment Undo is clicked, so an unrelated edit made while the toast was up survives. This is the opposite of the builder's whole-doc history (UnifiedWorkspace.tsx:160-162), and that difference is the point.
  • Several deletes accumulate into one Undo. Deleting again while a toast is up updates the same toast to "2 rules deleted" with one "Undo" that restores both, each at its own index (B35). Fixed in mock (snap, toastU, delRule).
  • Add the missing providers. QzToastProvider wraps only three routes today (app/routes/studio.tsx:31, app/routes/studio_.$id.tsx:117, app/routes/studio_.onboarding_.$quizId.tsx:38). Without a provider useQzToast falls back to a no-op context (qz-toast.tsx:31), so a delete would be silent and unrecoverable. In the embedded twins, app/routes/app.onboarding_.$quizId.tsx and app/routes/app.quizzes.$id_.studio.tsx, add the provider and nothing else (D21). The hardcoded /studio links and giving embedded decider quizzes the new Logic view are separate tasks.

Moving "Picks results" announces what it cleared (D9)

This is not a rule-window control, but it uses the toast this window ships and it changes what an open window can be looking at, so it is specified with the toast.

  • Moving "Picks results" to another question still clears both questions' answer mappings: the old picking question's targets and the new one's. Live already does this silently (mock ACT.setrole does the same).
  • It is now announced: a toast names what was cleared, for example "Q1's 6 recommendations were removed", and its "Undo" restores the role and every target. No confirm dialog.
  • One path serves all three callers: the role menu, the Table's role cell and Import. Build it as one mutation plus one inverse, not three call sites with their own copies.
  • An open rule window is unaffected: rules store answer ids, not roles, so nothing in the draft changes. In Filter Results + Rules the band's coverage readout does change, because recMapped depends on the mapping; let it re-render.

Draft normalization on save

The stored rule always equals its sentence (B13). Run one pure normalizeDecisionRule (see Data model), shared with Import and the import diff:

  • Drop "is not" on questions with no picks.
  • Drop "all of" on questions with fewer than two picks, on questions that are not multi-select, and on "is not" rows (D12).
  • Store conditions in question order, then answer order within a question.
  • Keep conditions that point at deleted answers or questions, and targets that point at deleted rows, until the merchant removes them. They are shown flagged, never silently dropped (DECISIONS.md:42-45).
  • Keep edit fidelity: a row the merchant never touched keeps its original conditions byte for byte, including mixed per-condition ops that the per-question toggle cannot express (live seededGroups / dirtyQs, CreateRuleModal.tsx:293-308, 394-404).
  • If the normalized draft equals the stored rule, skip the commit, then close and toast as usual, so an untouched Save never marks the quiz changed.

The live derivation already avoids stray flags by construction: it skips questions with no picks and writes any_of only for "is" rows with two or more picks (CreateRuleModal.tsx:390-410). The mock's tidy now does the same for its own model, including the multi-select test on "all of". Fixed in mock.

Storage mapping

In the windowStored on DecisionRule (quizSchema.ts:1742-1769)Rule
Each picked answer on an "is" rowconditions[]: {question_id, answer_id, op: "is"}One condition per pick; always answer ids, never positions (the mock stores answer indexes, which is a harness shortcut, not the contract)
Each picked answer on an "is not" row{question_id, answer_id, op: "is_not"}Means none of these answers; a skipped question satisfies it (recommendDecider.ts:342-351)
An "is" row with two or more picks left on "any of", or any non-multi row with two or more picksany_of includes the question idForced for non-multi rows (CreateRuleModal.tsx:405-410)
A multi-select "is" row on "all of"The question id is absent from any_ofAbsence means all of; an edit re-reads it that way (CreateRuleModal.tsx:340-345)
An "is not" rowNever in any_ofD12: the flag has no meaning on an is_not group, and the engine ignores it there (recommendDecider.ts:342-351)
Show / Pin / Hideaction: "show" / "prioritize" / "hide"CreateRuleModal.tsx:75-79. In Rules only a new rule is always "show" (D2).
An edited rule with no action, left on Showaction stays absentThe legacy replace rule (CreateRuleModal.tsx:633-636; quizSchema.ts:1762-1763)

Example: Show acne and redness when Q1 is Shiny or Blotchy (single-select), Q2 is all of Forehead and Cheeks (multi-select, max 3) and Q3 is not One or two.

{
  "id": "rule_k3x9q2mz",
  "conditions": [
    { "question_id": "q1", "answer_id": "a_shiny",    "op": "is" },
    { "question_id": "q1", "answer_id": "a_blotchy",  "op": "is" },
    { "question_id": "q2", "answer_id": "a_forehead", "op": "is" },
    { "question_id": "q2", "answer_id": "a_cheeks",   "op": "is" },
    { "question_id": "q3", "answer_id": "a_one_two",  "op": "is_not" }
  ],
  "target_id": "cat_acne",
  "target_ids": ["cat_acne", "cat_redness"],
  "action": "show",
  "any_of": ["q1"]
}
// footer sentence (D17): Show acne redness when (Shiny or Blotchy) and (Forehead and Cheeks) and not (One or two)
// Table and export (D17):  Q1 = Shiny OR Q1 = Blotchy · Q2 = Forehead AND Q2 = Cheeks · NOT (Q3 = One or two)

Rules that arrive from Paste and from Import

  • Paste splits a cross-question "or" (D13). The paste parser stays frozen: rulePaste.ts:326 keeps emitting match: "any" on a parsed line whose across-question connectors include "or". The change is at the write, in PasteRulesModal's commit loop (PasteRulesModal.tsx:112-122): a line carrying match: "any" becomes one createDecisionRule call per question group, adjacent, in order, with the same verb and the same recommendations, and no match field. Under first-match-wins that behaves identically, and every resulting rule is expressible in this window. New
  • Existing match-any rules are untouched. They render faithfully in the lists and the sentence, open here with the match-any note, and keep the field on save (CreateRuleModal.tsx:641-652). Do not migrate them.
  • Import brings identity (D16). The spreadsheet's Rules sheet carries a do-not-edit "Rule ID" column and every "When they answer" cell reads "Qn = answer", and the Answers sheet carries a do-not-edit "Answer ID" column. So a rule edited in the spreadsheet and imported back keeps the same id, and this window, which binds by id, opens the same rule from the Table, the list or a finding. Import never adds or deletes answers; the Recommendations sheet is read-only and edits to it are reported as ignored; a missing column means leave unchanged, never clear. The Rules sheet stays all-or-nothing: either the whole sheet applies or none of it does.
  • Export is the template (D16 template). The same file Export writes is the file Import reads, so the affordance reads as both. On a quiz with no rules, Export still writes both sheets with their headers, the id columns and one example row marked EXAMPLE in the do-not-edit Rule ID column, so a merchant can fill it in and import it back. There is no second format.
  • Library (D16). SheetJS CE 0.20.3 from the official SheetJS CDN tarball, vendored and loaded as a lazy chunk. Never npm xlsx 0.18.5: it has published CVEs and Import parses merchant-supplied files. There is no xlsx dependency in package.json on origin/main, so nothing has to be removed; the mock's loadXLSX pulls 0.18.5 from cdnjs and is a harness stand-in, not the build.

Save path

Keep the live path (CreateRuleModal.tsx:596-693) with these changes:

  1. Check the gate (above). Normalize the draft.
  2. Resources that are not already Category rows go to POST /api/categories/ensure-targets in batches of at most 12, per D15. The route rejects more than 12 resources (api.categories.ensure-targets.tsx:36) and the window sends them all in one uncapped request today (CreateRuleModal.tsx:598-613), so 13 or more picks can never save. Map each batch's returned rows back by index (CreateRuleModal.tsx:625-628) and lift them with onCategoriesCreated after every batch (CreateRuleModal.tsx:624). In the new band the picks are already Category rows, so this step usually does nothing; it stays because "+ Add recommendations" and the builder band both route through it.
  3. On any failure keep the draft exactly as it is, keep focus on the clicked button, toast and stop. Rows from batches that already succeeded stay: the route reuses them on retry (api.categories.ensure-targets.tsx:78-95). Reword the live toasts, which contain an em dash or the internal word "targets": "Couldn't reach the server — the rule wasn't saved" and "Couldn't save those targets — try again" (CreateRuleModal.tsx:615, 619) become "Couldn't reach the server. The rule wasn't saved." and "Couldn't add those recommendations. Try again." (D18).
  4. Build on getLatestDoc(), never the render-time doc (CreateRuleModal.tsx:637-640; the host passes docRef.current, LogicTabCard.tsx:127-129, 555).
  5. Edit: if the bound id is no longer in the latest doc, write nothing (see binding below). Otherwise updateDecisionRule(base, id, {conditions, target_ids, action, any_of}). Always pass the action key: its presence semantics clear the action for a kept legacy rule (deciderMutations.ts:332-335). Leave match out of the patch (deciderMutations.ts:310-313). An empty any_of deletes the field (deciderMutations.ts:314-317).
  6. Create: createDecisionRule(base, {conditions, target_ids, action, any_of?}), which appends the rule at the bottom (deciderMutations.ts:347-372).
  7. Commit once per save through the host's commit (the autosave path). The save pill belongs to the edited field, not to this window, and the ambient autosave chrome stays silent while healthy (D8). A failed autosave after that point belongs to the funnel's save chip ("Not saved" plus "Retry", app/components/onboarding/funnelChrome.tsx:104-106), not to the window.
  8. Toast, then close (focus returns to the opener) or start the next blank draft.

Delete path

  1. "Delete rule" shows in edit mode only. It asks for no confirmation.
  2. Read the rule and its index by id from getLatestDoc(). If the id is gone, close the window and toast "That rule was already removed" (mock ACT.mdel).
  3. Commit removeDecisionRule(base, id) (deciderMutations.ts:256-261) and close the window, discarding the draft.
  4. Toast "Rule N deleted" (N = index + 1) with an "Undo", through the D7 toast. Undo re-inserts the same rule at its index through restoreDecisionRule, built against the latest doc, never through a whole-doc snapshot. Deletes made while the toast is up join one Undo ("2 rules deleted"). Fixed in mock (snap, delRule, toastU).
  5. Move focus to the row now at that position, or the previous row, or the list's create button when the list is empty (B30). The Undo stays reachable from the keyboard (D7, B32).
Ship "Delete rule" and the Undo in the same change. It adds a second no-confirm delete path. Live row deletes already have no confirm and no Undo (toast "Rule deleted", LogicTabCard.tsx:463-471), and in the embedded twins there is no toast provider at all, so today an embedded delete is silent. D21 closes that hole, D7 supplies the Undo. Do not land the window's delete before either.

Rule rows, the controls on them, and reordering (D11)

The rows live in the Rules only rules row and the Filter Results + Rules rules column, not in this window, but they are the window's main entry and exit, so their contract is here.

  • Click the row to edit. The row body is a real button; Enter and Space open the window bound to that rule id. The "✎" button goes (LogicTabCard.tsx:423-438).
  • A trash icon on the row deletes it, with the same toast and Undo as the window's "Delete rule".
  • "↑" and "↓" reorder, revealed on hover and on keyboard focus, so a keyboard user can reorder without a mouse. Partial The buttons already exist with aria-label "Move rule up" / "Move rule down" and commit moveDecisionRule (LogicTabCard.tsx:404-420); what is new is the hover-and-focus reveal and their place among the row's controls. Keep the disabled state at the ends and keep the aria-labels.
  • "Duplicate" leaves the row and moves into the window's top row. Remove the "⧉" button (LogicTabCard.tsx:441-462) and carry its toast copy over, reworded.
  • Order is priority. Say so once near the list, because reordering changes which rule wins under first-match-wins, and in Rules only it changes the result outright.

Binding to the rule

  • Bind by id, for the life of the window. An edit window keeps its ruleId until it closes. Seed the draft once per open and once per new draft, never on a doc refresh (live seeds on [open, editId] and treats categories as a lookup only, CreateRuleModal.tsx:326-373). Fixed in mock (ACT.editrule stores edit: r.id; ACT.msave and ACT.mdel look the rule up by that id; keepM closes the window when the rule is gone).
  • Today's failure mode. When the rule under edit disappears, LogicTabCard passes editRule={null} (LogicTabCard.tsx:545-547). The seed effect then resets to a blank draft (CreateRuleModal.tsx:326-330) and the window silently becomes "Create a rule"; Save would add a new rule (B2).
  • If the rule vanishes while open (a delete Undo, an import Undo, the builder's ⌘Z): Save writes nothing, closes and toasts "That rule was removed, so nothing was saved." "Delete rule" closes and does nothing. updateDecisionRule already no-ops on a missing id (deciderMutations.ts:300), so detect the missing id before claiming "Rule saved". Saving the draft as a new rule is not offered.
  • Nothing behind the window may change the list. The page behind is inert (below). A delete's Undo toast that is still showing when the window opens sits above the scrim (toast z-index 200 over modal 120, quizocalypse.css:221-224), so its "Undo" stays clickable. That is safe only because restores work by id and never touch the bound rule, which is exactly why D7 rules out a whole-doc snapshot.
  • Builder ⌘Z. The builder's window-level ⌘Z / ⌘⇧Z handler skips only inputs, textareas, selects and contentEditable (UnifiedWorkspace.tsx:259-284), and its history is a stack of whole-doc snapshots (UnifiedWorkspace.tsx:160-162). With focus on any button inside the rule window, ⌘Z replays an older snapshot underneath it. Skip the shortcut while any dialog is open (for example when the active element is inside [aria-modal="true"]). This applies whenever the main-builder work adopts the window (D6), so build the guard now rather than leaving a trap for that project.

Keyboard, focus and overlays

  • Keep useFocusTrap (CreateRuleModal.tsx:256). It moves focus into the box (to the first focusable element unless given an initial ref), wraps Tab and Shift+Tab, and restores focus to the previously focused element on close (qz-overlays.tsx:30-68). In the new order the first focusable element is the verb switch; live it is the title bar's ×. Fixed in mock (drawModal focuses the selected verb or the first button on open and on a fresh draft, and restores focus through actKey / drawModal.back on close).
  • Make the page behind inert. useFocusTrap only wraps Tab. Set inert on the route's page container while the window is open, and on the rule window itself while Add recommendations is stacked on it (B31). Fixed in mock (drawModal sets inert on BG).
  • Esc closes the innermost layer only: an open popover, then Add recommendations, then the rule window (the draft is discarded with no prompt), one layer per key press. Keep the document-level listener, since a listener on the scrim misses keys once focus leaves it (CreateRuleModal.tsx:258-272), and extend its check. Today it yields only to an open .qz-popover (CreateRuleModal.tsx:267), so it would also close the rule window when Esc is meant for Add recommendations. One layer stack with a single Esc handler is the safest build.
  • Scrim clicks never close the window (draft-safe). Live renders the scrim with no click handler (CreateRuleModal.tsx:976-979) and is a bespoke shell for exactly that reason (CreateRuleModal.tsx:47-48). Keep it; do not move the window onto QzModal, whose scrim closes non-destructive modals on mousedown (qz-overlays.tsx:138-141).
  • Lock page scroll while the window is open (B28). The live scrim has no lock (quizocalypse.css:4287-4294). Fixed in mock (html:has(#modal:not([hidden]),…){overflow:hidden}; measured: the wheel over the scrim leaves the page at scrollY 0).
  • Focus return. On close, focus goes back to the opener if it is still in the document. Otherwise it goes to the new or edited rule's row (a covered pill can re-render as a different element), or per the delete path. Fixed in mock (drawModal falls back to the create button when the opener is gone).
  • Popovers inside the window. QzPopover portals outside the box (qz-overlays.tsx:419-432), so the box's Tab trap never sees its keys. It needs its own focus handling: focus the search on open, return focus to "See N more" on close, and keep Tab inside the popover or send it back to the window (B29). It positions itself only when it opens (qz-overlays.tsx:343-354); add re-anchoring for body scroll, resize and content changes (B28). Its trigger already gets aria-expanded and aria-haspopup (qz-overlays.tsx:405-418). The mock's placePop re-anchors and closes the popover once its anchor scrolls out of the window's scroll area; port that behaviour.
  • Buttons. Every bucket, chip, operator and verb is a real <button> with aria-pressed (CREATE-RULE-HANDOFF.md:352-361 still applies). Picks update in place and keep focus; nothing remounts on a pick.
  • Stacking. Add recommendations on top of the rule window is a modal-over-modal stack; see the conflict below.
Conflict The design-system overlay contract allows exactly one stack, a modal over a drawer ("Modal-over-drawer is the ONE legal stack", qz-overlays.tsx:16-25), and says the design system is amended first when a need does not fit. The approved Add recommendations window opens as a second modal over the rule window. Record a dated owner exception in that contract, in the same change and the same form as the toast-action exception D7 requires, before building the stack.

The live VERB_TO_ACTION map keeps "Pin" on the outside and prioritize on the inside (CreateRuleModal.tsx:75-79), which is the pattern: internal names stay in the storage layer and never surface.

Cases the mock does not draw

  • A deleted recommendation on an edited rule. Live drops it from the draft without a word when it opens (the seed skips targets whose Category row is missing, CreateRuleModal.tsx:351-369). Instead, show it as a picked chip flagged "recommendation deleted" that can be removed; saving keeps exactly what is shown (B1, B9). This is the stored-state rule again: show it, do not silently rewrite it.
  • Conditions on deleted answers or questions. Live keeps a deleted answer's condition invisibly, and drops conditions on a deleted question at the next save, because the derivation walks only the current questions (CreateRuleModal.tsx:390). An is_not on a missing answer matches every shopper, which brokenRuleRefs already reports as the more dangerous of the two cases (app/lib/pathAnalyzer.ts:151-178). Show a flagged "answer deleted" bucket at the end of its row, or a "Deleted question" row, each removable (B1, B8).
  • A quiz with no recommendations. Hide the fraction and leave "+ Add recommendations" as the band's only control. Live falls back to the catalogue band here (CreateRuleModal.tsx:515-517).
  • A rule with zero conditions (half-built, from older paths) opens with nothing picked, and Save stays disabled until an answer is picked. The engine never fires it (recommendDecider.ts:228).
  • Mixed per-condition ops on one question (from the older inline editor) show as "is not", because any is_not marks the row (CreateRuleModal.tsx:337). They are kept verbatim until the row is touched; touching the row rewrites every condition on it to one op.
  • A Rules-only quiz that still carries roles and mappings. Switching styles is lossless by design, so the doc can hold a decides role and filter values that the engine now ignores. The window lists those questions as ordinary rows and says nothing about their roles. Do not strip them, and do not show the merchant an "unused" warning here; that belongs to the step's checks if it belongs anywhere (D3).
Still open, and what it blocks here. Three items are not ruled on. Do not pick them while building; build everything around them and leave the seam.
  • D2, the Filter Results + Rules half. In that style "Show" appends after the base pool (applyRuleAction, recommendDecider.ts:313-316) and is then cut off by the results cap, while the hint promises "these become the results". The owner chooses between changing the engine so Show puts its products first and changing the hint to describe appending. Blocks: the Show hint string for that style only, and, if the engine option wins, a second runtime change with its own proof. Everything else in the window ships: the verb itself, the storage, the sentence and the Rules only hint are all settled. Build the hint as a per-style constant so the decision lands in one string.
  • D10, question-type changes. What a type change does to answers and to the rules that referenced them (scale conversions dropping answers, five-point trimming to five, and the conditions left pointing at answers that no longer exist). The mock trims and tells the merchant (ACT.settype, lossMsg, setPoints). Blocks: what an open rule window shows after a type change lands under it, and whether the resulting orphan conditions arrive as flagged buckets (the case above) or never arrive at all. Build the flagged-bucket case regardless, because deleted answers reach it by other routes.
  • D14, the second half. Whether used recommendations also move to the end of the tray, and how the armed state reads on the builder's editor surface, where the ink stand-down re-points the accent. Blocks: nothing in this window on the funnel surface. The band's own order is settled (uncovered first, then covered) and the colours are settled (green not placed, black placed, violet armed). The builder accent question lands with D6's work.
Parked, and what to do meanwhile.
  • D4, diagnostics. The check popover shows findings and opens from the CTA, and that is the whole diagnostics surface in this work. Do not rebuild "Check my logic", the Diagnose modal, "Test a path" or the AI review into the step, and do not add an "N to review" affordance. Leave the shipped app/components/logic/PathTester.tsx and app/components/shared/health/usePathQuality.ts in place and unreferenced from the new step; do not delete them. When diagnostics are built they hang off the popover's footer, so leave that footer able to take rows. "Explore every path" stays builder-only (D19).
  • D6, builder parity. The main builder is being rebuilt, so this work ships the funnel step 3 surface only. Consequences for this window: the style lives on the doc (D1), so it survives graduation and the new builder can read it; keep the band behind the existing flow prop rather than a new funnel-only branch; keep the ⌘Z guard; do not gate the new UI behind ruleFlow === "onboarding" in a way that makes it unreachable later. Name the gap in the handoff to that project: until it lands, a Rules-only quiz opens in today's builder as Filter Results + Rules, and today's builder Logic view still writes rules against the mapping model. That is a known, accepted gap for the duration, not a bug to work around here.

Verification for this window

  • Unit (pure, no DOM): the draft-to-rule mapping for every row shape (is, is not, any of, all of, single-select, multi-select, scale); an untouched edit round-trips byte-identical; a legacy rule with no action stays that way on Show; match: "any" is kept on edit; an untouched mixed-op row is kept verbatim; the normalizeDecisionRule cases of B13, including "all of" dropped from an "is not" row (D12); the impossible all-of predicate (B14) and that it never fires on an "is not" row; the style-aware coverage helper for both styles (B10, B41); restoreDecisionRule restores at the index and no-ops on a live id (D7); a paste line with match: "any" produces N adjacent rules with the same verb and targets and no match (D13); 13 picks go out as batches of 12 and 1 in order (D15).
  • Doc and engine (pure): a doc with no logic_style resolves exactly as today; resolveTarget with logic_style: "rules" ignores a decides role and returns the first matching rule's targets; a matching "Hide" with no base returns null; no matching rule returns null; a legacy doc and a decider doc without the field produce byte-identical results before and after the widening. Round-trip a published legacy doc through parse and save and diff the bytes.
  • Runtime (D1 safety net, the highest-risk class): a Rules-only shopper who matches no rule lands on the decider reveal with the Results step's "Fallback" products; the same for an empty result in Filter Results + Rules; with "Fallback" switched off the result page is the empty state, not a crash and not a different layout. Prove DOM-identical output for a decider doc whose target resolves normally, and for a legacy doc, by rendering on the local build and the pre-change deploy and diffing normalized outerHTML. Then the full e2e, the /q screenshot review, and the byte pin.
  • E2E: rewrite e2e/create-rule-verify.mjs for the D24 layout and both styles. Move its ensure-targets failure case (lines 250-266) to the Add recommendations write. Add: the binding case from B2 (delete rule 1, open another rule while its Undo toast is still up, click Undo, then Save; only the edited rule may change); a keyboard-only create, edit, duplicate, reorder and delete, with the Undo reached from the keyboard; Rules only offering "Show" only while a stored "Pin" rule still opens on "Pin"; an "is not" row showing no join control; the toast never covering the footer. Run it against the local build and fixture per e2e/README.md; local fixture cmr7khgd50001vkhscvox8dgt, deploy fixtures per the same file, and never against the byte-pinned quiz.
  • Embedded (D21): in /app, delete a rule and confirm the toast and its "Undo" appear and work. Before the provider lands the toast is silent, so this test fails for the right reason.
  • Screenshots at 1440×900 and 1280×720, both styles: create and edit; the verb switch in each style; 10 answers on one row (sideways fade); 30 recommendations with "See N more · K picked"; the all-of warning; an "is not" row; the legacy note; the match-any note; Add recommendations stacked; a toast with an "Undo" while the window is open (it must not cover the footer); "Save & add another" landing at the top; a rule row with its controls revealed by keyboard focus. Interactive states need screenshots, not DOM markers: a pointer-trapped overlay renders fine and is unclickable.
  • Gate chain before every commit, unpiped: npm run typecheck && npm test -- --run && npm run build && npm run lint && node scripts/check-tokens.mjs.

The Add recommendations window and the Add a question dialog

Two windows open over the Logic workspace. Add recommendations is new: it adds collections, tags, products or custom groups to the quiz without a trip back to step 1, from the Rules-only strip or from inside the rule window. Add a question is the live AddQuestionDialog, kept as it ships apart from the fixes listed below. LogicTabCard hosts both (LogicTabCard.tsx:536-579), so one implementation serves both logic styles.

Both styles use these windows, and they use them the same way. Rules only and Filter Results + Rules are two ways of deciding results, not a mode and a view of it (D1), so the window's contents, keyboard behaviour, catalogue and write path are identical in both; only which control opens it and which sentence the toast ends with differ. Nothing below is conditional on a decision: every line is the thing to build.

How this section cites things. Code refs are path:line on origin/main (b4aa278) and were re-read against that tree on 2026-09-22. The mock is cited by function and handler name, never by line number, because it is still being edited. The window is arHTML() and drawAR(), with the handlers ACT.addRecs, ACT.arTab, ACT.arTog, ACT.arAdd and ACT.arClose; the dialog is aqHTML(), drawAQ() and aqSync(), with ACT.addq; the Rules-only strip is vizRecs(); the rule window's recommendations band is mrecMoreHTML() and fitTwoRows(); the stand-in catalogue is CATALOG (29 rows: 6 collections, 10 tags, 10 products, 3 custom groups). Three mock fixes landed after the review and are tagged in place; every other defect cited here still reproduces.

What is settled for these two windows

RulingWhat it means hereWhere the rest of it is specified
D1 SettledRules only is its own engine mode, saved on the quiz. The window is style-neutral; the copy around it is not. In Rules only a recommendation reaches a shopper only through a rule, so “needs a rule” is literally true. In Filter Results + Rules a recommendation reaches a shopper through an answer mapping or a rule.Engine semantics, Data model
D3 SettledAdding a recommendation never creates a blocking finding by itself. The style-aware report surfaces an uncovered recommendation, and the Rules-only strip's “N/M have a rule” counter is the in-place version of the same fact.Checks and Continue
D5 SettledNo chooser stands in front of the step, so both entry points are reachable on first entry. The style is resolved from the saved field, then inference, then Filter Results + Rules, and nothing is written on load.Screen shell
D7 SettledThe shared toast gains one optional action, a duration, a live region and keyboard reach, and the missing providers are added. Neither window's own toasts carry an action; they use the extended toast for its duration and its live region.Data model
D14 (colours) SettledA recommendation added from the rule window joins the Filter Results + Rules tray green: it is on no answer yet. Black means placed, violet means armed.Filter Results + Rules, Edit view
D15 Settled“Add” writes through POST /api/categories/ensure-targets, extended with a group kind, tag keys normalized to Step-1 slugs, rows always quiz-scoped, at most 12 resources per call. Full contract below.this section

Parked, and what to do meanwhile.

  • D4 (diagnostics) comes later. Neither window gains a diagnostic affordance. The check popover opens from the CTA and shows findings; do not wire “Check my logic”, the Diagnose modal, “Test a path” or the AI review into either window, and do not add an “N to review” affordance. PathTester and usePathQuality stay in the tree, unreferenced from this step.
  • D6 (builder parity) is handed to the main-builder project, which is being rebuilt. This work ships the funnel step 3 surface. Build both windows as ordinary LogicTabCard children with no ruleFlow === "onboarding" gate around them, so the new builder can mount them unchanged. Until it does, the builder's rule window keeps its live “+ Add something else” catalogue (CreateRuleModal.tsx:912-919, 950-971) and its own raw-tag index (CreateRuleModal.tsx:416-431), and the known gap stands: a Rules-only quiz opens in today's builder as Filter Results + Rules. Name that gap in the handover, do not patch it here.

Layout and controls

The window is 580px wide and at most 640px tall. It has a title row, a pinned tools block (search, then tabs), the list, which is the only part that scrolls, and a pinned footer. Build it on QzModal with width={580} (qz-overlays.tsx:102-104, 145), and use className to cap the height at 640px (the default cap is max-height: 90vh, quizocalypse.css:4296-4305). Map the mock's hex colours to --qz-* tokens so check-tokens passes. B54 also suggests a fixed height rather than a max height, so the search box stays put as results shrink; that is optional.

The list: windowing and order

Render the list in windows, using step 1's picker pattern: a first window, more rows loaded on scroll, and a reset to the top on tab or search change (resetWindow and onListScroll, RecommendationBucketsStage.tsx:446-460). A real shop can have thousands of products and tags, and the funnel's catalogue payload is ungated and uncapped by design, with a budget warning rather than a throw (funnelLoader.server.ts:179-187). The review only ever exercised the mock's 29 stand-in rows.

  • Order inside a kind follows the catalogue feed, which sorts tags and collections by product count and then by label (funnelLoader.server.ts:145-147, 150-157). Products and custom groups follow the loader's order (funnelLoader.server.ts:163-178, 194-199).
  • “In this quiz” rows stay in place; they are never sorted to the bottom or hidden. A merchant looking for something needs to find it and see that it is already there.
  • The list keeps its scroll position across a toggle, and resets to the top on a tab or query change. The mock preserves the scroll (drawAR() saves and restores .arlist's scrollTop) but loses focus; React keeps both by construction once the window stops rebuilding its markup.

Keyboard, focus and stacking

  • Focus. Focus moves into the search on open, and Tab and Shift+Tab stay inside the window. Closing the window (×, Cancel, Esc or Add) returns focus to the control that opened it. useFocusTrap already does all three (qz-overlays.tsx:33-68). It does not make the page inert, though, so set inert on the app shell while the window is open, and on the rule window too when this window sits on top of it. B31 (medium): in the mock, Enter on a rule's trash behind the scrim deleted the rule while the window stayed open.
  • Page scroll. The page behind must not scroll while the window is open (B28). Fixed in mock by the html:has(#modal, #aqm, #addrec) overflow rule. In the product, the inert shell plus a scroll lock on the same container does the same job.
  • Scrim. QzModal closes any non-destructive modal on a scrim mousedown (qz-overlays.tsx:138-141). Add an opt-out prop (for example dismissOnScrim={false}) and pass it here. Don't use destructive for this: it also removes Esc and the × (qz-overlays.tsx:124-125, 150-156). The same prop fixes Add a question (below). The default stays as it is, so other modals don't change.
  • Over the rule window. The window opens above the rule window, and Esc closes it first, keeping the rule draft (the mock's Escape listener tests AR before M; confirmed in the review's rule-window run). On QzModal this already works: its Esc listener runs in the capture phase on document and calls stopPropagation (qz-overlays.tsx:124-134), so the rule window's bubble-phase document listener (CreateRuleModal.tsx:263-272) never sees the key. A bespoke shell must keep that ordering. Cover it in the probe.
  • Modal over modal. The design-system overlay contract allows exactly one stack, a modal over a drawer (qz-overlays.tsx:16-25), and says the design system is amended first when a need does not fit. Amend it in the same dated form D7 uses for the toast's action, and record the amendment next to the contract comment. The conflict and its wording live in The rule window; this window is where the stack actually happens.
  • Portals. Both shells portal to document.body at the modal z-index (120, quizocalypse.css:223; CreateRuleModal.tsx:976-1148), so the window mounted later paints on top. Mount the window as a sibling of CreateRuleModal in LogicTabCard (LogicTabCard.tsx:536-557), or stop propagation at its root: React events bubble from a portal to the handlers of its React parent. When LogicTabCard hosts it, pass the added ids back to the open rule window (a prop or callback) so the rule window can pick them.
  • Toasts. “Added and picked for this rule” appears while the rule window is still open, and must not cover the rule window's footer sentence or buttons (B34, medium). Fixed in mock by placeToast(), which lifts the toast above the footer of the topmost open window. Port the placement: the design-system toast is fixed 28px from the bottom, centred, at z 200 (quizocalypse.css:4406-4415; the z token at 224), so without a placement rule it lands exactly on the rule window's footer. The mock's other half, pointer-events: none, already ships (quizocalypse.css:4413); D7's action button is the one element that needs pointer-events: auto.
  • Keyboard reach for the toast. D7 gives the shared toast one optional action, a duration and keyboard reach. Neither window's toasts carry an action, but they share the component, so the toast must not steal focus when it appears here: it is announced through its live region (role="status" aria-live="polite", qz-toast.tsx:68) and reached by Tab, never focused automatically.

Opened fromEffectToast
The strip (Rules only)The rows join the quiz and show at once as uncovered pills (dashed amber border, “+ Create a rule”), after the pills that were already uncovered. In Filter Results + Rules they also join the tray as green chips: placed on no answer yet (D14).“Added and picked for this rule”, in both styles.
  • Recommendations are written as soon as “Add” is pressed, independently of the rule draft. If the merchant then cancels the rule window, the new recommendations stay in the quiz. That is the same trust boundary the rule window already keeps: the rows ensure-targets creates belong to the quiz, not the draft (CreateRuleModal.tsx:622-624).
  • Lift the returned rows into page state the way the rule window does today: onCategoriesCreated feeds LogicTabCard's extraCats, which merges them with the loader's categories by id (CreateRuleModal.tsx:624; LogicTabCard.tsx:113-115, 136-139, 554). Category writes go through fetch to an API route and trigger no loader revalidation. The loader re-runs only after the next autosave or intent, both of which go through fetchers (useQuizDraft.ts:29, 47-56). Without the lift, the new pills don't appear.
  • Mark a catalogue row “In this quiz” as soon as a lifted row has the same kind and key, so the next open of the window is already correct.
  • If a request fails, keep the window open with the unsent picks still ticked. Rows that did get added now read “In this quiz”. Never clear the selection on failure (CREATE-RULE-HANDOFF.md, “Never reset on failure”; the live equivalent is CreateRuleModal.tsx:614-621, which toasts and returns without touching the draft). Toast copy: “Couldn't reach the server. Nothing was added.” and “Couldn't reach the server. K of N recommendations were added.”
  • If the server skips an item (no products, or no longer in the catalogue), the toast names it: “1 wasn't added: it has no products.” The skip reason comes from the response, never from a client guess.
  • Neither toast carries an Undo. Nothing in step 3 removes a recommendation (see “What this window does not do”), so there is no inverse mutation to offer. D7's action slot stays empty here; the toasts that do carry Undo are the delete, reorder, import and role-change toasts specified in Data model.
  • The embedded /app routes get QzToastProvider as part of this work (D21), so these toasts are heard there. Today the provider is mounted only on the three standalone routes (studio.tsx:31, studio_.$id.tsx:117, studio_.onboarding_.$quizId.tsx:38), while the embedded twins render the same components without one (app.onboarding_.$quizId.tsx:39-47; app.quizzes.$id_.studio.tsx:45-56) and the default context is a no-op (qz-toast.tsx:31). Add the provider to both embedded routes and nothing else: the hardcoded /studio links and giving embedded decider quizzes the new Logic view are separate tasks.

// The client feed, identical on both surfaces
type LogicCatalogRow = {
  kind: "collection" | "tag" | "product" | "group";
  key: string;   // collection id · tag slug · product id · shop-global Category id
  label: string; // collection title · first raw tag label · product title · group name
  count: number; // products (1 for a product)
};
type LogicCatalog = { rows: LogicCatalogRow[]; inQuizKeys: string[] }; // "kind:key"

How new recommendations are written (D15)

“Add” writes through the existing POST /api/categories/ensure-targets, extended. It is additive and idempotent, it works on any surface that can reach the API route, and its rows survive re-grouping. The endpoint today accepts the kinds tag | collection | product | metafield (api.categories.ensure-targets.tsx:26-32) and 1 to 12 resources per call (35-38), after checking that the shop owns the quiz (61-65). For each resource it reuses a row of this quiz first, then a shop-global row (83-95). Otherwise it creates a quiz row whose members come from resolveMembership, stamped with discoveryRunId logic-tab-<quizId> (96-117). It returns the rows in input order (120-132). Only the rule window calls it today (CreateRuleModal.tsx:596-629).

TabKey the window sendsRow the server writesReused when a row of this quiz has
CollectionsCollection idsource collection, sourceRef = id, name = collection title, productIds = its productssource collection or smart_collection and the same id
TagsStep-1 slugsource tag, sourceRef = the slug the resolver matched, named the way step 1 names it (bucketPersist.ts:73-84; categoryGrouping.ts:180-185), members resolved by slugsource tag and a sourceRef that normalizes to the slug
ProductsProduct idsource product, sourceRef = id, name = title, productIds = [id]source product and the same id
Custom groups NewShop-global Category idsource group, sourceRef = that id, name, tags and productIds copied as a snapshot (bucketPersist.ts:62-72)source group and the same id

The changes to make, all additive:

  • Add the kind. ResourceSchema.kind gains "group" (api.categories.ensure-targets.tsx:29). The shop check is inherent: loadBucketInputs only loads groups where { shopId, quizId: null } (bucketPersist.server.ts:43-50), so an id that is not this shop's shop-global group resolves to nothing and is refused.
  • Stop trusting the client's name. The client sends the kind and the key; the server resolves membership and the name. That is step 1's trust boundary (bucketPersist.ts:8-15). name is required today (api.categories.ensure-targets.tsx:31) and written straight onto the row (107); keep accepting the field so the shipped caller is not broken mid-deploy, and ignore it for every kind the resolver can name.
  • Use step 1's resolver. Build rows with bucketRowFor over loadBucketInputs (bucketPersist.ts:48-85; bucketPersist.server.ts:35-59) instead of the inline resolveMembership call (api.categories.ensure-targets.tsx:96-102), so a key added in Logic and the same key added on step 1 produce the same row. This is what makes slug tags work: resolveMembership matches tag strings exactly (groupMembership.ts:62-79), so the slug dry-skin finds nothing on a shop whose tag is “Dry Skin”, while step 1's path normalizes both sides (categoryGrouping.ts:143-162) and matches.
  • Keep the metafield branch as it is. BucketType has no metafield (bucketPersist.ts:21-22), so metafield resources keep resolving through resolveMembership for the builder's rule window. This window offers no Metafields tab.
  • Reuse quiz rows only. Drop the { quizId: null } branch from the reuse lookup (api.categories.ensure-targets.tsx:83-91). A reused shop-global row has quizId null, so it never shows in the strip, the tray or the band (LogicQuestionWidget.tsx:155-172), and the merchant would see “Added” with nothing added.
  • Refuse empty or missing items. bucketRowFor returns null for them (bucketPersist.ts:59, 64, 75). Return the reason rather than writing an empty row.
  • Response. Return one result per input resource, in input order: { kind, ref, category } or { kind, ref, skipped: reason }. Keep categories as the successful rows so the existing lift keeps working (CreateRuleModal.tsx:624), but move the positional mapping of targets onto the new results (CreateRuleModal.tsx:625-628 maps j.categories[i] by index today), so one skip cannot shift a rule's targets by one.
  • Batches. The client sends at most 12 resources per call, since the schema rejects 13 or more (api.categories.ensure-targets.tsx:35-38). It sends one call at a time and lifts each batch as it lands, so a 20-row selection becomes two calls and two lifts.
  • Double submits. The reuse-then-create step runs outside a transaction, and Category has no unique key on (quizId, source, sourceRef), only two indexes (prisma/schema.prisma:216-217). A second submit can therefore create a duplicate row. Keep the primary disabled while a call runs.
  • Every row keeps quizId = this quiz (api.categories.ensure-targets.tsx:106) and discoveryRunId logic-tab-<quizId> (114). That stamp is load-bearing: it is what makes these rows survive step 1's destructive writes.
Never call step 1's intents (toggle-bucket, select-all, clear-visible, set-buckets, create-group) from Logic.
  • addBuckets deletes and recreates the row for a key (step1Build.server.ts:106-120). The Category id changes, and every answer and rule that pointed at the old id dangles.
  • toggle-bucket off and clear-visible delete by (source, sourceRef) with no logic-tab guard (step1Build.server.ts:123-133; funnelIntents.server.ts:227-229, 253-255), so they also delete rows that Logic added.
  • set-buckets and create-group write back the doc the server loaded at request start (funnelIntents.server.ts:323, 373), which races the autosave.
  • They exist only on the funnel route and take one type per call. The builder has no funnel route, so a Logic surface built on them could never be reused there.
  • Re-grouping keeps these rows. Rows stamped logic-tab-<quizId> survive a re-group (persistConfirmedGroups, step1Build.server.ts:58-66), clearBuckets, which is an Apply over an empty selection (147-151), and Apply or Revert through set-buckets (isLogicTabTarget and setBucketsLeaverIds, bucketPersist.ts:193-212).
  • Step 1 sees them. Collection, tag, product and group rows show up as picks on step 1's shelf (funnelLoader.server.ts:223-236). Turning one off there, or “Clear all” (clear-visible), deletes it. Step 1 warns before a single toggle-off only when a question or rule already references the row (RecommendationBucketsStage.tsx:304-313).

What this window does not do

  • No removal in Logic. Nothing in step 3 removes a recommendation: the only Category call the Logic surfaces make is ensure-targets (CreateRuleModal.tsx:605), the mock has no remove action, and D16 makes the Recommendations sheet read-only. Removal happens on the Recommendations step. This is a deliberate one-way door for now, not an oversight; it is also why the “Added” toasts carry no Undo. Not covered by the rulings: whether step 3 should gain a remove path at all.
  • Personas. The quiz copy of a group carries no membership (step1Build.server.ts:88-101, which writes no membership field), and publish reads a persona from the target row's membership (quizPublish.ts:25-32, 544-548). A group added here therefore reveals without its persona, exactly like one added on step 1. Fixing that means changing what step 1's resolver copies, which is a step-1-wide change and out of scope here.
  • Metafield recommendations. Rows the old rule window wrote for metafields belong to the quiz but never show on step 1's shelf, because BROWSER_SOURCES has no metafield (funnelLoader.server.ts:223-225). They still show in the strip and the band, which read every quiz-scoped row.
  • Products that aren't live. The catalogue carries each product's status (funnelCatalogPayload.ts:44, 52-55), and step 1 filters on it: a Status control defaulting to Active, a selected row always kept whatever the filter, and a footer ledger naming what is hidden (statusKeeps and ledgerHidden, bucketSelection.ts:99-109, 173-182; RecommendationBucketsStage.tsx:127, 425-427, 835-845). The mock has no rule here and the rulings do not cover it. Reusing those two helpers is a few lines whichever way it goes; get the owner's answer before wiring the control, and until then list what the feed returns.

Add a question Exists

Decided (owner ruling 2026-09-16, recorded at AddQuestionDialog.tsx:5-19). “+ Add question” opens the live AddQuestionDialog, the one dialog shared with the Questions step. It collects the type, the question and the answers, and nothing else. Role, required, mapping and images happen on the question once it exists.

Entry point and what the host does

  • “+ Add question” is a dashed button under the last question in the Filter Results + Rules rail (mock railItems()). It is live today (LogicQuestionWidget.tsx:226-230, wired at LogicTabCard.tsx:503). Rules only has no entry point for it, because that screen shows no question rail (D23); a Rules-only quiz gets its questions from the Questions step, and its rules then reference their answers. That is a difference in what each screen shows, not a difference in what each style can do.
  • On submit the host commits appendBankQuestion as one commit through useQuizDraft. The new question has no role, so it reads “Info only” (LogicTabMenus.tsx:449-460), and required: true. Its text is cut to 150 characters, it keeps at most 12 answers of at most 60 characters, and it gets fresh answer ids and edge handles (questionMutations.ts:127-159).

The rail's role counts update. Today LogicTabCard only commits and closes (LogicTabCard.tsx:568-579). The card owns the selection (LogicTabCard.tsx:133-135), so it can select directly.
  • The toast is heard on the embedded routes once they have the provider (D21).
  • When the dialog closes, focus returns to “+ Add question”; useFocusTrap restores it (qz-overlays.tsx:63-66).
The dialog has no Min or Max. A multi-select's limits are set on the new question's type line once it exists. The owner asked for “multi select with min / max req” on Sep-18, and the type line is where the mock put it. Confirm with the owner that nobody expects Min and Max inside the dialog.

Where the new question lands Conflict

The mock appends the new question after the last one (ACT.aqadd). appendBankQuestion instead splices it after the last node of straightThroughRun (questionMutations.ts:135-136, 158), and that run stops at the first node that branches, merges or fans out (questionMutations.ts:311-343, specifically the inTo and outOf guards at 335-337). Every route other than “The next question” adds an edge on that answer's handle (setAnswerRoute, edgeMutations.ts:96-128). So once any answer has its own route, the new question lands in front of that answer's question. A probe ran the origin/main mutations on intro → Q1 → Q2 → Q3 → result:

Doc stateWhere the new question lands
No routesQ4 of 4 (last)
Q3, answer A → “Straight to the results”Q3, in front of the old Q3
Q2, answer A → “Straight to the results”Q2
Q1, answer A → Q3Q1, the first question

Requirement. Land the new question after the last question on the quiz's main path (the one reached by following the default, handle-less edges from the intro), and keep every per-answer route. spliceQuestion already rewires only handle-less edges (questionMutations.ts:11-49, at 19 and 35). Gate the new anchor rule on logic_model === "decider": QuestionBankDrawer appends through the same mutation (QuestionBankDrawer.tsx:55-63), and legacy docs must keep today's result (CLAUDE.md, dual-model rule). Unit-test all four cases above, in both gate states.

  • The toast changes are the shared component's (D7): one optional action, a duration, keyboard reach, and the dated owner exception recorded against the “no actions” rule in the contract comment at qz-toast.tsx:13-17. Keep the queue-of-one reducer and its exported test seam (nextToastState, qz-toast.tsx:21-29).
