Table view, Export and Import

New The Table view shows the quiz's logic as editable sheets. "Export" writes the same sheets to quiz-logic.xlsx, which is also the template a merchant fills in, and "Import" applies an edited copy back as one change. None of this exists on origin/main: there is no Table view, no import or export code, and no spreadsheet library. The only related dependency is papaparse (package.json:50,56), which runs server-side for the manual catalogue (app/lib/catalog.server.ts:2,12-13). app/components/studio/LogicTableTab.tsx is an unrelated orphan (a per-result paths grid) that is kept on purpose (docs/design/logic-tab/DECISIONS.md:77-78). Do not reuse it and do not delete it.

Both logic styles get the Table, Export and Import, and they get them as equals. Rules only and Filter Results + Rules are two ways this product decides a result (D1), so neither one is a view of the other: the header, the view control, the file, the import contract, the toasts and the keyboard rules are the same in both. They differ only in which sheets there are to show, because a Rules-only quiz has no answer mappings for a sheet to carry.

What is settled for this section. The logic style lives on the quiz document through publish, and in Rules only the first matching rule's recommendations are the result (D1). One style-aware Tier-1 report feeds the row markers, the Recommendations sheet's Status column, the CTA and publish (D3). No first-entry chooser: the style is resolved, never written on load (D5). The shared toast gains one optional action, and every Undo in this section is built from inverse mutations against the latest document, never a whole-document snapshot (D7). A Picks move made from the Table or from Import announces what it cleared and offers Undo (D9). Rule rows carry click-to-edit, a trash and keyboard reorder; Duplicate is not on the row, it lives in the rule window (D11). "is not" and "all of" cannot combine, in the grammar and in Import (D12). A cross-question "or" is never created by a paste, and the file reads and writes the ones already stored (D13). Recommendations created from this surface go through ensure-targets, extended with a "group" kind, and the rows it returns are always quiz-scoped, so the Recommendations sheet lists them (D15). The file carries identity as well as text: "Qn = answer" in every When cell, a do-not-edit "Answer ID" column and a "Rule ID" column, the Answers sheet updating answers in place, the Recommendations sheet read-only, a missing column meaning "leave unchanged", and SheetJS CE 0.20.3 as a lazy chunk (D16). Export is the template: on a quiz with no rules it still writes the headers, the id columns and one example row (D16 template). Sentences stay verb-first in the rule lists; the Table and the file always use "Q7 = Yes" (D17). The renames land through shared constants (D18). The live surfaces the mock does not draw are kept (D19). The embedded twins get the missing toast provider (D21). Build all of it.

What this section relies on, and what it must not touch

  • The style is a field on the document (D1). Quiz.logic_style is added next to logic_model, optional and never .default(), and publish keeps it (section data-model-and-mutations). It replaces the draft-only field the funnel writes today, build_session.logic_style (app/lib/quizSchema.ts:1708), which only the set-logic-style intent writes (app/lib/funnelIntents.server.ts:1468-1480) and which publish strips with the rest of build_session (app/lib/quizPublish.ts:789,804). Two consequences land here. The resolver reads the document field first and the draft-only field second, so a quiz that picked a style before the field existed opens on the right sheets. And because the style is document content, it rides the same autosave PUT as everything else this screen writes, where build_session could not: the JSON autosave keeps the server's session and ignores the client's (funnelIntents.server.ts:124-132).
  • Nothing in this section is a runtime change. The Rules-only engine branch and the shared safety net for a shopper no rule matches are specified in section engine-semantics, and they carry the runtime proof rules there: legacy quizzes byte-identical, the full e2e, screenshot review and the byte pin. The Table, Export and Import touch the admin surface and the document only. They still ride the same document into publish, so they must write nothing the engine reads beyond the question nodes, their edges and decision_rules: Import never writes logic_style, build_session, results settings or design, and the sheets carry no style cell.
  • The report is one report (D3). The row markers and the Recommendations sheet's Status column read the same style-aware Tier-1 report as the CTA, the check popover and publish, so a sheet can never read safer than the gate. This section consumes it and never computes its own version (section checks-and-continue).

One sheet model for the Table, the file and the import diff

Build one pure module, app/lib/logicSheets.ts. From the doc, the recommendation list and the catalogue read-out it builds sheet models: the sheet name, the columns, the file column widths, and rows whose cells carry both the display text and the ids behind them. The Table renders these models, Export writes them, and Import compares a workbook with them. That is how the mock keeps the Table and the file identical: one sheets() function feeds both tableHTML() and buildWorkbook(). Keep that property.

  • The module never imports the spreadsheet library. It reads and writes a plain shape (sheets of string rows plus workbook properties). A thin adapter in LogicImportExport converts that shape to and from SheetJS, so the library stays swappable and logicSheets.test.ts runs without it.
  • The module takes the resolved style as an argument, never a global. One call site resolves it once through the shared helper (the document field, else build_session.logic_style, else inference, else Filter Results + Rules; D5, section header-and-shell), and passes it down to the sheets, the Table and Import. There is no chooser and no write on arrival: opening the Table, like opening the step, resolves the style and writes nothing (D5).
  • Table only: the trash and reorder controls, row markers, colours, bold joins, and the question-level cells, which show on the first row of each question only.
  • File only: joins in capitals; Q, Question, Type and What it does repeated on every Answers row (the mock writes them on every row in sheets()); the trailing ID columns; and the example row on a quiz with no rules.
  • Every Q number is the orderedQuestions number that the rail, the rule sentences and the check popover use (app/lib/questionOrder.ts:13-48).
  • Rule condition text comes from the one shared describer, describeRuleConditions (app/lib/ruleSummary.ts:11-29), extended with grouping and "not (...)" (D17, section filter-edit-view). The rule rows, the Table cell and the export all call it, with their own fmt. Nothing in this section writes its own condition formatter.

Table view

  • The Table replaces the Edit body. The status header stays: the title switch, the description, the outlined [Import | Export] pair and Edit | Table (section header-and-shell). "Paste rules" and "Create a rule" do not show in Table view (mock headRight()).
  • Filter Results + Rules shows the Rules sheet, then the Answers sheet. Rules only shows the Rules sheet, then the Recommendations sheet (mock sheets()). The order is fixed: rules first in both styles.
  • There are no sheet headings and no row counts: the column headers say what each sheet is (owner, 2026-09-18; B39 was rejected as deliberate). Give each <table> an aria-label with its sheet name so screen readers can tell them apart. The mock's .tsheet-h CSS is dead (B68).
  • An empty sheet shows one full-width row, "Nothing yet" (mock tableHTML()). In Rules only with no rules, the Recommendations sheet still lists every recommendation as "Needs a rule", and each of those rows opens "Create a rule", so the empty Table is not a dead end.
  • There is no create control in the Table (B39 rejected as deliberate). New rules come from "Needs a rule" rows (Rules only) or from the Edit view. The Filter Results + Rules Table has no rule-creation path, by design.
  • Switching the style from the title switch lands on Edit (section header-and-shell). The Table does not try to keep the view across a style change, because the sheets underneath it change.
  • Look (mock CSS in the .tview, .tsheet, .xl and .tdel blocks): sheets stacked 18px apart inside 14px 20px 20px padding. Each table sits in a 1px border with the 6px radius and scrolls sideways inside its wrapper when it is too wide; a wrapper that scrolls gets tabindex="0" so keyboard users can scroll it. Text is 13px/1.4. The header row is 11.5px/700 on the inset wash, no wrap. Cells are padded 7px 10px, top-aligned, with hairline separators, and the first row of each question gets a stronger top rule. Clickable rows tint on hover. Sizes are the mock's 100% sizes (D20, section layout-and-sizing).
  • Colours come from Quartz tokens, never hex in .tsx (scripts/check-tokens.mjs:4-7): --qz-cream-2 for the header wash, --qz-rule and --qz-rule-2 for borders and hairlines, --qz-accent-ink for verbs and Picks, --qz-ok for Narrows and "Has a rule", --qz-warn for "(not set)" and "Needs a rule", --qz-ink-4 for Info and dim cells. Recommendation names use the mock's blue (--res), which has no Quartz token on origin/main: the :root token block (app/styles/quizocalypse.css:44-237) has no blue, and --qz-pal-blue points at the violet accent (quizocalypse.css:139). Add a token in the stylesheet and share it with the rule-sentence chips.
  • Words come from the shared constants (D18): "Picks results", "Narrows", "Info only", "Recommendations", "Create a rule", "Choose a result". Internal words never reach a cell, a header, a tooltip or a toast: decider, bucket, branch, boost, weight, score. That includes the placeholder ruleSummary uses today, "(deleted bucket)" (app/lib/ruleSummary.ts:46), which this surface writes as "(deleted recommendation)". The Table's role cell reads the same constants as the pane, so the rename reaches the builder's Rules inspector and the tests that pin the old words in the same commit (section filter-edit-view).
  • Inline text cells show the field save pill at the edited field only; the ambient funnel chrome stays silent while saving is healthy (D8, section inline-editing-and-save-pill).

  • Markers. Each row shows the same tags, with the same wording, as the Edit rule lists: "never runs · rule N catches them first" (B15 Fixed in mock: the tag stays at full contrast and only the sentence dims), "answer deleted" and "recommendation deleted" (B8, B9 Fixed in mock), "can never match" for an impossible all-of (B14 Fixed in mock), and "(no answers)" for a half-built rule, which never fires (app/lib/pathAnalyzer.ts:180-188). They come from the same analyzer calls as the lists (app/lib/pathAnalyzer.ts:151-299, extended per section engine-semantics) and from the one style-aware report (D3), never from a Table-only computation, so a row can never read safer than the publish gate. Markers are not written to the file.
  • Reordering. "Move rule N up" and "Move rule N down" commit moveDecisionRule (app/lib/mutations/deciderMutations.ts:263-274), which is priority order, and keep focus on the moved row's button so a run of presses walks the rule up the list. The first row's up button and the last row's down button are disabled. A move toasts "Moved to position N · Undo", N being the final 1-based position, and the Undo moves that rule id back to its previous index, the same copy and the same inverse the Edit rows use (D7, section rules-only-edit-view). The Table's rows are not drag sources: in the Table, reordering is the two buttons. Drag belongs to the Rules-only Edit rows, where the grip is, and the mock's Table rows are not draggable either.
  • Trash. Faint until the row is hovered or focused, then crit colour, wash and border. Accessible name "Delete rule N". It must not also open the rule. It deletes through the same path as the Edit lists: removeDecisionRule by id (deciderMutations.ts:256-261), no confirm, toast "Rule N deleted · Undo" whose Undo calls restoreDecisionRule(doc, rule, index) against the latest doc (D7; both the mutation and the toast action are new, section data-model-and-mutations). Deletes made while the toast is still up accumulate into one entry: the toast reads "2 rules deleted · Undo" and the Undo calls restoreDecisionRules with the entries in reverse, which rebuilds the original order (B35 Fixed in mock). Today's ledger deletes by id and toasts "Rule deleted" with no Undo (app/components/studio/logicTab/LogicTabCard.tsx:463-471). After a delete, focus moves to the next row's "Edit rule" button, or to the toast's Undo when the last row went (B30).
  • The When cell updates while an answer is being typed anywhere (Answers sheet or Edit pane), because every view reads the one doc.

In Rules only the verb test is "not Hide", because the first matching rule's recommendations are the result (D1). Today's ruleCoverage counts every rule that targets a Category row, whatever its verb and whatever its state (app/components/studio/logicTab/createRuleBand.ts:23-33): that is the B10 defect in the live code, so do not feed the sheet from it unchanged.

  • A "Needs a rule" row has a real button in its first cell with the accessible name "Create a rule for <name>". The row click calls the same action, and Enter or Space on the button works too. It opens "Create a rule" with that recommendation already picked (the new initialTargetIds prop, section rule-window). "Has a rule" rows are inert.
  • Recommendations added from the rule window or the strip reach this sheet as soon as they exist, because ensure-targets always creates a quiz-scoped row (D15) and the caller lifts the returned rows into local state until the loader revalidates (CreateRuleModal.tsx:622-624; app/routes/api.categories.ensure-targets.tsx:26-38,100-116). Import never creates a recommendation: it resolves names against the rows this surface already loaded.
  • The sheet is read-only in the file. Import reports edits to it and never applies them (B36, D16).

One row per answer of every question, in rail order. Every question has at least one answer (app/lib/quizSchema.ts:219), so every question gets a row. The question-level cells (Q, Question, Type, What it does) show on the question's first row only.

  • The announced Picks move (D9). Promoting a question from this cell runs the one helper that the role menu, this cell and Import all call (section filter-edit-view, list item 2). It runs moveDecider, which clears both questions' answer targets (deciderMutations.ts:187-238), counts what it cleared, and returns the message and the inverse. The toast names the loss, for example "Q3 now picks the result. Q1's 6 recommendations were removed", and its Undo restores both roles, every target and the required flag the promote sets. No confirm dialog. Today three surfaces reimplement the promote and two of them toast without naming the loss (LogicTabMenus.tsx:465-477, QuestionWindow.tsx:470-479, QuestionSection.tsx:173).
  • No hidden selection changes (B40). The Table passes each row's question to the shared controls. RouteMenuButton and QuestionRoleControl already take the question as a prop (LogicTabMenus.tsx:305-319,416-438), so opening, cancelling or committing a Table popover never writes the Edit view's selected question. The mock routes Table popovers through the Edit selection, which is the B40 defect.
  • Same writes as Edit. Every cell calls the mutation the Edit view calls, through the same commit. Because both views read one doc, a switch to Edit shows every Table edit, and the reverse.
  • Read-only where Edit has no control. If the Edit view offers no control for a field, the Table cell is plain text. For example, a freeform question cannot pick the result (LogicTabMenus.tsx:447).
  • Then reads the truth (B64). Resolve the label the way the pane's route label does, walking past content steps to the next question or the results (LogicQuestionWidget.tsx:1275-1300). An answer on the last question with no route of its own therefore reads "Straight to results", because that is where it goes. The mock always writes "Next question" for an unset route (nextText).
  • A route that bypasses the picking question is a blocking finding in Filter Results + Rules (D3), not a refusal: the cell writes it and the report reports it, so the merchant can see the whole picture in one place. Rules only has no picking question, so that check does not run there (D3).
  • Keyboard: Tab reaches every cell control in reading order. Each button exposes aria-haspopup and aria-expanded and names its row ("Q3 answer B goes to: Next question"). Popovers follow the global overlay rules (section header-and-shell; B27 to B29).

Export

  • "Export" is the right half of the outlined [Import | Export] pair. Its title reads as both jobs, because the file it writes is the template: "Download the current logic as an Excel file, the same file Import accepts" (D16 template; the title is the shell section's copy, keep the two in step). One affordance, one format, no second "Download template" button. It shows in Table view only, in both styles, and is always visible. The Rules-only empty state points a merchant here (section rules-only-edit-view), so this button is the only route to the template. The mock hides it unless the artifact downloads capability loaded (headRight(), DL); that capability is not part of the product.
  • On click: disable the button, load the library chunk, build the workbook from the logicSheets models of the latest doc, and download quiz-logic.xlsx as a normal browser download (a Blob, an object URL and an anchor with download; revoke the URL afterwards). Re-enable the button in finally, then toast "Exported quiz-logic.xlsx", or "Exported quiz-logic.xlsx with one example row" when the quiz had no rules.
  • Keep "export in progress" in React state that drives the disabled prop, so the button stays disabled across re-renders and view switches, and style the disabled state visibly (B37). The mock disables only the node that was clicked, and any re-render brings back an enabled button.
  • If the library chunk fails to load: "Couldn't load the Excel writer. Check your connection and try again". Clear the cached loader promise so the next click retries, as the mock does in loadXLSX. A tab left open across a deploy can fail the same way, because the old chunk file is gone. Any other failure needs new copy (proposed: "Couldn't export the file. Try again"). The mock's "A save is already waiting for you" and "Export isn't available here" belong to the downloads capability; drop them.
  • The workbook has one sheet per Table sheet, in the same order and with the same rows, named Rules, Answers and Recommendations. Column widths in characters: Rules 5/14/26/80, Recommendations 24/10/16/14, Answers 5/52/22/36/14/34/20 (mock sheets()), plus 18 for each ID column.
  • Write text as text cells, never formulas, so an answer that starts with "=" stays text in Excel. Only "#" and Products are numbers.
  • Export as the template (D16 template). On a quiz with no rules the Rules sheet is still written: the header row, then one example row so a merchant who wants to build in a spreadsheet has the format in front of them. The example row's cells are drawn from this quiz's own vocabulary, so it resolves if the merchant keeps it: "#" is 1, "What happens" is "Show", "Recommendations" is the first recommendation's exact name, "When they answer" is "Q1 = " plus the exact text of Q1's first answer, and "Rule ID (don't edit)" is the reserved word EXAMPLE. With no recommendations or no questions to draw from, those two cells read "Your recommendation name" and "Q1 = your answer text". The marker sits in the Rule ID column because the sheet has no reason column and because the ID column is the only one whose contents Import reads as identity; nothing new is added to the format. The D16-template ruling asks for the row to be "commented in the reason column"; there is no such column in this contract, and this is where the comment goes instead. Every other section says it this way. Import skips a row whose Rule ID is EXAMPLE, whatever its capitalisation, and notes it (below). A quiz that already has rules gets no example row.
  • Verify the download on the embedded funnel (/app/onboarding/:quizId, which renders inside the Shopify admin, app/routes/app.onboarding_.$quizId.tsx:39-46). A sandboxed iframe can block downloads.

The file contract (D16)

  • Why every answer carries its question (B3). The mock qualifies only scale answers (ansText) and resolves bare text to the first question that has it (findAnswer()). Quizzes repeat "Yes", "No" and "Not sure", so an unchanged file moved a rule from Q7 to Q6.
  • Why the file carries ids (D16). Text alone cannot tell two answers with the same words apart, and it cannot survive a rename made in the app between the export and the import. The id columns are the row keys; the text stays in the file because the text is what a merchant edits. The columns are labelled "(don't edit)" and Import treats an unknown or repeated id as a bad row rather than guessing.
  • Why Narrows values carry their kind. The mock's labels cannot tell a metafield from a variant option with the same name (both read "Size · 30 ml") or a tag from a product type (both read "Serum"). The live chips keep the field separately from the label (LogicQuestionWidget.tsx:1232-1273), and the runtime matches metafield keys and option names with their exact stored casing (ValuePickerPopover.tsx:24-27). The file therefore writes the kind and the stored key.
  • Placeholders exist so every row the Table shows can be written. They survive an import only in a cell nobody changed. The existing ruleSummary uses "(deleted question)", "(deleted answer)" and "(deleted bucket)" (app/lib/ruleSummary.ts:42-46); never write "bucket" in merchant copy (D18). The "—" in "Shown by rules" and in Info cells is the design's empty-cell mark, not a sentence dash; keep it as drawn.
  • Stale-file guard New. Export also stores the ordered question ids as a custom document property of the workbook (SheetJS Custprops), which merchants do not see. If the property is present at import and the quiz's questions were added, removed or reordered since, nothing is applied, and the toast reads "Your questions changed since this file was exported. Export again, then redo your edits." (proposed copy). Pin the round-trip in a unit test; if the library drops the property on read, keep the guard to the id columns and the strict "Qn = text" resolution below, and do not invent a second carrier for it. A CSV cannot carry the property at all, so for CSV the id columns and the strict resolution are the only protection.

Import: reading the file

  • "Import" is the left half of the pair, with the title "Apply changes from a spreadsheet", and shows in Table view only, in both styles. It opens a hidden file input with accept=".xlsx,.xls,.csv". Clear the input's value before each open so choosing the same file again still fires. Cancelling the chooser does nothing. Import is disabled while a file is being read or applied.
  • Refuse files over 1 MB before reading them (proposed copy: "That file is too big to be a quiz logic sheet"). The mock's sample quiz exports at about 19 KB (measured during the mock review). Cap the rows read per sheet too, for example 2,000 with SheetJS's sheetRows read option.
  • Decoding (B26). Check the first bytes. "PK" (xlsx), D0 CF (xls) and a UTF-16 byte-order mark (FF FE or FE FF) go to the library as binary. Everything else is text: decode it with new TextDecoder("utf-8", { fatal: true }), which also drops a UTF-8 byte-order mark, fall back to windows-1252 only when that throws, then parse the text as CSV. Do not pass codepage 65001 instead: it breaks UTF-16 CSVs and makes windows-1252 files worse (B26). The mock hands raw CSV bytes to the library in importFile(), which reads a UTF-8 file without a BOM as Latin-1.
  • Read values only (no formulas, no HTML). Read rows as arrays (header: 1), never as objects keyed by header text, and use Map for lookups, so a crafted header cannot pollute object prototypes.
  • Errors: the library chunk failing to load gives "Couldn't load the spreadsheet reader. Check your connection and try again"; an unreadable file gives "Couldn't read that file" (mock importFile()). Neither changes anything.
  • Sheets are recognized by their headers, never by sheet name (case-insensitive, spaces collapsed): Rules has "what happens" and "when they answer"; Answers has "answer" and "shows / keeps"; Recommendations has "recommendation" and "status". Columns are found by header text in any order.
  • Nothing is ignored silently (B36). Report these in the toast notes: a sheet that is not recognized ("Ignored sheet “Sheet2”: it isn't a Rules or Answers sheet"); two sheets of the same kind (neither applies); a Recommendations sheet that differs from what Export would write ("Recommendations sheet is read-only, so edits there were ignored"); an extra column; the template row ("Ignored the example row"). A file with no Rules or Answers sheet changes nothing (proposed copy: "Couldn't find a Rules or Answers sheet in that file").
  • Import applies every recognized sheet whatever the current style, and says what that means. A Rules-only quiz has no Answers sheet in its own export, so an Answers sheet there came from a file exported under the other style or built by hand. Apply it: question text, answer text and routes matter in both styles, and switching styles is lossless by design, so the role and Shows / keeps columns are stored and kept, not stripped. Because the Rules-only engine ignores roles and answer mappings (D1), add the note "This quiz decides by rules, so the roles and results on the Answers sheet were saved but don't change what shoppers see" whenever such a cell was applied. Never drop the edit silently and never rewrite the style.

Import: what counts as an edit

  • Base doc. Apply against the latest doc at the moment of applying (the getLatestDoc() pattern, CreateRuleModal.tsx:637-640), not the doc from when the button was clicked. Reading the file and loading the library are both asynchronous.
  • Cell-level diff. Serialize the base doc with logicSheets. A file cell equal to what Export would write now is unchanged: it is never parsed and never written. This makes several guarantees hold by construction: an unchanged export imports as "Nothing changed" (B3, B25); half-built and broken rules round-trip exactly as stored, because their placeholder cells are unchanged (B23); a legacy action-less rule stays action-less unless its "What happens" cell changed; a stored "Pin" or "Hide" survives an import made while the quiz is Rules only; and an answer renamed only on the Answers sheet does not invalidate the Rules sheet, whose unchanged When cells keep the stored answer ids.
  • The file wins. If the quiz was edited in the app after the export, the cells that now differ are applied as edits. The toast counts them and Undo takes them back.
  • "Qn" in the Q column and in "Qn =" resolves against the base doc's numbering, before anything is applied.

Import: apply order and parity with the in-app controls

Apply phase by phase across the whole file, never row by row, so the outcome does not depend on row order:

  1. Recommendations sheet: compare only, and note edits.
  2. Answers sheet, question-level cells for every question: What it does, then Type, then Question.
  3. Answers sheet, answer cells: Answer text, then Shows / keeps, then Then.
  4. Rules sheet. It sees the renamed answers, the new types and the new selection limits.
  5. Run Quiz.safeParse on the result, then commit once (below).

Answers sheet

  • Row matching (B4). Match rows by Answer ID. A row with an unknown or repeated ID, or whose Q does not match its answer's question, is skipped and reported. Without the ID column, match by Q plus the exact answer text. Leftover rows and answers of one question pair up in order only when there are equally many of each (a rename in place); otherwise they are skipped and reported. Never pair by row position: the mock writes the Nth "Q1" row onto Q1's Nth answer (applyImport()), so deleting one row rewired every later answer. Duplicate answer texts on one question can only be told apart with the ID column.
  • Import never adds, deletes or reorders answers (D16). Report instead: "Q1 · “Shinyy”: no such answer on Q1; import doesn't add answers", "Q1: 1 answer isn't in the file; import doesn't delete answers", and "Answer order can't be changed by import" when rows were reordered.
  • Question-level cells sit on every row of the question in the file. A change applies when every changed row of that question agrees; if rows disagree, the cell is skipped with a reason. The mock reads them from the first row only (applyImport()).
  • Text. setQuestionText and setAnswerText (trim, collapse spaces). A blank cell, a question over 150 characters and an answer over 60 characters are skipped and reported, never truncated. Text is required (quizSchema.ts:102,209), and an empty text would make the autosave fail.
  • What it does. Accept "Picks results", "Picks the result", "Narrows", "Narrows results" and "Info only", in any case. "Picks results" runs the announced Picks move helper (D9), so the same clearing, the same named toast and the same inverse serve the role menu, the Table and Import; the count goes into the import notes instead of a toast of its own, for example "Q3 now picks the result. Q1's 6 recommendations were removed". "Narrows" runs setQuestionRole(…, "filter") and takes the values the file gives: no AttributePickerDialog, no guessed values. "Info only" runs setQuestionRole(…, "qualifier"), which leaves targets in place (deciderMutations.ts:15-51). If more than one row asks for "Picks results", none of them applies ("Only one question can pick the result"). moveDecider refuses a freeform question (deciderMutations.ts:192). The mock demotes the old picking question without clearing its targets, which is B24.
  • Type. Accept only what the Question type popover offers: Single select, Multi-select · pick a–b, Five-point scale, Scale · 1–N, and Image select only when it already is the type (TypeChipSelector.tsx:30-36,169-174). A hyphen is read as the en dash. Apply through changeQuestionType, the same wrapper the popover uses: leaving multi-select converts that question's all-of rules to any-of, adds the note "Rules on Qn now match any of their answers", and clears min and max. Multi-select limits follow the steppers, 1 ≤ a ≤ b ≤ the answer count (TypeChipSelector.tsx:286-303). Import never adds or removes answers, so "Scale · 1–N" needs exactly N answers and "Five-point scale" needs five; otherwise the cell is skipped ("Q3 has 6 answers. Change its points in the app"). The mock applies the same count check. End labels are not in the file. D10 is open only for what a type change does to answers it would drop, which this path cannot reach because the counts must already match.
  • Shows / keeps on a Picks question. Resolve the names to an ordered target list and write it with setAnswerTargets, the public wrapper that dedupes and keeps order (section data-model-and-mutations); never setAnswerTarget, which replaces the whole list with one id (deciderMutations.ts:56-87). An unknown or ambiguous name skips the cell. On a question that does not pick the result after step 2, the cell is skipped with a reason.
  • Shows / keeps on a Narrows question. "Keeps everything" writes setAnswerFilterValues(…, { no_preference: true }). "(not set)" or a blank cell writes the empty set. A value list writes one full-set setAnswerFilterValues call (deciderMutations.ts:398-463) built from the typed values, with metafield keys and option names in their stored case. A bare value without a kind resolves only when exactly one kind carries it. An unchanged cell is never written, so values nobody touched cannot be lost.
  • Shows / keeps on an Info question. "—" is ignored; anything else is skipped with a reason.
  • Then. Make exactly the route menu's writes (LogicTabMenus.tsx:350-388): "Next question" is setAnswerRoute(…, null); "Skips to Qn", for a question after the next one, routes to Qn; "Straight to results" routes to the result node. Compare by where the answer actually goes, so "Straight to results" on an unset last-question answer is no change. setAnswerRoute refuses a route that would revisit a question by returning the doc unchanged (edgeMutations.ts:106-111); report it ("“Yes” on Q4: routes only go forward"). A route that bypasses the picking question is written, not refused, and the style-aware report blocks Continue on it (D3).
  • Refusals are skips. When a mutation returns the doc unchanged, report a skip with its reason. Never count it as a change.

Rules sheet

  • Every row with content is a rule, in row order, and row order is priority. Blank rows are skipped, and so is the template row, whose Rule ID is EXAMPLE: it is noted, not counted as bad, so a merchant who exported an empty quiz, filled in the sheet below the example and imported it gets their rules and keeps the example out.
  • "#" is not a key and never reorders (B36). A filled row with a blank "#" is still a rule (B5). If the numbers are not ascending, add the note "# ignored: rules keep their row order, so move rows to reorder".
  • With the Rule ID column (the exported file always has it): a known ID is that rule, patched only in its changed cells with updateDecisionRule's presence semantics (deciderMutations.ts:276-339); match is never written, as in the rule window (CreateRuleModal.tsx:641-644), so a rule stored with match "any" keeps behaving that way (D13). A blank ID is a new rule, and all its cells are parsed. An unknown or repeated ID makes the row bad ("Rules row 5: this rule ID isn't in the quiz. Clear it to add the row as a new rule"). Stored rules missing from the file are removed, and the notes name them.
  • Without the Rule ID column (a hand-built file): match rows to stored rules by their exported cells, in order (longest common subsequence). Unmatched rows are new rules and unmatched stored rules are removed.
  • Parsing a changed When cell. After "Qn = ", match the longest exact answer text of question n, then expect a join, a ")" or the end. Never split on "and" or "or" first: answers contain those words, which is the lesson the paste parser encodes (app/lib/rulePaste.ts:21-23). An answer's text matches as it reads after the Answers sheet applied or as it read before the import, so a rename made on the Answers sheet does not break an edited When cell that still uses the old text. Bare text without "Qn =" resolves only when exactly one question has that answer; otherwise the row is bad ("Rules row 6: “Yes” is an answer on Q6 and Q7. Write it as Q7 = Yes"). Nothing is guessed, the same contract as rulePaste.ts:3-8,113-119,216-219.
  • Parsing Recommendations and What happens. Names resolve exactly, longest first, against the recommendations this surface loads. A name that two recommendations share is refused, as paste refuses it (rulePaste.ts:135-150,195-198). "Pin" is stored as prioritize, the paste mapping (rulePaste.ts:75-80). While the quiz is Rules only the rule window offers "Show" alone (D2), so a changed cell that sets "Pin" or "Hide" there is refused with a named reason ("Rules row 3: this quiz decides by rules, so every rule shows its recommendations. Use Show"). An unchanged "Pin" or "Hide" cell is never parsed, so a rule written under the other style still round-trips.
  • Validity matches the rule window (B24, B13, B14). A new or edited row needs at least one answer and one recommendation (createDecisionRule refuses less, deciderMutations.ts:359, and target_id is required, quizSchema.ts:1753). AND inside a group needs a multi-select question; model the reason on paste's refusal (rulePaste.ts:294-299), without its em dash: "Q1 is single select, so a shopper can't pick both. Use OR". No AND after NOT (D12): "Rules row 6: an is-not line means none of these answers, so write NOT (A OR B), not NOT (A AND B)". One group per question. No OR between groups on a new row (D13): "Rules row 4: answers from two questions joined with OR. Write one row for each question; both rows can show the same recommendations." A row whose Rule ID names a rule already stored with match "any" may keep its OR. No all-of with more picks than max_selections ("They can pick at most 2 on Q2, so all 3 can never happen together"). Every parsed rule goes through normalizeDecisionRule.
  • All-or-nothing (D16). One bad row means no rule changes. The toast names the first bad row by its spreadsheet row number (the header is row 1) with the reason, and says no rule changed (B22). The Answers cells in the same file still apply. The mock drops the whole sheet and says only "1 skipped" (applyImport()).

Change count, toasts, commit and Undo

  • Count (B25). Each changed Answers cell counts 1, and a question-level cell counts once per question. Each rule added, removed or edited counts 1. For moves, count only the rules outside the longest run kept in the same order, so moving one rule counts 1. Compare rules in canonical form: normalizeDecisionRule (conditions in question order, no stray is-not or any-of flags) with targets as an ordered list. Without IDs, use max(old, new) minus the longest common subsequence. An unchanged file counts 0. The mock compares JSON position by position, so stray flags showed changes and one inserted rule counted as six (applyImport()).
  • Toast copy (mock toastImp()): "Imported N change(s) · K skipped" with Undo; "Nothing changed · K skipped"; "Nothing changed". Append " · " and the first note, plus "(+M more)" when there are more. Example with a bad rule row: "Imported 2 changes · No rule changed: Rules row 4 has no recommendation called “acnee”". The toast shows one note by design: listing every skip needs a surface this design does not have, so do not invent one.
  • Toast component (D7). The design-system toast is message-only, 2.4 s, queue of one, and its own comment says it carries no actions (app/components/qz-toast.tsx:13-19, AUTO_DISMISS_MS at :20). Extend it with one optional action, a duration, a live region and keyboard reach, and record the dated owner exception (2026-09-22) against the design-system rule in the component's comment and in the design-system notes, so the next reader sees the exception rather than a violation. Keep the mock's 7 seconds for a toast with an action, pause while hovered or focused, and make Undo reachable from the keyboard (B32). One action per toast, still a queue of one.
  • Providers (D21). Add QzToastProvider to the two embedded routes that lack it, app/routes/app.onboarding_.$quizId.tsx:39-46 and app/routes/app.quizzes.$id_.studio.tsx:48-58, so Undo is never invisible there and a delete or an import stays recoverable. The studio twins already wrap it (app/routes/studio_.onboarding_.$quizId.tsx:38-40). The provider is the whole change: the hardcoded /studio links and giving embedded decider quizzes the new Logic view are separate tasks (D21, D6).
  • One commit. applyLogicImport(doc, parsed, ctx) returns { doc, changes, skipped, notes, undo } by composing the pure mutations named above (section data-model-and-mutations). Validate the result with Quiz.safeParse before committing: the server answers an invalid doc with 400 "Invalid quiz document" (app/lib/funnelIntents.server.ts:114-123; app/lib/quizEditorIO.server.ts:342-354), and every later autosave fails until the doc is valid again. If the check fails, commit nothing (proposed copy: "Couldn't apply that file. Nothing changed"). Otherwise commit once through useQuizDraft, whose commit schedules one debounced whole-doc PUT through a Remix fetcher (app/components/studio/useQuizDraft.ts:47-76). Never commit row by row: a debounced PUT could land between rows and save a half-applied doc; every PUT re-runs the page loaders, because no route defines shouldRevalidate (the funnel's loader is loadStep1FunnelData, app/routes/studio_.onboarding_.$quizId.tsx:21-33); and in the builder each commit pushes its own undo snapshot (app/components/studio/UnifiedWorkspace.tsx:194-202). One commit makes one import one Cmd-Z step there.
  • What Import can change. Question nodes (text, type, limits, role, targets, filter values), edges (routes) and decision_rules. Nothing else: not build_session, not the document's logic_style (the title switch is the only thing that writes it, D5, and the file carries no style cell), not results settings, not design.
  • Undo (D7). Import's Undo is an inverse, not a snapshot of the document. applyLogicImport returns undo as the parts it touched, captured before and after through captureLogicParts (the changed questions' data, those questions' outgoing edges, and the rules it added, removed or patched, by id). Undo calls restoreLogicParts against the latest doc, which writes the "before" parts back only while every captured part still equals the "after" it left, and returns null otherwise; the toast's Undo is then withdrawn (proposed: "Can't undo the import: the quiz changed after it"). An inverse step whose question, answer or recommendation has since been deleted is skipped and named, so Undo can never resurrect a dangling reference (B1 Fixed in mock). Undo is disabled while any dialog is open, so it can never change the rule list under an open rule window (B2 Fixed in mock). The rule-row trash and the reorder buttons use their own smaller inverses, restoreDecisionRule(s) and moveDecisionRule, as specified in the Rules sheet above.

Library, security and limits

  • Library (D16). SheetJS Community Edition 0.20.3, from the official cdn.sheetjs.com tarball. Never the npm xlsx package: npm stops at 0.18.5, the build the mock loads from cdnjs in loadXLSX. That build has CVE-2023-30533 (prototype pollution when reading a crafted file, fixed in 0.19.3) and CVE-2024-22363 (regular-expression denial of service, fixed in 0.20.2), and Import reads files merchants supply.
  • Load the library with a dynamic import() inside the Export and Import handlers, so Vite emits a separate chunk that is fetched only on use. Nothing else in the bundle may import it, and logicSheets.ts must not.
  • Install path. A tarball URL is fetched at install time by CI (npm ci, .github/workflows/ci.yml:33) and by the Fly image build (npm install, Dockerfile:26). If cdn.sheetjs.com should not be a build dependency, vendor the tarball in the repo and use a file: dependency. Regenerate the lockfile only with npx npm@10 install --package-lock-only (CLAUDE.md).
  • papaparse is not needed. It runs server-side only today (app/lib/catalog.server.ts:12-13), and SheetJS parses CSV text after the decoding step above.
  • The file never leaves the browser. The only thing that reaches the server is the resulting doc, through the normal autosave.
  • Limits and hardening, all covered above: the 1 MB file cap, the per-sheet row cap, values only, arrays and Map instead of header-keyed objects, and text cells without formulas on export.
  • Escaping (B21). Every imported string (answer, question and recommendation text, notes, reasons) renders as React text, including inside toasts and title attributes. Never use innerHTML; the mock's import toast does (toastImp()). Test with <img onerror>, <b> and a double quote in every text column.

Build order for this section

  1. app/lib/logicSheets.ts, pure, with logicSheets.test.ts: the sheet models for both styles, the "Qn = text" grammar in both directions, the placeholders, the id columns, the example row, and the cell-level diff. No library import, no React.
  2. The Table inside LogicTabCard: the two sheet layouts, the shared controls wired per row (B40), the row markers from the style-aware report (D3), the row actions with keyboard reorder (D11), and the Rules-sheet trash with its accumulating Undo (D7).
  3. Export: the lazy SheetJS chunk, the workbook writer, the widths, the custom property, the template row, the disabled state in React state (B37), and the embedded-iframe check.
  4. Import: the decoder (B26), the header-based sheet recognition, applyLogicImport with its phases, the notes, and the single commit with Quiz.safeParse in front of it.
  5. The toast action and the providers (D7, D21), with the dated exception recorded.
  6. The shared pieces this section depends on, if they have not landed with the Edit views already: the announced Picks move helper (D9), restoreDecisionRule(s), captureLogicParts / restoreLogicParts, setAnswerTargets, changeQuestionType, normalizeDecisionRule, the grouping and "not (...)" in describeRuleConditions (D17), and the shared word constants (D18).

Inline text editing and the field save pill

Question titles and answer texts are edited where they are shown, in place, with no dialog and no Save button. This section specifies that editor, the mutations it writes through, and the small "Saving… / Saved" pill that appears at the edited field after a change lands (D8). It also fixes what a rename does to every other place the same text appears, and what the merchant sees for the edits that are not text (those belong to toasts, not to the pill).

Both logic styles are in scope, equally. "Filter Results + Rules" and "Rules only" are two ways a quiz decides, not a screen and a lens on it (D1). They differ in where a merchant meets this editor, not in whether they get it. In Filter Results + Rules the step itself shows the question pane and the Table's "Answers" sheet, so text is edited on the Logic step. In Rules only the step shows the rules and the "Your recommendations" strip, and question and answer text is edited one step back, on the Questions step, which this work does not touch: it keeps today's editor and today's mutations. Both styles get the same editor, caps, escaping, keyboard behaviour and pill wherever this step renders text; the Questions step is named as a separate task below, not built here.

How this section cites things. Code references are path:line on origin/main (b4aa278) and were re-read against that commit for this pass. The reference mock is docs/design/logic-tab/rules-row/index.html, cited by function, handler or CSS class name (pane(), svStart(), the focusout listener on [data-edit]) because the file is still being edited and its line numbers move. Defect ids (B21, B45, B59, B61) are the mock QA review's; decision ids (D1, D7, D8) point at Owner decisions for the reasoning, and are not a signal that anything is still being weighed.
The owner has ruled. Build what follows; do not re-open it.
  • D8. The save pill shows at the edited field only, after a committed change. The ambient autosave chrome stays silent when healthy.
  • D7. The shared toast gains one optional action, an optional duration, a live region and keyboard reach, and Undo is inverse mutations against the latest document, never a whole-document snapshot. Text edits take no toast and no Undo action: they have the pill and the browser's own text undo.
  • D1. The logic style lives on the quiz document and survives publish, and Rules only is a real engine mode. Nothing in this section is conditional on which style is running: the text mutations are style-independent and decider-gated.
  • D5. No first-entry chooser. The style resolves; nothing is written on load. LogicStyleChooser and its inert "Point based" row are deleted, so the editors never render behind a chooser.
  • D3. One style-aware Tier-1 report drives the CTA, the check popover and publish. Findings re-render from the document as the merchant types; a rename never changes the blocking count.
  • D16. Import writes text through these same mutations, matches rows by the do-not-edit id columns, updates answers in place and never adds or deletes them, and treats a missing column as "leave unchanged".
  • D17. Rule sentences are verb-first and answers-only; the Table and the export always use the machine form Q7 = Yes. Both re-derive from the document on every keystroke.
  • D18. Every label in this section comes from the shared copy constants; internal words (decider, bucket, branch, boost, weight, score) never reach the merchant, including in aria-labels and live-region announcements.
  • D21. The embedded (/app) twins get the missing toast provider, so the Undo that belongs to the other edits is never invisible there.
Still open, and what each one blocks here. Do not pick them.
  • D10. What a question-type change does to answers and to the rules that referenced them (a scale conversion dropping answers, a five-point trim to five points). Blocks: nothing about the editor itself, which is specified below for every type this step renders. It blocks one thing on this surface: whether a label a merchant typed on a scale point can be destroyed by a later type change without an Undo. Build the editor and the B45 scale-point rules now; leave the type-change path as it ships and mark the seam in the code.
  • D14, second half. Whether used recommendations move to the end of the tray, and how the armed state reads on the builder's editor surface, which re-points the accent colour. Blocks: the focus ring and the spinner head colour when this editor renders on the builder's editor surface, where --qz-accent and --qz-accent-line resolve to the ink ladder (quizocalypse.css:250-257). On the funnel surface, which is what ships now, the accent is the Quartz violet and nothing is blocked.

Parked, and what to do meanwhile.

Findings that name a question or an answer re-render as the merchant types, because they read the document. Do not rebuild "Check my logic", the Diagnose modal, "Test a path" or the AI review into the step, and do not add an "N to review" affordance. The known gap while parked: a Rules-only quiz opens in today's builder Logic view as Filter Results + Rules, and that view shows question and answer text read-only. Name the gap in the handoff to the main-builder project; do not patch today's builder to close it.

Scale points (B45)

  • Every point of a Scale or Five-point question is a real Answer (TypeChipSelector.tsx:16-19). That view renders endpoint_label_min before the row and never renders endpoint_label_max, which only the slider branch draws (QuestionView.tsx:235-247, 545-549). Do not fold it into this change, whose runtime half is already the D1 safety net.

Building the editor

Build on useContentEditable (useContentEditable.ts:24-140), the primitive the Questions step already uses through EditableText (EditableText.tsx:10-36). Keep its invariants:

  • It never rewrites the text under a focused caret: the value is written into the element only while it is unfocused (useContentEditable.ts:42-48).
  • Plain text only: contentEditable="plaintext-only", a paste handler that inserts clipboard text, and a beforeinput filter that drops formatting and line breaks (useContentEditable.ts:100-138).
  • IME composition defers the write to compositionend (useContentEditable.ts:63-81); Enter blurs (83-91); a write that changes nothing is skipped (56).
  • It is announced as a single-line textbox: role="textbox", aria-multiline false, an aria-label, tabIndex 0 (EditableText.tsx:24-35). Label by position, for example "Question 3 text" and "Question 3, answer B"; give an empty scale point aria-placeholder "Add label". Labels come from the shared copy constants (D18), and no label names an internal concept.

What the primitive does not do. The first two were also confirmed with a jsdom test run against the unchanged file:

  • An emptied field writes the empty string: commitFrom has no empty guard (useContentEditable.ts:50-61).
  • maxLength only truncates the written value (useContentEditable.ts:55). Nothing stops typing or pasting past the cap, and because the element is rewritten only when value changes (43-48), a field typed past its cap keeps showing characters that were never saved, even after blur. Passing maxLength alone does not meet B59.
  • No Esc handling and no snapshot. Every keystroke is already in the document, so Esc has to write the snapshot back.
  • Paste folds only line breaks and has no cap (102-110); the blur only trims, so whitespace runs are never collapsed (93-98).
  • The Enter handler ignores isComposing (83-91), so confirming an IME candidate with Enter can end the edit.
  • The final text is never written back into the field, and nothing signals the end of an edit, which the pill needs.

Add the missing pieces as opt-in options of the hook, keeping today's defaults so useContentEditable.test.tsx passes unchanged, or write one Logic component on the same invariants and use it in the pane and the Table. Either way:

  • Run the end-of-edit step on every blur, independent of the hook's no-op skip. When the mutation refuses an empty write, nothing re-renders and the hook's last written value stays empty, so its own blur commit is skipped (useContentEditable.ts:39-40, 56-57, 93-98).
  • Handle Esc in a keydown listener on window, capture phase, that exists only while the field is focused, and stop propagation there. QzModal handles Esc on document in the capture phase (qz-overlays.tsx:124-134), and the builder clears its selection on any Esc with no editable guard (UnifiedWorkspace.tsx:462-475).
  • Send every keystroke write through the mutation. The document then never holds an empty, over-long or unnormalized text, even if the field unmounts without a blur, and a debounced PUT that fires mid-edit is always valid.
  • Call commit only when the mutation returns a new document (a reference check), so keystrokes that change nothing cause no save and no history entry.
  • Keep React keys stable (the pane by node id and answer rows by answer id, as today at LogicQuestionWidget.tsx:235 and 401; Table rows the same way), so a keystroke re-render never remounts the focused field.
  • Keep the component host-agnostic (D6): props only, no funnel-only imports, no ruleFlow check inside it. The funnel mounts it now; the rebuilt builder mounts the same file later.

startInlineTextEdit (studioShared.tsx:59-116), the builder canvas's double-click editor (UnifiedWorkspace.tsx:582-597), has the right end-of-edit semantics: a snapshot at start (71), Esc restores it, an empty or unchanged result restores the original (84-98), and key events stop at the field (100-103). It writes once, at the end, so it cannot drive the live views. Use it as a reference, not as the implementation.

The component contract

// app/components/studio/logicTab/LogicEditableText.tsx  (new, host-agnostic)
export function LogicEditableText(props: {
  /** The stored text. Never written into the element while it is focused. */
  value: string;
  /** Every input event, with the text already capped and plain. */
  onType: (text: string) => void;
  /** Once, at the end of a session whose stored text changed. Drives the pill. */
  onCommitted: () => void;
  /** Written back when the field ends empty (a scale point passes its number). */
  emptyFallback: string;
  maxLength: number;          // QUESTION_TEXT_MAX | ANSWER_TEXT_MAX
  ariaLabel: string;          // from the shared copy constants (D18)
  ariaPlaceholder?: string;   // "Add label" on an empty scale point
  /** Builder history coalescing; a host without history ignores it. */
  coalesceKey: string;
  className?: string;
}): JSX.Element;
  • onType and onCommitted are separate on purpose: the document is written on every keystroke, the pill fires once. A host that shows no pill passes an onCommitted that does nothing.
  • The component owns the snapshot, Esc, the cap, paste normalization, the end-of-edit write-back and focus placement. Hosts own the mutation call and the pill.
  • It renders plain text, not an editable, when the host passes no onType, which is how read-only previews and tests stay read-only.

One undo step per edit where a history exists

The funnel's commit (useQuizDraft) has no history, so it ignores coalesceKey and nothing more is needed for the surface that ships. Keep the option in the contract anyway, because the builder's commit pushes the previous document onto its undo history on every call (UnifiedWorkspace.tsx:160-166, 194-202; 50 entries), and keystroke writes would fill that history with one entry per character. A host with a history pushes one snapshot per coalesceKey, for example "text:" + nodeId + ":" + (answerId ?? "q"), and drops that snapshot when the edit ends on it (Esc, or typing that was removed again) so ⌘Z has no empty step. This is what the rebuilt builder inherits (D6); do not wire it into today's builder.

The text mutations

// app/lib/mutations/questionMutations.ts: new exports
export const QUESTION_TEXT_MAX = 150;
export const ANSWER_TEXT_MAX = 60;

/** Collapses every whitespace run (line breaks, tabs, NBSP) to one space,
 *  trims, clamps to max without splitting a surrogate pair, trims again. */
export function normalizeEditText(raw: string, max: number): string;

/** Decider docs only. Returns doc itself when the node is missing or is not a
 *  question, when the normalized text is empty, or when it equals the current
 *  text. Otherwise writes nodes[i].data.text and nothing else. */
export function setQuestionText(doc: QuizDoc, nodeId: string, text: string): QuizDoc;

/** The same contract for one answer's text. */
export function setAnswerText(
  doc: QuizDoc,
  nodeId: string,
  answerId: string,
  text: string,
): QuizDoc;

// app/lib/mutations/nodeMutations.ts: one more, where message nodes live
/** The same contract for a message node's heading (MessageData.text). */
export function setMessageText(doc: QuizDoc, nodeId: string, text: string): QuizDoc;
  • The first line is if (doc.logic_model !== "decider") return doc;, per this handoff's gating rule (quizSchema.ts:1992), so legacy documents stay byte-identical.
  • They gate on logic_model and on nothing else. There is no style check: the same mutation serves Filter Results + Rules and Rules only, the Questions step and Import.
  • Pure and immutable. Import ./shared and other concrete modules only, never the quizMutations barrel (quizMutations.ts:5-7).
  • Write the one text field only. Ids, edge_handle_id, target_id and target_ids, narrowing values, no_preference, answer order and decision_rules stay untouched. Rule conditions reference answer ids (quizSchema.ts:1735-1739), so a rename never breaks a rule, never reorders one and never changes a rule id; the sentences just show the new text.
  • Returning the same reference means "nothing to commit", and callers rely on that.
  • Export the caps and use them in the editors, the Table, Import and the "Add a question" dialog. Today the numbers are repeated file by file (ContentTab.tsx:24-25; AddQuestionDialog.tsx:152, 200; WalkQuestion.tsx:68, 135; questionMutations.ts:142, 148).
  • Nothing in the Logic surfaces writes text with updateNodeData, which shallow-merges any patch with no checks (studioDoc.ts:179-191).

Import writes through the same mutations (D16)

  • applyLogicImport (section Table view, Export and Import) calls setQuestionText and setAnswerText for text, never updateNodeData, so the cap, the trim and the empty guard apply to a spreadsheet exactly as they apply to a caret.
  • Rows are matched by the do-not-edit "Answer ID" column, not by text, so renaming an answer in the sheet updates that answer in place. The "Answers" sheet never adds or deletes an answer.
  • A blank cell means "leave unchanged", never "clear", which is the same rule as the empty guard above and the reason an empty cell can never break a save.
  • Import reports a cell it had to shorten, and does not count unchanged text as a change. Text that matches what is stored produces no commit, because the mutation returns the same reference.
  • Imported text is never parsed as HTML and never escaped on write (see B21 below).
  • The reader and writer are SheetJS CE 0.20.3 from the official SheetJS CDN tarball, loaded as a lazy chunk, never the npm xlsx 0.18.5 build. The mock still loads 0.18.5 from a public CDN in loadXLSX(); do not copy it. The full contract, including the id columns, the read-only "Recommendations" sheet and Export writing the template on a quiz with no rules, is in the Table section.

What a rename changes elsewhere, and what it never changes

  • Rule sentences (D17). Sentences are verb-first and answers-only, with parentheses around multi-answer groups, bold joins, "not (...)" for a negated group and full-text tooltips on truncated answers. They read the document, so they follow a rename keystroke by keystroke (mock sentence(), whenHTML()).
  • The disambiguating question label (D17). A question label appears in a sentence only when the same answer text exists on another question. That test is derived, not stored, so renaming an answer to "Yes" can add a label to two sentences at once, and renaming it away can remove one. Recompute it from the document on every render; never cache it on the rule.
  • The machine form (D17). The Table's "When they answer" cells and the export always read Q7 = Yes, so they change with the text and with the question's position, and they never carry the disambiguating label.
  • Negation (D12). An "is not" row means none of these answers and reads "not (A or B)". A rename changes the words inside the parentheses and nothing else; the any/all toggle stays hidden on that row.
  • Checks (D3). Findings name questions and answers, so their wording follows a rename. The blocking count does not: every Tier-1 check keys off ids, roles, rules and structure, not text. Renaming can never move the CTA between "Continue" and "Fix N issues". Use that when profiling: the report can be recomputed on a keystroke, but nothing about the CTA needs to animate.
  • Rules, ids and order. Untouched, in both styles. A rename cannot make a rule half-built, dead or impossible, cannot reorder the stack under first-match-wins, and cannot change what "Duplicate" (in the rule window's top row, D11) produces.
  • Recommendations. Untouched. Recommendation names come from the catalogue and from "+ Add recommendations" (D15); this editor never writes one, and a renamed answer keeps the same targets.
  • The published document. Untouched until the merchant publishes. A rename is an ordinary draft edit that rides the same autosave PUT as every other edit.
The Questions step has the same hole today, and it is a separate task. Its editors pass whatever EditableText hands them to updateNodeData, including the empty string: the walkthrough question (WalkQuestion.tsx:54-55, 133-146) and the edit-mode overview (QuestionsWalkthrough.tsx:177-186, 209-224), message headings included (MessageData.text is also min(1), quizSchema.ts:576-577). Clearing a title there fails every later save until it is filled again. Both surfaces are decider-only (QuestionBuilderStage.tsx:76, 180). Do not fix it in this change. The Questions step is not in the surface list this work ships to (Scope, sources and ground rules, What ships today) and no phase covers it, so switching its editors to the new mutations would be unscoped work in a step nobody reviewed for it. Raise it as its own task, with the same empty guard, the same end-of-edit handling and the message headings, and name it in your report; in Rules only it is where a merchant renames a question, so it matters. The builder inspector has the same gap (ContentTab.tsx:369-375) and goes to the main-builder work (D6).

The field save pill New

Decided (D8, owner 2026-09-18). The pill appears only at the edited field, after a committed change: "Saving…" with a spinner, then a green "Saved" with a check, then it fades. Typing stays silent. There is no ambient save chip anywhere. FunnelSaveChip keeps "Not saved · Retry" and "Paused while AI edits". This is a field-scoped exception to the 2026-08-18 silent-autosave ruling recorded at funnelChrome.tsx:70-80.

When it shows

  • Only after a committed inline text edit: at the end of the edit, the stored text is not empty and differs from the snapshot.
  • Never while typing, and never for a no-op, an Esc, an emptied field that was restored, an Import, or any other kind of edit. The other kinds have their own feedback; the table below fixes which.
  • One pill at a time; a newer committed edit replaces it. Focusing the same field again dismisses it (the mock's focusin listener does this, and it is correct).
  • If the field unmounts (another question selected, the view switched), the pill goes with it. The save continues, and a failure still shows in the bar chip. The mock carries a Table pill over into the Edit pane after a view switch because svSel() finds the field again by its data attributes and render() re-places it; do not copy that. Bind the pill to the mounted field instance, not to a selector.
  • The pill is style-independent. It shows wherever this editor renders, which in this work means the Filter Results + Rules pane and the Table, in a quiz of either style. The Questions step keeps today's editor and gets no pill until its own task ships.

What every other edit shows instead

The pill is for text. Everything else on this step is either silent or a toast, and the toast is the one that carries Undo (D7). Nothing on this step uses a confirm dialog.

States

StateShowsHow long
SavingSpinner and "Saving…"From the end of the edit until the PUT that carries it returns. A short minimum is fine so it does not flash; "Saved" never appears before the save has succeeded.
SavedCheck and "Saved", green. The live region says "Saved".About 1.5 s, then a 0.4 s fade: the mock's timings in svStart(), started only after the real result.
