Tie it to the real save

The mock fakes the save with timers (650 ms, 1.5 s, 0.4 s, in svStart()). The product follows the PUT, and useQuizDraft cannot report it today:

  • isSaving is the fetcher's state (useQuizDraft.ts:121), so it stays false through the 700 ms debounce (58-68).
  • savedAt is the timestamp of the latest response, for the whole document (122-123); nothing ties it to an edit.
  • flushSave returns nothing (136-142).

Add an awaitable flush (or a per-commit pending token) to useQuizDraft. It is additive, so current callers keep working:

// useQuizDraft: flushSave becomes awaitable; existing callers ignore the result
flushSave: () => Promise<"saved" | "failed">;
  • Every commit takes a sequence number, and each PUT records the newest sequence it carries.
  • flushSave() sends the pending document now and settles "saved" once a PUT carrying that sequence or a newer one returns ok, or "failed" if it returns an error. If the outcome is already known, it settles at once.
  • Settle by sequence, not by request. A new submit on the same fetcher aborts the one in flight (@remix-run/router 1.23.3: fetch() calls abortFetcher(key) first, node_modules/@remix-run/router/dist/router.js:2377), so an aborted PUT never reports back and its edit is confirmed by the later PUT that carries it.
  • Respect the AI pause. Today flushSave submits the pending document even while autosave is paused (136-142, against the pause at 60-64); the new flush waits for the resumed save instead.
  • A later success, including one from "Retry", settles an earlier failure as saved, so a Failed pill still on screen turns to Saved.
  • Keep the sequence bookkeeping in a small pure module next to the hook so it can be unit-tested without a Remix fetcher.

Plumbing. Give LogicTabCard one new optional prop:

/** useQuizDraft.flushSave, widened. Absent = no pill (read-only hosts). */
onFlush?: () => Promise<"saved" | "failed">;
  • Step3Shell already receives flushSave as onFlush (Step3Shell.tsx:73, 94-95; passed at QuestionBuilderStage.tsx:211), typed () => void. Widen the type to return the promise and hand it to LogicTabCard beside logicStyle and ruleFlow (Step3Shell.tsx:520-532).
  • The Questions step needs the same flush for its own editors: QuestionsWalkthrough takes commit today (QuestionBuilderStage.tsx:180-184) and would need the flush passed the same way. That goes with the separate Questions-step task, not this one.
  • In the builder, UnifiedWorkspace has flushSave (UnifiedWorkspace.tsx:155) and BuilderLogicView does not take it (BuilderSettings.tsx:33-43), which stays true while D6 is parked: today's builder mounts LogicTabCard without the prop (BuilderSettings.tsx:69-75), so it shows no pill and no editors. Do not add the prop there.
  • "Continue" needs the same awaitable flush (Checks, the Fix-N gate, the check popover and Continue), so build it once.

Funnel chrome stays silent

  • No ambient save chip. FunnelSaveChip still renders only the error and paused states (funnelChrome.tsx:81-129).
  • Wire isAiPaused: Step3Shell renders FunnelSaveChip without it (Step3Shell.tsx:325-327), and QuestionBuilderStage never reads it from useQuizDraft (QuestionBuilderStage.tsx:61-72).
  • Append the exception to the ruling comment at funnelChrome.tsx:70-80, for example:
   Owner 2026-09-18 (Logic step): after a committed inline text edit, a
   field-level "Saving… / Saved" pill shows at the end of the edited text
   (LogicEditableText). Typing stays silent and the pill is never ambient;
   this chip still renders only Not saved · Retry and Paused while AI edits.

The matching note in the bar at Step1Funnel.tsx:145-148 stays true as written: the pill is not a bar chip.

Placement

  • Anchor: the last line box of the edited text (Range.getClientRects() over the field's contents), 8px after its right edge and centred on that line, as svPlace() does.
  • Stay inside the text's own column: the pane title block, the answer-text cell, the Table cell. If the pill does not fit beside the last line, put it just under the end of that line, clamped to the column. Decide once per pill using the wider "Saving…" width, so it does not jump when the label changes (B61).
  • Never cover a neighbour: the role button beside the title, the type line under it, the answer's mapping cell, the next Table cell.
  • Float without reflow: position: fixed, pointer-events: none, aria-hidden. Portal it to document.body, as the app's floating elements do, because an in-flow fixed element gets trapped by transformed or container-type ancestors (qz-overlays.tsx:21-22).
  • z-index below --qz-z-topbar (40, quizocalypse.css:221), so it slides under the funnel's sticky bar with its text (quizocalypse.css:4165-4166; TopBar.tsx:29, 41) and stays under popovers (quizocalypse.css:4393-4394), modals and toasts.
  • Re-place it on scroll (capture phase, so inner scrollers count), on window resize, and when the field or its column changes size (ResizeObserver). Hide it while the field is focused, and when the field is unmounted or scrolled or clipped out of view (an IntersectionObserver on the field). Wherever the field scrolls inside an inner scroller, the clipping check is what hides it; the builder is a full-height flex column (quizocalypse.css:8948-8952), and the rebuilt one will be too.
  • When the editor renders on a host that re-points the accent tokens, put data-qz-surface="editor" on the portal container so the pill's tokens match the surface it floats over (quizocalypse.css:250-257). On the funnel surface, which is what ships now, nothing re-points them.
  • DS-V2 §7.5 lists four floating surfaces (qz-overlays.tsx:16-20). Record the pill in the design-system notes as a field-level status badge, not a fifth surface, next to the dated D7 toast-action exception.

Look and announcements

  • Size: 20px tall, 11.5px/600 text, padding 0 8px 0 6px, a 5px gap and a 10px spinner (the mock's #svb rules).
  • Tokens: Saving on --qz-cream-2 with --qz-ink-4 text, and a spinner track of --qz-ls-line2 with an --qz-accent head; Saved on --qz-live-wash with --qz-ok text (the same values as the mock's --ok-wash and --ok); Failed on --qz-crit-tint with --qz-crit text (quizocalypse.css:60, 68, 84, 97, 99, 101, 108, 176). Corners: --qz-radius-pill. Quartz pills are deliberately 6px rounded rects (quizocalypse.css:184); the mock's 999px is a literal, not a token.
  • Reuse the autosave chip's glyphs and state classes (SvIcon, funnelChrome.tsx:52-68; .qz-sv, quizocalypse.css:10683-10707), so the spinner stops under reduced motion (quizocalypse.css:10699). The CSS goes in app/styles/quizocalypse.css; no hex in .tsx (scripts/check-tokens.mjs).
  • One shared, visually hidden aria-live="polite" region announces "Saved", as the mock's #svlive does from svStart(). It does not announce failures: the bar chip is already a live region (funnelChrome.tsx:125). It announces "Saved" and nothing else, so the announcement never leaks an internal word (D18).

The builder, parked (D6)

  • This work ships the funnel's step 3 surface. Today's builder Logic view keeps what it has: LogicTabCard mounted without logicStyle, without onFlush and without a commit-driven editor (BuilderSettings.tsx:33-43, 69-75), so it shows question and answer text read-only and no pill. Do not add editors or the pill to it now.
  • The style lives on the document (D1), so a quiz keeps its style when it graduates to the builder. The known gap while parked: a Rules-only quiz opens in today's builder Logic view as Filter Results + Rules, because that view does not read the style. Record it for the main-builder project rather than patching it here.
  • Everything this section builds is reusable as written: no funnel-only imports in the editor or the pill, no ruleFlow === "onboarding" gate inside them, the mutations in app/lib/mutations/, the flush in a pure module beside useQuizDraft, and the coalesceKey option already in the contract for a host with an undo history.
  • When the new builder mounts these components it will also need the builder's own save reporting: its top bar already shows "Saving…", the error with "Retry" and "All changes saved" in a live region (UnifiedWorkspace.tsx:1667-1688). A host that announces saves itself should pass an onCommitted that shows the pill with its live region silent, so one save is never announced twice. Write that down in the handoff; do not build it now.
  • The builder's editor surface points --qz-accent and --qz-accent-line at the ink ladder (quizocalypse.css:250-257), so the focus ring and the spinner head turn neutral there. Whether a Logic-scoped violet survives on that surface is the open half of D14; it changes nothing on the funnel surface.

Escaping (B21)

  • Render question and answer text only as React text children and plain props (title, aria-label, value, placeholder). Never use dangerouslySetInnerHTML: on origin/main the only use anywhere under app/ is the persona page's JSON-LD script (app/routes/q.$id_.persona.$slug.tsx:140). Keep it that way.
  • The editor reads and writes textContent only (useContentEditable.ts:47, 52) and pastes plain text (104-107); keep both in any new code.
  • Where a view shortens text (sentence chips, the rail clamp, the rule window's answer buckets), cut the raw string and then render it as text, with the full text in title. A cut can then never split markup. This matters in both styles: the Rules-only rules row and the Filter rules column render the same sentences.
  • Store raw text and never HTML-escape on write. React escapes on render, and the runtime renders answer labels as plain strings (app/components/runtime/bits/answerLabel.ts:4); escaping on write would show shoppers &amp; where they should see &.
  • Imported text goes through the same mutations and is never parsed as HTML (D16).
  • Do not take the mock as a model here. It escapes inside its editors (escA() in pane() and tableHTML()) but inserts text raw elsewhere: the rail label and its tooltip in railItems(), the sentence chips in sentence(), the answer buckets in whenHTML(). Its live typing path is safe because syncText() assigns textContent, which is exactly the rule to follow everywhere.

Verification

Unit tests

  • Mutations (app/lib/quizMutations.test.ts): whitespace runs that include a line break and a non-breaking space (U+00A0) collapse to one space; text is trimmed; clamps at 150 and 60 keep an emoji at the cut whole; the empty string and a whitespace-only string return the same document reference; the same text returns the same reference; an unknown node, a non-question node, an unknown answer and a legacy document (no logic_model) all return the same reference; only the target field changes (everything else deep-equal, decision_rules the same reference); the same calls behave identically on a document with logic_style: "rules" and on one with "attributes".
  • Editor (jsdom, beside useContentEditable.test.tsx): Esc restores the snapshot in the field and in the document, and a document capture listener never sees the key; an emptied field restores the snapshot on blur (a scale point stores its number) and reports no change; an insert past the cap is refused; a 600-character paste inserts 150; after blur the field shows exactly what was stored; Enter and Esc with isComposing do nothing; after Enter, focus is on the next control and never on <body>; a scale point whose text equals its number is still editable (B45 case C).
  • Save tracking (the pure module): "saved" after an ok response carrying its sequence; "failed" after an error, then "saved" after a later success; an edit whose PUT was aborted settles with the later PUT; nothing is submitted while paused, and it settles after the resumed save; it settles at once when already confirmed.
  • Import (with the Table section's tests): a renamed answer cell updates that answer in place and keeps its id, its targets and every rule that referenced it; a blank cell changes nothing; a 200-character question cell is shortened and reported.
  • Re-run useContentEditable.test.tsx if the hook changes, and the Questions step's tests with it.

Probe and screenshots

  • In the new logic-filter-verify probe (Tests), edit a title and an answer and check that the rail label and tooltip, the rules-column sentence, the Table's "When they answer" cell and the check popover's wording change on each keystroke, while the CTA's count does not move.
  • Delay the autosave PUT with request interception: the pill stays on "Saving…" until the response and turns to "Saved" only after it (check against the network log). Make the PUT fail: the pill reads "Not saved" and the bar reads "Not saved · Retry"; "Retry" turns the pill to "Saved".
  • Clear a field and leave it: the original text returns, no pill shows, and no request body carries an empty text.
  • Type past the cap and paste 600 characters: the field stops at 150 (title) or 60 (answer), and after blur it shows exactly what was saved.
  • Arm a tray chip, edit an answer, press Esc: the text is restored and the chip stays armed.
  • On a Five-point question every row is editable with "Add label"; a typed label shows; clearing it restores the number; the first and last rows show their end labels.
  • Switch the view from Table to Edit right after a committed edit: the pill does not reappear on the other view's field.
  • In a Rules-only quiz, walk back to the Questions step, rename a question and an answer there, return to Logic and check that the rules row's sentences and the Table's "When they answer" cells carry the new text, that no rule changed id, order or recommendations, and that the blocking count is unchanged.
  • Put the B21 strings in a title and an answer (<img src=x onerror=alert(1)>, <b>bold</b>, Do you prefer "clean" formulas?): nothing renders as markup in the rail, tooltips, sentences, the rules row, the Table, the rule window or menu titles, and tooltips keep the quotes. Run this in both styles.
  • Screenshots, because the pill is an interactive state and CLAUDE.md requires screenshots rather than DOM markers, at 1440x900 and 1280x720: beside a short title; on a title that ends at the role button; under an answer that fills its cell; in a Table cell; and after scrolling the field under the sticky bar.

Gates and proof rules

  • The gate chain, unpiped, before every commit: npm run typecheck && npm test -- --run && npm run build && npm run lint && node scripts/check-tokens.mjs.
  • Legacy documents stay byte-identical. Every mutation here returns its input unchanged on a document without logic_model: "decider", and no new schema field carries a .default().
  • This change as a whole carries the runtime proof rules, because the D1 safety net changes what a shopper sees when no rule matches and when a result resolves empty (GlobalFallback, quizSchema.ts:1339-1354; specified in Engine semantics): full e2e, screenshot review, and the byte pin after every deploy. Nothing in this section touches app/components/runtime/, so keep the editor work in commits of its own and let the runtime half carry its own proof.
  • Re-run e2e/q3-questions-verify.mjs whenever the Questions step's editors or useContentEditable change.

Done when

  • A merchant can rename any question and any answer from the pane and the Table, in a quiz of either style, and every read-only echo follows as they type. Renaming from the Questions step keeps working as it does today, with today's editor.
  • No empty, whitespace-only or over-long text can reach the document from a caret, a paste, an IME or a spreadsheet.
  • A committed edit shows "Saving…" until its PUT returns, then "Saved", at that field and nowhere else; a failed save shows "Not saved" at the field and "Not saved · Retry" in the bar.
  • Esc restores the text and closes nothing else; Enter and Tab leave focus on a real control.
  • A rename never changes a rule, an id, an order or the blocking count, and never renders as markup anywhere.
  • The editor, the pill and the mutations mount on a host that is not the funnel without an edit to their source.

Engine semantics and the engine changes

Every rule sentence, verb hint, coverage count and check in the new Logic workspace tells the merchant what the decider engine will do for a shopper, so each one has to match the engine exactly. This section states that behaviour as shipped on origin/main (b4aa278), then specifies the engine, validation, publish and runtime changes this build makes. The owner has ruled: Rules only is a real engine mode (D1), unmatched shoppers get the Results step's safety net in both styles (D1 safety net), and the checks are one style-aware Tier-1 report (D3). Those are implementation work, not options. One question inside this section is still open and is marked where it bites: what Show does in Filter Results + Rules (D2). Diagnostics (D4) and builder parity (D6) are parked; what to do meanwhile is stated below.

Both styles are first-class. Filter Results + Rules and Rules only are two ways the same quiz document decides a result, not a full mode and a reduced one. Filter Results + Rules resolves a base from the picking question, narrows it with filter questions and lets a rule act on top. Rules only resolves the whole result from the first matching rule. Neither is a view of the other, neither is a subset of the other, and the checks, copy and tests in this section exist twice over, once per style.
How this was verified. The four engine files (recommendDecider.ts, recommendationEngine.ts, filterMatching.ts, pathAnalyzer.ts) were copied byte-identical from origin/main into a scratch harness outside the repo and run against small fixture docs. Every result marked "probe" comes from those runs. The harness is not in the repo; the cases are listed in the probe table below so they can be pinned as unit tests before anything changes. Mock behaviour marked "mock" was read from the current docs/design/logic-tab/rules-row/index.html and confirmed by driving that file with Playwright; mock code is cited by helper name because the file's line numbers move with every fix. Refs: all on origin/main. Bare file names are in app/lib/; runtime/ is app/components/runtime/; logicTab/ is app/components/studio/logicTab/; mutations/ is app/lib/mutations/; onboarding/ is app/components/onboarding/.

How a decider quiz picks products today

One pass, in this order, when the shopper reaches the result node. This is the engine Filter Results + Rules keeps unchanged; Rules only replaces stages 2, 3 and 5 (next section). The engine runs in the shopper's browser (QuizRuntime calls it at result time, runtime/QuizRuntime.tsx:1544-1552), so a change to these files changes live results for every published decider quiz on the next deploy, with no republish.

StageWhat the engine doesorigin/main
0. DispatchOnly docs with logic_model: "decider" take this path. Every other doc runs the legacy walkLadder path unchanged.recommendationEngine.ts:392, 494-529
1. RulesRules are checked top to bottom in array order. A rule with zero conditions is skipped: it never fires and does not stop the scan. The first rule whose conditions match wins and the scan stops, so at most one rule applies per shopper, whatever its action. A rule with no action (legacy replace) returns its own targets as the result at once. A Show, Pin or Hide rule is remembered and the base still resolves.recommendDecider.ts:226-240
2. BaseThe targets of the one question with role: "decides": its answers are walked in authored order (never click order); each selected answer adds answerTargets(a) (target_ids, else target_id); duplicates keep their first position. A multi-select picking question therefore unions every selected answer's recommendations. The first entry is the anchor.recommendDecider.ts:74-82, 242-259
3. AnchorThe anchor (targetIds[0]) supplies the results-page settings (global plus that target's override), the persona and the analytics resolved_target_id. When a Show, Pin or Hide rule fires on top of a base, all three still come from the base anchor, not from the rule's recommendation.recommendDecider.ts:189-202; recommendationEngine.ts:399, 471-480; runtime/views/DeciderViews.tsx:576-583
4. SellableProducts whose baked status is not active (on indexes that carry a status), and products that are both out of stock and unpriced or $0, are dropped for the whole pass: narrowing and hero/grid both use the sellable index.recommendationEngine.ts:122-129, 403, 424, 454
5. NarrowingRuns only when the quiz has a filter-role question. Within one filter question: OR across the shopper's selected answers. Across filter questions: AND. Inside one answer a product matches if any configured value kind matches (tag, collection, metafield including comma-list members, variant option, product type; case-insensitive). no_preference ("Keeps everything") and valueless answers pass through, and a filter question the shopper skipped or never reached contributes nothing. There is no relaxation: narrowing to zero leaves an empty pool. Narrowing applies to whatever pool resolved: the base, a replace rule's targets, or (with no base) a Show or Pin rule's own targets.filterMatching.ts:55-117, 145-151, 172-206; recommendationEngine.ts:411-433; probe
6. Rule actionThe winning Show, Pin or Hide rule acts on the narrowed pool, using the union of all its recommendations' members (next table).recommendationEngine.ts:434-440; recommendDecider.ts:301-317
7. Hero and gridIn-stock products only, unless the whole pool is out of stock (then heroOos decides). Hero = first by heroLogic; grid = the rest by gridSort, cut to gridMax. Defaults are collection_order and gridMax 3, so 4 products show in the default hero + grid layout (single_hero shows 1). A single product-shaped target shows the hero only; a multi-target union never does. A bestseller, reviewed or newest sort re-sorts the pool after the rule action whenever rank data exists.recommendDecider.ts:117-141, 394-416, 427-462, 482-502; recommendationEngine.ts:446-458
8. FallbackOnly for a result that resolved but is empty: if fallbackOn is not false, global_fallback (when enabled and it finds products), else emptyFallbackCol, else safetyNetCol. The last two use in-stock products only, cap at gridMax, and are switched off by emptyFallback: "hide". A null resolution skips all of this today; this build changes that (safety net, below).runtime/QuizRuntime.tsx:1579-1595; recommendDecider.ts:522-538; recommendationEngine.ts:547-580

The rule predicate

ruleConditionsMatch (recommendDecider.ts:330-357) is the only definition of "this rule matches these answers", and it is identical in both styles: the style changes what a matching rule produces, never what matching means. The engine calls it through the private ruleMatches wrapper (recommendDecider.ts:359-361), which resolveTarget calls at recommendDecider.ts:229; the rule-impact endpoint calls it directly (app/routes/api.quizzes.rule-impact.tsx:94-96). Rule sentences, coverage, "never runs", Import validation, "Shown by rules" and the pill hover-lighting must use it, or pathAnalyzer functions built on it. The mock carries its own evaluators and none of them is the engine: coverage is showsRecs, rulesShowing, ruleCount, recMapped, ruleShows and recCovered; "never runs" is picksFor, holds, shadowedBy, overMax, overQ, impossible, deadCalc, deadWhy and deadTag (memoized per state by dwFp and DW); the check list is findings(). Do not port them. They are the reference for which cases must be caught and what the copy says (both quoted below); the implementation is a pathAnalyzer function over ruleConditionsMatch, and the mock's rule shape (conds, not, all per question) is not the doc's (conditions with per-row op, any_of, match).

Condition shapeMatches whenorigin/main
GroupingConditions are grouped by question; each group is judged on its own.recommendDecider.ts:335-340
is (default "all of")Every listed answer was picked. Only a multi-select can hold two or more picks; every other type records one answer.recommendDecider.ts:349-351; runtime/views/QuestionView.tsx:172
is, question listed in any_ofAt least one listed answer was picked. any_of on a one-answer group changes nothing.recommendDecider.ts:349-350
is_notNone of the listed answers was picked. A question the shopper skipped or never reached satisfies it. any_of is ignored for these conditions (probe: "is not b1, b2" with the question listed in any_of and b1 picked does not match; the noneSelected test at 343-347 runs before anyOf is consulted). This is why D12 needs no new storage: the stored shape is already unambiguous for an is-not row.recommendDecider.ts:213-216, 343-347; probe
Mixed is and is_not on one questionBoth parts hold: none of the "not" answers, plus all (or any) of the "is" answers.recommendDecider.ts:342-352; probe
Across questionsAND. match: "any" makes it OR. Under D13 the new build stops writing it (paste split, below); rules that already carry it keep working and keep it on edit.recommendDecider.ts:353-356; rulePaste.ts:326
Zero conditionsNever matches.recommendDecider.ts:228, 334
Condition on a deleted answer or questionis never holds; is_not always holds for that group, so the rule can catch nearly everyone. V6 blocks publish either way.pathAnalyzer.ts:151-178; quizValidation.ts:188-208; probe

The predicate's own tests (recommendDecider.test.ts:1006-1099) are the only pin today. They cover the skipped-question case for a pure is_not group (1064-1073) and a mixed group with any_of where the picked "not" answer vetoes (1075-1086). Two cases are not pinned and are added next to the probe table: (1) a pure is_not group on a question listed in any_of, with one of its answers picked, does not match; (2) a mixed group needs none of the "not" answers plus all of the "is" answers without any_of and at least one with it.

What Show, Pin and Hide do

A "base" exists when the shopper picked a mapped answer on the picking question. In Filter Results + Rules every shopper of a published quiz has one, because V1 to V4 require exactly one required, fully mapped picking question on every path (quizValidation.ts:124-185). In Rules only there is never a base, by construction: the engine does not read the picking question at all. So the two columns below are the two styles, not a normal case and an edge case.

Stored action (UI verb)Filter Results + Rules (with a base)Rules only (no base)What the shopper actually sees
absent (legacy replace; neither style's UI writes it)Returns the rule's recommendations as the result before the base is computed.The rule's recommendations, narrowed in Filter Results + Rules; settings, persona and analytics from the rule's first recommendation. Probe: X only.
show ("Show")Appends the rule's members that are not already in the pool to the end, in their own baked order, after narrowing, so they skip the shopper's narrowing answers.The rule's own recommendations are the result. This is the only verb the Rules-only rule window offers (D2, settled).Filter Results + Rules: under the default sort, appended products appear only when fewer than hero + gridMax in-stock products come before them; on a product-shaped base they never appear; a bestseller, reviewed or newest sort with rank data can pull them up. Probe: 5-product base shows p1 to p4 and never X; 1-product base shows p1, x1, x2; bestseller sort shows x1, x2, p1, p2. Rules only: the rule's products, sellable-filtered, hero and grid as configured.
prioritize ("Pin")Moves members already in the pool to the front, keeping their order. Never adds products.The rule's own recommendations become the result: indistinguishable from Show. The UI does not offer Pin here, but the engine must keep this path for rules that arrive by style switch or Import.Filter Results + Rules: pinned products lead only under collection_order; a non-default sort with rank data re-sorts them away. Probe: pin p5 gives p5, p1, p2, p3 by default and p1, p2, p3, p4 under bestseller; pinning products not in the pool changes nothing.
hide ("Hide")Removes the union of the rule's members from the narrowed pool.No result. Under this build that shopper gets the safety net, not a bare card. The UI does not offer Hide here; the engine must keep the path.Filter Results + Rules: the rest of the pool; if that is empty, the fallback chain runs and does not exclude the hidden products.

Refs: recommendDecider.ts:230-237 (replace), 261-284 (action rule with or without a base), 276-283 (the no-base path Rules only runs on), 301-317 (applyRuleAction), 394-416 and 447-449 (re-sort after the action), 439-442 (product-shaped base); recommendationEngine.ts:432-458; runtime/QuizRuntime.tsx:1586-1595.

No result versus an empty result

  • Null target. resolveTarget returns null when no rule matched and no picked answer on the picking question is mapped, or when a Hide rule matched with no base (recommendDecider.ts:278, 286). Today the engine then returns no decider payload (recommendationEngine.ts:393-398) and the runtime renders only a card reading "We couldn't find a perfect match for your answers. Try retaking the quiz with different choices." (no_results_match, runtime/chromeStrings.ts:48; runtime/QuizRuntime.tsx:1713-1721). There is no fallback. The email capture and loading gates sit inside the explained.decider branch (runtime/QuizRuntime.tsx:1579-1712), so that shopper also gets no capture and no loading beat. For decider docs, quiz_completed, recommendation_viewed and the session post fire only from DeciderResultView (runtime/views/DeciderViews.tsx:566-590), so the shopper is reported as quiz_abandoned when the page hides (runtime/QuizRuntime.tsx:673-687). This build replaces that bare card with the safety net for every decider doc (below).
  • Resolved but empty. A recommendation resolved but nothing is showable (empty group, narrowed to zero, hidden away, all unsellable). The normal result view renders with the fallback chain, or the same no-match line inside the view when no fallback finds products (runtime/views/DeciderViews.tsx:557-561, 766-770). Probe: hiding the whole base leaves an empty result with the decider payload present. This is already the safety-net behaviour the ruling asks for in Filter Results + Rules, and it stays.
  • In a published Filter Results + Rules quiz the null case cannot happen today (V1 to V4, above); it occurs in drafts and in previews, where a jump to the result substitutes the first mapped picking answer (runtime/QuizRuntime.tsx:1560-1578). In Rules only it is the normal outcome for every shopper no rule catches, which is why the safety net is part of D1 and not an afterthought.

Rules only today is a display lens; this build makes it an engine

The audit below is what origin/main does now. Every line of it is what the D1 work replaces.

  • The style lives in build_session.logic_style (quizSchema.ts:1708), is written only by the set-logic-style intent (funnelIntents.server.ts:1468-1481) and is stripped at publish with the rest of build_session (quizPublish.ts:803-816). The only reader is Step3Shell (onboarding/questionsLogicV3/Step3Shell.tsx:141); no engine, validation or publish code reads it.
  • In Rules only every question displays as Info (displayRole, logicTab/LogicQuestionWidget.tsx:89-97), but the stored roles still drive the shopper: the hidden decides question is the base (recommendDecider.ts:242-259) and hidden filter questions still narrow (filterMatching.ts:145-151; recommendationEngine.ts:420-428). Publish still needs one required, fully mapped picking question (quizValidation.ts:124-185).
  • The builder twin never enters the lens. BuilderSettings renders LogicTabCard without the optional logicStyle prop (app/components/studio/BuilderSettings.tsx:69; the prop at logicTab/LogicTabCard.tsx:105, rulesOnly = logicStyle === "rules" at 112), so the main builder's Logic view shows Picks and Narrows roles again for a quiz whose funnel chose Rules only. D6 parks closing that gap; see "What is parked" below.
  • RulesSetupScaffold writes one action: "show" rule per answer of the chosen question, which defaults to the picking question itself (logicTab/RulesSetupScaffold.tsx:34-41, 54-66). Those rules append to the hidden base, so with default settings, on a group with 4 or more in-stock products, they change nothing a shopper can see. After D1 the same rules become the result.
  • So the mock's Rules-only copy is a promise the shipped code does not yet keep: "Every outcome is a rule you write: which products to show, based on how someone answered." (STYLE_HINT.rules, rendered by hintHTML(); the title menu's row sub-label in styleMenu() repeats "every outcome is a rule you write") and "No rules yet. In Rules only every result comes from a rule, so nothing shows until you create one." (the .rempty2 empty state built by rulesBand()). D1 makes that copy true. The BuildSession comment that filter values are "kept on the doc and ignored" in Rules only (quizSchema.ts:1701-1705) becomes true at the same time, and moves to the new field.

What copy, counts and checks must say

SurfaceMust match this engine factorigin/main
Rule numbers, order, ↑/↓ and DuplicateArray order is priority and only the first matching rule applies. Rules never stack: a shopper caught by rule 2 gets nothing from rule 5 even when rule 5 also matches. No copy may imply that rules combine. Partial overlap between rules is normal and is not flagged; only full shadowing is ("never runs"). Two consequences of D11: every ↑/↓ reorder changes which rule wins, so the analyzer and the AI-review hash must both re-run on it; and a rule duplicated directly below its source is by definition fully shadowed, so it gets the ordinary "never runs · rule N catches them first" tag the moment it appears. That tag is correct, not an error state, and the copy must not read like one.recommendDecider.ts:226-240; pathReportMeta.ts:37-48
"is not" in sentences, the Table and Import"not (A or B)" means none of those answers was picked, which includes shoppers who skipped the question or were routed past it. Never word it as "answered something else". There is no "not all of": on an is-not row the any/all toggle is hidden and the row means none of these answers (D12).recommendDecider.ts:213-216, 343-347

The live and mock strings are identical today: the mock's VERBS constant (show "these become the results", pin "these move to the top", hide "these never show"), rendered by modalHTML() and read by sentence() for the verb chip, matches logicTab/CreateRuleModal.tsx:70-74 word for word. Hide never covers. The engine changes to build

1. The style becomes a document field (D1)

The style has to survive publish and reach the shopper's browser, so it stops being draft-only state and becomes a schema field on the quiz, next to logic_model.

// quizSchema.ts, beside logic_model (quizSchema.ts:1992)
// LOGIC STYLE: which method this decider quiz uses to decide a result.
//   "attributes" → Filter Results + Rules: picking question + filter roles.
//   "rules"      → Rules only: the first matching rule IS the result.
// .optional() and NEVER .default() (the dual-model discipline): absent
// round-trips absent, and absent means Filter Results + Rules, which is
// exactly what every existing decider doc does today.

2. The Rules-only engine branch (D1)

In Rules only the first matching rule decides. A Show or Pin rule's recommendations are the result, which is the existing no-base path (recommendDecider.ts:276-283). A legacy replace rule is unchanged. A first-matching Hide, and no match at all, resolve to nothing and hand the shopper to the safety net. Stored decides and filter roles stay on the doc and are ignored, so switching styles is lossless in both directions. A doc without the field, or with logic_style: "attributes", resolves exactly as it does today; that covers every existing decider doc, published or draft.

3. The safety net, in both styles (D1 safety net)

Settled. A shopper no rule matches gets the safety net the Results step already has, and the same net covers an empty result in Filter Results + Rules. One behaviour for both styles. This is a shopper-facing runtime change and carries the full proof the repo demands: legacy quizzes byte-identical, DOM-identical /q output for the published decider fixtures, full e2e, screenshot review, written 2-lens review, and the byte pin after deploy.

The chain itself already exists and does not change: global_fallback when it is enabled and finds products, else emptyFallbackCol, else safetyNetCol, all in-stock only, capped at gridMax, and switched off by emptyFallback: "hide" (runtime/QuizRuntime.tsx:1586-1595; recommendDecider.ts:522-538). What changes is that a null resolution reaches it instead of falling through to the bare no-match card.

Build it as an empty payload, not a second branch. In a decider doc whose target does not resolve, the engine returns a decider payload built on the global settings (resolveRecPageGlobal, recommendDecider.ts:181-185) with no products and no targetId, instead of returning none. The existing explained.decider branch (runtime/QuizRuntime.tsx:1579-1712) then runs unchanged and the shopper gets the fallback chain, the loading beat, the email capture and the completion analytics. This makes decider.targetId nullable (recommendationEngine.ts:160-179) and changes DeciderResultView's analytics payload, which stops sending resolved_target_id for these shoppers (runtime/views/DeciderViews.tsx:576-583).

The alternative, a second fallback call inside the else if (isDecider) branch at runtime/QuizRuntime.tsx:1713-1721, is smaller but keeps everything else broken for that shopper: still no capture, no loading beat, no quiz_completed or recommendation_viewed, and a quiz_abandoned event when the tab closes (runtime/QuizRuntime.tsx:673-687; runtime/views/DeciderViews.tsx:566-590). In Rules only that is every shopper no rule catches, so it is not enough. Build the empty payload.

  • Scope. Apply it to every decider doc, not only Rules only. That is what "one behaviour for both styles" means, and it is what makes the change provable: a published Filter Results + Rules quiz can never reach the null branch today (V1 to V4), so its rendered /q output must be byte-identical after the change. Any diff on the decider fixtures is a bug, not an intended change.
  • Legacy. Untouched by construction: the branch sits inside isDecider, and legacy docs never enter it (recommendationEngine.ts:392, 494-529).
  • The merchant needs somewhere to set it. With default settings nothing is configured: global_fallback is off by default and the two fallback collections are unset (quizSchema.ts:1340; recommendDecider.ts:526-537), so an unmatched shopper sees the no-match line inside the result view until the merchant configures a fallback. The decider funnel has no live fallback chooser today: FallbackSection (the chooser that writes doc.global_fallback, onboarding/resultsGuided/FallbackSection.tsx:41-50) is rendered only by LogicScroll (onboarding/questionsLogicV3/logic/LogicScroll.tsx:398), which has no importer on origin/main; ResultsGuided records that the section left the Results step (ResultsGuided.tsx:513-515, owner 2026-08-18, "FallbackSection.tsx stays on disk"); and RecPageV2Panel's "Fallback collection" and "Safety-net collection" pickers (onboarding/RecPageV2Panel.tsx:472-488) render only inside RecommendationStage (RecommendationStage.tsx:112), which Step1Funnel mounts for non-decider docs only (Step1Funnel.tsx:328-346 sends decider docs to ResultsGuided). Build the net over the chain as it stands (global_fallback, then emptyFallbackCol, then safetyNetCol), do not invent a control for it, and raise the unconfigured-net gap with the owner in your report. Putting a chooser back on the Results step would need the owner's explicit OK and is not part of this work. Scope, sources and ground rules and Connections say the same thing; nothing here blocks the ship.
Highest-risk edit class. QuizRuntime.tsx, views/DeciderViews.tsx and recommendationEngine.ts's payload shape are app/components/runtime/** and the /q bundle. Decompose, don't rewrite. Render the same doc on the local build and on the pre-change deploy and diff normalized outerHTML, for the byte-pinned legacy doc cmqqcb0ao004mqvkwjug7t0ya and the published decider fixtures cmqwd15f0001aqvl19onkpwm6 and cmr3ku9kb0014qvl1ub8n5092 (e2e/README.md:157-163). Every diff must be exactly the intended change, and on those three there should be none.

4. The style-aware Tier-1 report (D3)

One report drives the CTA, the check popover and publish, and it branches on the style. "Fix N issues" counts blocking findings only; the popover groups them per question or per rule. The report must never read safer than the publish gate: anything validateQuiz or publishQuiz throws on must appear as a block in the report, in both styles. The full finding list, severities and copy live in checks-and-continue; what this section owes is the engine truth behind each one.

"No rule that can show anything" is the coverage helper run over the whole doc: at least one rule that lists a recommendation, can run, and whose verb adds under this style (copy table above). "Missing its answers" is the zero-conditions case the engine already skips (recommendDecider.ts:228). It blocks in Rules only, where such a rule is a whole result that can never appear, and a warning in Filter Results + Rules, where the base still carries the shopper.

5. No first-entry chooser (D5)

The style resolves without asking, and nothing is written to the quiz on page load.

  1. doc.logic_style, if set.
  2. Else build_session.logic_style, the migration read.
  3. Else inference: any question with role: "filter" means Filter Results + Rules; any rule and no filter role means Rules only.
  4. Else Filter Results + Rules.

The inference is already written and already correct (Step3Shell.tsx:150-154); the change is that its final return null becomes return "attributes", and the logicStyle === null branch that mounts the chooser (Step3Shell.tsx:422-427) goes with it. Delete LogicStyleChooser.tsx and with it the inert "Point based" row, which renders, is clickable, writes nothing and toasts "Point based isn't available yet." (LogicStyleChooser.tsx:88-89, 105, 169-170). The local localStyle override goes with the chooser. It exists because build_session is server-owned and never refreshes mid-session, so without it the style bar's Switch appeared to do nothing (Step3Shell.tsx:142-149). The document field has no such problem: the switch commits setLogicStyle and the client doc carries the new style straight through the remount, so there is no second in-session override to build.

Acceptance: loading the Logic step on a fresh decider quiz issues no mutation and no intent, and the step renders Filter Results + Rules. Loading it on a quiz with one rule and no filter role renders Rules only and still writes nothing. The first write happens when the merchant uses the title switch.

6. Toast with one action, and inverse-mutation Undo (D7)

Undo is how a destructive edit stays safe in a surface with no confirm dialogs, so the shared toast grows exactly one action.

  • Extend app/components/qz-toast.tsx: an optional action (label plus handler), an optional duration overriding AUTO_DISMISS_MS (qz-toast.tsx:19), and keyboard reach so the action can be taken without a pointer. The live region is already there (role="status" aria-live="polite", qz-toast.tsx:68); the work is making the action part of what gets announced and focusable, not adding the region.
  • Record the exception. The file's own header states the design-system rule this breaks: "Not clickable, no actions: if an action is needed, it isn't a toast" (qz-toast.tsx:15-18). Replace it with the dated owner exception (2026-09-22, D7) naming the one permitted action, so the next reader does not "fix" it back.
  • Undo is inverse mutations, never a snapshot. Capture what the mutation removed, then apply the inverse against the latest document via getLatestDoc(), the same post-await rule PasteRulesModal.handleCreate already follows (PasteRulesModal.tsx:108-124). A whole-document snapshot would silently roll back every unrelated edit the merchant made while the toast was up, including autosaved ones.
  • Restore a rule at its index. Array order is priority (recommendDecider.ts:226-240), so an Undo that appends a restored rule changes which rule wins for some shopper. The inverse of a delete is "insert this rule object at index i"; several deletes in a row accumulate into one Undo that restores all of them at their original indexes.
  • Providers. Every useQzToast() call outside a provider silently resolves to the no-op default (qz-toast.tsx:31), so Undo would be invisible and the delete unrecoverable. The standalone routes have providers (studio.tsx:31, studio_.$id.tsx:117, studio_.onboarding_.$quizId.tsx:38); the embedded twins do not (D21, below).

7. The announced mapping clear (D9)

Moving "Picks results" to another question still clears both questions' answer mappings: moveDecider demotes the old decider to qualifier and drops target_id and target_ids from every answer on both questions, including a pre-existing mapping on the promoted one (mutations/deciderMutations.ts:187-238). That behaviour is correct and stays; what changes is that it is announced and reversible.

  • The mutation stays pure and unchanged. The caller captures, before the call: the old decider's node id and role, the new question's prior role, and every (answerId, target_ids) pair about to be dropped on both questions.
  • A toast names what was cleared, in the mock's shape: "Q1's 6 recommendations were removed". Its Undo restores the role and every target.
  • One path serves the role menu, the Table and Import. Three callers, one helper, one toast, one Undo. No confirm dialog.
  • The toast must not claim rules were cleared. moveDecider deliberately leaves decision_rules untouched (deciderMutations.ts:183-185), so rules that referenced the old decider's answers survive and surface through the analyzer as V7/V8 findings. Say "recommendations", not "logic".

8. What the rule rows do (D11)

View work, with two engine consequences worth pinning. Rows are clicked to edit; each row carries a trash icon and ↑/↓ revealed on hover and on keyboard focus, so rules reorder without a mouse. Duplicate moves into the rule window's top row next to Delete rule; the live row's ✎ Edit is replaced by the row click.

  • A ↑/↓ reorder changes which rule wins. Re-run the analyzer on every reorder, so the memo key must include rule order (today's card memoizes per doc, logicTab/LogicTabCard.tsx:206-225), and make the AI-review hash change too, which it does not today (below).
  • A duplicated rule placed directly below its source is fully shadowed by it and correctly tags "never runs · rule N catches them first" at once. Expected, not an error; the merchant edits the copy and the tag clears.

9. "is not" never combines with "all of" (D12)

On an is-not row the any/all toggle is hidden and the row means none of these answers. Sentences read "not (A or B)". Import rejects NOT (A AND B) with a named reason. No new storage: the engine already ignores any_of for is_not conditions, because the noneSelected test runs before anyOf is consulted (recommendDecider.ts:343-347, probe). So a stored document that carries a question in any_of alongside an is-not group is already unambiguous; render it as none-of and leave the inert key where it is rather than rewriting documents to tidy it.

10. Paste splits a cross-question "or" (D13)

The parser stays frozen. parsePastedRules keeps returning match: "any" when the connectors between questions are all "or" (rulePaste.ts:317-327), and keeps refusing a line that mixes "and" with "or" across questions. The split happens where the parsed lines become rules, in PasteRulesModal.handleCreate (PasteRulesModal.tsx:108-124): a line carrying match: "any" emits one createDecisionRule per question group, adjacent, with the same action and the same target_ids, instead of one rule carrying match.

  • Identical under first-match-wins. Whichever group a shopper satisfies, the first of the adjacent rules that matches wins, and every one of them carries the same verb and the same recommendations, so the result is the same. Only matchedRuleId in analytics differs, which no merchant surface reads.
  • The preview list shows the split, so the merchant sees N rules before committing, not one rule that turns into N.
  • Existing rules keep working. Rules already carrying match: "any" render faithfully and keep it when edited. Build requirement updateDecisionRule uses presence semantics for match: if ("match" in patch) stores "any" and deletes the key for every other value, including undefined (mutations/deciderMutations.ts:294, 310-313). So a rule editor that always spreads a match key into its patch silently converts a stored OR rule into an AND rule, which changes who it matches. Either omit the key or pass the rule's existing value; pin a test on editing a match: "any" rule's recommendation and asserting match survives. overbroadRules (pathAnalyzer.ts:307-326) stays as its own reason for exactly those rules.

11. "+ Add recommendations" writes through ensure-targets (D15)

The existing endpoint gains one kind and is otherwise reused as-is. ResourceSchema.kind is z.enum(["tag", "collection", "product", "metafield"]) and the body takes resources: z.array(ResourceSchema).min(1).max(12) (app/routes/api.categories.ensure-targets.tsx:29, 37); add "group", which copies an existing group's membership into a quiz-scoped row the way Step 1 does. Tag keys normalize to Step-1 slugs. Rows are always created quiz-scoped, reusing before creating (the endpoint's existing quiz-scoped-then-shop-global lookup, lines 80-111). Batches stay at the endpoint's existing 12 per call. The call is additive and idempotent, works in the funnel and later in the builder, and its rows survive re-grouping.

Engine acceptance: a rule whose only recommendation was created by "+ Add recommendations" publishes. Publish collects every rule target (collectDeciderTargetIds, quizPublish.ts:128-146) and bakes its ordered membership by dereferencing the fetched row (quizPublish.ts:515, 532), so a row this endpoint can create but publish cannot find would throw at publish time. Pin that round trip as a test.

12. The spreadsheet carries identity (D16)

Export and Import share one file format, and that file is also the template.

  • Identity in every cell that names a thing. Every "When they answer" cell reads Qn = answer. The Answers sheet gains a trailing do-not-edit "Answer ID" column, the Rules sheet a "Rule ID" column. A re-import updates the rule and the answer the ids name, rather than matching on text and creating duplicates.
  • Answers updates in place and never adds or deletes answers. The Recommendations sheet is read-only; edits to it are reported as ignored, not silently dropped. A missing column means "leave unchanged", never "clear".
  • The Rules sheet is all-or-nothing. A rejected Rules sheet leaves decision_rules untouched. This is an engine-safety rule, not a convenience: rules are a priority-ordered array, so a partial import would reorder which rule wins for shoppers the merchant was not editing.
  • Import runs the same validators as the UI, because it is the one path that can write a rule the rule window would refuse: reject NOT (A AND B) with a named reason (D12); reject an all-of listing more answers than max_selections allows on that multi-select (the impossible reason below); reject a condition on a deleted answer or question (V6's shape, quizValidation.ts:188-208). Every rejection names the sheet, the row and the reason.
  • Export is the template. Label the affordance so it reads as both: "Export" downloads the current logic as the template. On a quiz with no rules, Export still writes the sheets with their headers, the id columns and one example row marked EXAMPLE in the do-not-edit Rule ID column, so a merchant who wants to build in a spreadsheet has the format and can import it back. There is no second file format.
  • Library: SheetJS CE 0.20.3, from the official SheetJS CDN tarball, loaded as a lazy chunk. Never the npm xlsx 0.18.5 build, which carries published CVEs, and Import parses files a merchant supplies, so this is a parser handling untrusted input. origin/main has no xlsx dependency in package.json at all, so this is a clean first choice, not a downgrade.

13. Sentence grammar (D17)

Rule sentences stay verb-first and answers-only ("Show dryness when ..."), with parentheses around multi-answer groups, bold joins, "not (...)" for negated groups and full-text tooltips on truncated answers. A question label is added only when the same answer text exists on another question. The Table and the export always use the machine form, "Q7 = Yes".

The generator reads the document's shape (conditions with per-row op, plus any_of and match), not the mock's, and its join words mean exactly what the predicate does: inside one question group "and" is all-of and "or" is any-of (recommendDecider.ts:349-351); between groups "and" is AND and "or" appears only for a stored match: "any" rule (recommendDecider.ts:353-356). A negated group is always "not (A or B)", never "not all of", and never "answered something else" (D12, and the skipped-question fact at recommendDecider.ts:213-216).

14. The renames (D18)

Through shared constants, everywhere, including the builder's Rules inspector and the pinned tests. "Attributes + Rules" becomes "Filter Results + Rules"; "Asked only" becomes "Info only"; "Recommendations from step 1" becomes "Recommendations"; "+ Add rule" becomes "Create a rule" / "+ Add"; the empty Picks cell and its picker both read "Choose a result". Internal words never reach the merchant: decider, bucket, branch, boost, weight, score, "Tag buckets".

A rename cannot reach the engine, and that is the point: stored values do not change. role: "qualifier" stays "qualifier" on the document and only its label moves (quizSchema.ts:362). Sites on origin/main: Step3Shell.tsx:482; onboarding/questionsLogicV3/logic/QuestionSection.tsx:427; app/components/studio/ContextPanel.tsx:932 with its pinned tests ContextPanel.rules.test.tsx:99, 108; logicTab/Explainers.tsx:173; logicTab/logicTabFields.ts:596; logicTab/LogicQuestionWidget.tsx:59, 70-75, 775; logicTab/LogicTabMenus.tsx:460; logicTab/LogicTabCard.tsx:34, 186; and the schema comments at quizSchema.ts:1702. LogicStyleChooser.tsx:64 is deleted by D5 rather than renamed.

15. Live surfaces that survive the mock (D19)

The mock does not draw these; they ship anyway, in the mock's visual language: the attribute picker on the Narrows flip; every rule-flag reason rendered in the mock's tag style (half-built, dead, target deleted, fires for everyone); product-count popovers on chips; the product-group picker's kind filters and drill-in. Drop the "won't work as written" banner. "Explore every path" stays builder-only.

Those flags are pathAnalyzer output rendered today at logicTab/LogicTabCard.tsx:206-226, and "fires for everyone" is overbroadRules (pathAnalyzer.ts:307-326), which keeps its own copy and is not folded into "never runs"; see the reason table below for why the two are different claims.

16. The embedded twins get the toast provider (D21)

Scope: the provider only. QzToastProvider wraps the standalone routes (app/routes/studio.tsx:31, studio_.$id.tsx:117, studio_.onboarding_.$quizId.tsx:38) but appears in none of the embedded ones (app/routes/app.tsx, app.quizzes.$id.tsx, app.quizzes.$id_.studio.tsx on origin/main). Every useQzToast() consumer in the embedded tree (LogicTabCard, CreateRuleModal, LogicTabMenus, QuestionWindow, PasteRulesModal, LogicTableTab) therefore resolves to the no-op default context (qz-toast.tsx:31), so an embedded delete is silent today and, once Undo lives on the toast, would be unrecoverable. Add the provider. The hardcoded /studio links and giving embedded decider quizzes the new Logic view are separate tasks and are not part of this work.

17. "never runs": extend shadowedRules

V8 (pathReport.ts:236) and today's rule-row chip (logicTab/LogicTabCard.tsx:213) both read pathAnalyzer.shadowedRules. Extend that one function so the report and every rule list stay one computation, in both styles. Today it flags a lower rule only when every condition key (question, answer, op) of a higher rule also appears in it, and it skips any lower rule that is match-any or has an any-of group of two or more answers (effectivelyConjunctive and shadowedRules, pathAnalyzer.ts:249-299). It ignores the verb, which is correct: first match wins whatever the action, in both styles. Catch-all"Q1 any of" all six answers above "Q3 is One or two" (case G)New missedflag, only when Q1 is always answered; "rule 1 catches them first"
Not shadowed (control)"Q5 all of Vitamin C, Retinol" above "Q5 any of Vitamin C, Retinol"not flaggedmust stay unflagged; mock: no tag
  • Sound, never optimistic. Flag rule i only when every shopper who can match it also matches an earlier rule that has at least one condition. A false "never runs" on a working rule is worse than a missed one (pathAnalyzer.ts:198-200, 273). In Rules only a false flag is worse still, because the flagged rule is a whole result the merchant may then delete.
  • Use the predicate. Evaluate candidate answer sets with ruleConditionsMatch; don't re-derive set logic. Only questions named by rules 1 to i matter. Candidate states per question: on a one-answer type, one named answer, or an unnamed answer when one exists; on a multi-select, any subset of the named answers that fits min_selections/max_selections once unnamed answers are counted (at least one pick in total when answered); plus "unanswered" when the question is optional or a route can reach the end without it. Treating questions independently only adds combinations, so a flag stays sound. Match-any rules and any-of groups then need no special case, so the effectivelyConjunctive skip can go. The mock's picksFor and holds are this enumeration in the mock's rule shape; the walk itself (shadowedBy) keeps the earlier rules still alive per branch, stops a branch once the first live earlier rule is fully decided, tries each earlier rule alone before the union, and returns the catching rule indexes.
  • "Always answered." The mock adds the "unanswered" state when the question has an answer no rule names or when an earlier answer routes past it (picksFor); it has no required flag, because the mock has no optional questions, so its catch-all flag can be optimistic on an optional question. The live definition wins: a question is always answered when it is required (required defaults true, quizSchema.ts:211) and the stop-at walk from the intro that never passes the question reaches no result or end, the primitive V2 already uses (stopAtWalk, pathAnalyzer.ts:90-101). Branch nodes count as edges in that walk (outboundTargets, pathAnalyzer.ts:30), matching how the runtime routes (routing facts, below).
  • Cost. Multi-select candidates grow as 2^k. Walk only branches where rule i holds, drop earlier rules that fail on a branch, and stop a branch once an earlier rule fully holds. B12's measurement of this walk is about 8 ms at 25 rules and 131 ms at 40 rules naming up to 10 answers each. Cap the work: the mock stops at 200,000 candidate combinations and then shows no tag (shadowedBy returns null), which is sound but silent. Fall back to today's subset test at the cap instead, which is also sound and keeps the coverage origin/main has; say so in a comment. Compute once per document change, keyed on the rules and their order plus each question's type, min, max, answer count and routes (the mock's dwFp; the card already memoizes per doc, logicTab/LogicTabCard.tsx:206-225), never per render, and the key must change on a ↑/↓ reorder (D11).
  • Not a shortcut: don't build this on enumeratePaths or the rule-impact endpoint. Both fork one answer per question with no Skip branch and stop at 2,000 paths (pathEnumeration.ts:24-27, 121-123, 190-220). enumeratePaths does resolve each path with resolveTarget, so it records wins (140-148); the rule-impact endpoint counts ruleConditionsMatch hits over those paths, so it counts matches rather than wins, refuses all-of groups as "not estimable", and has no client caller (app/routes/api.quizzes.rule-impact.tsx:66-96).
  • One format everywhere. The brief says "never runs · rule N catches them first"; the current mock renders that when one earlier rule suffices and "never runs · rules 1, 3 and 4 catch them first" only when a union is needed (deadCalc joins the list with nlist; deadTag prefixes "never runs · "). Use exactly that: name the single catching rule when one is enough, the union otherwise, and let the report, the rule rows and the Table print the same string.
  • Structured output. Return the catching rule ids and a reason code, not only a message, so V8, the tag in every rule list and Table, and the coverage helper each render their own copy. Today's analyzer messages are merchant-facing in the report and use em dashes and "fire".

18. New dead-rule reasons in pathAnalyzer

These feed V7 and V9 (pathReport.ts:230-237), the tags in every rule list, and the coverage helper (a flagged rule never counts). Severities are D3's, stated in the report table above: block in Rules only when a rule is missing its answers or its recommendations, warn otherwise, and the same warnings in Filter Results + Rules. The mock computes one reason per rule (deadCalc, cached by deadWhy) in this order: incomplete, impossible all-of, shadowed; deadTag is its single renderer, called by rulesBand() (the Rules-only list) and ruleRows() (the Filter rules column), and the Table's Rules sheet mutes the row through the same flag (muted: !!deadWhy(i) in sheets()) without printing the reason; the built Table prints it. Build the same shape: one analyzer call returning a reason per rule, one renderer, both styles.

Routing facts to keep

  • A multi-select routes by its first checked answer in authored order (runtime/views/QuestionView.tsx:409-411, 422-424). Don't change it: QuestionView also serves legacy docs, and the byte pin hashes the published JSON, so it cannot catch a behaviour change.
  • Skip on an optional question records no answer and follows the question's default edge (runtime/views/QuestionView.tsx:114-118); that shopper satisfies every "is not" on the question.
  • An answer follows the edge on its own handle, else the handle-less edge, else the first edge (nextNodeFor, recommendationEngine.ts:881-895). The runtime and path enumeration do not call it directly: they call resolveNextStep (recommendationEngine.ts:1023-1043; runtime/QuizRuntime.tsx:1034; pathEnumeration.ts:203), which wraps it and walks branch nodes by their slot until it reaches a non-branch node. The "always answered" primitive and the new route-based dead reason must model branch nodes the same way; outboundTargets in pathAnalyzer already follows every edge (pathAnalyzer.ts:30).
  • setAnswerRoute refuses any route that would revisit a question (mutations/edgeMutations.ts:106-111; wouldCreateRevisit, pathAnalyzer.ts:439-446), so every route is forward-only.
  • "Straight to the results" routes to the result node (logicTab/LogicTabMenus.tsx:377-388). In Filter Results + Rules, that route from any question before the picking question, or a skip past it, fails V2 decider_bypass (quizValidation.ts:148-174; its answer-level twin feeds the report, pathAnalyzer.ts:119-142 and pathReport.ts:161-180). In Rules only V2 does not apply, but the same route can make a rule's answers unreachable (the route-based dead reason above).

AI review staleness

pathReportHash sorts the outcome keys and the rule shapes before hashing; a rule shape is id, match, any_of and conditions, and an outcome key carries target_id only (pathReportMeta.ts:29-31, 37-48; pathAnalyzer.ts:412, 427). So reordering rules, changing a verb, or adding a second recommendation to a rule or an answer leaves a Tier-2 AI review looking current. Reorder is now a primary interaction (D11), so include each rule's position and action, the full ruleTargets list, every picking answer's answerTargets, and logic_style. The client and the server share the function (app/components/shared/health/usePathQuality.ts:35-36, 47; app/routes/api.path-quality.tsx:120), so they stay in step. Every stored review reads stale once after the change ships; that is expected. This lands even though the AI review is not surfaced in the new step (D4, parked): the hash is what keeps a later review honest.

Gating and the risk procedure

  • Every new branch in the engine, validation, publish, analyzer and mutations starts from logic_model === "decider", like the existing gates (recommendationEngine.ts:392; quizValidation.ts:113; quizPublish.ts:130, 482, 635; the analyzer runs only from decider-gated call sites, pathAnalyzer.ts:21-23). Rules-only branches also require logic_style === "rules", and an absent field means Filter Results + Rules, which is today's behaviour. The legacy walkLadder path (recommendationEngine.ts:494-529) is not touched.
  • New schema fields are .optional(), never .default() (CLAUDE.md on origin/main, the dual-model split; quizSchema.ts:1988-1992).
  • Engine files in app/lib/ ship in the /q bundle, and the byte pin proves only that the legacy JSON did not change, not what any quiz does. So for the D1 branch, the safety net, or any engine edit: pin the probe cases as unit tests first; prove DOM-identical /q output (render the same doc on the local build and on the pre-change deploy, diff normalized outerHTML) for the byte-pinned legacy doc cmqqcb0ao004mqvkwjug7t0ya and the published decider fixtures cmqwd15f0001aqvl19onkpwm6 and cmr3ku9kb0014qvl1ub8n5092 (e2e/README.md:157-163), where any diff must be exactly the intended change; run the full npm run e2e; review /q screenshots; write the 2-lens adversarial self-review; run the gate chain unpiped before the commit (npm run typecheck && npm test -- --run && npm run build && npm run lint && node scripts/check-tokens.mjs); after deploy the byte pin must still start c02ccaec98a0fe9e (CLAUDE.md on origin/main, working agreements).
  • QuizRuntime.tsx and views/DeciderViews.tsx are app/components/runtime/**, the highest-risk edit class: decompose, don't rewrite (CLAUDE.md on origin/main).
  • Ship order that keeps each proof small: (1) the schema field and its migration read, with no reader in the engine, which is inert and provable by tests alone; (2) the analyzer and check work, which touches no runtime file; (3) the Rules-only resolveTarget branch plus validation and publish, gated on a field no existing doc carries; (4) the safety net, the only runtime commit, with the full proof above.

Checks, the Fix-N gate, the check popover and Continue

This section covers five things. First, the one style-aware report that decides what stops a merchant leaving the Logic step and what only warns, in both styles. Second, how "Fix N issues to continue" and its popover behave. Third, the publish gate, which must change in the same commit or a Rules-only quiz can never be published. Fourth, the runtime safety net, which changes what the checks are allowed to promise. Fifth, what must change so that moving between steps never loses an edit or the saved style. Diagnostics and builder parity are parked; both are named below with what to do meanwhile.

What this section builds

Written in the indicative. A parenthesised decision id points at the reasoning in Owner decisions; it is not a sign that anything is still being weighed.

  • One report, style-aware (D3). buildTier1Report takes the style as an input and drives the CTA label, the check popover and the publish gate. Rules only blocks on three things: no rules, no rule that can show anything, and a rule missing its answers or its recommendations. It skips the picking-question checks. Filter Results + Rules keeps today's blocks and adds route bypass and broken or impossible rules, with warnings for a recommendation nothing can show, a rule that never runs and an impossible all-of. N counts blocking findings only.
  • The style the report reads is the style the engine runs (D1, D5). The report reads doc.logic_style ?? "attributes", never the inferred screen style, so it can never read safer than the gate. Nothing is written on load.
  • The publish gate becomes style-aware in the same change (D1, D3). validateQuiz and the three decider gates in quizPublish learn the style, or nothing built in Rules only can ever be published.
  • The safety net (D1). A shopper no rule matches gets the same named fallback chain as an empty result in Filter Results + Rules. This is a shopper-facing runtime change and carries the full runtime proof.
  • The CTA and the popover. "Fix N issues to continue" toggles a 360px check popover anchored under it, and it is the only door: the Logic step publishes no bar health pill, and the "Diagnose & preview" modal is no longer mounted here (D4, D23).
  • Jump-links that actually land. A controlled selection and a focus request on LogicTabCard, a stable anchor on rule rows, and a recommendation link kind.
  • Continue and Back never lose an edit or the style. Single-flight saves, an awaitable flush, a beforeNavigate hook on the funnel bar, and navigation intents that change only build_session on a fresh read.
  • Copy through the shared constants (D18). Finding messages and check titles carry no internal words and no em dashes, and the pinned tests move to the constants.

Open items that touch this section. Do not pick them.

D2, the Filter Results + Rules half. In that style "Show" appends after the base pool and the results cap usually cuts it off, while the hint promises "these become the results" (recommendDecider.ts:301-317; Engine semantics steps 7 and 8). Blocks here: whether the Filter branch of the coverage helper may count a Show rule as covering a recommendation at all, and therefore the exact behaviour of the "“X” is never recommended" warning in Filter Results + Rules. Build that warning with the Filter branch as one clearly marked predicate that can take a second condition later, and say in your report that the predicate is waiting. Does not block: anything in Rules only, where D2 is settled (Show is the whole result), and none of the blocking checks in either style.

D10, question-type changes. What a type change does to answers and to the rules that referenced the dropped answers. Blocks here: nothing in the report itself. The checks already describe the outcome of a trim (V6 fires on a rule whose answer was deleted, and it fires differently for "is" and "is not"), so they stay correct whichever way D10 lands. What waits is the Undo that a trim will need and the copy that announces it. Do not wire the type-change path to a finding row until D10 is ruled.

D14, the second half. Whether used recommendations also move to the end of the tray, and how the armed state reads on the builder's editor surface. Blocks here: only the resting position of the tray after the "“X” is never recommended" row's fix action arms X. Arm it and scroll it into view; do not build a tray reorder on top of that action.

When a step needs one of these, stop, ask the owner and name the waiting step in your report. Never pick an option silently.

One report, one count

Exists Step3Shell builds one memoized report, buildTier1Report(doc, categories, productIndex) (Step3Shell.tsx:126-129; signature pathReport.ts:93-104). The bar override reads report.verdict.blocking for both the health pill and the Continue spec (Step3Shell.tsx:318-347), and DiagnoseModal gets the same instance as a prop (Step3Shell.tsx:536-548). verdict.blocking is the number of findings in block-severity checks (pathReport.ts:421-423).

  • Keep exactly one instance. The CTA label, the check popover and the builder's publish card all read it. Do not port the mock's findings() and blocking() as a second counter; port their shape, which is already style-aware, into buildTier1Report.
  • Style goes inside the report. The signature becomes buildTier1Report(doc, buckets, productIndex, { style }), and style joins the memo deps. The style type moves out of LogicStyleChooser.tsx (its only declaration today, imported at Step3Shell.tsx:34) into the resolver module that D5 introduces, because the chooser is deleted.
  • Rule tags and popover rows come from the same analyzer calls. A rule tagged "never runs" or "can never match" in the rules column always has a matching finding, and the two carry the same words.
  • Number questions the way the rail does. The report numbers them by node array order (pathReport.ts:112-114). The rail numbers them by flow order (orderedQuestions, questionOrder.ts:22-42). moveStep only rewires edges (questionMutations.ts:353-396), so the two disagree after any reorder, and the builder reorders this way (BuilderFlowTab.tsx:162-169; ContextPanel.tsx:1409). A probe on origin/main moved Q2 above Q1; afterwards the question the rail labels Q2 was reported as "Q1". Build the report's numbering from orderedQuestions.
  • Grouping never drops a finding the gate counts. Grouping changes how many rows the popover shows and what N reads; it never removes a blocking condition. Any check whose findings the gate also raises keeps at least one finding whenever the gate raises one.

The style the report reads is the style the engine runs

Two style values exist and they are not the same value (D1, D5).

  • The screen style is resolveLogicStyle(doc): doc.logic_style, then build_session.logic_style (migration only), then inference, then Filter Results + Rules (Data model). It decides which screen renders.
  • The engine style is engineLogicStyle(doc) = doc.logic_style ?? "attributes", exported from the same module and defined in Data model, persistence and the mutations to add. The report, validateQuiz and the publish gate read it and nothing else reads it. An absent field means the shopper gets today's engine, so the report must check today's engine.

The two differ in exactly one situation: a draft that has rules, no question with a filter role and no saved logic_style. That draft opens on Rules only by inference (the live inference, Step3Shell.tsx:151-154) while its shoppers still run the picking question's mapping. Every draft whose style sits only in build_session.logic_style is in the same position until the merchant switches the style once.

  • The report keeps checking Filter Results + Rules for that draft. Its blocks are real: publish enforces them.
  • New A warning row always listed first names the mismatch: "This quiz still decides results the Filter Results + Rules way. Choose 'Rules only' in the title menu to save it." (proposed). Its action opens the header's "Logic style" menu with the current style focused. It never writes the style by itself, because the title menu is the one place the style is written (D5).
  • Every Filter block that fires alongside it carries the same explanation, so a merchant looking at a Rules-only screen is never told to fix a control that screen does not draw.
  • Nothing about this is written on page load, and no check ever writes to the quiz.

The publish gate becomes style-aware in the same change

Without this, nothing built in Rules only can be published at all. validateQuiz emits missing_decider for every doc with no deciding question (quizValidation.ts:125-134), and publishQuiz throws on any issue it returns (quizPublish.ts:407-414). Ship the gate change and the engine branch together, or a merchant who finishes a Rules-only quiz hits a wall at the last step of the funnel.

What blocks and what warns

Count rule (D3). N is the number of blocking findings after grouping.

  • When one check fires on several answers of the same question, they become one finding, for example "Q1 · 3 answers have no recommendation".
  • V2 is the exception: one finding per route, because each route is a separate fix.
  • Rule findings group per rule. A rule that is both broken and shadowed shows one row per check, never one row per condition.
  • Warnings and notes never change N.
  • Rows list blocking findings first, then warnings, then notes. Within each group they follow quiz order: question number, then rule number. The style-mismatch warning is the one exception and sits at the top of the warnings.

Today the count is higher than the rule above gives. V4 emits one finding per unmapped answer (probe: 3 unmapped answers read "Fix 3 issues"), and V2 over-reports (below).
