Why V12's gap warns in Rules only. A band gap means a shopper lands on a slider value that selects no answer. In Filter Results + Rules that shopper reaches no mapping and no route, so it blocks, as it does today. In Rules only it means the rules that needed that band cannot fire for them, and the safety net now catches exactly that shopper. It is a real authoring mistake and it is not one of D3's three Rules-only blocks, so it warns. It is UI-only in both styles: the publish gate has no band check, so warning here can never read safer than the gate.

V2: report the route, not every answer upstream of it

Today V2 flags every answer from which some path can finish without meeting the picking question (answersReachDecider, pathAnalyzer.ts:119-142; pathReport.ts:161-174). Its copy says that answer "ends the quiz".

Probe on origin/main: Q1 leads to Q2, Q2 leads to Q3 (the picking question), and only Q2 "B2" routes to the results. That produces four blocking findings ("Fix 4 issues"). Three of them sit on Q1 answers that only lead to Q2.

Flag the answers whose own route causes the skip: a route to the results, or to a question numbered after the picking question. Keep the three guarantees pathReport.test.ts pins:

  • Answers that feed a branch whose lane skips the picking question are still flagged (pathReport.test.ts:106-131).
  • Only the skipping answer is flagged, not its siblings (pathReport.test.ts:185-199).
  • A skip with no answer to pin it on falls back to the gate's message (pathReport.ts:175-179; pathReport.test.ts:148-160).

If the refinement finds nothing while answersReachDecider or validateQuiz still sees a bypass, keep today's findings, so the count never drops below the gate. B17 is a mock-only defect: the live report already blocks bypasses. This change is about precision and copy.

V3 gets its fix control in the Logic step

Choosing "Picks results" forces required: true (setQuestionRole and moveDecider, deciderMutations.ts:15-51, 187-238). But moveDecider returns early when the question already picks (deciderMutations.ts:193), and the only Required control a decider quiz can reach is the builder inspector's "Answering" field (ContentTab.tsx:452-469). So in the funnel V3 is close to unreachable and has no fix, while the builder can still produce it on a hand-edited or inspector-edited doc.

Give the V3 row its own action, "Make it required", which calls a pure mutation that sets required: true on the picking question and commits it through useQuizDraft. The save pill shows at the row's target the way every other committed edit does (D8). Do not add a Required control to the Logic screen: the finding is the control.

V4 keeps blocking even when a rule covers the answer

This is deliberate. The gate requires every answer of the picking question to be mapped (quizValidation.ts:176-185), and the review rejected B42 as a design question. Keep it.

What “X” is never recommended counts

  • Iterate quiz-scoped recommendations only: Category rows with quizId set. The funnel's category list also carries every account group (funnelLoader.server.ts:81-96, 305-314), and all of those would read "never recommended". The tray already applies this filter (LogicQuestionWidget.tsx:155-172).
  • X counts as recommended when an answer of the picking question lists it (answerTargets), or when a rule that can fire shows it. Decide the second half with the shared style-aware coverage helper, which also feeds the strip's fraction and the Table's "Shown by rules" column (Rules only · Edit, section 3.1). One helper, one answer: the warning and the strip can never disagree.
  • Rules only. A stored Hide never counts as coverage: under first-match-wins a matching Hide resolves to no target (recommendDecider.ts:278, inside the no-base path at :276-284), the shopper falls to the safety net and no later rule runs for them. New rules in this style can only be Show (D2).
  • Filter Results + Rules. A Pin rule only moves products an answer already brought in; it never adds new ones (applyRuleAction, recommendDecider.ts:301-317). So Pin alone never makes X appear there, and B10's fix counts only Show in that style. Whether a Show rule counts at all is D2's open half: build the Filter branch as one marked predicate that can take a second condition later, and do not let that condition leak into the Rules-only branch.

Two rule checks follow the settled rule grammar

  • "is not" never combines with "all of" (D12). The impossible all-of check runs over "is" groups only, which is what it already means, and the sentence a finding quotes reads "not (A or B)" for a negated group (D17). No new storage and no new check: the rule window stops offering the combination, so the check can only meet it on a rule written before this change or imported from a file, and V6's "matches every shopper" message already covers the dangerous half.
  • Cross-question "or" stops being created (D13). "Paste rules" splits such a rule into adjacent rules with the same verb and the same recommendations before it commits, which behaves identically under first-match-wins. The analyzer's existing discipline stays: V7 skips match: "any" rules on purpose (deadRules, pathAnalyzer.ts:201), and V8 only tests a lower rule that is effectively conjunctive (pathAnalyzer.ts:249, 286), because an any-rule matches more as it gains conditions. Rules that already carry a cross-question "or" still render faithfully, still keep it when edited, and still take that path through the checks.

Copy rules for finding messages and check titles

  • Finding messages and check titles render in the popover and in the builder's publish card, so rewrite them in the report. Use no em dashes, and never use decider, deciding, bucket, branch, boost, weight or score (D18). The strings to replace: V1 "No question decides the result yet — promote one with the Make decider toggle.", V4 and V5 "points at a deleted bucket — pick a new result.", V3 "The deciding question is optional — a shopper could skip it and get no result.", and the titles "Exactly one deciding question", "Every path reaches the decider", "Every deciding answer has a result" and "Rules point at existing buckets" (pathReport.ts:138-221, 382-409).
  • Take the merchant-facing names from the shared constants module (D18), so the report, the screen and the Table cannot drift apart. "Filter Results + Rules" and "Rules only" are names, not descriptions: never write "the attributes style" in a finding.
  • Strings marked (mock) are approved. Strings marked (proposed) need the owner to confirm the wording.
  • Update pathReport.test.ts wherever it pins wording, for example /deleted bucket/ at pathReport.test.ts:215 and the verdict label at pathReport.test.ts:87 and 233. Assert against the constant, not a re-typed string.

The safety net, and what the checks may promise

Partial A shopper no rule matches gets the safety net the Results step already has, and the same net covers an empty result in Filter Results + Rules (D1). One behaviour for both styles.

  • Today. The named fallbacks run only for a target that resolved and turned out empty: global_fallback, then emptyFallbackCol, then safetyNetCol (QuizRuntime.tsx:1584-1595; deciderFallbackProducts, recommendDecider.ts:522-538). An unresolved target never reaches them: the engine returns { products: [] } with no decider block (recommendationEngine.ts:393-396), so QuizRuntime's decider reveal is skipped (QuizRuntime.tsx:1579) and the shopper gets a bare card holding the localized no_results_match string (QuizRuntime.tsx:1713-1721).
  • After this change. The unresolved case runs the same chain. When the chain resolves nothing, the bare card renders exactly as it does today, so the current DOM is the floor and never a regression. Build it inside the decider arm; the legacy result path at QuizRuntime.tsx:1722 onwards, with its own globalFallback prop, is untouched.
  • Publish already bakes what the net needs for decider docs: both fallback collections join the product index (quizPublish.ts:443-448).
  • There is no merchant control for the net on a decider quiz, and you are not building one. Read the risk callout in Scope before you write the copy, and raise the gap in your report.

What the checks may say because of it.

  • "No rule matches this shopper" is not a broken quiz any more, so Rules only does not block on it. Its blocks stay the three D3 names.
  • No finding, and no line in the popover, may claim that every shopper gets a recommendation. The net can itself resolve to nothing, and the report cannot see the merchant's collections.
  • The net is not an excuse for a looser gate. Every publish gate above stays exactly as strict as it is today in Filter Results + Rules.
This is a runtime change, so the runtime proof rules apply in full (Repo rules; CLAUDE.md:77-80). Decompose, do not rewrite. Prove three documents explicitly: a legacy doc, a decider doc with no logic_style, and a decider doc with logic_style: "rules". Render each on the local build and on the pre-change deploy and diff normalized outerHTML; only the third may differ. Run the full e2e and review screenshots of /q. After any deploy, curl -sS https://quizocalypse-studio.fly.dev/q/cmqqcb0ao004mqvkwjug7t0ya.json | shasum -a 256 must still start c02ccaec98a0fe9e. The engine branch in resolveTarget (recommendDecider.ts:217-292) carries the same burden even though no file under app/components/runtime/ moves for it.

The clean state says "Nothing to fix" and nothing more

Fixed in mock The mock's checkPop() now reads "Nothing to fix" with no second line. Build that. Do not add "Every shopper path ends in a recommendation.": no check behind it computes it, and the safety net means an empty result is no longer proof of a broken quiz.

If the owner later asks for a positive line, it needs a computed flag on the report, for example verdict.allPathsResolve, and it means different things in the two styles:

  • Filter Results + Rules: true when V1 to V4 pass and V2 finds no bypass. Every finished path then meets the picking question and every answer maps to an existing recommendation. Narrowing can still empty the pool and the net can still catch it, so the line would be about recommendations, not product counts.
  • Rules only: true only when enumeratePaths returns truncated: false (pathEnumeration.ts:61-66) and every path matches a rule that can show something (ruleConditionsMatch). Enumeration forks one answer per question and never expands multi-select combinations (pathEnumeration.ts:24-27), so the line can never be claimed when a rule has conditions on a multi-select question.

Row actions and the live jump bug

  • Every row click closes the popover and first switches the workspace to Edit. Fixed in mock the mock's ACT.goto now sets the view as well as the selection (B38); the live handler must do the same, because a jump from Table view otherwise changes nothing a merchant can see.
  • Question rows select the question inside LogicTabCard, scroll it into view and focus the control named in the table above.
  • Rule rows scroll to the rule in the rules column or the rules row and highlight it. For V5, V6, V7, V9 and impossible all-of the row also opens the rule in the rule window (mock ACT.editrule). For V8 it only scrolls and highlights both rules, because the fix is a reorder.
  • The style-mismatch row opens the header's "Logic style" menu.
  • The "“X” is never recommended" row arms X in the tray (Filter) or opens "Create a rule" with X picked (Rules only).

Conflict The live jump links select nothing in the card. Fix this first: every new row depends on it.

  • Step3Shell's handler sets its own selectedId, which is state for the parked content view. It then scrolls to the first [data-node-id] inside the card (Step3Shell.tsx:192-199, 289-307).
  • LogicTabCard keeps its rail selection in local state (LogicTabCard.tsx:132-135), so the pane goes on showing the previous question.
  • Rule links only scroll to the top of the card (Step3Shell.tsx:297-300), and rule rows carry no id to scroll to.

Give LogicTabCard a controlled selection and a focus request. Give rule rows a stable anchor, for example data-rule-id, and keep data-node-id on rail rows and the pane (LogicQuestionWidget.tsx:213, 355).

  seq: number;                              // bump to re-fire the same target
  target:
    | { kind: "question"; nodeId: string; answerId?: string;
        control?: "role" | "route" | "picks" | "values" | "required" }
    | { kind: "rule"; ruleId: string; open: boolean }
    | { kind: "recommendation"; categoryId: string }
    | { kind: "style" };
};
// On a request: switch to Edit, select, scroll into view, focus, flash.
  • Tier1Link (pathReport.ts:34-40) gains the optional fields the rows need: answer id, control, open, and the recommendation and style kinds. It is shared with the builder's handler (onHealthNavigate, UnifiedWorkspace.tsx:628-640), whose if-chain ignores kinds it does not know; make that explicit rather than leaving it to luck, and keep its setHealthOpen(false) first so the popover always closes.
  • The Questions-step rule hand-off (pendingRuleJumpStash, Step3Shell.tsx:51-54, 201-207) uses the same fixed handler. It stashes a rule id, advances with to-logic and replays on mount, so it must survive the beforeNavigate flush below.
  • Tier1CheckList's "Go to it →" links (HealthPopover.tsx:183) keep working on the builder side through the same handler.

Continue and Back: no lost edit, no lost style

What goes wrong today

  1. Continue does not save first. submitContinue posts the intent immediately (QuestionBuilderStage.tsx:91-93). An edit made inside the 700 ms debounce (useQuizDraft.ts:58-68) exists only in the browser. Nothing flushes on Continue or on unmount.
  2. Navigation intents write back a stale doc. Each intent writes back the document it read when the request started: loadFunnelDraft at funnelIntents.server.ts:106, then writeDoc({...doc, build_session}) in to-logic (:1457), set-logic-style (:1476-1479), goto-stage (:1510-1513) and to-rec-page (:1531). writeDoc replaces the whole draftJson (funnelDraft.server.ts:170-175), so a PUT that commits between the read and the write is overwritten. The client never notices: useQuizDraft seeds from initial once (useQuizDraft.ts:28), so a later loader payload does not correct its copy.
  3. D1 makes that race worse, not better. Quiz.logic_style is top-level document content, so it travels with the autosave PUT and is exactly the kind of edit a navigation intent can now overwrite. A merchant who switches the style and clicks Continue inside the debounce can arrive at Results with the old style saved.
  4. The PUT has the mirror race. It writes the build_session it read at its own start (funnelIntents.server.ts:106, 124-133). A navigation write that lands between that read and the PUT's write is undone and the stage goes back. The comment at :124-128 says either order is safe, and that holds only while the requests do not overlap. Clicking Continue while a PUT is in flight, or just as the debounce fires, makes them overlap. (From reading the code; no probe was run.)
  5. Results keeps whatever the loader read. ResultsGuided seeds its own draft once (ResultsGuided.tsx:204), and its autosave writes that document back. Any Logic edit that reached the server after the loader read is lost for good.
  6. Saves can land out of order. useQuizDraft uses one fetcher (useQuizDraft.ts:47-56). A new submit on the same fetcher aborts the in-flight request in the browser: the Remix router's fetch() calls abortFetcher(key) (@remix-run/router 1.23.3, locked at package-lock.json:4336-4337). The server may still apply the aborted request, so an older document can land after a newer one. (Code reading.)
  7. Other navigation does not save first either. "Back ‹" and the stepper submit goto-stage from Step1Funnel (Step1Funnel.tsx:91-92, 138, 157) without asking the step to save. "Open builder" on Results does the same (Step1Funnel.tsx:106-117, 337).
  8. Step3Shell remounts on Back then Continue. Steps 2 and 3 share one QuestionBuilderStage element (Step1Funnel.tsx:297-315), so its useQuizDraft state survives the stage change while Step3Shell itself unmounts and remounts. Today that loses localStyle and falls back to build_session, inference or the chooser (Step3Shell.tsx:140-155). After D1 the style is part of the client document that useQuizDraft holds, so the remount keeps it with no re-sync trick: the only way to lose it is to lose the save.
  9. set-logic-style stops being a moving part. It shares the funnel fetcher and does not count as navigating (QuestionBuilderStage.tsx:77-81, 96-101), so a Continue click can abort it in the browser and a failed write is never reverted in the UI (Step3Shell.tsx:156-162). The new UI never calls it: the style is written by a mutation on the save path. Delete the caller with the chooser and leave the server branch in place for one release (Screen shell).

Required fixes

Client

  • Single-flight saves in useQuizDraft. Keep one PUT in flight at a time and send the newest pending document when it returns. Add flushAndWait(): Promise<{ ok: boolean; error?: string }>, which resolves once no debounce is pending and nothing is in flight. fetcher.submit returns void in this Remix version (react-router-dom 6.30.4), so resolve from the fetcher's return to idle. Keep flushSave (useQuizDraft.ts:136-142) for existing callers, or migrate them.
  • A save hook on the bar. Add beforeNavigate?: () => Promise<boolean> to FunnelBarOverride (funnelChrome.tsx:32-36). Step1Funnel awaits it before every navigation submit: Continue, "Back ‹", the stepper and "Open builder". Step3Shell (through QuestionBuilderStage), QuestionsWalkthrough and ResultsGuided publish it, memoized and stable (funnelChrome.tsx:11-14).
  • Continue on Logic. Show the loading state, await the flush, then submit to-rec-page. If the save fails, stay on Logic and let FunnelSaveChip show "Not saved · Retry" (funnelChrome.tsx:69-80).
  • Step3Shell's onFlush prop (Step3Shell.tsx:73, 95) loses its only consumer when DiagnoseModal goes. Repoint it at flushAndWait and use it for beforeNavigate rather than deleting it.
  • The style needs no special handling. It is document content on the one save path, so it rides the same flush. Do not add an intent, a second fetcher or a local mirror for it.

Server (persistence work: include the written 2-lens review, per CLAUDE.md:74-76)

  • Navigation intents change only build_session, on a fresh read, in one atomic step. Use an interactive transaction that locks the row (SELECT … FOR UPDATE), or a compare-and-set on Quiz.updatedAt with one retry. loadFunnelDraft already selects updatedAt (funnelDraft.server.ts:158).
  • The PUT branch writes content together with the session it reads inside that same atomic step (funnelIntents.server.ts:124-133).
  • These changes apply to both quiz models and change no stored shape. Legacy drafts go through the same intents and only gain correct ordering; prove that with a legacy fixture, because this is persistence code on the shared path.
  • Optional: add a health guard to to-rec-page that recomputes the same style-aware report from the same inputs and returns { intent, ok: false, error } while blocking > 0. Step1Funnel shows that error in its "That didn't go through" banner (Step1Funnel.tsx:50-51, 191-195). Only add it when the inputs are identical to the client's, or it will refuse a Continue the CTA allowed.

Result: the loader read after to-rec-page contains every Logic edit and the saved style, so ResultsGuided's seed is correct and the Results step cannot write an old style back. Results' own Back and "Open builder" go through the same beforeNavigate. The builder already avoids this race for Publish by sending the live document with the intent (UnifiedWorkspace.tsx:651-659).

Data model, persistence and the mutations to add

Every control on the Logic screen reads the draft Quiz document (app/lib/quizSchema.ts) and changes it through pure mutations in app/lib/mutations/. useQuizDraft then saves the result. Recommendations are the one exception: they are Prisma Category rows, and the document stores only their ids, as answer targets and rule targets. Selection, view, open popovers and window drafts are client state and never reach the document. One stored field is new, and it is the spine of this change: the logic style now lives on the quiz document, because it decides how the shopper's result is resolved.

How to read this section. The owner has ruled, so what follows is written in the indicative: it is the thing to build, not a menu. A parenthesised decision id, "(D7)", points at the reasoning in Owner decisions; it never means the point is still being weighed. Three items are genuinely open (D2 for Filter Results + Rules, D10, and the second half of D14). Each is marked where it touches this section and gathered again under Still open and parked, where they touch this section. Refs are origin/main (b4aa278) unless marked mock; read them with git show origin/main:<path>, because the working tree is stale. The mock is docs/design/logic-tab/rules-row/index.html; it is still being edited, so it is cited by identifier (ACT.setstyle, sentence(), snap()), never by line number.

Both styles are equal, and the difference is stored. Filter Results + Rules and Rules only are two methods of deciding a result, not a screen and a lens on it (D1). The style rides on the quiz document, survives publish, and the shopper-facing engine branches on it. Nothing below treats Rules only as a reduced Filter Results + Rules, or the other way round: each style stores exactly what it needs and ignores what it does not, and switching is lossless in both directions because nothing is stripped on the way through.

The logic style is a field on the quiz document New

The style is a real engine mode (D1), so it has to reach the shopper. build_session cannot carry it: publish strips build_session out of publishedJson (quizPublish.ts:789, 804-810), so a style stored there is invisible to /q/:id and to /q/:id.json. A top-level key is carried through publish untouched, and stripPublicJsonPayload drops only review_enrichment_sources and translations (quizPublish.ts:49-50), so the public JSON carries it too.

  • Schema. Add logic_style: z.enum(["rules", "attributes"]).optional() to Quiz, next to logic_model (quizSchema.ts:1992-1995). Never .default(): a default would inject the key into every legacy document on its next parse and write, which is the discipline logic_model itself is held to (quizSchema.ts:1988-1991). The stored values stay "rules" and "attributes" whatever the merchant-facing names are (D18).
  • The old field stays parsed forever. build_session.logic_style (quizSchema.ts:1698-1708) is not deleted and not repurposed; it is read once, as the second step of resolution, so drafts that picked a style before this change keep it. Its comment block is stale on two counts and is corrected in the same commit: it names the style "Attributes + Rules" (renamed to Filter Results + Rules, D18) and it says an absent value means "the Logic stage shows the style chooser", which stops being true when the chooser goes (D5).
  • Two readers, two helpers, one module, and they are not the same value. resolveLogicStyle(doc) decides which screen opens: doc.logic_style, then doc.build_session?.logic_style, then inference, then "attributes". Inference is the live rule, lifted out of Step3Shell: any question with role: "filter" means Filter Results + Rules; a document with at least one rule and no filter role means Rules only (Step3Shell.tsx:151-153). It never returns null and never writes (D5), and it takes the whole document, so no caller passes a question list. engineLogicStyle(doc) = doc.logic_style ?? "attributes" is what the engine will actually run, and it is what recommendDecider, buildTier1Report, validateQuiz and publishQuiz read, never the inferred screen style. No component re-implements either one.
  • Nothing is written on page load. Today the funnel writes the style the first time the merchant answers the chooser. After this change the only writer is the title switch (the mock's styleMenu() and ACT.setstyle). A quiz that is never switched keeps no logic_style key at all and behaves by inference, which is what makes the change safe to deploy over existing drafts.
  • Write it with setLogicStyle(doc, style) in deciderMutations.ts. It is logic_model-gated, returns its input when the style is unchanged, and is committed through useQuizDraft's commit on both admin surfaces. A failed save surfaces in FunnelSaveChip's "Not saved · Retry" (funnelChrome.tsx:81-106) instead of failing silently. Because the style travels in the client document, it survives Back then Continue and needs no in-session override: delete localStyle and its "the Switch does nothing" workaround (Step3Shell.tsx:140-155).
  • Delete the chooser. With resolution always producing a style, the LogicStyleChooser branch (Step3Shell.tsx:422-428) has no reachable state. Remove the component and with it the inert "Point based" row, which renders, is clickable, writes nothing and toasts "Point based isn't available yet." (D5; LogicStyleChooser.tsx:89, :170).
  • Publish keeps it. publishedJson spreads the document minus the strip list (quizPublish.ts:804-810). Do not add logic_style to that list. The engine and the validation gate read it from publishedJson.
  • Legacy documents never gain the key, because only the gated setLogicStyle writes it, and decider documents without the key keep resolving exactly as they do today.
  • unpublishedChanges needs no code change. Its settings unit is "everything else top-level" (unpublishedChanges.ts:242-255), so a style change counts as one unpublished change on its own. That is correct: under D1 the style changes what shoppers get.
  • The set-logic-style intent loses its caller. Leave the intent (funnelIntents.server.ts:1461-1481) in place, parsed and unused, and stop sending it; nothing may read build_session.logic_style ahead of the document field. The two probe blocks that pin it move with it: the chooser click-through (e2e/q3-logic-verify.mjs:173-178) is deleted because no chooser renders, and the two persistence assertions (e2e/q3-logic-verify.mjs:327-336) read logic_style off the draft document instead of build_session. The same probe pins the bar text "Attributes + Rules", which the D18 rename changes (Tests and probes).
// app/lib/logicStyle.ts (new, pure; no component may re-implement this)
export type LogicStyle = "rules" | "attributes";
// Which screen opens. Screen only: no engine, report or gate may call it.
export function resolveLogicStyle(
  doc: Pick<Quiz, "logic_style" | "build_session" | "decision_rules" | "nodes">,
): LogicStyle;                       // saved → build_session → inference → "attributes"

// What the engine will run. Read by recommendDecider, buildTier1Report,
// validateQuiz and publishQuiz, and by nothing that only draws a screen.
export function engineLogicStyle(doc: Pick<Quiz, "logic_style">): LogicStyle;  // saved ?? "attributes"

// app/lib/mutations/deciderMutations.ts
export function setLogicStyle(doc: QuizDoc, style: LogicStyle): QuizDoc;
D6 is parked, and the field is why that is safe. The main builder is being rebuilt, so this work ships the funnel step 3 surface only. The style lives on the document, so the new builder reads it with the same helper and writes it with the same mutation. Two rules while it is parked. Build nothing that only works inside the funnel: resolveLogicStyle, setLogicStyle and every mutation below take a document, not a stage, and the new screen must not be gated on ruleFlow === "onboarding". And name the gap in your report: today's builder mounts LogicTabCard with no logicStyle prop, so a Rules-only quiz opens there as Filter Results + Rules and the builder's Logic view still writes rules against the other style's assumptions (BuilderSettings.tsx:67-79; LogicTabCard.tsx:105, :112). That is the main-builder project's work, not yours.

What the engine reads from the document

Two shopper-facing behaviours follow from the stored style. Both land in app/lib/recommendDecider.ts and app/components/runtime/**, which is the highest-risk edit class in the repo. Engine semantics specifies the resolution order in full; what matters here is which stored fields each style reads, and which it must ignore.

StyleFields the engine readsFields it ignores
Filter Results + Rules (logic_style absent or "attributes")Today's chain, unchanged: decision_rules top to bottom, then the role: "decides" question's target_id / target_ids as the base, then the filter questions' answer values (recommendDecider.ts:226-291).Nothing new is ignored. A question's filter values stay stored and read.
Rules only (logic_style === "rules")decision_rules only. The first rule whose conditions match is the result: its target_id / target_ids are the whole recommendation set.Question role, answer target_id / target_ids and answer filter values. They stay on the document, untouched, so switching back restores them (D1).
  • The branch has a home already. resolveTarget already has a no-base path: when a rule matches and no base mapping exists, show and prioritize degrade to the rule's own targets and a bare hide resolves nothing (recommendDecider.ts:276-283). Rules only takes that path unconditionally instead of computing a base. In Rules only the rule window offers Show only (D2), so a stored hide can only come from a document that was authored in the other style or edited by hand; treat it as it is treated today and do not add a second meaning for it.
  • The signature widens by one key. resolveTarget(selectedAnswerIds, doc) takes Pick<QuizDoc, "nodes" | "decision_rules"> (recommendDecider.ts:217-219). Add "logic_style" to that Pick rather than threading a flag: both callers already pass the whole document (QuizRuntime.tsx:513; pathEnumeration.ts:140), so nothing at the call sites changes and the admin's path enumeration branches with the runtime automatically. A document with no logic_style key resolves exactly as it does today, which is the legacy-byte-identical proof in one line.
  • The safety net is a runtime change, for both styles (D1 safety net). Today a decider document whose target does not resolve renders a bare card holding the localized no_results_match string and nothing else (QuizRuntime.tsx:1713-1721), and the comment there assumes the case is impossible once the publish gates pass. Rules only breaks that assumption by design: a shopper whom no rule matches resolves nothing. The net reuses the chain that already exists for a resolved-but-empty target: global_fallback, then rec_page_settings.global.emptyFallbackCol, then safetyNetCol (QuizRuntime.tsx:1584-1595; recommendDecider.ts:522-538, whose comment at :520-521 says the unresolved case is deliberately not handled). The same net covers an empty result in Filter Results + Rules. No new stored field: publish already bakes both named collections into product_index for decider documents (quizPublish.ts:443-447).
  • Publish needs no bake change for Rules only. collectDeciderTargetIds already unions every rule's target_id and target_ids alongside the deciding question's answer targets (quizPublish.ts:128-146), so a Rules-only quiz's targets land in target_product_ids_map and target_index as they stand.
  • Publish validation does need the style. validateQuiz emits missing_decider whenever the count of role: "decides" questions is not exactly one (quizValidation.ts:124-134), and publishQuiz throws PublishError on any issue (quizPublish.ts:408-414). A Rules-only quiz has no deciding question by definition, so validateQuiz becomes style-aware in the same change as the report (D3), or nothing built in Rules only can ever be published. The untargeted-answer gate needs no change: it iterates role: "decides" nodes only, so it is vacuous in Rules only (quizPublish.ts:494-510).
The runtime proof rules apply in full to both of the changes above. They touch app/components/runtime/** and the engine every published decider quiz runs through. Prove: legacy documents byte-identical (render the same document on the local build and the pre-change deploy and diff normalized outerHTML); the byte pin curl -sS https://quizocalypse-studio.fly.dev/q/cmqqcb0ao004mqvkwjug7t0ya.json | shasum -a 256 still opening c02ccaec98a0fe9e; the full e2e run, not a subset; and a screenshot review of /q. Decompose, do not rewrite (CLAUDE.md:77-80). A decider quiz with no fallback configured resolves nothing from the net and the shopper still sees the bare card; that is the shipped gap named in Scope, and you are not building a merchant control for it in this work.

What the style-aware checks read from the document

One Tier-1 report drives the CTA, the check popover and publish, and it branches on the same resolved style (D3). Checks and Continue specifies the findings and their copy; what belongs here is which stored fields each style's checks read, and the invariant that binds the report to the gate: the report must never read safer than validateQuiz, which is already encoded at pathReport.ts:125-128 and stays true after the branch. "Fix N issues" counts blocking findings only.

StyleBlocks onReads
Rules onlyNo rules at all; no rule that can show anything; any rule missing its answers or its recommendations. It skips every picking-question check: no decider, unmapped answers, decider bypass and filter values are not findings here.decision_rules (empty list, empty conditions through halfBuiltRules at pathAnalyzer.ts:181-188, targets that resolve to no Category row through brokenRuleRefs at pathAnalyzer.ts:158-178 and the loader's rows), and the rule's action.
Filter Results + RulesToday's blocks, unchanged (missing_decider, decider_optional, unmapped_decider_answer, broken_rule_reference, the kinds pathReport.ts:130-136 already groups), plus a route that bypasses the picking question and a rule that is broken or impossible. Warnings, which never block: a recommendation nothing can show, a rule that never runs, an impossible all-of.Question role and required, the picking question's answer targets, answer filter values, the edges (route bypass, pathAnalyzer), and decision_rules.

validateQuiz carries the same branch, because publish throws on any issue it returns (quizPublish.ts:408-414) and its missing_decider check counts role: "decides" questions (quizValidation.ts:124-134). Both the report and the gate read engineLogicStyle(doc), never the resolved screen style and never a second copy of the rule. If the report read the inferred style, a draft with rules and no saved field would validate as Rules only and publish with no picking question, then run the Filter engine for its shoppers: the report reading safer than the gate is the one failure this split exists to prevent.

Persistence rules

  1. Document edits go through commit. useQuizDraft updates the live document immediately and sends a whole-document JSON PUT after a 700 ms debounce (useQuizDraft.ts:47-76). The route runs Quiz.safeParse and returns 400 "Invalid quiz document" on any violation (funnel: funnelIntents.server.ts:114-123; builder: quizEditorIO.server.ts:342-354). Every PUT carries the whole document, so a single invalid value makes every later save fail until it is removed. Invalid values include empty question or answer text, a selection bound of 0, an end label over 40 characters, a card question with fewer than two answers and a rule with an empty target id. On every PUT the funnel keeps the server's copy of build_session (funnelIntents.server.ts:124-131), while the builder stores whatever build_session the client sent (quizEditorIO.server.ts:355-358).
  2. build_session changes only through form intents sent on the stage's shared fetcher (QuestionBuilderStage.tsx:83-101). An intent writes {...draft, build_session} through writeDoc (funnelDraft.server.ts:171-176; for example funnelIntents.server.ts:1476-1479,1531), using the draft it read when the request started (funnelIntents.server.ts:106). A PUT that lands in between is therefore overwritten. The client's copy of build_session never refreshes during a session. This is exactly why the style is a top-level field and not a build_session key: it needs no intent, it rides the ordinary autosave on both surfaces, and it cannot be lost to an intent race. Flush and await the autosave before any intent you do still send (Checks and Continue).
  3. From the Logic workspace, Category rows change only through POST /api/categories/ensure-targets. It takes at most 12 resources per call, reuses rows by (source, sourceRef), only adds rows and never deletes (api.categories.ensure-targets.tsx:26-38,78-118). This work extends its kind enum with "group" and makes every returned row quiz-scoped (D15). The loader doesn't see a new row until it revalidates, so lift the returned rows into local state, as CreateRuleModal does with onCategoriesCreated (CreateRuleModal.tsx:622-624). Never call toggle-bucket, select-all or set-buckets from Logic.
  4. Writes after an await start from getLatestDoc() (LogicTabCard's docRef, LogicTabCard.tsx:127-129), as CreateRuleModal does (CreateRuleModal.tsx:637-640). Never start them from the document captured at render. Undo is held to the same rule: it composes inverse mutations onto the latest document, which is what makes it safe for the toast to outlive an unrelated edit (D7).
  5. Commit once per user action. commit replaces the document outright (useQuizDraft.ts:70-76), and docRef only updates on render (useQuizDraft.ts:36-37; LogicTabCard.tsx:128-129). A second commit in the same handler therefore starts from the stale document and drops the first. Chain the mutations on a local variable and commit once, as applyNarrowField does (logicTabFields.ts:550-562). An import is one commit; so are a Picks move with its cleared mappings, a type change with its rule conversion, a paste that splits into several rules, and any Undo that restores several parts.
  6. A refusal returns the same object. The decider mutations and setAnswerRoute return their input when they refuse or when nothing changes. Examples: updateDecisionRule on a missing id (deciderMutations.ts:300), createDecisionRule with no conditions or no targets (357-359), moveDecisionRule to the index it already has (270), and a route that would revisit a question (edgeMutations.ts:109-111). Test next === prev, and if they match, skip the commit, the toast and the save pill. The rule window uses the same test to notice that its rule is gone. addAnswer, removeAnswer and setQuestionType return a new object even when nothing changed.
  7. The style is written on one gesture only. setLogicStyle runs from the title switch and from nowhere else: not on load, not on Continue, not as a side effect of adding a rule or a filter role. Inference covers every quiz that never touches the switch, so an untouched draft keeps no logic_style key and cannot drift (D5).

New mutations

Every new mutation follows these conventions:

  • It is pure: a document goes in and a document (or {doc, …}) comes out, with no I/O. New ids come only from uid().
  • Its first line is if (doc.logic_model !== "decider") return doc; (or the {doc, …} equivalent). A legacy document comes back as the same object and never gains a key. That includes setLogicStyle: the style field can never appear on a legacy document.
  • It returns its input object when it refuses or when nothing changes, so callers can test next === prev.
  • It never returns a document that fails Quiz.safeParse. New objects carry every defaulted field (answers get tags: [], as in questionMutations.ts:146-151), so Quiz.parse(next) leaves them unchanged.
  • It writes an optional field only when the field means something, and deletes it when it returns to the default, following deciderMutations.ts:310-317,366-369.
  • It is style-blind unless the style is its subject. A mutation does not read logic_style to decide whether to write: the screen decides which mutations to offer, the engine decides what to read. The one exception is setLogicStyle.
  • Inside app/lib/mutations it imports the concrete module, never the quizMutations barrel (quizMutations.ts:4-7). Re-export new functions from the barrel for UI callers. deciderMutations.ts may import questionMutations.ts, but not the reverse.
  • It has unit tests for the happy path, a refusal that returns the same object, a legacy document that comes back as the same object with no new keys, and a Quiz.parse round trip (Tests and probes).

The captured parts are each question's data (role, required, answers with their targets and values), each question's outgoing edges, and either the listed rules (by id) or the whole rule list. restoreLogicParts writes before back only if every captured part in the document still equals after. Otherwise it returns null and the caller withdraws the Undo rather than clobbering a later edit (D7). Compare with sorted-key JSON, as unpublishedChanges.ts:84-99 does.Undo for a Picks move (D9), for type and point changes (B7) and for Import
normalizeDecisionRule(rule, questions) → {rule, notes} NewdeciderMutations.ts (a pure function, not a document mutation)It removes duplicate conditions and sorts conditions by question flow order, then by answer order; unknown ids go last, in their existing order. It keeps a question in any_of only when that question has two or more "is" conditions and no "is not" condition (D12). It adds every question that isn't multi-select and has two or more "is" conditions to any_of, and reports each one in notes. It keeps mixed is and is-not groups from older rules as they are. It removes duplicate targets and applies the G1 mirror. It leaves match and action alone, so a stored cross-question "or" survives an edit (D13), and it never drops a missing question or answer. Nothing else changes behaviour. Flags on questions with no picks never reach storage in the first place, because the draft emits conditions only for picked answers and writes any_of only for two or more picks (CreateRuleModal.tsx:390-411).Saving in the rule window (B13); applyLogicImport; the paste apply step; the import diff (B25)
applyLogicImport(doc, parsed, ctx) → {doc, changes, skipped, notes, undo} Newapp/lib/logicSheets.tsPure; the caller commits once. It applies the Answers sheet first, then Rules. Within the Answers sheet, question cells (text, type, role) apply before answer cells, so a Picks move clears the old targets before the sheet writes its own. Every write goes through the mutations above: setQuestionText, setAnswerText, changeQuestionType, setSelectionBounds, movePicksResults or setQuestionRole, setAnswerTargets, setAnswerFilterValues (built from baseValueSet) and setAnswerRoute. Answers are matched by the sheet's Answer ID column and updated in place; the sheet never adds or deletes an answer, and a missing column means "leave unchanged", never "clear" (D16). A refused write becomes a skipped cell with its reason, and so does a "NOT (A AND B)" rule, with the reason naming the combination (D12). Recommendations resolve only against ctx.categories, never a raw id from the file, and any edit to the Recommendations sheet is reported as ignored. The Rules sheet applies entirely or not at all. Rows keep their Rule ID when the file has one, and new rows get uid("rule"). Every rule goes through normalizeDecisionRule. changes counts real differences, matched by id and compared in normalized form (B25). undo holds the parts captured before and after.Import

Undo is inverse mutations, and the toast carries it

Undo is offered on exactly the actions that destroy something the merchant cannot retype in a second: a rule deleted, several rules deleted in a row, a rule moved, a Picks results move that cleared mappings, an answer count cut, and an import. Every one of them is the same shape (D7).

  1. Capture before the write. A delete captures {rule, index}. A move captures the old index. A Picks move and a type or point change capture before and after through captureLogicParts, scoped to the questions and rules the action touched.
  2. Commit once, then show the toast with its action.
  3. Undo composes inverse mutations onto the latest document from getLatestDoc(), never onto the document the action started from. Two deletes while one toast is up accumulate into one Undo that restores both, in reverse order, at their own indices.
  4. Undo withdraws itself when restoreLogicParts returns null, which means something it would overwrite has changed since. Close the toast and say nothing further; do not restore a stale part.
  5. Never snapshot the document or the whole rule list. The mock does (snap(), undoLive(), ACT.undo, and IMP_UNDO for the import) because it has no other store; a snapshot in the product would silently revert edits made while the toast was up Conflict.

The toast primitive itself gains one optional action, a duration, a live region and keyboard reach, and the design-system rule that toasts carry no actions (qz-toast.tsx:13-17) gets a dated owner exception recorded against it (D7). That work, and the missing providers on the two embedded routes (D21), are specified in Screen shell. Two facts belong here because they change what Undo can promise: useQzToast resolves to a no-op when no provider is mounted (qz-toast.tsx:31), so on the embedded twins today every Undo would be invisible and every delete unrecoverable; and the toast is a queue of one (qz-toast.tsx:23-29), so a second destructive action replaces the first toast, which is exactly why the accumulating Undo above has to exist.

Pure helpers (one computation each)

One rule describer

Rule text is produced three ways today. describeRuleConditions (ruleSummary.ts:5-29) returns a string and honours any_of and match. ruleSummary() (:31-50) always joins with AND and names a single target. RuleSentence re-implements the grouping in JSX, ordered by first appearance (LogicTabCard.tsx:603-712). None of them reads an is-not group correctly when its question is also in any_of: describeRuleConditions joins every condition in a group with that group's word (ruleSummary.ts:23-28), but the engine requires none of the is-not answers (recommendDecider.ts:342-352). Add one structured describer to ruleSummary.ts. The rule rows, the rule-window footer, the Table and the export all render from it. Keep the two string functions for their current callers.

// app/lib/ruleSummary.ts
export interface AnswerToken { answerId: string; text: string | null; qualified: boolean }
export interface RuleTokens {
  verb: "show" | "pin" | "hide" | "replace";            // "replace" = a legacy rule with no action
  targets: Array<{ id: string; name: string | null }>; // null = recommendation deleted
  across: "and" | "or";                                  // "or" only for a stored match "any" (D13)
  groups: Array<{
    questionId: string;
    qNumber: number | null;                              // null = question deleted
    is: { join: "and" | "or"; answers: AnswerToken[] } | null;
    not: AnswerToken[] | null;                           // none of these
  }>;
}
export function describeRule(rule: DecisionRule, ctx: {
  questions: readonly OrderedQuestion[];
  categories: ReadonlyArray<{ id: string; name: string }>;
}): RuleTokens;
  • Sentences are verb-first and answers-only: "Show dryness when …" (D17). Groups follow the question flow order. Within a group, "is" answers join with "or" when the question is in any_of and has two or more of them, and with "and" otherwise. A group of several answers is wrapped in parentheses and the join word is bold.
  • "is not" answers always mean none of them and render as not (A or B). There is no "not all of" form to render, because the row cannot be written (D12).
  • qualified is true when the same answer text (trimmed, ignoring case) exists on another question, and only then is a question label added (D17). That rule is the whole of it. The mock instead qualifies scale answers unconditionally: ansText() prefixes "Q5 = " on any scale question, and sentence()'s ns branch drops the prefix only on the second and later chips of the same group. The build qualifies a scale point only when another question carries the same answer text Conflict.
  • A truncated answer carries its full text in a tooltip and in the accessible name (D17).
  • A deleted question, answer or recommendation comes back as null, so every renderer shows it flagged instead of throwing (B1, B9).
  • It has three renderers. Sentence chips show answers only, qualified where needed. A plain-text form serves tooltips and accessible names. The machine form serves the Table and the file and always reads Q7 = Yes, for every question type and not only for scales, with not/and/or in bold lowercase on screen and NOT/AND/OR in the file (D17). The mock's Table already takes this route through whenParts(), which calls the same ansText().

One recommendation coverage helper

createRuleBand.ruleCoverage (createRuleBand.ts:23-33, used at CreateRuleModal.tsx:493) counts every rule that names a target. That includes Hide rules, rules with no conditions and rules that never run (B10). buildRuleCoverage in app/lib/ruleCoverage.ts (:37-70) is a different thing again: it works per question, and its only consumer, CoverageSidebar (CoverageSidebar.tsx:4,24), leaves the screen with the top section (D23). One home and one name, and this section is where they are set: recommendationCoverage in the new file app/lib/recommendationCoverage.ts. It sits in app/lib so pathReport, also in app/lib, can import it without reaching into a component module, and it takes a new file so neither existing name is quietly reused. The strip, the rule-window band, the Table's "Shown by rules" and Status columns and the Filter warning about recommendations nothing can show all read from it. Every other section quotes this path and this name; nothing goes in ruleCoverage.ts or createRuleBand.ts.

What happens to the two names that exist today. createRuleBand.ruleCoverage is deleted, not left beside the new helper: CreateRuleModal.tsx:493 and splitRecommendationGroups (createRuleBand.ts:38-49) call recommendationCoverage instead, and the ruleCoverage cases in createRuleBand.test.ts:35-57 move with it. buildRuleCoverage and app/lib/ruleCoverage.ts are deleted with CoverageSidebar, their only importer (CoverageSidebar.tsx:4), along with ruleCoverage.test.ts; if CoverageSidebar survives the D23 removal for any reason, the module stays untouched and the new helper is still not put in it.

// app/lib/recommendationCoverage.ts (new)
export interface RecCoverage { ruleIds: string[]; mappedByAnswer: boolean }
export function recommendationCoverage(
  doc: Quiz,
  categoryIds: readonly string[],
  neverFires: ReadonlySet<string>, // rule ids the analyzer says can never fire
): Map<string, RecCoverage>;

A rule counts for each of its targets only when all of these hold:

  • its action is show, prioritize or absent (a legacy replace rule also shows its targets);
  • it has at least one condition;
  • its id isn't in neverFires;
  • the target is a known row.

neverFires is the union of the analyzer's broken-reference, dead, shadowed and impossible findings, computed once per document change (pathAnalyzer.ts:158-299, plus the reasons added in Engine semantics). mappedByAnswer lets Filter Results + Rules count a recommendation already mapped to an answer as covered (B41); in Rules only it is always false, because answer mappings are not read there. The colours the strip paints from this are settled: green means the recommendation is placed on no answer, black means placed, violet means armed (D14). Open (D14, second half): whether used recommendations also move to the end of the tray. The helper returns coverage, not order, so the ordering decision changes one comparator and nothing else.

One sheet model

Add app/lib/logicSheets.ts, with no spreadsheet library inside it:

  • buildLogicSheets produces the rows for both the Table view and Export, so the screen and the file can't drift apart.
  • readLogicWorkbook turns plain string grids into a parsed model.
  • applyLogicImport is specified above.
// app/lib/logicSheets.ts (pure; no spreadsheet library)
export interface SheetCell { text: string; ref?: { nodeId?: string; answerId?: string; ruleId?: string } }
export interface SheetModel {
  name: "Rules" | "Answers" | "Recommendations";
  columns: Array<{ header: string; width: number }>;
  rows: SheetCell[][];
}
export function buildLogicSheets(doc: Quiz, ctx: LogicSheetContext): SheetModel[];
export function readLogicWorkbook(grids: Array<{ name: string; rows: string[][] }>): ParsedLogic;
export function applyLogicImport(doc: Quiz, parsed: ParsedLogic, ctx: LogicSheetContext): {
  doc: Quiz; changes: number; skipped: ImportIssue[]; notes: string[];
  undo: { before: LogicParts; after: LogicParts } | null;
};
// LogicSheetContext = { questions, categories (the quiz's rows), productIndex, style }

The file carries identity as well as text (D16), and that is a data-model contract, not a formatting preference:

  • Every "When they answer" cell reads Qn = answer, the machine form the describer already produces (D17).
  • The Answers sheet ends with a do-not-edit Answer ID column holding Answer.id, and the Rules sheet with a Rule ID column holding DecisionRule.id. Import matches on those ids, which is what lets a merchant retitle an answer without orphaning the rules that name it.
  • The Answers sheet updates answers in place and never adds or deletes one. The Recommendations sheet is read-only; edits to it are reported back as ignored. A missing column means leave unchanged, never clear.
  • The Rules sheet applies entirely or not at all, so a merchant never ends up with half a priority order.
  • Export is the template (D16, owner addition). The affordance reads as both, because the file Export writes is exactly the file Import accepts. On a quiz with no rules, Export still writes all three sheets with their headers, their id columns and one example row marked EXAMPLE in the do-not-edit Rule ID column, so a merchant who wants to build the logic in a spreadsheet has the format in front of them. There is no second file format.
  • Library: SheetJS CE 0.20.3, from the official SheetJS CDN tarball, loaded as a lazy chunk (D16). Never the npm xlsx 0.18.5 build: it has published CVEs and this code parses files a merchant supplies. The repo has no spreadsheet dependency today (package.json has papaparse for CSV and nothing else), so this is a new one and it goes through the owner's dependency review. The mock's loadXLSX() pulls xlsx 0.18.5 off cdnjs at runtime; it is a stand-in and is not ported Conflict.

The adapter between the grids and the library is client-only and holds no logic beyond conversion. Column sets and parsing rules are in Table view, Export and Import.

Recommendations are Category rows

  • Model (prisma/schema.prisma:173-218): id (cuid), shopId, quizId (null for shop-global rows), name, description, tags, productIds (the resolved members), source, sourceRef, manualProductIds, membership and discoveryRunId. The client sees them as BuilderCategory {id, name, description, tags, productIds, source, sourceRef, quizId} (stepProps.ts:17-26).
  • What Logic lists. Only the quiz's own rows, the ones with quizId set (LogicQuestionWidget.tsx:155-172). These are:
    • Step-1 picks (discoveryRunId "rb_buckets", step1Build.server.ts:84-100);
    • copies of custom groups (source "group", sourceRef = the shop-global group's id; bucketPersist.ts:17-22,62-72);
    • rows Logic created (discoveryRunId "logic-tab-<quizId>", api.categories.ensure-targets.tsx:103-115).
    Shop-global rows (quizId null) are the custom groups themselves. "+ Add recommendations" copies one into the quiz rather than targeting it in place (D15).
  • ensure-targets gains a "group" kind (D15). Today the resource kinds are tag, collection, product and metafield (api.categories.ensure-targets.tsx:29). Add "group", whose ref is the shop-global Category id, and resolve it the way Step 1 already does: copy the group's name, tags and productIds into the new quiz-scoped row with source: "group" and sourceRef: <that id> (bucketPersist.ts:62-72). A group has no membership rule to resolve, so it takes its own branch beside the four the route builds today (api.categories.ensure-targets.tsx:96-102): copy productIds from the source row instead of calling resolveMembership, and store the group's membership as it stands. Never store the group's own dominant source, or the type-scoped delete in Step 1 treats the row as a tag (bucketPersist.ts:17-22).
  • Rows are always quiz-scoped. Today ensure-targets reuses a matching shop-global row when the quiz has none (api.categories.ensure-targets.tsx:80-91), so a rule or answer can end up targeting a row the tray and the strip never list. Under D15 the endpoint always returns a quiz-scoped row: reuse the quiz's own row when there is one, otherwise create one, copying a shop-global match rather than returning it.
  • Matching. "In this quiz" and every duplicate check match on (source, sourceRef), with tag keys normalized to Step 1's slug form (D15), never on name.
  • Batching. At most 12 resources per call (api.categories.ensure-targets.tsx:37), which the Add recommendations window enforces by chunking its selection, and the calls are additive and idempotent, so a retry cannot duplicate a row.
  • Counts are productIds.length: the resolved members, not a count of sellable products. If the UI shows a sellable count, compute it from productIndex.
  • Ids must stay stable, because answers and rules store them. set-buckets (which diffs) and re-grouping keep logic-tab rows (funnelIntents.server.ts:270-314; step1Build.server.ts:58-66). Step 1's toggle-off and clear-visible delete rows by (source, sourceRef) without sparing logic-tab rows. A toggle-on for a key that already has a row deletes that row and creates a new one with a new id (step1Build.server.ts:103-133; funnelIntents.server.ts:227-229,244,253-255). The Logic workspace itself never deletes a row.
  • Deleted rows. Every lookup must tolerate a missing id: show the reference as a deleted recommendation and keep it removable (B9). A referenced row that no longer exists blocks publish with "A mapped result bucket no longer exists — re-pick the mapping before publishing." (quizPublish.ts:486-489). That text says "bucket" and contains an em dash, so never show it verbatim on the Logic screen; the check popover writes its own sentence (D18).
  • Trust. Publish fetches Category rows by id without a shop filter (quizPublish.ts:464-470). Logic must therefore write only ids it got from its own loader or from ensure-targets. applyLogicImport resolves recommendation names against ctx.categories and never accepts an id typed into the file.

Merchant-facing names come from shared constants, and none of them is stored

D18 renames the vocabulary everywhere at once, through the constants that already exist, and changes no stored value: the role stays "qualifier", the style stays "attributes", the action stays "prioritize". What changes is only what is drawn.

  • ROLE_JOBS (logicTabFields.ts:593-597) is the one source for role names: "Picks the result", "Narrows", and "Asked only" becomes "Info only". Its consumers are the role menu and the question window, which both import it rather than spelling the names out (LogicTabMenus.tsx:21, :564; QuestionWindow.tsx:26).
  • The widget's COPY block (LogicQuestionWidget.tsx:58-67) carries the rest: trayLabel "Recommendations from step 1" becomes "Recommendations", and chooseResult already reads "Choose a result", which is what both the empty Picks cell and the picker must say.
  • The style name lives beside the switch (Step3Shell.tsx:482 renders "Attributes + Rules" today): it becomes "Filter Results + Rules", and the string moves into the shared constants so the title switch, the popover and any future builder surface cannot drift.
  • Internal words never reach the merchant: decider, bucket, branch, boost, weight, score. That includes REC_SOURCES's "Tag buckets" group heading in the picks picker (LogicQuestionWidget.tsx:70-71).
  • The renames reach the builder whether or not D6 is parked, because both surfaces mount the same components: the builder's Rules inspector prints "Asked only" at ContextPanel.tsx:932 and a pinned test asserts it (ContextPanel.rules.test.tsx:99,108). Update the constant, the inspector and the test together, and re-run the builder's Logic view once before handing back.

Live surfaces that keep their data (D19)

Four things the mock does not draw are live today and stay live. None of them adds a stored field; they all read what is already on the document or in the product index.

  • The attribute picker on the Narrows flip: AttributePickerDialog in front of applyNarrowField (logicTabFields.ts:526-563), which seeds the values and the role in one result.
  • Every rule-flag reason, rendered in the mock's tag style rather than the shipped banner: half-built (halfBuiltRules, pathAnalyzer.ts:181-188), dead, target deleted and the broken-reference pair, whose two messages differ because is <missing> can never fire while is_not <missing> fires for everyone (pathAnalyzer.ts:151-178).
  • Product-count popovers on chips, from the product index.
  • The product-group picker's kind filters and drill-in.

The "won't work as written" banner is dropped, and "Explore every path" stays builder-only.

Still open and parked, where they touch this section

Three items are open. Build the plumbing, do not pick the behaviour.

D2, Filter Results + Rules only. In that style a Show rule appends after the base pool and is often cut off by the results cap, while the window's hint promises "these become the results". The owner chooses between changing the engine so Show puts its products first and changing the hint. Blocks in this section: nothing structural. No stored field changes either way; what waits is the Filter hint copy and, if the engine option wins, the ordering inside applyRuleAction (recommendDecider.ts:301-329) with the runtime proof rules attached. Settled for Rules only: the rule's recommendations are the whole result, the window offers Show only, and Pin and Hide are not drawn.

D10, question-type changes. What a type change does to the answers it drops and to the rules that named them. Blocks in this section: the final contract of changeQuestionType and setScalePoints, and the shape of their toast and Undo. Meanwhile: build both mutations as specified, keep the mock's behaviour (trim, name what went, offer Undo in the D9 pattern), and ship nothing that trims silently. The conditions that named a dropped answer stay on the rule and come back flagged, which is the state the analyzer and publish already understand.

D14, second half. Whether used recommendations also move to the end of the tray, and how the armed state reads on the builder's editor surface. Blocks in this section: the tray's comparator only. recommendationCoverage returns coverage and not order, and nothing about armed or placed is stored, so neither answer changes the data model.

When a step needs one of these, stop, ask the owner and name the waiting step in your report. Never pick an option silently.

Two areas are parked. Build neither now.

D4, diagnostics. The check popover shows findings and opens from the CTA; that is all. Do not rebuild "Check my logic", the Diagnose modal, "Test a path" or the AI review into this step, and do not add the "N to review" affordance. What this means for the data model: the analyzer stays a read-only dependency of recommendationCoverage and the Tier-1 report, nothing writes path_report_ai from this step, and the shipped PathTester and usePathQuality stay in place and unreferenced. They are not dead code and they are not yours to delete.

D6, builder parity. This work ships the funnel step 3 surface only. The style lives on the document so the new builder can read it with the same helper; keep every mutation, helper and constant in app/lib or in shared components rather than inside the funnel's shell, and do not gate the new screen on ruleFlow === "onboarding". Name the gap in your report and hand it to the main-builder project: a Rules-only quiz opens in today's builder as Filter Results + Rules (BuilderSettings.tsx:67-79; LogicTabCard.tsx:105, :112).

Connections to Recommendations, Questions, Results and the main builder

The owner has ruled, so this section is written in the indicative: what it describes is the thing to build, not a menu. A parenthesised decision id, "(D7)", points at the reasoning in Owner decisions; it is not a sign that anything is still being weighed. Three items are genuinely open and two areas are parked. Both are named again at every seam they touch, and neither is yours to settle.

The Logic step edits the same draft as its neighbours. It owns the quiz's logic style (Quiz.logic_style, new at the top level), question roles, Picks mappings (Answer.target_id / target_ids), narrowing values, per-answer routes and decision_rules, and it can add Category rows (recommendations). It reads the Category rows Step 1 produces and the questions Step 2 produces, hands the whole doc to Step 4 and, after "Open builder", to the builder's Logic view, which mounts the same LogicTabCard. From this work on it also writes to a seam it never touched before: the shopper runtime, because the style reaches publishedJson and the engine branches on it (D1). This section lists what crosses each seam, what must hold there and what changes on each side. None of it applies to legacy docs: they never reach Step3Shell or LogicTabCard (QuestionBuilderStage.tsx:76; BuilderSettings.tsx:52-65), and the engine branch and the safety net both sit inside the logic_model === "decider" arm. Every path:line is on origin/main unless marked mock.

The two styles are equals at every seam in this section. "Filter Results + Rules" and "Rules only" are two engine modes of the same logic_model: "decider" document (D1). Rules only is not a view of the other, not a simplified lens on it and not a beginner mode: it is its own method of deciding a result, it decides results for published quizzes, and it crosses these seams with exactly the same weight. Where a seam behaves differently in the two styles, this section says so for both; where a table row names only one, the other is unaffected.

The logic style, the one thing every seam now carries (D1, D5, D6)

What exists today

  • The style lives only in build_session.logic_style (quizSchema.ts:1708), a z.enum(["rules","attributes"]).optional() field whose comment block says it is "set once on first entry to the Logic stage via the set-logic-style intent" and that absent means "chooser not yet answered" (quizSchema.ts:1698-1708).
  • It has exactly one reader on origin/main, Step3Shell.tsx:141, and exactly one writer, funnelIntents.server.ts:1478. Nothing else in app/ mentions it. The builder does not read it, publish does not carry it, the engine does not see it.
  • Publish strips build_session wholesale before writing publishedJson (quizPublish.ts:789,803-810), so a style kept there can never reach the runtime by any route.
  • Step3Shell resolves a style from an in-session click, then the session field, then inference, else null, and null renders LogicStyleChooser instead of the workspace (Step3Shell.tsx:140-155,427).

What ships

  • A top-level Quiz.logic_style field, decider-gated and .optional(), never .default(). It rides the ordinary save path: the funnel's autosave writes every field of the client doc except build_session (funnelIntents.server.ts:124-131) and the builder's PUT writes the whole document (quizEditorIO.server.ts:341-359), so a pure mutation through useQuizDraft's commit persists it on both surfaces and no new intent is needed. New
  • Migration, read-only. build_session.logic_style becomes the migration source and stays parsed forever: read it when the top-level field is absent, never write it again. Leave the set-logic-style intent on disk (funnelIntents.server.ts:1468-1481) even though the chooser's removal takes its only caller. Partial
  • Resolution, with nothing written on load (D5). doc.logic_style, else build_session.logic_style, else inference (any question with role === "filter" means Filter Results + Rules; any rule and no filter role means Rules only), else Filter Results + Rules. It never returns null. Delete the null branch, LogicStyleChooser and its inert "Point based" row (Step3Shell.tsx:422-428; LogicStyleChooser.tsx:88-89,169-170), and delete the chooser's "nothing matches / your fallback" row with it (LogicStyleChooser.tsx:85): the safety net is real now and is not described by a chooser that no longer exists. Conflict
  • Publish carries it. The field is top-level, so it survives into publishedJson with the rest of the doc. Confirm this explicitly in a publish test: a decider doc with logic_style: "rules" publishes with the field present, and a decider doc without it publishes byte-identically to today. New
  • The engine reads it. resolveTarget takes doc: Pick<QuizDoc, "nodes" | "decision_rules"> today (recommendDecider.ts:217-220); widen the Pick to include logic_style and update all four live call sites: QuizRuntime.tsx:513, recommendationEngine.ts:393, pathEnumeration.ts:140 and the public rec-copy route q.$id.rec-copy.tsx:128. Missing one of these is how a Rules-only quiz ends up resolving differently on the page and in the AI copy for the same shopper. New

Why the field, and not the session

Three seams need it and the session reaches none of them. Publish strips build_session, so the runtime cannot see a session-held style. The builder's PUT writes the client's build_session back wholesale (quizEditorIO.server.ts:342-359) while the funnel's PUT keeps the server's (funnelIntents.server.ts:124-133), so the two surfaces can hold different copies of the session for the same quiz. And Step3Shell remounts on every Questions-to-Logic move (QuestionBuilderStage.tsx:180-234), which resets its local style and lets the stale session win. One top-level field on the document fixes all three at once, and it is what lets the parked builder work (D6) close its gap with a read rather than a migration.

Step 1 Recommendations

What Step 1 produces

  • Each recommendation is one Prisma Category row, referenced everywhere by its cuid (prisma/schema.prisma:173-218). Step 1 writes rows through funnel intents: toggle-bucket, select-all and clear-visible (funnelIntents.server.ts:216-268), set-buckets (funnelIntents.server.ts:284-325) and create-group (funnelIntents.server.ts:352-375), for the types product | tag | collection | group (bucketPersist.ts:21-22). The server resolves membership; the client only names keys (bucketPersist.ts:48-85).
  • Tag keys and tag names are the normalizeTags slug: lowercased, spaces and underscores turned into hyphens (enrichTags.ts:150-175; categoryGrouping.ts:143-185). A tag recommendation reads like dry-skin.
  • Custom groups are shop-global rows (quizId null) made by createShopGroup, from Step 1's "New group" wizard and from /studio/groups (groupCreate.server.ts:52-93; studio.groups.tsx:138-141). Adding one to a quiz writes a copy row with source "group", sourceRef set to the global id and a product snapshot, without membership or persona (funnelIntents.server.ts:352-375; step1Build.server.ts:88-101). The mock's Custom groups note "Groups you made on the Recommendations step." (index.html:753, mock) is narrower than that; the wording is the owner's.

What the Logic step reads

  • The funnel hands the Logic stage this quiz's rows plus every account group (funnelLoader.server.ts:59-97,305-314,346-349; Step1Funnel.tsx:298-316). The live tray keeps rows with quizId != null only (LogicQuestionWidget.tsx:155-172). The new tray, strip, pills and rule-window band keep that filter, in both styles.
  • The live rule window indexes every category, shop-global groups included (CreateRuleModal.tsx:443-450,511), so existing rules can target a shop-global group id directly. Those targets are not quiz rows: they never become pills or count in "N/M have a rule", but rule rows, the Table and the export must still name them. The funnel loader ships every account group and the builder loader ships the ones the draft references (quizEditorIO.server.ts:111-142), so both surfaces can resolve the name.
  • The Step-1 catalog (FunnelData.catalog: products, slug-keyed tags, collections, groups) ships on every stage (funnelLoader.server.ts:467-474), but Step1Funnel passes only the doc, categories, productIndex and collections to the Logic stage (Step1Funnel.tsx:298-316). Thread it through QuestionBuilderStage and Step3Shell into the card for the Add recommendations window (The Add recommendations window and the Add a question dialog). Both styles need it: Rules only reaches Add recommendations from the rule window's band and from the strip, Filter Results + Rules from the tray as well.

What the Logic step writes back

  • Logic adds recommendations only through POST /api/categories/ensure-targets: additive, idempotent, 1 to 12 resources per call, new rows stamped discoveryRunId "logic-tab-<quizId>" (api.categories.ensure-targets.tsx:35-38,103-116). It reuses this quiz's row first and a shop-global row second (api.categories.ensure-targets.tsx:80-95). D15 keeps that endpoint and extends it, and adds no second write path.
  • The group kind (D15). ResourceSchema.kind is z.enum(["tag","collection","product","metafield"]) today (api.categories.ensure-targets.tsx:29). Add "group", and copy a shop-global group into the quiz the way Step 1 does: source "group", sourceRef set to the global row's id, and the product snapshot, with no membership and no persona (funnelIntents.server.ts:352-375; step1Build.server.ts:88-101). New
  • Tag keys normalize to the Step-1 slug (D15). The live rule window keys tags by the raw, case-exact tag (CreateRuleModal.tsx:420-431), so its tag rows never match a Step-1 slug key and one tag can become two recommendations for the same quiz. Run every tag ref and name through the same normalizeTags slug Step 1 uses (enrichTags.ts:150-175) before the call, so the reuse lookup on (source, sourceRef) actually hits. Conflict
  • Rows are always quiz-scoped (D15). The reuse pass can return a shop-global row, which has quizId null and therefore stays out of the tray and the strip (LogicQuestionWidget.tsx:155-172). Create a quiz-scoped row instead of reusing a shop-global one from this endpoint, so a recommendation the merchant just added in Logic is visible where they added it. New
  • Batched at 12 (D15). BodySchema.resources already caps at 12 (api.categories.ensure-targets.tsx:36-38). The Add recommendations window batches to that cap and never sends a larger array. Exists
  • New rows appear before the loader revalidates only because the card merges them (extraCats, LogicTabCard.tsx:113-115,136-139,554). The Add recommendations window lifts its rows the same way.
  • When the merchant goes back to Step 1, Logic-added product, tag, collection and group rows show as selected picks, because the shelf lists every quiz row that has a sourceRef and a browser source, and group is one of them (funnelLoader.server.ts:223-236); metafield rows never show there. With tags normalized, a tag added in Logic now lights the same shelf key the merchant would have clicked in Step 1.
  • Logic never calls the Step-1 bucket intents, even though they check no stage. addBuckets deletes and recreates any row with the same (source, sourceRef), so the Category id changes and every answer and rule that points at it dangles (step1Build.server.ts:103-120). This is the single most destructive thing a wrong endpoint choice can do at this seam.

When a recommendation the Logic step uses is removed

  • Step 1 only warns. The single-row warning and both bulk confirms tell the merchant that "the Questions step will flag anything that breaks" (RecommendationBucketsStage.tsx:375,483,1562-1563). Since Logic became its own step that is wrong: reword all three to name the Logic step, without the em dashes they carry today.
  • The funnel never reconciles targets. reconcileDeciderTargets runs only when the builder leaves its Products view and in the upgrade wizard (UnifiedWorkspace.tsx:521-533 through reconcileBucketsToResultNodes's decider branch at bucketReconcile.ts:136-138; proposeDeciderConversion.ts:395), and even there it drops only dangling answer targets and override keys; rules keep theirs (bucketReconcile.ts:76-125).
  • Deleting a group on /studio/groups removes the shop-global row (studio.groups.tsx:132-136). A rule that targets that id directly dangles; quiz copies are separate rows and survive.
  • So the Logic step receives answers and rules that point at deleted rows, in both styles. Every place that names a recommendation (Picks chips, rule-sentence chips, rule rows, the rule window, the strip, Table cells, the export) renders a missing one as flagged and removable, and never throws (B9). The live card already guards this with "(deleted target)" chips and a "target deleted" rule flag (LogicQuestionWidget.tsx:1004-1012; LogicTabCard.tsx:214-222,696-700); keep the guard, keep rendering the reason in the mock's tag style (D19), and reword it as "recommendation deleted" (D18).
  • The report blocks with V4 for a deciding answer and V5 for a rule (pathReport.ts:193-221), and publish refuses with "A mapped result bucket no longer exists" (quizPublish.ts:482-490). All of these say "bucket"; reword them where they reach the merchant (D18). In Rules only the V4 family does not run at all, because that style has no deciding answers to check (D3), but V5 does: a Rules-only quiz whose only rule points at a deleted recommendation must still block, and its check popover must say so per rule.
Going back to Step 1 after Logic can replace all Logic work. The stepper and ‹ allow backward moves to any finished step (funnelIntents.server.ts:1488-1515). On Step 1, Continue on a manual-flow decider draft opens "What is your goal for the quiz?" (RecommendationBucketsStage.tsx:574-579,1181-1193,1496-1531), and "Generate with AI" fires continue-buckets, which starts a fresh headless generation (funnelIntents.server.ts:469-551). Goal-first and template-first drafts restart generation straight from Continue (flow1-confirm and flow3-confirm, funnelIntents.server.ts:823-905,938-1005). The question build re-seeds the draft and carries over only design tokens, logic_model and rec_page_settings (step2Build.server.ts:741-750,762-797; onboardingBuild.server.ts:182-204), and the decider flow writes every question with fresh answer ids (smartBuild.ts:360-374,420-446). Every role, Picks mapping, narrowing value, route and rule from steps 2 and 3 is replaced, with no warning. "Start from blank" keeps the built doc (funnelIntents.server.ts:1056-1107; smartBuild.ts:500-504). One thing does change here: add logic_style to the carry-over list beside logic_model, so a merchant who chose Rules only and then regenerates their questions comes back to Rules only rather than being silently moved. Everything else about this path is outside the redesign: do not change it silently; it is open call 1 below.
