Two Step 2 confirms promise more than the code does:

  • The delete confirm ends ", including references to them in Logic." (QuestionsWalkthrough.tsx:524-528), but deleteNode never touches decision_rules. Change the copy to say that rules using them will be flagged on the Logic step. Pruning the conditions instead would contradict the rule that dangling references are rendered flagged, never silently dropped (docs/design/logic-tab/DECISIONS.md:42-45), so that needs the owner.
  • The regenerate confirm says "Answer mappings are retained only where wording is unchanged." (QuestionsWalkthrough.tsx:563-565). That holds for Picks targets only: rules stay on the answer position, and narrowing values are replaced even when the wording is unchanged. Reword the confirm now; changing the merge is open call 2 below.

Moving "Picks results": one path, announced, with Undo (D9)

This is a Logic-step control that writes Step-2 data, so its contract belongs at the seam. Three surfaces can move the role and they must not behave differently.

  • What the mutation does. moveDecider demotes the old decider to qualifier and drops target_id / target_ids from every one of its answers, and the promote branch drops any pre-existing targets on the new decider as well, so it always arrives unmapped. decision_rules are deliberately untouched (deciderMutations.ts:178-238). That clearing is the behaviour D9 keeps: both questions' mappings go.
  • What the merchant is told today. Both live role menus already toast "X" now picks the result (was "Y") (LogicTabMenus.tsx:472-479; QuestionWindow.tsx:474-481). That sentence does not say anything was cleared and offers no way back. Partial
  • What ships. Count the targets the move drops before committing, and toast what was lost in the merchant's own words, for example Q1's 6 recommendations were removed, with an Undo action on the toast (D7). No confirm dialog: the toast plus Undo is the whole affordance. New
  • Undo restores the role and every target. It is an inverse mutation against the latest document, not a snapshot: re-promote the previous decider and write its answers' targets back by answer id, and restore the newly promoted question's role and any targets that were dropped from it. Nothing else the merchant did while the toast was up is reverted (D7). New
  • One path for all three writers. The role menu and the Table already share QuestionRoleControl, which swaps only the pill's dress by variant (LogicTabMenus.tsx:417-438). Import must call the same setJob rather than reimplementing the move: the mock's importer sets q.role directly and demotes the previous decider without clearing its targets (mock applyImport), which would leave a demoted question carrying live-looking mappings, exactly the cross-UI resurrection the promote branch's comment warns about (deciderMutations.ts:199-206). New
  • In Rules only this control does not appear. Roles do not decide anything in that style (D1), so there is no role menu, no role column in the Table and no role column in the export. The Rules-only export carries no Answers sheet, so that style's role column cannot round-trip. If a merchant imports a file that has one, leave roles unchanged and report the column as ignored, the same way an edited Recommendations sheet is reported (D16). The path still exists in the mutation layer that both styles call, so building it once here is what keeps the two styles honest.

Mounting and hand-off between steps 2 and 3

  • Continue on Questions opens the unread gate when screens are unread (QuestionsWalkthrough.tsx:88-121,438-470), then fires to-logic (QuestionBuilderStage.tsx:87-93; funnelIntents.server.ts:1453-1459).
  • One QuestionBuilderStage instance serves both steps: same ClientOnly slot, no key (Step1Funnel.tsx:298-316; ClientOnly.tsx:17-27). Its useQuizDraft doc reads the loader once (useQuizDraft.ts:27-28), so edits carry straight from Questions into Logic, and its build_session is the one loaded at first mount. Step3Shell remounts on every Questions-to-Logic move (QuestionBuilderStage.tsx:180-234), so its local style (Step3Shell.tsx:140-155) resets and the stale session wins: Back then Continue loses the chosen style. The doc-level field closes this. With the style on the document it rides the same client doc that already survives the remount, so the resolved style is stable across Back and Continue without any lifting of component state. Delete localStyle, sessionStyle, pickLogicStyle and the onPickLogicStyle prop with the chooser (Step3Shell.tsx:140-162; QuestionBuilderStage.tsx:94-101). Conflict
  • Coming back from Results is different: QuestionBuilderStage unmounts on the Results stage and remounts with the loader's fresh doc (Step1Funnel.tsx:298). The doc-level style survives that too, because it was saved; the session field, which the funnel autosave never writes, would not have been.
  • Undo toasts commit into this shared doc. An inverse commit reverts only its own change; a whole-doc snapshot, the pattern the regenerate Undo uses (QuestionBuilderStage.tsx:116,125-130), would also revert anything edited since, in either step. That is why D7 forbids the snapshot for every Logic-step Undo, including the D9 role move and the deletes.
  • pendingRuleJumpStash (Step3Shell.tsx:54,203-207) is set only by Step3Shell's parked content mode (Step3Shell.tsx:297-303), which QuestionBuilderStage never mounts today (QuestionBuilderStage.tsx:180-203), and the Questions walkthrough has no rule links. Keep the stash and its mount-time consumer for the parked A/B, but have the consumer open or scroll to the stored rule id through the card's new rule focus instead of scrolling to the card top: in Filter Results + Rules the rules sit in the right column (D22), and in Rules only they are the rules row under the header (D23).
Routes set in Logic move where new questions land (live bug). appendBankQuestion promises to append "to the END of the spine" but anchors on the last node of straightThroughRun (questionMutations.ts:124-136,158). That run stops at the first node that does not have exactly one inbound and one outbound edge (questionMutations.ts:311-343), and a route set in Logic adds a handle edge beside the plain edge (edgeMutations.ts:96-128), so the routed question ends the run. The new question is spliced onto the anchor's plain out-edge (questionMutations.ts:11-33). Running the origin/main logic on a three-question doc: with a route on Q2 the new question lands between Q1 and Q2; with a route on Q1 it becomes the first question. Both hosts still say "Adds Q{n}" with n = count + 1 (AddQuestionDialog.tsx:101; LogicTabCard.tsx:570; QuestionsWalkthrough.tsx:569). Fix it in the pure mutation, gated on logic_model === "decider" so legacy editing is unchanged: anchor on the last question along the default path before the result terminal. Compute the "Qn added" number from orderedQuestions after the commit, and add a unit test with a routed doc. This bites both styles, because routes are per-answer and independent of the style.

The spreadsheet and Paste rules as write paths (D16, D13, D12, D17)

Import and Paste rules are the only bulk writers into the draft, and Import is the only place outside the Questions step that rewrites question text, answer text, types and roles. That makes the file format a seam contract, not a feature of the Table view, so its identity rules live here as well as in Table view, Import and Export.

The file carries identity, not just text (D16)

  • Every "When they answer" cell reads Qn = answer. The mock's findAnswer already accepts that form and falls back to a bare answer-text search across every question; the export does not always write it. Write it always, so a file round-trips without depending on answer text being unique. Partial
  • A trailing, do-not-edit "Answer ID" column on the Answers sheet and "Rule ID" on the Rules sheet. Identity comes from the id when it is present and resolvable; the text columns are then edits to apply, not keys to match on. Label the columns so a merchant knows not to touch them, and ignore an unknown id with a named reason rather than creating anything. New
  • The Answers sheet updates in place and never adds or deletes an answer. A row whose id does not resolve is reported as skipped. Adding and removing answers stays in the Questions step and the question window, where the route, mapping and rule consequences are visible. New
  • The Recommendations sheet is read-only. It exists so the merchant can see what a rule may point at. Any edit to it is reported as ignored, with the count, in the import summary. Recommendations are created through ensure-targets only (D15), never by typing a name into a spreadsheet. New
  • A missing column means leave unchanged, never clear. This is the rule that makes a partially filled template safe. The mock's importer is already close to this (it reads each column with ci(name) and skips what it cannot find), but state it as a contract and test it: a file with only the "Answer" column changes only answer text. Partial
  • The Rules sheet stays all-or-nothing. The mock applies the Rules sheet only when every row parsed (mock applyImport: if(bad)skipped+=bad;else{...}). Keep that. Rule order is priority, so a half-applied sheet silently reorders the quiz's logic.
  • Apply the Answers sheet before the Rules sheet. Rule conditions reference answers, so a file that renames an answer and adds a rule about it must resolve in that order. The mock sorts the sheets to guarantee it (mock applyImport's isRules sort); keep the ordering explicit rather than relying on sheet order in the file.

Export is the template (D16, owner addition)

  • Export already writes exactly the file Import reads. Label the affordance so it reads as both: "Export" downloads the current logic, and that download is the template. Do not add a second format, a second button or a separate "Download template" path. New
  • On a quiz with no rules, Export still writes every sheet with its headers, the id columns and one example row marked EXAMPLE in the do-not-edit Rule ID column, so a merchant who wants to build in a spreadsheet has the shape. Import accepts that same file back. New
  • The example row must not import as a rule, and the file contract already says how (Table view, Export and Import owns it): the row carries the reserved Rule ID EXAMPLE, Import skips it whatever its capitalisation and reports "Ignored the example row". Do not give it a blank id and do not key the skip off "#": a blank Rule ID means a new rule, and "#" is never a key and never causes a skip (B5, B36). The mock's applyImport skips a row whose "#" cell is empty or a dash; that part is not ported.

The library (D16)

  • SheetJS CE 0.20.3, from the official SheetJS CDN tarball, loaded as a lazy chunk so it is not in the funnel's initial bundle. Neither the read nor the write path may pull it eagerly.
  • Never npm xlsx 0.18.5. It has published CVEs, and Import parses files the merchant supplies, which is precisely the threat model those CVEs describe. There is no spreadsheet dependency in package.json on origin/main today, so this is a clean first choice rather than a swap.
  • Both failure modes get merchant-readable copy, as the mock already does: the writer failing to load, and an unreadable file (mock importFile and the xport handler).

Answers · Question, AnswerQuestion and answer text, in place, by idAn unresolvable Answer ID; any attempt to add or remove a row
Answers · TypeThe question type, through the shared type-change wrapperA type string it cannot parse. What the wrapper does to answers and rules is still open (D10), so route it and do not special-case it here
Answers · What it doesThe role, through the one D9 path (moveDecider / setQuestionRole), toasting what was clearedAn unknown role name. In Rules only the column is ignored and reported as ignored
Answers · Shows / keepsPicks targets on a deciding answer; narrowing values on a filter answerA name that matches no recommendation. It never creates one
Answers · ThenThe per-answer routeA destination that is not a later question or the results
Rules · What happens, Recommendations, When they answerThe whole rule list, all or nothing, matched by Rule ID where presentAny unparsable row, which skips the entire sheet. NOT (A AND B) is rejected by name: "is not" and "all of" cannot be combined (D12)
Recommendations, any columnNothingEverything, reported as ignored with a count

"is not" and "all of" cannot combine (D12)

  • The engine already behaves this way: groupOk applies any_of only to the is conditions of a question group, while is_not conditions always require that none of the listed answers are selected (recommendDecider.ts:341-353). Listing a question in any_of whose group is negated therefore changes nothing at runtime. That is why D12 adds no storage: it makes the UI and the file agree with the engine.
  • In the rule window, an "is not" row hides the any/all toggle and the row means none of these answers. Sentences read not (A or B) (D17).
  • Import rejects NOT (A AND B) with that reason in the skipped-row summary. The mock's parseWhen currently accepts it and sets both the negation and the all-of flag; that is the one parser change this ruling requires. Conflict

Paste rules splits a cross-question "or" (D13)

  • rulePaste.ts is frozen and stays frozen. It resolves an across-question OR into a single line carrying match: "any" (rulePaste.ts:56-60), and PasteRulesModal writes that straight onto the created rule (PasteRulesModal.tsx:113-121).
  • The split happens at the commit, not in the parser: a parsed line whose match is "any" becomes one rule per question group, adjacent, in the parsed order, with the same verb and the same recommendations. Under first-match-wins this is identical in behaviour and readable as a sentence, which a cross-question "or" is not. New
  • Existing rules that already carry a cross-question match: "any" still render faithfully and keep it when edited. The field stays parsed forever (quizSchema.ts:1746); nothing migrates it.
  • The toast counts the rules actually created, so a line that split into three says three (PasteRulesModal.tsx:124-128). It gets the same Undo as any other rule write (D7).

Sentences, the Table and the export read differently on purpose (D17)

  • Rule sentences are verb-first and answers-only, for example "Show dryness when ...", with parentheses around multi-answer groups, bold joins, not (...) for negated groups and full-text tooltips on truncated answers. A question label appears only when the same answer text also exists on another question. The mock's sentence() is the reference, including the bare variant the rule rows and the window footer use.
  • The Table and the export always use the machine form, Q7 = Yes. That is what makes the D16 identity contract work and what lets findAnswer resolve without guessing. The two forms are not alternatives to pick between: the readable one is for reading, the machine one is for round-tripping.

Step 4 Results

  • Continue fires to-rec-page (QuestionBuilderStage.tsx:87-93; funnelIntents.server.ts:1525-1533). Nothing flushes the 700 ms debounce first (useQuizDraft.ts:58-68), the intent writes back the doc it loaded when the request started, and ResultsGuided seeds its own draft once from the loader (ResultsGuided.tsx:204) and autosaves that whole doc. The last Logic edit can be lost. With the style on the document, so can the style itself, which raises the stakes on this fix. The fix (flush and await, and navigation intents that patch only build_session on a freshly read draft) is in Checks, the Fix-N gate, the check popover and Continue. The same race runs the other way on Back from Results (funnelIntents.server.ts:1510-1513).
  • Results edits the page settings (rec_page_settings.global, ResultsGuided.tsx:345; resultsGuided/state.ts:88-101) and the offer (discount_config, resultsGuided/state.ts:142-144); it never touches roles, mappings, routes, rules or the style. Its "How many to show" stepper and layout (gridMax 1 to 5, ResultsGuided.tsx:429-472) decide how many products a shopper sees: the engine shows a hero plus up to gridMax more, default 3 (recommendDecider.ts:120,418-462), and the merchant sets this after writing rules.
  • The Results preview draws productIndex.slice(0, 8) (GuidedPreview.tsx:91), not what the logic resolves. Nothing here changes that; don't treat the preview as a check of the Logic step, in either style.
  • Per-recommendation pages exist in schema and engine (rec_page_settings.overrides, quizSchema.ts:1909-1931; recommendDecider.ts:189-202), but their only editor, RecPageV2Panel, is mounted only in RecommendationStage's decider branch (RecommendationStage.tsx:106-121), which Step1Funnel never mounts for decider drafts (Step1Funnel.tsx:325-347). Out of scope: recommendations added on the Logic step use the global page settings, in both styles.
  • "Open builder" fires generate-build (Step1Funnel.tsx:106-116) once every guided step has been visited (ResultsGuided.tsx:293-343). On a built draft it upgrades an untouched seed intro, sets buildState to null and redirects to /studio/:id?mode=ai or /app/quizzes/:id/studio?mode=ai (funnelIntents.server.ts:1936-1964; studio_.onboarding_.$quizId.tsx:30-32; app.onboarding_.$quizId.tsx:34-36). The builder ignores ?mode and opens on Build (studio_.$id.tsx:111-112; UnifiedWorkspace.tsx:510-516).

The safety net, and why Results gains no control (D1)

  • What ships. A shopper no rule matches gets the safety net, in Rules only and in Filter Results + Rules, and the same net covers a result that resolves but turns out empty in Filter Results + Rules. One behaviour for both styles.
  • Where it lands. Today a decider doc whose target does not resolve renders a bare card containing the localized no_results_match string and nothing else (QuizRuntime.tsx:1713-1721), and the named fallbacks run only for a target that resolved and came back empty (QuizRuntime.tsx:1579-1595; deciderFallbackProducts at recommendDecider.ts:522-538). The unresolved branch is where the net goes. Partial
  • What it resolves over. The existing chain, unchanged: global_fallback, then rec_page_settings.global.emptyFallbackCol, then safetyNetCol, and an explicit "hide" is respected (QuizRuntime.tsx:1584-1595; recommendDecider.ts:515-538). Publish already fetches and bakes both collections into product_index for decider docs (quizPublish.ts:438-448), so no live fetch is added and no publish change is needed for it.
  • No new merchant control. The owner removed FallbackSection from Results on 2026-08-18 (ResultsGuided.tsx:194-199,513-515); its only importer is the unmounted LogicScroll (LogicScroll.tsx:24), and Step3Shell's comment that the fallback lives on Results is stale (Step3Shell.tsx:513-519). Putting a control back on Results would need the owner's explicit OK and is not part of this work. Build the net over the chain as it stands, and raise in your report that a decider quiz can reach publish with nothing configured in that chain, in which case the shopper sees the same bare card as today.
  • It is a runtime change, so it carries the runtime proof rules. Legacy docs byte-identical, full e2e, screenshot review, the byte pin. Prove three cases explicitly: a legacy doc, a decider doc with no logic_style, and a decider doc with logic_style: "rules". Only the third may differ. The shopper runtime still has to work on phones, so the no-match and fallback states get a phone screenshot as well as a desktop one.
  • No Logic copy promises a fallback the merchant did not configure. The check popover may say a Rules-only quiz has shoppers no rule catches; it does not claim they will see products.
Still open at this seam (D2, Filter Results + Rules only). Do not pick it. In Filter Results + Rules, a Show rule appends its products after the base pool and is then cut off by the results cap, while the window's hint promises "these become the results". The owner must choose: change the engine so Show puts its products first, or change the hint to describe appending. It blocks the Show hint's wording in the rule window and any Logic copy that says how many products a Show rule puts in front of a shopper. Until it is settled, write no copy on either side of that promise. For Rules only this is settled: the first matching rule's recommendations are the whole result, so "these become the results" is true there, and the rule window in that style offers Show only, because Pin and Hide have nothing to act on under a no-base resolution (recommendDecider.ts:276-284). The mock still draws all three verbs in both styles (VERBS in modalHTML()); change that when you build it.

Main builder

Parked by the owner (2026-09-22): builder parity (D6). The main builder is being rebuilt, so this work ships the funnel step 3 surface only. Do not build the two-style screen into the builder, do not gate the new UI behind ruleFlow === "onboarding" or anything else that would make it unreusable there, and do not delete what the new builder will mount. The style lives on the document (D1), so the new builder can read it with one line rather than a migration. Meanwhile: run the builder's Logic view once before you hand back, because the shared leaves change under it whether you aim at them or not, and name the gap in your report so the main-builder project inherits it.

Undo and keyboard in the builder

  • The builder keeps a 50-deep whole-doc history: every commit pushes the pre-edit doc, and undo and redo replay through the autosave (UnifiedWorkspace.tsx:160-233). ⌘Z, ⌘⇧Z and Ctrl+Y are bound on window and skipped while focus is in an input, textarea, select or contentEditable (UnifiedWorkspace.tsx:256-284). The funnel has no history (QuestionBuilderStage.tsx:61-72).
  • So every toast Undo is an inverse mutation sent through the host's commit (D7): the builder records it as its own entry and ⌘Z keeps working. Never wire a toast to the builder's undo(), which pops the latest commit whether or not it was the delete. Never snapshot the whole doc, which would revert unrelated edits made while the toast was up.
  • Accumulation is part of the contract: several deletes in a row while the toast is still showing join one Undo, so one click takes the whole run back. Build it as a run of inverse mutations against the latest document, restoring each rule at its index by its id, not as a stored document.
  • Every commit is one history entry. Committing an inline edit on every keystroke, as useContentEditable does and as the Build inspector's text fields already do (ContentTab.tsx:369-375,447,631), fills the 50 entries with single letters. Commit once per edit session in the card (Enter or blur), or give the host's commit a way to fold one session into one entry.
  • The builder's window key handlers also run on the Logic view: Esc clears the Build selection with no field guard (UnifiedWorkspace.tsx:464-475); Delete or Backspace arms a delete of the Build-selected step when focus is outside a field (UnifiedWorkspace.tsx:481-502); "[" toggles the left panel outside fields (UnifiedWorkspace.tsx:425-439). The card stops propagation for the keys it handles (Esc per layer, arrows in menus) and binds no Delete or Backspace on rows. The new keyboard reorder on rule rows (D11) uses the existing ↑/↓ buttons, which are real buttons and therefore consume the key as a click; it never binds a bare arrow key on the row.

The ✎ Edit button goes, replaced by the row click. Partial

Invariants every seam keeps

  1. Nothing Logic does changes a Category id that answers or rules reference: new rows come from ensure-targets only (D15), never from the Step-1 bucket intents.
  2. A removal anywhere (a Step-1 row, a Step-2 question or answer, a builder re-group, a deleted group) leaves the reference flagged in Logic and blocking in the report and at publish, never silently dropped (docs/design/logic-tab/DECISIONS.md:42-45), and never crashes a render (B9). This holds identically in both styles.
  3. Rules reference answer ids. Anything that keeps ids by position (regenerate) says so to the merchant, and the spreadsheet carries the ids so a round-trip never has to guess (D16).
  4. One type-change path serves Step 2, Logic, Import and the builder inspector, including the all-of to any-of conversion and clearing min_selections / max_selections. Its body is still open (D10); the routing is not.
  5. One role-move path serves the role menu, the Table and Import: moveDecider to promote, setQuestionRole to demote, a toast naming what was cleared, and an Undo that restores the role and every target (D9). No confirm dialog.
  6. One stored logic style on the document that every surface reads and publish carries (D1). Never state that dies when Step3Shell remounts, and nothing written to the quiz on page load (D5).
  7. No navigation loses an edit: flush and await the pending save before any intent, and navigation intents patch only build_session on a freshly read draft.
  8. Undo is an inverse mutation committed through the host's commit on both surfaces, never a whole-doc snapshot, and every route that mounts the card or the funnel has a QzToastProvider (D7, D21).
  9. One style-aware Tier-1 report drives the CTA, the check popover and publish, and it never reads safer than the publish gate (D3).
  10. The merchant never meets an internal word. No decider, bucket, branch, boost, weight, score or "Tag buckets" in any string that reaches a screen, a toast, a spreadsheet header or a publish error, on either surface (D18).
  11. data-testid="logic-tab-card" on every Logic screen and view, data-node-id on rail rows and the pane, and one controllable selection plus rule focus that Step3Shell, openLogicAt, health links and the path explorer all drive.
  12. Legacy docs see none of it: each new branch is gated on logic_model === "decider", the appendBankQuestion anchor fix and the runtime safety net included. A decider doc with no logic_style resolves and renders exactly as it does today.

Seam checks

  • Unit. appendBankQuestion on a routed decider doc lands the question last, and a legacy doc keeps today's anchor (quizMutations.test.ts).
  • Unit. resolveTarget with logic_style: "rules" ignores the decider mapping and returns the first matching rule's targets; with no matching rule it returns null; with the field absent it returns exactly what it returns today for the same doc. Pin the third case against the current output so a regression is loud.
  • Unit. A doc parsed and re-serialized without a logic_style is byte-identical, in both the legacy and the unstyled decider case.
  • Unit. The D9 role move clears both questions' targets, the announcement counts what was dropped, and Undo restores the previous decider's role and every target by answer id, leaving an unrelated edit made in between untouched.
  • Unit. Import: an Answers sheet with only the "Answer" column changes only answer text; a row with an unresolvable Answer ID is skipped with a reason; a Recommendations-sheet edit is reported as ignored; a Rules sheet with one unparsable row changes nothing; NOT (A AND B) is rejected by name.
  • Unit. Paste: a line whose parse carries match: "any" commits as one rule per question group, adjacent, same verb, same recommendations, and the toast counts the rules created.
  • Unit. Leaving multi-select through TypeChipSelector runs the shared wrapper; TypeChipSelector.test.tsx:141-162 changes only if D10 changes Five-point.
  • Probe, local build and fixture. Back to Questions then Continue keeps the chosen style, in both styles; the draft read right after Continue holds the last Logic edit; a recommendation removed on Step 1 shows flagged in Logic and the CTA reads "Fix N issues to continue"; Export on a quiz with no rules downloads a file that imports back with no changes and no skips.
  • Probe. q3-questions-verify.mjs passes with the dialog fixes; builderv3-verify.mjs:458-466 finds one logic-tab-card in both styles; create-rule-verify.mjs passes on both surfaces; "Open in Logic →" selects the question.
  • Runtime proof (the safety net and the engine branch). The same doc rendered on the local build and on the pre-change deploy, normalized outerHTML diffed, for a legacy doc and for a decider doc with no logic_style: identical. For a decider doc with logic_style: "rules": the difference is the expected one and nothing else. Full e2e, screenshot review of the no-match and fallback states on desktop and on a phone, and the byte pin after the deploy.
  • Screenshots. The builder's Logic view with the tray armed, an Undo toast on the embedded funnel and on the embedded builder after D21, a Rules-only quiz opened in the builder (the named D6 gap, captured as evidence rather than as a bug to fix here). The full list is in Tests.

Implementation plan: phases, files and gates Draft · not yet fact-checked

The work splits into seven phases. Pure library code comes first, so that every screen is built on tested mutations and helpers. The style field, the engine and the runtime come next, because the Rules-only copy promises an engine that must already exist. Then the shared primitives, then the shared Logic workspace, and last the two hosts: funnel step 3, which is what ships, and the builder, which is parked and only has to keep working.

The owner has ruled. Everything below is written in the indicative: it is the thing to build, not a menu. A parenthesised decision id, "(D7)", points at the reasoning in Owner decisions; it does not mean anything is still being weighed. Three items are genuinely open and two areas are parked; both lists are immediately below, and each is marked again at the step it touches. Never pick an open item silently.

Every path:line is origin/main at b4aa278 unless it is marked as the mock. Read code with git -C /Users/chase/code/quizocalypse-builder show origin/main:<path>; the working tree is stale. Mock behaviour is cited by identifier (ACT.msave, fitTwoRows, sentence()), never by line number, because the file is still being edited.

Before Phase 1

  • Build on origin/main, never on the local builder branch. That branch is 163 commits behind and lacks most of the shipped Logic step: there is no LogicQuestionWidget.tsx and no ValuePickerPopover.tsx in its logicTab/. Create a worktree on a new local branch, for example: git -C /Users/chase/code/quizocalypse-builder fetch origin, then git -C /Users/chase/code/quizocalypse-builder worktree add -b logic-redesign /Users/chase/code/quizocalypse-logic origin/main. The main checkout holds unrelated uncommitted work (integrations, design docs). Leave it alone.
  • In the worktree, run npm ci and npx prisma generate. .env is gitignored, so it exists only in the main checkout. Start every Bash block with set -a; source /Users/chase/code/quizocalypse-builder/.env; set +a.
  • Make no commits unless the owner asks. This overrides the repo's commit-to-main habit. A phase is finished when its checks pass on the uncommitted worktree.
  • The mock source is untracked and is still changing: on 2026-09-21 it is 1,200 lines. Re-read the current file at the start of each phase, and search it by identifier.

Three items are still open. Do not pick them.

D2, in Filter Results + Rules only. There, "Show" appends after the base pool and is often cut off by the results cap, while its hint promises "these become the results". The owner chooses between changing the engine so Show puts its products first and changing the hint to describe appending. Blocks: the applyRuleAction show branch (recommendDecider.ts:301-316, Phase 2), the Filter-side Show hint copy in the rule window (Phase 4), and the Filter-side test that pins what Show does (Phase 1). Does not block: anything in Rules only, where Show is settled as the whole result, or the verbs themselves. Build the hint from one style-aware function so the answer is a one-line diff.

D10, question-type changes. What a type change does to answers and to the rules that referenced them: scale conversions dropping answers, five-point trimming to five, and the rules pointing at the dropped answers. Blocks: the answer-removal rule inside setScalePoints and the type-change wrapper (Phase 1), and QuestionTypePopover plus Five-point stamping in AddQuestionDialog (Phase 4). Build meanwhile: the text, bounds and end-label mutations, the wrapper's skeleton and its single doc commit, and the snapshot restore its Undo will use. Ship no silent trim.

D14, second half. Whether used recommendations also move to the end of the tray, and how the armed state reads on the builder's editor surface, which re-points the accent colour (UnifiedWorkspace.tsx:1804; quizocalypse.css:250-278). Blocks: tray ordering (Phase 4) and the builder accent token (Phase 6, itself parked). Does not block: the colours or the one-row "+N more" layout.

When a step reaches one of these, stop, ask the owner, and name the waiting step in your report.

Two areas are parked. Build neither now.

D4, diagnostics. The check popover shows findings and opens from the CTA. Do not rebuild "Check my logic", the Diagnose modal, "Test a path" or the AI review into this step, and do not add the "N to review" affordance. Leave PathTester and usePathQuality in place and unreferenced from the new step: PathTester is still rendered by the legacy builder Logic view (LogicView.tsx:246, 248), by DiagnoseModal (:80) and by ContextPanel (:657), while BuilderSettings and RecPageDiagram only name it in comments, so it is not dead code and it is not yours to delete. When diagnostics are built later they hang off this popover's footer, so give the popover a footer slot and leave it empty. Meanwhile: Step3Shell stops publishing the funnel-bar healthPill (Step3Shell.tsx:328-340) because the CTA carries the count; the healthPill slot itself stays in the chrome (Step1Funnel.tsx:150).

D6, builder parity. The main builder is being rebuilt, so this work ships the funnel step 3 surface only. The style lives on the document (D1), so the new builder can read it. Three things follow. First, build every shared component so the main-builder work can mount it: the new features stay behind LogicTabCard props, and nothing is gated on ruleFlow === "onboarding" or on anything else that would make the screen unreusable. Second, the builder still has to keep working, because both surfaces mount the same card (Phase 6). Third, name the gap in your report and hand it to the main-builder project: a Rules-only quiz opens in today's builder as Filter Results + Rules, because BuilderLogicView passes no logicStyle (BuilderSettings.tsx:67-79; the prop at LogicTabCard.tsx:105 and rulesOnly = logicStyle === "rules" at :112), and today's builder Logic view still writes rules.

Phase 1 · Pure library work

No UI. Everything here is pure and unit-tested, and every later phase consumes it. The last column names the ruling a row implements, or the open item a single function waits on.

FileKindWorkRuling
app/lib/mutations/questionMutations.tsChange

Text. Add setQuestionText(doc, nodeId, text) and setAnswerText(doc, nodeId, answerId, text). Each collapses whitespace, trims, and clamps to 150 characters (questions) or 60 (answers). Both return the doc unchanged when the result is empty. Text is min(1) (quizSchema.ts:102,209), and a PUT that fails the parse returns 400 (funnelIntents.server.ts:117-123).

Shape. Add setSelectionBounds (multi-select only, 1 ≤ min ≤ max ≤ answer count) and setScaleEndLabels (at most 40 characters, quizSchema.ts:319-320; an empty label removes the key).

Points. Add setScalePoints for 2 to 10 points. It adds numeric answers with fresh ids, or removes the last answers together with their handle edges, as removeAnswer does (questionMutations.ts:261-288). It reports which rules now dangle and never prunes them.

Undo. Add a question-snapshot restore, which is the inverse the type and points Undo commits (B7). It restores text, type, role, required, bounds, scale_config, answers and answer targets for one node, by id.

Five point. appendBankQuestion (127-159) takes an optional scale_config and writes it only when it is passed, so every existing caller gets byte-identical output.

The new functions carry the decider gate. The shared appendBankQuestion stays ungated.

D7 (the restore); open: D10 for what a points change does to answers
app/lib/mutations/deciderMutations.tsChange

Each new function opens with the decider gate, as its neighbours do (24, 188, 257).

The style. Add setLogicStyle(doc, style). It is gated, returns its input when the value is unchanged, and writes the top-level logic_style field and nothing else. It is the only writer of that field, which is why legacy docs can never gain the key.

Restore. Add restoreDecisionRule(doc, rule, index) and a batch form (B35). Both re-insert by id at the clamped index, lowest index first, and do nothing when the id already exists. These are the inverses the delete and import Undos commit; no flow ever restores a whole-document snapshot (D7).

Rule shape. Add convertRulesToAnyOf(doc, questionId), which returns the count for the toast, and normalizeDecisionRule, which produces the canonical stored shape (section rule-window, B13). Under D12 normalizeDecisionRule also drops a question from any_of when that question's group is all "is not": an is-not group already means "none of these answers" in the engine (recommendDecider.ts:344-347), and any_of only relaxes the "is" conditions (341, 349-351), so the stored shape needs no new key.

Type change. Add the type-change wrapper: setQuestionType, then convertRulesToAnyOf, then clear min/max when the question is not multi-select, then the Five-point scale_config. It imports ./questionMutations directly, never the barrel (quizMutations.ts:5-7). One doc commit.

The Picks move. Add the inverse for moveDecider. It restores both questions' role, required flag and answer targets from a snapshot taken before the move. moveDecider keeps clearing them by a locked rule (178-238); D9 changes nothing about the clear, only that it is announced and reversible.

The paste split. Add the splitter that turns one cross-question "or" rule into adjacent rules with the same verb and the same targets. Under first-match-wins the result is identical, which is why the split is safe.

D1, D7, D9, D12, D13; open: D10 inside the wrapper
app/lib/logicStyle.tsNew

One pure module holding the two style readers, so the style is read identically everywhere. They are not the same value; see Data model, persistence and the mutations to add, which owns the contract.

resolveLogicStyle(doc) decides which screen opens, returns "rules" or "attributes" and never null (D5). Order: doc.logic_style; then build_session.logic_style, for drafts that picked a style before the field existed; then inference, where any question with the "filter" role means Filter Results + Rules and any rule with no filter role means Rules only (the shipped inference lives at Step3Shell.tsx:142-155); then "attributes". It writes nothing, and only the screen calls it.

engineLogicStyle(doc) = doc.logic_style ?? "attributes" is what the engine will run. recommendDecider, buildTier1Report, validateQuiz and publishQuiz read this one and never the inferred screen style.

Why two and not one. D5 forbids writing on load, so a quiz whose style was only ever inferred carries no field, and an absent field means today's engine: that is the invariant that keeps every existing quiz byte-identical. Publish never bakes an inferred style; it carries logic_style exactly as stored. So a draft that opens on Rules only by inference still runs the Filter engine for its shoppers until the merchant uses the title switch once, and the report must check the engine's answer, not the screen's. The check popover carries the warning that says so (Checks, the Fix-N gate, the check popover and Continue).

Parse and diff. It parses rows and diffs canonical rules by identity. A missing column means "leave unchanged", never "clear".   • Full local e2e against the local build, with screenshots.
  • The written 2-lens review.

Name the docs one click could re-point, before any deploy. Publish bakes nothing, so no existing quiz changes what it does for a shopper on its own. The risk is one click away instead. The screen resolver infers a style for a document that has none, and one class of existing decider quiz infers wrong: rules, no question with the "filter" role, and answers already mapped to targets. Inference opens that quiz on Rules only while its shoppers still run the Filter engine, and the header's rule that choosing the style already shown writes it (see Screen shell) means a single click on the title menu saves "rules", after which the first matching rule is the whole result and the answer mappings are ignored. For a quiz the merchant actually built rules-only that is the point of D1; for one built on mappings it is a change in what shoppers get.

So: write a test that enumerates this class from a document, run it over the deploy fixtures (cmqwd15f…, cmr3ku9kb…, cmr9gir03…), and put the list in your report with the question. Republish nothing until the owner has seen it. The byte-pinned quiz is legacy and is not in this class.

The CI smoke and the byte pin run only after a deploy the owner has approved.

  2. Phase 2 on its own. The runtime slice, with the full runtime procedure. It ships before any Rules-only copy, because that copy promises this engine.

There is no fourth slice: builder parity is parked and belongs to the main-builder project.

Rules for every phase

  • Decider gate. Every new mutation, and every engine or validation branch, is gated on logic_model === "decider" (patterns: deciderMutations.ts:24, recommendationEngine.ts:392, quizValidation.ts:113). The style branch goes inside the decider arm, never beside it. Legacy docs stay byte-identical.
  • Schema fields. New schema fields use .optional(), never .default() (quizSchema.ts:1992).
  • Two first-class styles. Copy, checks, tests, probes and screenshots cover both. Rules only is never written as a lens on, or a simplified version of, Filter Results + Rules.
  • One report. Each surface has one Tier-1 report (Step3Shell.tsx:126-129; UnifiedWorkspace.tsx:571-574). Style awareness goes inside buildTier1Report, never into a second counter, and the report never reads safer than the publish gate.
  • Two style readers, one module. The screen calls resolveLogicStyle(doc); the engine, the report, validateQuiz and the publish gate call engineLogicStyle(doc). No component re-implements either. Nothing reads build_session.logic_style ahead of the document field, nothing writes a style on page load, and publish bakes no inferred style.
  • Undo is inverse mutations. Never a whole-document snapshot, and always against getLatestDoc(). Every destructive action that is not confirmed is announced with an Undo.
  • One doc commit per user action. An import, a type change with its rule conversion, a Picks move and an Undo each commit once. Every PUT revalidates the whole route loader, because no file in app/routes exports shouldRevalidate.
  • Latest doc after an await. Writes made after an await commit against getLatestDoc()/docRef (CreateRuleModal.tsx:637-640; LogicTabCard.tsx:127-129).
  • build_session. It changes only through intents, and only through writeSession after Phase 5. The funnel PUT keeps the server's copy (funnelIntents.server.ts:124-131), while the builder PUT writes it wholesale (quizEditorIO.server.ts:342-359).
  • Funnel bar. useFunnelBar overrides stay memoized with stable handlers (funnelChrome.tsx:11-14).
  • Mutations.
    • UIs call pure mutations and never hand-edit JSON.
    • Rules are addressed by id.
    • Targets are read through answerTargets() and ruleTargets() (recommendDecider.ts:63-82).
    • Never call setAnswerTarget, which replaces the whole list (deciderMutations.ts:56-87).
    • Build partial filter edits from baseValueSet (logicTabFields.ts:603-618).
  • Copy. All merchant-facing strings come from logicCopy.ts. No em dashes, and reword any existing string you touch that has one. Never "bucket", "decider", "branch", "boost", "weight" or "score".
  • Styling. No hex literals in .tsx: check-tokens scans app/components and app/routes. Admin CSS lives in app/styles/quizocalypse.css, and /q loads only quiz-runtime.css.
  • Test hooks. Every new surface gets a data-testid. Keep logic-tab-card and data-node-id.

Tests: unit coverage, e2e probes that break, new probes

This is the test plan for the whole redesign. It covers what guards the Logic step today, the unit tests to add, the existing tests and probes that pin today's UI and must change with it, the new probes, the extra proof the engine and runtime change needs, and the protocol for running all of it. Each item names the confirmed defects it closes (B-numbers). The pass/fail wording for every defect is in QA part 1 and QA part 2.

The owner has ruled, so this plan is written in the indicative: every test below guards a decided behaviour. A parenthesised decision id, "(D7)", points at the reasoning in Owner decisions; it never means the behaviour is still being weighed. Three items are genuinely open and two areas are parked; both lists are immediately below and are marked again wherever they touch a test. Both logic styles are first-class here. Rules only is a real engine mode with its own engine branch, its own checks and its own probe, and Filter Results + Rules keeps today's engine with its own checks and its own probe. Neither is a view of the other, and neither gets thinner coverage.

Three items are still open. They block these tests. Do not pick them.

  • D2, in Filter Results + Rules only. In that style "Show" appends after the base pool and is often cut off by the results cap, while its hint promises "these become the results" (applyRuleAction's show branch, recommendDecider.ts:313-316). The owner chooses between changing the engine so Show puts its products first and changing the hint. Blocks: recommendDecider.test.ts:727-729 ("show appends missing members"), which stays exactly as it is until the owner rules; the Filter rule window's Show hint copy assertion in logic-filter-verify.mjs; and the before/after product-order record in the runtime walk. Does not block: anything in Rules only. There D2 is settled: with no base, Show is the whole result (recommendDecider.ts:276-284), the hint is true, and the rule window offers Show only.
  • D10, question-type changes. What a type change does to answers and to the rules that referenced them. Blocks: the changeQuestionType unit cases that assert what happens to dropped answers and to the rules pointing at them, and the Type column cases in logicSheets.test.ts and logic-filter-verify.mjs that follow from them. Does not block: the settled half, which is already pinned: a type change keeps the answers (TypeChipSelector.test.tsx:148-162; quizMutations.test.ts:695-752) and Five-point stamps scale_config {min:1, max:5}. Write those cases now and leave the drop behaviour untested rather than guessing it.
  • D14, second half. Whether used recommendations also move to the end of the tray, and how the armed state reads on the builder's editor surface. Blocks: the tray-order assertion in logic-filter-verify.mjs step 5 and the builder's armed-state screenshot. Does not block: the colours, which are settled and must be asserted: green means placed on no answer, black means placed, violet means armed, all from Quartz tokens.

When a test needs one of these, stop, leave the case unwritten, and name the waiting test in your report. Never pick an option silently to get a green suite.

Two areas are parked. Test neither into existence.

D4, diagnostics. The check popover shows findings and opens from the CTA, and that is all this work tests. Do not write tests or probe steps for "Check my logic", the Diagnose modal, "Test a path", the AI review or an "N to review" affordance, because none of them is built here. PathTester and usePathQuality stay shipped and unreferenced from the new step; their existing behaviour is not yours to change, so do not delete their code and do not add coverage that would pin the new step to them. The one thing that does carry over from the AI-review work is the flush-and-await contract on useQuizDraft, because "Continue →" needs it (usePathQuality.ts:38-53 shows the current fire-and-forget shape; flushSave returns nothing to await, useQuizDraft.ts:136-142).

D6, builder parity. The main builder is being rebuilt, so no parity probe is written and no builder feature is tested into place. What replaces it is a regression probe (builder-logic-regression-verify.mjs, below): the shared components and the D18 renames reach the builder whether you aim at them or not, so prove the builder's Logic view still loads, still renders, still saves and still passes axe after your change. Record the known gap in your report and hand it to the main-builder project: a Rules-only quiz opens in today's builder as Filter Results + Rules, because BuilderSettings renders LogicTabCard with no logicStyle prop (BuilderSettings.tsx:69; the prop at LogicTabCard.tsx:105, rulesOnly = logicStyle === "rules" at :112).

A change can pass every CI gate and still break the Logic step, because CI runs no browser test against it. The unit suite is the regression net; the probes below are the evidence you hand back.

This work raises that bar, because it is no longer editor-only. The Rules-only engine branch and the safety net both land in shopper-facing code (D1), so the full e2e suite, a local decider walk, DOM-identical proof for the docs that must not change, runtime screenshots and the byte pin are all required, not optional. That list is in The engine and runtime proof below, and it is the part of this plan you cannot skip.

Unit tests to add or extend

Follow the patterns the suites already use:

  • A legacy doc comes back as the same object: expect(mutation(legacy, …)).toBe(legacy) (quizMutations.test.ts:798-802, 972-978).
  • A refused edit returns its input: toBe(base) (quizMutations.test.ts:1049-1052).
  • Every result re-parses: expect(() => Quiz.parse(next)).not.toThrow() (quizMutations.test.ts:845, 871, 1061).
  • Unset optional keys are absent, never undefined or defaulted, checked with hasOwnProperty (quizMutations.test.ts:839, 866-870).
  • When a test needs to know which shoppers a rule catches, compute it with ruleConditionsMatch (recommendDecider.ts:330-357), the engine's own predicate. Never re-implement the predicate in a test.

The logic style: the doc field, the migration and the resolver (D1, D5) New

The style is a top-level Quiz.logic_style field, decider-gated and .optional(), written only by setLogicStyle and carried through publish (Data model and mutations). It replaces the draft-only build_session.logic_style (quizSchema.ts:1708), which publish strips with the rest of build_session (quizPublish.ts:803-810) and which therefore can never reach the engine. Both fields stay parsed forever; only the reader order changes.

  • setLogicStyle in app/lib/mutations/deciderMutations.ts: a legacy doc returns the same object; a decider doc gains the key; writing the style it already has returns the input; the result re-parses; the key is absent, not undefined, on a doc that never had one. Both values, "rules" and "attributes", are covered, and neither is treated as the default.
  • resolveLogicStyle, a pure function, new file or beside setLogicStyle. Test the whole order in one table: doc.logic_style wins; then build_session.logic_style, which is the migration path for drafts that picked a style before the field existed; then inference, where any question with role: "filter" gives "attributes" and any rule with no filter role gives "rules"; then the default "attributes". It never returns null, so there is no chooser branch left to hit (D5). It is pure, so a test proves the other half of D5 directly: calling it does not change the doc.
  • The migration is read-only. Assert that resolving a draft whose style lives in build_session returns that style and leaves both the doc and build_session byte-identical. The doc field is written only when the merchant switches, never on load. The probe proves the same thing end to end by diffing draftJson before and after a page load.
  • Publish keeps it. quizPublish.test.ts: add logic_style to the net-new optional field cases (quizPublish.test.ts:374-455) so an unset field stays absent from publishedJson and a legacy publish is unchanged; then a positive case, where a decider doc with logic_style: "rules" publishes with the key intact, because the engine reads it from publishedJson. It must not join the strip list at quizPublish.ts:803-810, and stripPublicJsonPayload drops only review_enrichment_sources and translations (quizPublish.ts:47-54), so the public JSON carries it too. Assert that.
  • unpublishedChanges.test.ts (from :123): a style change counts once. It should count, because under D1 the style changes what shoppers get.
  • Type home. The LogicStyle type is exported from LogicStyleChooser.tsx today (Step3Shell.tsx:31-35 is its only importer, for LogicStyleChooser, buildChooserScan and the type). D5 deletes that file, so move the type to the schema or to the resolver first and let the typecheck prove nothing else referenced it.

Closes the persistence half of the style work and gives logic-rules-only-verify.mjs and logic-filter-verify.mjs something to assert against in the DB.

Mutations: app/lib/quizMutations.test.ts and app/lib/moveDecider.test.ts Exists

  • setQuestionText / setAnswerText: trim and collapse spaces; clamp to 150 / 60 characters; an empty result, an unknown id and a legacy doc all return the input unchanged.

Undo: inverse mutations against the latest doc, never a snapshot (D7, D9) New

Every Undo in this step is an inverse mutation applied to whatever the document is when Undo is pressed, so it can never silently revert an edit the merchant made while the toast was up. That is the whole point of the ruling, and it is what these tests prove. A whole-document snapshot restore must not appear anywhere in the diff, including in ported mock code (the mock's UNDO / snap / ACT.undo restore S.rules wholesale; do not port that shape).

  • restoreDecisionRule / restoreDecisionRules in deciderMutations.ts: re-insert by id at the saved index, clamped; do nothing when the id already exists; several deletes come back in their original order, entries applied in reverse; a restored rule keeps its targets in G1 form; a rule whose answers or recommendations were removed since the delete comes back as it was, flagged, and nothing throws (B1, B35).
  • The independence case, once per Undo. Delete rule 2, then edit rule 5, then Undo. Rule 2 returns at index 1 and rule 5 keeps the edit. A snapshot restore fails this test; an inverse mutation passes it. Write it for the rule trash, for "Delete rule" in the rule window, for the reorder Undo and for the D9 role move.
  • captureLogicParts / restoreLogicParts in app/lib/mutations/logicUndo.ts: capture only the scoped questions' data, their outgoing edges and the named rules; restoreLogicParts writes before back only when every captured part still equals after, and returns null otherwise so the caller withdraws the Undo. Compare with sorted-key JSON, as unpublishedChanges.ts:84-99 does. Cases: nothing else touched, so the restore is exact; one captured question edited in the meantime, so the restore refuses and returns null; a captured question deleted in the meantime, same result.
  • D9, the announced mapping clear. Moving "Picks results" to another question clears both questions' answer mappings, as moveDecider already does, and the caller captures the parts first. Test the pair: moveDecider then restoreLogicParts gives a doc deep-equal to the original, with both roles back and every target_id / target_ids in G1 form; the Undo refuses when the old question was deleted meanwhile; the count the toast quotes ("Q1's 6 recommendations were removed") is computed from the captured parts, not guessed, so a question with no mapped answers produces no count in the copy. One path serves the role menu, the Table and Import, so this is one test, not three (B6).
  • Import Undo. applyLogicImport returns undo holding the parts captured before and after. Undo restores the pre-import doc; a later edit inside the captured scope makes restoreLogicParts return null and the Undo is withdrawn rather than applied.

Closes B1, B2, B6, B35.

Analyzer and the style-aware Tier-1 report (D3): app/lib/pathAnalyzer.test.ts and app/lib/pathReport.test.ts Exists

One report drives the CTA, the check popover and publish, and it takes the resolved style as an input (Checks and Continue). Both styles get their own fixtures; neither inherits the other's checks by accident. The invariant that the report must never read safer than the publish gate is already encoded at pathReport.ts:124-136 and stays asserted.

  • Never runs. B12 cases A to G as QA part 1 states them; a rule covered only by the union of earlier rules; an earlier catch-all; single-select exclusivity ("is Blotchy" implies "is not Tight", case D); the verb ignored (an earlier Hide catches a later Show); the finding names the first catching rule. Keep the exact-subset case (pathAnalyzer.test.ts:257-268) and the match-any guard (:272-287).
  • An oracle test. Generate small quizzes (up to three questions of up to four answers, single- and multi-select with max_selections), enumerate every answer set the types allow (a skipped optional question is no answer), run first-match-wins with ruleConditionsMatch, and assert that shadowedRules flags exactly the rules no answer set reaches. This is what makes the extension of shadowedRules (pathAnalyzer.ts:265-299) trustworthy. Run the oracle against both styles: in Rules only the same predicate decides the result outright, so a rule the oracle says is unreachable is a rule that can never recommend anything.
  • Dead-rule reasons. All-of with more picks than max_selections; all-of on a non-multi question; a condition on a deleted answer, where an is_not on a deleted answer matches every shopper (pathAnalyzer.ts:151-178) and therefore also shadows every rule below it; no targets or deleted targets. One reason per rule, one format everywhere.
  • Filter Results + Rules. Today's blocks stay blocks: V1 to V6, V11, V12 and S1, with V2 the route bypass. Broken rule references stay blocks (V5, V6), because publish blocks on them (quizPublish.ts:482-490) and the report may not read safer. New warnings: a recommendation nothing can show ("“X” is never recommended"), a rule that never runs, and an impossible all-of. V13 and V15 stay warnings.
  • Rules only. Blocks: no rules at all; no rule that can show anything, meaning every rule is Hide or half-built; a rule with no answers; a rule with no recommendation; a broken reference. Warnings: a rule that never runs, and a recommendation no rule can show. Skipped entirely: the picking-question checks, which have no subject in this style, so V1 (no deciding question), V2 (decider bypass), V3 (decider optional), V4 (unmapped deciding answers) and V13 (unmapped narrowing answers) do not appear in the report at all. Assert their absence, not merely that they pass: a passing check the merchant cannot act on is noise.
  • The gate agrees. quizValidation.test.ts: on a logic_style: "rules" doc, validateQuiz emits no missing_decider, no decider_bypass, no decider_optional and no unmapped_decider_answer (the kinds at quizValidation.ts:24-27, gated by doc.logic_model === "decider" at :113 and emitted at :125-185), and does emit the Rules-only blocks. Without this, nothing built in Rules only can ever be published, because publish throws on any validateQuiz issue (quizPublish.ts:408-414).
  • Parity with publish, both styles. A property-style case: for a set of fixture docs, whenever publish's target check would throw (quizPublish.ts:128-139, 482-490), the report is not safe. V4 reads only target_id today (pathReport.ts:193-209) while publish blocks on every member, so the fixture set must include an answer whose target_ids[1] points at a deleted Category row.
  • V2 stays answer-level in Filter Results + Rules: "Straight to the results" and a skip past the picking question each give one blocking finding per answer, linked to that question (pathReport.test.ts:185-200 pins the message matcher and the link; keep both, follow the new copy).
  • V13 skips answers set to "Keeps everything". The code does (pathReport.ts:319) but no test pins it.
  • V14 is computed from productIndex (pathReport.ts:328-341), never a fixed "56 of 339". buildBuilderHealthReport takes no product index today (pathReport.ts:451-455), so V11 and V14 to V16 vanish in the builder; D6 parks closing that gap, so record it and do not fix it here.

Recommendation coverage helper: app/lib/recommendationCoverage.ts and createRuleBand.test.ts Partial

One helper feeds the strip counter, the rule-window band, the Table's "Shown by rules" and "Status" columns and the Filter warning about recommendations nothing shows. Test it once, in one place. Put recommendationCoverage in the new file app/lib/recommendationCoverage.ts, the one home set in Data model, persistence and the mutations to add, so pathReport can import it without reaching into a component module and without reusing either existing coverage name.

  • A rule covers a recommendation only when it can actually put those products into a result: it lists the recommendation, it can run (at least one condition, at least one recommendation, not impossible, not shadowed, not broken) and its verb adds. Hide never covers. Half-built, never-runs and broken rules leave the recommendation at "Needs a rule".
  • The verb split is style-specific and engine-true. In Filter Results + Rules there is a base pool, so only Show adds; Pin reorders what is already there (recommendDecider.ts:308-311) and cannot cover. In Rules only there is no base, so both Show and Pin resolve to the rule's own targets (recommendDecider.ts:276-284) and both cover. Write one fixture per style with the same Pin rule and assert the two different counts. The rule window offers Show only in Rules only (D2), so a Pin rule there can only have arrived from an edit made in the other style; it still counts, because the engine still honours it. Fixed in mock The mock's showsRecs already makes exactly this split, and rulesShowing / ruleCount feed the strip counter, the pill dots, the rule-window band and the Table columns from it, so port the split, not a fresh one.
  • Rewrite the ruleCoverage cases in createRuleBand.test.ts:35-57 for this definition. Today they count every rule that names a target, zero-condition rules included (the fixtures pass conditions: [] at :38-40), which is wrong by design now. Keep the per-rule dedupe case at :48-53.
  • In Filter Results + Rules the rule-window band counts a recommendation placed on a Picks answer as covered, or the band is relabelled as optional exceptions (B41). Pin the choice you make with a test either way.
  • Do not name the new export ruleCoverage and do not put it in app/lib/ruleCoverage.ts. That name is taken twice already: createRuleBand.ruleCoverage (createRuleBand.ts, used at CreateRuleModal.tsx:493), which this change deletes and re-points, and buildRuleCoverage in app/lib/ruleCoverage.ts, whose only importer is CoverageSidebar.tsx:4 and which goes with it.

Import and export: new app/lib/logicSheets.test.ts (D16, D16-template) New

The module is pure and never imports the spreadsheet library, so these tests run on plain rows (see Table view, Export and Import). The library is SheetJS Community Edition 0.20.3 from the official SheetJS CDN tarball, loaded as a lazy chunk. Never the npm xlsx package, which stops at 0.18.5 and carries published CVEs, because Import parses files merchants supply. Neither package is a dependency today; package.json has no spreadsheet library at all, so the addition is visible in the lockfile diff and should be reviewed there.

  • Identity round trip. An unchanged round trip (serialize, parse, diff) is "Nothing changed" in both styles, and the Table and the file carry the same rows for the same doc. Every "When they answer" cell reads "Qn = answer"; the Answers sheet carries a trailing "Answer ID (don't edit)" column and the Rules sheet a "Rule ID (don't edit)" column.
  • Export is the template. On a quiz with no rules, Export still writes both sheets with their headers, both id columns and one example row, so a merchant can fill it in and import it back. Test that the example row round-trips: importing the untouched template changes nothing and is reported as nothing changed, and importing it with the example row filled in creates exactly one rule. There is no second file format, so no test may assume one.
  • B3: "Yes" and "No" on two questions, and "Cheeks" on two questions, stay on their own question; ambiguous bare text is reported, never resolved to the first match. With the id columns present this is decided by id; without them, by Q plus exact text.
  • B4: a deleted or inserted Answers row changes nothing else and is reported; rows match by Answer ID or by Q plus exact text, never by position. The Answers sheet updates in place and never adds or deletes an answer: a row with an unknown id is skipped and reported, and a stored answer with no row is left alone.
  • B5: a missing column means leave unchanged, never clear. Without a "#" column no rule is deleted; without a "Then" column no route is reset; an Answers sheet with neither Q nor Answer ID applies nothing and says so; a Rules sheet with no Recommendations column applies nothing and says so.
  • B22: a bad Rules row names its spreadsheet row and the reason, no rule changes at all, and valid Answers cells still apply. The Rules sheet is all-or-nothing; the Answers sheet is cell by cell.
  • The Recommendations sheet is read-only. An edited Recommendations sheet changes nothing and is reported as ignored, with copy that says so rather than failing silently (B36). Renumbered "#" values are reported the same way; rules keep their row order.
  • B23: names with commas (quoted), "(no answers)" and "(none)" import back unchanged, and the half-built rules stay flagged.
  • B24: all-of on a non-multi question is rejected or converted with the in-app toast; a Type change off multi-select clears all-of and min/max; a new "Picks results" goes through moveDecider and produces the D9 toast and Undo; routes stay forward-only. D12: a row that reads NOT (A AND B) is rejected with a named reason, not silently coerced.
  • B25: rules compare in canonical form (normalizeDecisionRule) and by identity, so stray flags count 0 and one inserted rule counts 1.
  • B26: the decoder reads UTF-8 without a BOM (an apostrophe-and-dash answer survives), falls back to windows-1252 only on invalid UTF-8, strips a BOM, and sends xlsx, xls and UTF-16 bytes down the binary path.
  • Both styles. Filter Results + Rules exports Rules then Answers; Rules only exports Rules then Recommendations. Import accepts either file against either style and reports sheets it cannot apply, so a merchant who switched style between export and import is told, not silently half-applied.

Closes B3, B4, B5, B22, B23, B24, B25, B26, B36.

Component tests (new files, jsdom) New

  • LogicHeader. The "Logic style" menu uses menu and menuitemradio roles and carries aria-expanded; choosing the other style forces the Edit view; re-choosing the current style keeps the current view; choosing a style calls the style mutation exactly once.

There is no title bar, so the accessible name comes from aria-label; the top row carries "Delete rule" and "Duplicate" side by side in edit mode and neither in create mode; Save stays disabled until an answer and a recommendation are picked; an impossible all-of blocks Save with its copy (B14); an "is not" row hides the any/all toggle entirely (D12) and the footer sentence reads "not (...)"; Save normalizes the draft through normalizeDecisionRule, so no stray flags reach storage (B13); edit is bound to the rule id, so Save after the rule disappeared never writes over another rule, and "Delete rule" deletes only the rule shown; in Rules only the verb row offers Show alone, and in Filter Results + Rules it offers Show, Pin and Hide (D2).

This is a deliberate exception to the design-system rule that toasts carry no actions (qz-toast.tsx:13-17 states the rule; record the dated owner exception in the code comment beside it). Cases: the queue of one still holds, so a new toast replaces the current one (keep nextToastState green, qz-toast.tsx:23-29); the action variant renders role="status" aria-live="polite" as the message variant does (qz-toast.tsx:68); its Undo is a real focusable button reachable from the keyboard as soon as the toast appears; the toast does not expire while hovered or focused, which the fixed 2400 ms timer cannot do today (qz-toast.tsx:19, :56-58); an optional duration overrides that timer; dismissing or replacing a toast whose action was never pressed runs no mutation.

New probes

Add five probes as e2e/<name>-verify.mjs. Never name one *.spec.* or *.test.*: playwright.config.ts sets only testDir: "./e2e" (playwright.config.ts:7), so Playwright's default file match would pull it into the post-deploy smoke that runs against production.

The contract every new probe follows

  • Target. A local production build and the local fixture cmr7khgd50001vkhscvox8dgt (e2e/README.md:157-158). BASE defaults to http://localhost:3000, as most probes do. Authenticate once with /studio?key=… and mask the key in every error (q3-logic-verify.mjs:19-20, 154-161).
  • Seed your own state. Do not rely on a leftover fixture state, as logic-widget-verify.mjs and create-rule-verify.mjs do. Before the first write, snapshot draftJson, buildState and every quiz-scoped Category row to a backup file; seed; restore all of it in finally, deleting Category rows the probe created (q3-logic-verify.mjs:29-55; create-rule-verify.mjs:345-349). One shared seed module for the five probes is fine.
  • Seed before you open a page, and close pages before any later prisma write: an open tab can flush a stale autosave over the seed (fix3-verify.mjs:94-96).
  • The seed doc (decider). Q1: single select, Picks results, answers mapped, one of them to two recommendations (G1). Q2: multi-select, max_selections: 3, Narrows, one answer with values, one "Keeps everything", one unset. Q3: a 1 to 5 scale with end labels. Q4 and Q5: single select, both "Yes" / "No" (B3). At least 10 quiz-scoped Category rows built from the local shop's products (the recipe at q3-logic-verify.mjs:77-103), so the tray overflows and the product-group picker shows its search. Rules: a Show on Q2 any of, an exact duplicate below it (never runs), a Hide-only rule, a Pin rule, a rule on Q3's point 5 and a rule on Q5 "Yes". build_session: { stage: "logic", built: true }. Two style variants of the same seed: one with logic_style: "rules" and one with "attributes", plus a third with no style at all, to exercise inference and the build_session migration.
  • Read the DB; do not sleep. Poll the draft until the expected state holds; autosave is 700 ms plus a round trip (q3-logic-verify.mjs:62-71).
  • Real input only. Use Playwright's pointer and keyboard (locator.click, keyboard.press), never element.click() inside page.evaluate: a pointer-trapped overlay must fail the probe (CLAUDE.md:101-103).
  • Stub only what costs money or cannot be forced. The AI review is parked (D4), so the new step makes no AI call at all; assert that, by failing the probe if any request reaches /api/path-quality. Use page.route to hold or fail the autosave PUT, the style write, the library chunk and ensure-targets.
  • Evidence. Zero page errors; a screenshot of every interactive state the probe names, at 1440×900 and 1280×720; open and look at every screenshot before reporting; print pass counts the way the existing probes do.
