QA acceptance criteria, part 1: data integrity, rules, undo and import

This part is the pass/fail contract for everything the Logic step writes: the logic style itself, the engine branch that reads it, question roles and mappings, answers, rules, Undo, the checks that gate Continue, and the spreadsheet round trip. It turns 30 of the 63 confirmed mock defects into requirements and adds the requirements for the behaviour the owner settled on 2026-09-21 and 2026-09-22. Part 2 covers the other 33 defects, which are interaction, focus, colour and layout. A row passes only when every clause holds in both styles and on every surface that ships the feature.

The rulings are built, not weighed. Every row below is written in the indicative. A parenthesised decision id, "(D7)", points at the reasoning in Owner decisions; it never means the row is conditional. Three items are genuinely open and two areas are parked; both lists sit immediately below and are marked again wherever they touch a row.

Severity: high B1 to B9; medium B10 to B17 and B22 to B26; low B35, B36, B41, B43, B45, B63, B66 and B67. B9, B66 and B67 were found through the mock's test harness (its Reset action and the two shell checkboxes); each still gets a product-level criterion. Rows whose id starts with S carry no B number: they pin settled behaviour that the mock never had. The last column says where the real build stands on origin/main (b4aa278): Exists already behaves this way (keep it and pin it with a test), Partial part of it exists, New nothing exists yet, Conflict shipped code contradicts the requirement, and Fixed in mock the current mock no longer fails (its fix is not automatically the one to copy). Probe names refer to the probes in Tests: logic-rules-only-verify.mjs, logic-filter-verify.mjs, logic-table-io-verify.mjs, create-rule-verify.mjs (updated) and builder-logic-regression-verify.mjs. Component tests run in jsdom with react-dom/client and act, the pattern already used by ValuePickerPopover.test.tsx.

Refs. Every path:line is on origin/main. Bare file names are in app/lib/; mutations/ is app/lib/mutations/; logicTab/ is app/components/studio/logicTab/; runtime/ is app/components/runtime/; Step3Shell.tsx, HealthPopover.tsx, TypeChipSelector.tsx, PhoneScreen.tsx and QuestionSection.tsx are under app/components/onboarding/questionsLogicV3/; UnifiedWorkspace.tsx, BuilderSettings.tsx and ContextPanel.tsx are under app/components/studio/; qz-toast.tsx and qz-overlays.tsx are under app/components/.

What is settled, and what every row here builds on

  • D1. Rules only is a real engine mode, its own method of deciding a result. The style lives on the quiz document and survives publish (decider-gated, .optional(), never .default()). In "rules" the engine ignores roles and answer mappings, and the first matching rule's recommendations are the result. Filter Results + Rules keeps today's engine.
  • D1 safety net. A shopper no rule matches gets the safety net the Results step already has, and the same net covers an empty result in Filter Results + Rules. This is a shopper-facing runtime change and carries the full proof (legacy byte-identical, DOM-identical /q, full e2e, screenshots, the byte pin).
  • D3. One style-aware Tier-1 report drives the CTA, the check popover and publish. Rules only blocks on no rules, no rule that can show anything, and any rule missing its answers or its recommendations, and skips every picking-question check. Filter Results + Rules keeps today's blocks and adds route bypass and broken rules. N counts blocking findings only.
  • D5. No first-entry chooser. The style resolves from the saved field, else the draft-only field, else inference, else Filter Results + Rules. Nothing is written on load.
  • D7. The shared toast gains one optional action, a duration, a live region and keyboard reach, and the dated exception to the no-actions rule is recorded in the file. Undo is inverse mutations against the latest document, never a whole-document snapshot.
  • D9. Moving 'Picks results' still clears both questions' mappings, and a toast names what was cleared with an Undo that restores the role and every target. One path serves the role menu, the Table and Import. No confirm dialog.
  • D11. Rule rows are clicked to edit and carry a trash and ↑/↓ on hover and on keyboard focus; Duplicate moves into the rule window's top row next to 'Delete rule'.
  • D12. 'is not' and 'all of' never combine. D13. Paste rules splits a cross-question 'or' into adjacent rules; the parser stays frozen and stored 'or' rules keep working.
  • D15. '+ Add recommendations' writes through ensure-targets, extended with a group kind, quiz-scoped rows, at most 12 per call.
  • D16 and its template addition. The file carries identity as well as text, the Answers sheet updates in place, the Recommendations sheet is read-only, a missing column means leave unchanged, Export doubles as the template, and the library is SheetJS CE 0.20.3 from the official SheetJS CDN tarball.
  • D17. Sentences are verb-first and answers-only; the Table and the file always use the machine form 'Q7 = Yes'. D18. The renames land through shared constants; internal words never reach the merchant.
  • D19. The live surfaces the mock does not draw are kept. D21. The embedded twins get the missing toast provider so Undo is never invisible.
  • D8, D20, D22, D23, D24 settled earlier: the save pill shows at the edited field only, the build is at the mock's 100% sizes, the rules column sits on the right, the step's top section is gone, and the rule window has the ruled layout.

Build all of it.

Both styles are first-class in every row. Filter Results + Rules and Rules only are two ways the same decider document decides a result, not a full mode and a reduced one. Rules only is not a view of the other, not a lens on it and not a beginner mode: it decides results for published quizzes. Where a row behaves differently in the two styles it says so for both; where a row names only one style, the other is unaffected. No row may be satisfied by proving one style and assuming the other.

Three items are still open. They block these rows. Do not pick them.

  • D2, in Filter Results + Rules only. In that style 'Show' appends after the base pool and is often cut off by the results cap, while its hint promises 'these become the results' (the show branch of applyRuleAction, recommendDecider.ts:313-316). The owner chooses between changing the engine so Show puts its products first and changing the hint. Blocks: in §4, B10's Filter Results + Rules clause about whether a Show recommendation that the cap cuts off still counts as covered, and the Filter warning copy that hangs off the same helper. Build the coverage helper so it counts a Show rule as covering in both styles and does not model the cap, leave that clause untested, and name it in your report. Does not block: anything in Rules only. There D2 is settled: with no base, Show is the whole result, the hint is true, Pin and Hide are meaningless under first-match-wins, and the rule window offers Show only.
  • D10, question-type changes. What a type change does to the answers it cannot keep, and to the rules that referenced them. Blocks: B7's type-change half, B43's choice between refusing and clamping a Scale above 10, B45's type-line clause, B24's Type column and B66's type-change clause. Build the plumbing that is already settled (changeQuestionType with its refused: "too-many-points" path and the optional clampTo10, setScalePoints returning what it removed), keep the mock's behaviour of trimming and telling the merchant with an Undo in the D9 pattern, and ship nothing that trims silently. Does not block: the points stepper, which is settled and specified in full below.
  • D14, second half. Whether used recommendations also move to the end of the tray, and how the armed state reads on the builder's editor surface. Blocks: nothing in this part. The colour half is settled and is asserted here and in part 2: green means a recommendation is placed on no answer, black means placed, violet means armed. Assert the colours, never the order, until the owner rules.

When a row needs one of these, stop at that clause, leave it unproven, and name the waiting clause in your report. Never pick an option silently to close a row.

Two areas are parked. Do not build them back in.

D4, diagnostics. The check popover shows findings and opens from the CTA, and that is the whole of the diagnostics surface in this work. Do not rebuild 'Check my logic', the Diagnose modal, 'Test a path' or the AI review into the step, and do not add an 'N to review' affordance. PathTester (app/components/logic/PathTester.tsx) and usePathQuality stay shipped and unreferenced from the new step; leave their code alone. Rows B11 and B15 are written against that surface: warnings are computed, carried in the same report and shown in the popover, and nothing else opens them.

D6, builder parity. The main builder is being rebuilt, so this work ships the funnel step 3 surface. The style still lives on the document, so the new builder can read it, and nothing in these rows may be gated so tightly that it cannot be reused there. Two consequences for QA. First, the shared components, the shared constants and every pure mutation reach the builder whether you aim at them or not, so the builder clauses below are a regression floor, proven by builder-logic-regression-verify.mjs: the Logic view still loads, renders, saves and passes axe. Second, record this gap in your report and hand it to the main-builder project: a Rules-only quiz opens in today's builder as Filter Results + Rules, because BuilderSettings renders LogicTabCard with no logicStyle prop (BuilderSettings.tsx:69; the prop at LogicTabCard.tsx:105, rulesOnly = logicStyle === "rules" at :112).

How to read the mock refs here. docs/design/logic-tab/rules-row/index.html is still being edited (last touched 2026-09-21), so this part cites it by function or handler name only: fitRule, snap(), ACT.undo, ACT.msave, ACT.reset, lossMsg, toastU, applyImport, sentence(), isPt. Search for the name. Fixed in mock means fixed in that source file, and the fix is evidence, not the specification: the mock's B1 fix clips conditions and recommendations that no longer exist (fitRule), and the product must never do that (build rule 3).

Six build rules that make most rows pass by construction.

  1. Identity, never position. Rules point at answers and recommendations by id (DecisionRuleCondition.answer_id, DecisionRule.target_id and target_ids, quizSchema.ts:1735-1770; Answer.id, quizSchema.ts:101). The rule window binds to a rule id, Table rows and Import resolve by id, and every Undo restores by id.
  2. Undo is an inverse mutation applied to the latest document (D7): re-insert a rule at its index, re-insert removed answers with their ids, restore cleared targets, always against getLatestDoc(). Never re-commit a whole-document or whole-list snapshot; that silently reverts edits made in between, including autosaved ones.
  3. Dangling references are kept and flagged, never clipped or dropped (DECISIONS.md:41-46). A rule that points at a deleted answer or recommendation keeps the id, shows a flag, drops out of coverage and blocks (V5, V6).
  4. One source per fact. One analyzer decides broken, never-runs and impossible (extend pathAnalyzer.ts), plus one coverage helper, one sentence describer, one rule normalizer (normalizeDecisionRule), one style resolver (resolveLogicStyle) and one memoized style-aware Tier-1 report for the CTA, the check popover and Publish.
  5. Every lookup tolerates a missing question, answer or Category row: the describer, the coverage helper, the tray, strip and pills, Table rows, the rule-window seed and the export. Nothing in the Logic workspace may throw on a document that parses.
  6. The style is read, never assumed. Every screen reads resolveLogicStyle(doc) and the engine, the report, validateQuiz and the publish gate read engineLogicStyle(doc); no component re-implements either. Mutations stay style-blind, with setLogicStyle as the single exception: the screen decides which mutations to offer and the engine decides what to read (D1, D5).

1. The style, the engine branch and the safety net

These five rows are new work with no mock defect behind them. They are the part of this build that reaches shoppers, so they carry the heaviest proof. The engine truth behind each one is in Engine semantics; the mutations are in Data model.

RequirementPass whenVerifyReal build
S1 · high. The logic style is a field on the quiz, resolved without asking (D1, D5).
  • logic_style: z.enum(["rules", "attributes"]).optional() sits beside logic_model (quizSchema.ts:1992-1995) and is never .default(). Parsing and saving a legacy document adds no key.
  • One pure resolveLogicStyle(doc) decides which screen opens, in this order: doc.logic_style; else doc.build_session?.logic_style, the migration read (quizSchema.ts:1698-1708, kept parsed forever); else inference, where any question with role: "filter" means Filter Results + Rules and any rule with no filter role means Rules only; else Filter Results + Rules. It never returns null and it never writes.
  • Opening the step writes nothing: no mutation, no set-logic-style intent, no autosave PUT caused by the load. The first write is the title switch calling setLogicStyle.
  • setLogicStyle writes the key even when it matches what inference would have produced, so deleting the rule or role that inference was reading can never move the quiz to the other style behind the merchant's back.
  • Publish keeps it: logic_style is not added to the strip list that builds publishedJson (quizPublish.ts:803-810), so /q/:id and /q/:id.json carry it and the engine can branch in the shopper's browser.
  • A regenerate from Step 1 carries logic_style over beside logic_model, so a merchant who chose Rules only and then rebuilds their questions comes back to Rules only.
 Unit: resolveLogicStyle table test over the four resolution cases plus an empty document; setLogicStyle on a legacy document returns the same object with no new key; a Quiz.parse round trip on a document carrying the key. Probe logic-rules-only-verify: record the network, load the step on a fresh decider draft, assert zero PUTs and zero intents, then switch the style and assert exactly one PUT whose document carries logic_style. Byte pin after deploy. The doc field, the resolver, the publish carry and the chooser deletion are all new.
S2 · high. In Rules only the first matching rule is the result (D1).
  • On a decider document with logic_style === "rules", resolveTarget treats the base as empty: it skips the role: "decides" lookup and the base walk, and the existing no-base path decides. A replace rule returns its targets; a Show or Pin rule returns the rule's recommendations; a first-matching Hide and no match at all resolve to nothing and hand the shopper to the safety net (S3).
  • Roles, answer target_id and target_ids, and filter values stay on the document and are ignored, never stripped.
  • Filter Results + Rules is unchanged: rules top to bottom, then the picking question's mapping as the base, then the filter questions narrowing it (recommendDecider.ts:226-291).
  • A document with no logic_style key resolves exactly as it does today. That is the whole legacy proof for this branch, and it is one line of code: the branch reads a field no existing document carries.

5. Checks that gate Continue

One style-aware Tier-1 report drives the CTA, the check popover and Publish (D3). It is built once per document change and read everywhere; the copy and the grouping live in Checks and Continue, the engine truth behind each finding in Engine semantics. Nothing in the popover is static text, and the report may never read safer than the publish gate.

6. Export and Import

Nothing exists yet: package.json has no spreadsheet library, only papaparse (package.json:50, 56). The file contract is settled (D16 and its template addition) and is specified in full in Table view, Export and Import: every 'When they answer' cell reads 'Qn = answer', the Answers sheet carries a do-not-edit 'Answer ID' column and the Rules sheet a 'Rule ID' column, the Answers sheet updates in place and never adds or deletes answers, the Rules sheet is all-or-nothing, the Recommendations sheet is read-only, a missing column means leave unchanged, and Export writes the template. Every row below is verified in a new app/lib/logicSheets.test.ts and end to end in logic-table-io-verify, where "unchanged" means Export followed by Import of the same file. The Table and the file are identical in both styles; only the Answers sheet's role cells are inert in Rules only.

7. Words, recommendations and the surfaces that must survive

RequirementPass whenVerifyReal build
S12 · '+ Add recommendations' writes through ensure-targets (D15).
  • Adding a recommendation posts to the existing POST /api/categories/ensure-targets, extended with a "group" kind that copies an existing group's membership into a quiz-scoped row the way Step 1 does. Tag keys are normalized to Step-1 slugs. Rows are always created quiz-scoped, reusing before creating. Batches stay at the endpoint's existing 12 resources per call.
  • It is additive and idempotent: re-adding the same (source, sourceRef) returns the same row id, never a duplicate, and the rows survive re-grouping. Nothing on this surface deletes a Category row.
  • A rule whose only recommendation was created this way publishes: publish collects every rule target (collectDeciderTargetIds, quizPublish.ts:128-146) and bakes its ordered membership, so a row this endpoint can create but publish cannot find would throw at publish time (quizPublish.ts:476-490). QA acceptance criteria, part 2: interaction, layout, accessibility and copy

This part turns the other 33 confirmed mock defects into pass/fail requirements for the real build: B18, B19, B20, B21, B27, B28, B29, B30, B31, B32, B34, B37, B38, B40, B47, B48, B49, B50, B51, B52, B53, B54, B55, B56, B57, B58, B59, B60, B61, B62, B64, B65 and B68. It also turns the owner's rulings into criteria of the same kind, so that the interaction, layout, accessibility and copy consequences of each ruling are testable rather than implied. Part 1 covers data, rules, undo and import. Each row gives the defect or the ruling, what the mock does today, the requirement, the minimum evidence, and whether code on origin/main (b4aa278) already meets it. A row passes only when every clause holds in both logic styles. Mock-only defects still get a product criterion.

Both styles are equals here. "Filter Results + Rules" and "Rules only" are two engine modes of the same decider document (D1), not a screen and a view of it. Where a criterion differs between them, the row says so in both directions. Nothing in this section may read as though Rules only were a simplified version of the other.

What the rulings settle for this section. Every item below is build work, not a choice:
  • D1. The style is a document field, Quiz.logic_style, decider-gated and .optional(), resolved by resolveLogicStyle and written by setLogicStyle. In "rules" the engine ignores roles and answer mappings and the first matching rule's recommendations are the result. Every label, sentence, hint and count on this screen has to agree with that engine.
  • D1 safety net. A shopper no rule matches gets the Results step's safety net, and the same net covers an empty result in Filter Results + Rules. That is a shopper-facing runtime change, so it carries the runtime proof rules in full.
  • D3. One style-aware Tier-1 report drives the CTA, the check popover and publish. "Fix N issues to continue" counts blocking findings only.
  • D5. No first-entry chooser. The chooser screen and its inert "Point based" row are deleted.
  • D7. The shared toast gains one optional action, an optional duration, a live region that stays mounted and keyboard reach. Undo is inverse mutations against the latest document.
  • D9, D11, D12, D13, D15, D16, D17, D18, D19, D21. Each adds concrete criteria below.
  • D8, D20, D22, D23, D24. Settled earlier: the save pill sits at the edited field, the build uses the mock's 100% sizes, the rules column sits on the right in Filter Results + Rules, the step's top section is gone, and the rule window has the D24 layout.
The mock is being corrected in place since the review. Several rows below are marked Fixed in mock: the popover now tracks its anchor through scroll and resize (placePop on a capture-phase scroll listener and on resize), the page behind a window is scroll-locked (html:has(#modal:not([hidden]),#aqm:not([hidden]),#addrec:not([hidden]))), the rule window makes the page inert and restores focus (drawModal with BG and drawModal.back), and a new draft opens scrolled to the top while a redraw keeps its scroll. Fixes were still landing while this section was written, so its line numbers keep moving. Read the mock by function name, never by line number. Every row stays a product criterion whether or not the mock still shows the defect.

Four traps when composing these primitives.
  • QzModal handles Esc in the capture phase and stops propagation (app/components/qz-overlays.tsx:126-133), so a QzPopover inside a QzModal never gets Esc (its listener is bubble-phase, :394-398) and the whole modal closes. The rule window hosts "See N more", so keep its own pattern: a bubble-phase Esc that stands down while a .qz-popover exists (app/components/studio/logicTab/CreateRuleModal.tsx:258-272). The reverse also bites: two stacked windows that both listen in the bubble phase close together on one Esc. Pass: Esc in Add recommendations over the rule window closes only Add recommendations and keeps the draft.
  • focus() on an inert element does nothing. Clear inert before a window's focus restore runs, and keep portals that must stay usable (toasts, popovers opened from the window) outside the inert subtree. The mock makes this mistake survivable by listing its background roots explicitly (BG in drawModal); do the same, and never mark the toast portal inert.
  • A window's focus trap keeps Tab away from a toast rendered outside it, so an Undo toast shown over a window is unreachable by keyboard unless it renders inside the window or has a shortcut. D7 settles this: the toast gains keyboard reach, and the rule window renders the toast inside its own subtree while it is open (B32, B34).
  • A focused button that becomes disabled can lose focus in current browsers ("Export" while preparing, "↓" on the last rule). If the walkthrough shows focus on <body> there, move focus to the sibling control or use aria-disabled with an ignored click.

Keyboard-only walkthrough

Run it on the local build with the local fixture, entering the funnel's Logic step through the to-logic intent as e2e/q3-logic-verify.mjs:161-165 does, at 1440×900, with no mouse input. logic-a11y-verify records, after every key press, the key, document.activeElement (role and accessible name) and whether it sits inside the topmost [aria-modal="true"] dialog. It fails on <body> and on focus outside an open dialog, and it saves the log and a screenshot per step. Run the whole walkthrough twice, once per style, starting from whichever style the fixture resolves to. The builder is parked (D6), so the walkthrough does not repeat there; run builder-logic-regression-verify instead after any shared-leaf change.

  1. Entry. Land on the Logic step. Expect the workspace, never a chooser (D5), and expect the document to be byte-identical to before the visit. Focus starts inside the card.
  2. Style. Tab to the title switch (for example "Filter Results + Rules ▾"), press Enter. Expect the "Logic style" menu with exactly two items, focus on the checked item and aria-expanded=true. ArrowDown, Enter on "Rules only": the menu closes, the style is written to the document once, the view is Edit, focus is on the title switch now reading "Rules only ▾", and the CTA re-counts under the Rules-only checks (D3). Reopen, press Esc: closed, focus on the title, nothing written. Switch back the same way and confirm every mapping and filter value is still on screen (R1).
  3. Questions. Tab into the rail, Enter on Q2. Expect the pane to show Q2, focus to stay on Q2's rail item, and its selected state to be exposed.
  4. Type. Enter on the type line ("Single select ▾"). Expect "Question type" with focus on the checked radio; arrow keys move and select; on Multi-select, Tab reaches the Min and Max steppers, whose label reads "Points" on a scale (B64); Esc closes with focus back on the type line, whose label updated. Any conversion is announced in the status region. D10 is open, so assert only that the announcement happens and that focus is not on <body>; do not pin the text.
  5. Role (Filter Results + Rules only; Rules only has no role control). On Q3, Enter on the role button. Expect "Question N does" with focus on the current item. ArrowDown to "Narrows", Enter. The attribute picker opens (D19), focus is inside it; Esc returns focus to the role button with nothing written; repeat and confirm with "Use" so Q3 narrows (step 8 needs it). On Q2, choose "Picks the result": the D9 toast names what was cleared, the status region announces it, its Undo is reachable by keyboard and restores the role and every target, and focus returns to the role button.
  6. Route. Enter on an answer's "→ Next". Expect focus on the current destination; ArrowDown to "Straight to the results", Enter: the button reads "→ Results" and keeps focus.
  7. Arm and place (Filter Results + Rules only). On the picking question, Tab to a tray chip, Enter: aria-pressed=true, focus stays. Tab to an answer's "Place <name> here", Enter: placed once, tray disarmed, focus on that cell's control. Enter on "+N more": focus in its search; type, ArrowDown to a row, Enter: armed, popover closed, focus on the armed chip, which is visible (B52). Esc disarms.
  8. Pickers. Enter on a Picks cell: focus in the product-group picker's search (its first row when it has no search); Space toggles a row and focus stays on it; the kind filters and the drill-in are reachable by keyboard (D19); Esc closes with focus on the cell's control. On a Narrows answer, Enter opens the value picker with focus in its search; Space stages a value; Tab to "Done", Enter: one write, focus on the cell's control. Repeat with "Cancel": nothing written.
  9. Create a rule. Enter on "+ Add" in the Rules column (in Rules only, on "Create your first rule" or "+ Add"). Expect the window open, focus on its first control, the page behind inert; 40 Tab and 40 Shift+Tab presses stay inside. In Rules only the verb control offers "Show" only and its hint says those recommendations become the result; in Filter Results + Rules all three verbs are there. Space on answers and a recommendation keeps focus on each. Pick two answers on one question, then Enter on "is": the row flips to "is not" and the any/all toggle disappears (D12), and the footer sentence reads "not (A or B)" (D17). Enter on "+ Add recommendations": the stacked window opens with focus in its search; tick a row; Esc closes only that window, focus returns to "+ Add recommendations" and the draft is intact. Enter on "Create rule": the window closes, the rule appears, focus is on "+ Add" or on the new row.
  10. Edit, Duplicate and Delete rule. Enter on a rule row: "Edit rule" opens for that rule (the row body is the edit control, D11). Esc: closed, focus on the row. Reopen, Tab to "Duplicate" in the top row, Enter: the window closes, the copy sits next to the original with focus on it, and the toast offers Undo. Reopen the original and press "Delete rule": the window closes, "Rule N deleted" is announced with how to undo, and focus is on the neighbouring row.
  11. Reorder. Focus a rule's "↓", press Enter three times. Expect one slot per press, "Moved to position N" announced each time, focus on that rule's "↓" (on its "↑" once "↓" disables). Undo by the keyboard path restores the order. Repeat in the other style's list (B19).
  12. Delete and Undo from the list. Tab to a row's trash, press Enter. Expect focus on the next row (the previous one if it was last), the status region naming the deletion and how to undo, Undo restoring the rule at its index by its id, and focus on the restored row. Delete twice in a row: one Undo takes back both (D7).
  13. Rules only strip and windows. In Rules only, Tab to a covered pill: its rules light. Enter on an uncovered pill's "+ Create a rule": the window opens with that recommendation picked; Esc returns focus to the pill. Enter on "Paste rules": focus inside, Tab trapped, Esc returns focus to "Paste rules"; paste a cross-question "or" line and confirm the preview count matches what is created (D13). Enter on "+ Add recommendations": focus in the search; type; Tab to rows; Space ticks; Enter on "Add N recommendations": the window closes, the toast is announced, focus is back on "+ Add recommendations".
  14. Add a question. Switch to Filter Results + Rules, Enter on "+ Add question". Expect focus in the title. Space on a type card keeps focus on it; "+ Add answer" focuses the new row and is disabled at 12 (B58); ArrowDown on a grip moves the row with focus on its grip; × moves focus to the next row (B57). Enter on "Add question": the dialog closes, the new question is selected, the toast is announced, focus is on the new rail item or on "+ Add question".
  15. Table. Enter on "Table": focus stays on the "Edit | Table" control. Tab to a Question cell, type, press Enter: committed, focus stays, and the save pill sits inside the cell's column (B61). Enter on a "What it does" button, Esc: focus back on it, and the Edit selection is unchanged (B40). Enter on "Export": disabled while preparing, one download, focus not on <body>; the downloaded file is the template (D16). Enter on "Import", choose a file: the toast with Undo is announced and focus is back on "Import".
  16. Check and jump. Make something block, stay in Table, Tab to the CTA ("Fix 1 issue to continue"), press Enter. Expect the check popover with focus on its first finding, findings grouped per question or per rule, and no "Check my logic", Diagnose, "Test a path" or "N to review" affordance anywhere (D4). Enter on a finding: Edit view, the target selected, focus on its rail item or its rule row (B38).

Pass: no step leaves focus on <body>, no Tab leaves an open dialog, every announcement named above appears in the status region, and the run completes in both styles.

Mock stand-ins, harness and limits (what not to port)

The reference mock is one static HTML file. It fakes the server, the catalogue, the save and the file download, and it carries a test harness above the product. This section says what the product builds in place of each fake, which mock routines shipped code replaces, which leftovers not to copy, and which mock behaviours are the design. It ends with what the review behind the confirmed defects did and did not cover.

The owner has ruled, so everything below is written in the indicative: each line says what to build, not what to weigh. A parenthesised decision id, "(D7)", points at the reasoning in Owner decisions; it never means the behaviour is still open. Three items are genuinely open and two areas are parked. Both lists are immediately below and are marked again wherever they touch a stand-in.

Both logic styles are first-class here. Rules only is a real engine mode with its own engine branch, its own checks and its own screen; Filter Results + Rules keeps today's engine with its own checks and its own screen (D1). Neither is a view of the other. When a mock routine reads one style as a display variant of the other, that is a stand-in to replace, not a shortcut to port.

Three items are still open. Do not pick them.

  • D2, in Filter Results + Rules only. In that style "Show" appends after the base pool and is cut off by the results cap, while its hint promises "these become the results" (applyRuleAction's show branch, recommendDecider.ts:313-316). The owner chooses between changing the engine so Show puts its products first and changing the hint wording. Blocks in this section: the verb-hint copy in the VERBS table row, and nothing else. Does not block: Rules only, where D2 is settled. There the first matching rule's recommendations are the whole result, so "these become the results" is literally true (the no-base path, recommendDecider.ts:276-283), and the rule window offers Show only. The mock has not caught up: its VERBS constant still offers Show, Pin and Hide in both styles, so do not read the mock's verb segment as the Rules-only spec.
  • D10, question-type changes. What a type change does to answers and to the rules that referenced the dropped answers. Blocks in this section: the setPoints() / ACT.settype / ACT.tpts row of the replacement table, and the reworded type-line tooltip that today promises "your answers are kept". Does not block: the settled half, which is already pinned by shipped tests: a type change keeps the answers (TypeChipSelector.test.tsx:148-160) and Five point stamps scale_config {min: 1, max: 5} (TypeChipSelector.tsx:59-65).
  • D14, second half. Whether used recommendations also move to the end of the tray, and how the armed state reads on the builder's editor surface, where the accent resolves to ink (quizocalypse.css:250-252). Blocks in this section: the ordering inside trayMoreHTML(), which today does not sort placed recommendations last while its two siblings do. Does not block: the colours, which are settled: green means placed on no answer, black means placed, violet means armed.

When a stand-in needs one of these, leave it as it is, mark it, and name it in your report. Never pick an option quietly to finish a row.

Two areas are parked. Build neither into existence.

D4, diagnostics. The check popover shows findings and opens from the CTA, and that is all this work builds. The mock's checkPop() is the whole diagnostics surface for now. Do not rebuild "Check my logic", the Diagnose modal, "Test a path" or the AI review into the step, and do not add an "N to review" affordance. PathTester and usePathQuality stay shipped and unreferenced from the new step: do not delete them, and do not wire them in. When diagnostics arrive they hang off this popover's footer.

D6, builder parity. The main builder is being rebuilt, so this work ships the funnel step 3 surface only. The style still lives on the quiz document (D1), so the new builder can read it, and nothing in the new UI may be gated on ruleFlow === "onboarding" in a way that makes it unreachable there. Name the known gap in your report and hand it to the main-builder project: a Rules-only quiz opens in today's builder as Filter Results + Rules, because BuilderSettings renders LogicTabCard with no logicStyle prop (BuilderSettings.tsx:69; the prop at LogicTabCard.tsx:105, rulesOnly = logicStyle === "rules" at LogicTabCard.tsx:112).

How to read the mock refs here. Every mock reference below names a function, handler, constant or CSS selector, never a line number: the file docs/design/logic-tab/rules-row/index.html is still being edited and has grown from the 1,067-line copy the review read to 1,200 lines on 2026-09-22. Search for the name. Fixed in mock means fixed in that source file, not necessarily in the hosted artifact. The QA criteria (part 1, part 2) are the contract whatever the mock does today.

The confirmed harness defects map to product criteria in QA part 1:

  • B9 Fixed in mock "Reset" left questions and answer mappings behind, and the pane crashed on a mapping to a recommendation that no longer existed. Product criterion: an answer cell, pill, rule or sheet row whose Category row is gone renders flagged and removable, never crashes, and style and view switches always re-render.
  • B66 Fixed in mock unticking "10 answers on Q5" assumed Q5 still had six answers and left a hole in the list. Product criterion: any action that removes answers leaves a hole-free list, and the type label, point count, pane, Table and rule window agree.
  • B67 Fixed in mock unticking "30 recommendations" also deleted user-added recommendations that shared a name. Product criterion: recommendations are removed by Category id only.

Identity: the mock keys by name and position, the product by id

  • Recommendations. A mock recommendation's id is its name: rec() looks it up by name, "Add" creates {id: name} (ACT.arAdd), "In this quiz" compares names (inQuiz) and import resolves names case-insensitively (applyImport). The product keys every reference by Category id (cuid; prisma/schema.prisma:174) and only displays Category.name. Two rows can share a name (a tag and a collection, or a Logic-added copy), which is how B67 happened. "In this quiz" matches on (source, sourceRef), which is also the pair ensure-targets dedupes on (Add recommendations).
  • Answers. Mock rule conditions store answer positions (conds: {qid: [answer index]}), so trimming or inserting answers renumbers them (setPoints() and the harness toggles). The product stores answer_id (quizSchema.ts:1735-1739): deleting an answer renumbers nothing, and a rule that points at a deleted answer stays and is flagged (brokenRuleRefs, pathAnalyzer.ts:158).
  • Rules. Mock rules carry an id (rid()) but the list is still addressed by index in the row handlers (ACT.editrule, ACT.delrule and the drag handlers all take data-i or data-ri). DecisionRule.id is required (quizSchema.ts:1743): bind the window, the row controls, the reorder, Undo and the row keys to it, never to a position (B2).
  • Questions. Mock ids are q1 to q5 plus "q" + S.uid for added ones (ACT.aqadd), and "Qn" is the position in S.qs (qIndex). Product node ids come from the mutations; "Qn" is display-only, taken from quiz order, and never stored.
  • Narrowing values. Mock values are src:attr:value strings (vkey). The product stores them by kind in one full-set payload: tags (as family:value), metafield_filters, variant_filters, product_type_filters, with collection_filters carried through (ValuePickerPopover.tsx:39-45), each value written under every member source of its attribute (ValuePickerPopover.tsx:20-33).
  • The spreadsheet carries identity too (D16). The mock's workbook is text only, so findAnswer() falls back to matching an answer's text across every question and applyImport() resolves recommendations by name. The product's file carries both: every "When they answer" cell reads Qn = answer, the Answers sheet gains a trailing do-not-edit "Answer ID" column and the Rules sheet a "Rule ID" column, so a round trip through Excel keeps identity instead of rebuilding it from strings (Table, Export and Import).

The pill shows at the edited field only, and the ambient autosave chrome stays silent when healthy (D8).

It renders the merchant's screen only, so the outcome of a shopper no rule catches is invisible in it.The safety net, in both styles (D1 safety net). A shopper no rule matches gets the safety net the Results step already has, and the same net covers an empty result in Filter Results + Rules. One behaviour for both styles. It replaces the bare no-match card the runtime shows today (QuizRuntime.tsx:1713-1721; recommendationEngine.ts:392-398). This is a shopper-facing runtime change and carries the full proof rules: legacy quizzes byte-identical, DOM-identical /q output for the published decider fixtures, the full npm run e2e, screenshot review, a written 2-lens adversarial self-review, and the byte pin after deploy (Engine semantics).

Rule and question model mapping

  • conds[qid] (answer positions) becomes one condition per picked answer, {question_id, answer_id, op} (quizSchema.ts:1735-1739).
  • not[qid] becomes op: "is_not" on that question's conditions ("none of these"). It never coexists with an "all of" join on the same question: the toggle is hidden on an "is not" row, the sentence reads "not (A or B)", and Import rejects "NOT (A AND B)" with a named reason (D12). No new storage is added for this.
  • all[qid] has the opposite default. The mock reads a question's picks as "any of" unless all is set; the schema reads them as "all of" unless the question id is in any_of (quizSchema.ts:1747-1749). Write the id of every "is" question with two or more picks left on "any of" into any_of.
  • verb "show", "pin", "hide" becomes action "show", "prioritize", "hide" (quizSchema.ts:1768). In Rules only the window offers Show only, because the first matching rule's recommendations are the whole result and Pin and Hide are meaningless under first-match-wins (D2, settled half). The mock has not caught up: VERBS still renders all three in both styles.
  • recs (names) becomes Category ids: target_id, plus target_ids when there are several (the G1 mirror; quizSchema.ts:1753-1759).
  • No mock counterpart: the required id (quizSchema.ts:1743); match, which nothing writes any more and which is kept on edit (quizSchema.ts:1746); the legacy action-less rule that replaces the results, parsed forever (quizSchema.ts:1760-1768). Paste rules stops creating match: "any" rules and splits a cross-question "or" into adjacent rules with the same verb and recommendations; existing rules that carry one still render faithfully and keep it when edited (D13).
  • Question fields: q.type single, multi, image, scale becomes question_type single_select, multi_select, image_tile, rating; q.five becomes rating with scale_config {min: 1, max: 5} (TypeChipSelector.tsx:59-65); q.min and q.max become min_selections and max_selections (quizSchema.ts:212-215); q.lo and q.hi become scale_config.endpoint_label_min and endpoint_label_max, 40 characters at most (quizSchema.ts:319-320).

The mock renders only its own "never runs · reason" tag (deadTag()). Render all four, in that tag style.

What the mock does not model

The stand-in quiz is simpler than real ones. The product must handle these cases although the mock never draws them:

  • Content steps between questions (intro, email gate, message, branch and the other node kinds; quizSchema.ts:57-68). The mock's route cells hop from question to question. The live RouteMenuButton walks past content steps to name the destination (LogicTabMenus.tsx:323-339); keep that resolution.
  • Freeform questions (text, email, numeric, date, slider; quizSchema.ts:52), which cannot pick the result (deciderMutations.ts:29). The mock has none, so it does not show how their rows read in the pane, the Table or the rule window.
  • Legacy rules: action-less rules that replace the results, and match: "any" rules (quizSchema.ts:1746, 1760-1768). Mock rules always have a verb and join questions with "and". Render real ones faithfully, and keep match: "any" on edit even though nothing writes it any more (D13; rule window).
  • Collection values on narrowing answers, which the live picker carries through untouched (ValuePickerPopover.tsx:28-31; baseValueSet, logicTabFields.ts:606-618). The mock has none.
  • Products and sellability. The mock never shows a product, and its counts are fixed numbers. Real counts are productIds.length (LogicQuestionWidget.tsx:169), and V14 reports products that are not live.
  • Network states. No loading, no "Not saved · Retry" or "Paused while AI edits" (FunnelSaveChip, funnelChrome.tsx:81-129), no ensure-targets failure, no AI regenerate.
  • The shopper. The mock draws the merchant's screen only, so it never shows what an unmatched shopper sees. That outcome is the safety net (D1 safety net), and it is the one place where this redesign reaches the shopper-facing runtime.
  • The builder. The mock draws the funnel only. D6 is parked: build the funnel surface, keep the components reusable, and hand the builder gap to the main-builder project.
