Mock behaviours that are the design

These look like shortcuts but are deliberate. Build them.

  1. A scrim click never closes a window (rule window, "Add recommendations", "Add a question"): the click dispatcher ignores elements without data-act, and scrims have none. The live rule window and PasteRulesModal already behave this way (CreateRuleModal.tsx:47-48, 976-979; PasteRulesModal.tsx:46-47, 136-137). The live AddQuestionDialog is a QzModal (AddQuestionDialog.tsx:92), which closes on a scrim mousedown (qz-overlays.tsx:138-141); its only opt-out today, destructive, also removes Esc and the × (qz-overlays.tsx:124-125, 150-156). Add an additive opt-out prop (dismissOnScrim={false}), pass it from both windows, and leave the default alone so no other modal changes (Add recommendations and Add a question). The Questions step's composer is the same dialog, so it gets the same behaviour.
  2. Esc closes the innermost layer first: popover, then "Add a question", then "Add recommendations", then the rule window (draft discarded, no prompt), then the armed chip. Inside an inline edit, Esc only restores the text, caught in the capture phase. The live parts already do this for two layers: the rule window ignores Esc while a popover is open (CreateRuleModal.tsx:263-272), and QzModal takes Esc in the capture phase and stops it (qz-overlays.tsx:124-134), so a QzModal on top closes before the layer under it. The stacked "Add recommendations" window joins the same order.
  3. A second click on whatever opened a menu or popover closes it, and only one popover is open at a time (openPop(); one #pop). QzPopover already does both (qz-overlays.tsx:292, 332-341, 386-403, 411).
  4. Choosing the other style lands on Edit, even from Table; choosing the current style keeps the view (ACT.setstyle). In the product that same gesture is the only thing that writes logic_style (D5).
  5. Deleting a rule never asks for confirmation (row trash, Table trash, "Delete rule" in the window); Undo recovers it (delRule(), ACT.mdel). Owner ruling of 2026-09-18; Undo is inverse mutations by rule id (D7).
  6. Typing is silent; the save pill appears only after a committed change (the focusout handler, svStart()), at the edited field, while the ambient autosave chrome stays silent when healthy (D8).
  7. The rule window has no title row and one scrolling body; only the footer stays put (modalHTML(); B33 rejected; D24).
  8. "Image select" appears in the type menu only while it is the question's type (typeMenu()), like the curated live picker (TypeChipSelector.tsx:30-36, 169-174; TypeChipSelector.test.tsx:141-146; B46 rejected).
  9. The points stepper can turn a Five-point question into "Scale · 1–6" without a message (B44 rejected). The live picker does the same: its 2 to 10 stepper shows for every rating question (TypeChipSelector.tsx:306-312), and Five point is only the 1–5 preset (TypeChipSelector.tsx:59-65).
  10. Table sheets carry no headings, and Table has no create control: new rules come from "Needs a rule" rows or the Edit view (tableHTML(), headRight(); B39 rejected).
  11. A Rules-sheet import is all-or-nothing: one bad row leaves every rule unchanged (applyImport()). D16 keeps this, and the toast must name the bad row and its reason (B22). The Answers sheet is the exception by design: it updates in place, row by row, and never adds or deletes an answer.
  12. In Filter Results + Rules, an unmapped answer on the picking question blocks Continue even when a rule covers those shoppers (findings(); B42 rejected). It mirrors the shipped V4 block (pathReport.ts:193, 386; quizPublish.ts:507). In Rules only that check does not run at all, because the engine never reads the mapping there (D1, D3).

Acceptance criteria for this section

These are the checks that say the stand-ins are gone. Each is observable in the shipped step; the wording for every defect is in QA part 1 and QA part 2, and the probes are in Tests and probes.

  • No harness ships: no shell bar, no heading above the stage, no stress checkboxes, no "Reset", no "Show it empty", no pitch line. Grep the built bundle for "Show it empty" and "10 answers on Q5" and find nothing.
  • No stub toast ships: no "Opens the existing Paste rules window", "Back to Questions" as a toast, "Continues to Results", "A save is already waiting for you" or "Export isn't available here". Every one of those controls does its real work.
  • Nothing is keyed by name or position: rules, answers, recommendations and questions are addressed by id in the window, the rows, the reorder, the Undo and the import. Deleting an answer renumbers no rule.
  • Quiz.logic_style is written by the title switch and by nothing else. Loading the step writes nothing: a draft that is never switched round-trips byte-identical, and its style comes from inference. build_session.logic_style is still parsed and is read only as the second resolution step.
  • In Rules only the engine takes its own branch: roles and answer mappings are ignored, the first matching rule's recommendations are the result, and the stored roles, mappings and filter values are still on the document afterwards. In Filter Results + Rules the chain is unchanged. A document with no logic_style key resolves exactly as it does today.
  • A shopper no rule matches reaches the fallback chain, the loading beat, the email capture and the completion analytics, in both styles. The bare no-match card is gone for decider documents. The legacy byte pin still starts c02ccaec98a0fe9e after deploy.
  • One Tier-1 report drives the CTA, the check popover and publish, and it is style-aware. The popover never reads safer than the publish gate, in either style, and "Fix N issues" counts blocking findings only.
  • No style chooser renders, and LogicStyleChooser and its "Point based" row are deleted.
  • The toast carries at most one action, announces itself in a live region, can be reached from the keyboard, and lasts long enough to be used. The dated exception is written into the contract comment at qz-toast.tsx:13-17. Undo restores by id and never rolls back an unrelated edit made while the toast is up.
  • Moving "Picks results" announces what it cleared and its Undo restores the role and every target, from the role menu, the Table and Import alike.
  • A rule row is edited by clicking it, reordered from the keyboard, and deleted without a confirm; Duplicate is in the rule window's top row.
  • An "is not" row shows no any/all toggle, reads as "none of these", and its sentence reads "not (A or B)". Import rejects "NOT (A AND B)" with a named reason.
  • Paste rules never writes a cross-question "or"; an existing one still renders and survives an edit.
  • "+ Add recommendations" writes through ensure-targets, handles the group kind, normalizes tag keys to the step-1 slugs, creates quiz-scoped rows, and sends at most 12 per call. Adding the same resource twice creates one row.
  • Export downloads the file Import accepts back, including on a quiz with no rules, where it still writes headers, the id columns and one example row. The workbook is built by SheetJS CE 0.20.3, loaded as a lazy chunk; no xlsx entry appears in package.json.
  • Rule sentences are verb-first and answers-only everywhere, and the Table and the export use "Q7 = Yes" everywhere. One describer serves both.
  • Every renamed label comes from the shared constants and reads the same on this screen, in the builder's Rules inspector and in the pinned tests. No internal word reaches the merchant.
  • The live surfaces of D19 all render: the Narrows attribute picker, four rule-flag chips, product-count popovers, the picker's kind filters and drill-in. The "won't work as written" banner is gone, and "Explore every path" is still builder-only.
  • The embedded twins mount QzToastProvider, so an Undo is never invisible there (D21). Nothing else in the embedded surface changes in this work.

Limits of the review

  • What was reviewed. The 1,067-line copy only, loaded locally in headless Chromium through Playwright; never the hosted artifact and never the app. The source file has since grown to 1,200 lines.
  • Outcome. 68 findings from six test passes (216 control checks). 63 are confirmed, each reproduced by 3 of 3 independent verification runs (9 high, 24 medium, 30 low); 5 were rejected as deliberate (B33, B39, B42, B44, B46).
  • Viewports. Mostly 1440×900 and 1280×720, with spot checks from 800×600 to 1920 wide.
  • Browsers. Chromium only. Firefox and WebKit were not installed, so Safari's habit of not focusing a clicked button (raised under B56) is unverified.
  • Input. Mouse and keyboard; no touch. IME was tested only for B54, through Chromium's DevTools IME commands rather than an operating-system input method.
  • Accessibility. axe-core 4.12.1 and Chromium's accessibility tree; no screen reader.
  • Data. Stand-in sizes only: 6 recommendations (30 with the harness), 29 catalogue items, 34 narrowing values, 5 questions with at most 10 answers. Long names, hundreds of tags or recommendations and long rule lists are untested, for fit and for speed.
  • Export. Exercised only against a stubbed downloads capability, because the button is hidden when the file runs outside the artifact. The template behaviour D16 adds (Export on a quiz with no rules) has never run anywhere.
  • No server. Autosave and its 700 ms debounce, failed saves, Undo racing a pending save, ensure-targets failures and its 12-resource cap, the intents, loader revalidation and the publish gates are untested there; cover them in the real build's probes (Tests).
  • No shopper. The review never ran a quiz. Nothing in it touches the engine branch, the safety net or the runtime, which is why those carry their own proof rules (Engine semantics).
  • Timing. The 2026-09-19 fixes to the source came after the review, and the rulings came after those. Check any mock behaviour you rely on against the QA criteria and the rulings, not against the mock.
  • Live code. The review never ran the app: statements about origin/main in this handoff come from reading the code at b4aa278, plus the engine probes cited in Engine semantics.

Mock QA: every confirmed defect as a build requirement

A button-to-button review of the reference mock (six testers, 152 raw reports, 68 after merging duplicates, each re-tested by three independent reproducers) confirmed 63 defects. Every one is fixed in the published mock, and each fix was proved by re-running its original reproduction. Treat every row as an acceptance criterion for the real build regardless: the severity is the mock's, but the underlying mistake is one the app can repeat. Expand a row for the reproduction, the root cause and what the fix was.

Two things to know before reading a row.

  • The wording is the review's, and the owner's rulings supersede it. Every "Requirement" cell was written during the review, before the 2026-09-22 rulings. Where a cell offers options the owner has since closed, it has been rewritten and says so; where it does not, the settled sections win. The Decisions section is the authority, not this table.
  • The CODE line numbers quote the reviewed copy, not the current mock. They are line numbers of the 1,067-line copy kept at scratchpad/review/rules-row.before-fixes.html. The source file docs/design/logic-tab/rules-row/index.html is still being edited and has grown to about 1,200 lines, so on the current file search for the identifier or the quoted copy instead. Every other section cites the mock by identifier for this reason.
IdDefectSeverityStatus in the mockRequirement (expand for detail)
B1Undo restores rules that point at answers or recommendations removed since, and every render then crasheshighFixed in mock
Ruled behaviour (supersedes the review wording). Undo restores the rule exactly as it was, by id, including conditions and targets that poin…

Requirement. Ruled behaviour (supersedes the review wording). Undo restores the rule exactly as it was, by id, including conditions and targets that point at answers or recommendations removed since. Nothing is trimmed and nothing is clipped, and the Undo is never withdrawn. Every renderer resolves a missing reference to null and draws it flagged (a 'recommendation deleted' or 'answer deleted' marker) instead of throwing, which is what keeps the page rendering. The mock fixes this by trimming; do not copy that part.

Reproduction on the mock. 1) Title ▾ → Filter Results + Rules (Q1 selected). 2) Hover rule 1 in the Rules column and click its trash; the toast 'Rule 1 deleted · Undo' shows for 6 s. 3) Within 6 s, click 'Single select ▾' under the Q1 title → Scale, then click '−' beside Max three times (6 → 3 points). 4) Click Undo in the toast. Shell variants: (a) tick '10 answers on Q5', create 'Show sensitive when Q5 = Salicylic acid for breakouts' (or 'Ceramides…'), delete it or click 'Show it empty', untick the box, click Undo. (b) Tick '30 recommendations', create a rule that shows 'hydration', delete it, untick the box, click Undo.

Root cause found in the mock. **Undo restores a stale snapshot without checking it.** ACT.undo (index.html:1020) runs `S.rules=JSON.parse(UNDO)` and does no other check. The snapshot comes from snap() (index.html:657, `UNDO=JSON.stringify(S.rules)`). snap() is called from delRule (:859), wipe / "Show it empty" (:1019) and the drop handler (:1060). It stores only the rules, as answer indexes and recommendation ids. **The code that removes answers or recommendations only fixes live rules.** These paths trim S.rules and the M draft but never the pending UNDO snapshot: - setPoints (:607-608), reached from tpts (:963) and from settype's five-point option. - The #stress uncheck handler (:1035). - The #stress30 uncheck handler (:1055). - settype's multi-only `all` strip (:959). **Why a restored stale index breaks every render:** - sentence() (:643) calls ansText(q,i) (:606), which reads `q.answers[i].t` and throws a TypeError. The Table path throws the same way through whenParts() (:755). - renderInner() (:726) builds the whole #stage HTML in one expression before assigning innerHTML. So the throw leaves the old DOM on screen. - Every later render() throws again: sel, setstyle, vw, and reset while the shortened question stays short. **Stale recommendation ids** don't throw. sentence prints r.recs as-is, but vizRecs, modalHTML and sheets() list only RECS. So a restored "hydration" rule shows up in the rule row but nowhere else.

Fixed in the mock by. Undo can no longer bring back a reference to a removed answer or recommendation. UNDO is now an object {rules,n,dels} holding a deep copy, not a JSON string (index.html ~665-673). Two helpers sit next to it. eachRule(f) (~669) visits S.rules, the open draft M and the pending Undo's rules; setPoints (~611), the '10 answers on Q5' untick and the '30 recommendations' untick now trim or re-index through it, so the snapshot stays in step with the live rules. fitRule(r) (~670) drops conditions on missing questions or answers, removes 'all of' from non-multi questions and filters recs against RECS. ACT.undo restores UNDO.rules.map(fitRule) (~1042). settype's multi-only 'all' strip also reaches the pending Undo (~980). The import Undo (ACT.impUndo ~1001) now fits too: it filters answer targets against RECS, fits the rules and fits and redraws an open M. Before, that path crashed pane() after the 30-recs box was unticked.

B2The open rule window edits by list position, so an Undo or a keyboard action behind it makes Save or Delete hit a different rulehighFixed in mock
The window stays bound to the rule it opened (by identity, not index), or closes or refuses when the list changes underneath it. The page be…

Requirement. The window stays bound to the rule it opened (by identity, not index), or closes or refuses when the list changes underneath it. The page behind the aria-modal window is inert: focus moves into the window, Tab stays inside, focus returns to the opener on close, and the Undo toast can't change the list while the window is open. Save and Delete only touch the rule shown.

Reproduction on the mock. Rules only, Edit view, sample rules. Path A (toast): 1) Hover rule 1 (dryness) and click its trash; toast 'Rule 1 deleted · Undo' (6 s). 2) Click the new rule 2 (redness); the window opens as Edit rule with M.edit=1. 3) Click Undo in the toast, which sits above the scrim (z-index 60 over 40) and stays clickable. 4) Click Save rule without changes, or click 'Delete rule'. Path B (keyboard): 1) Tab to rule row 2 (acne) and press Enter; Edit rule opens but focus stays on the row behind the scrim. 2) Press Tab once (focus lands on rule 2's trash behind the window) and press Enter: 'Rule 2 deleted', the window stays open. 3) Click Save rule. The drag toast 'Moved to position N · Undo', the import toast's Undo (Table view) and the shell's 'Show it empty' reached by Tab do the same.

Root cause found in the mock. The rule window points at its rule by array position, and nothing stops the list from changing while the window is open. 1) ACT.editrule (index.html:1008) stores the row's position in the draft (`M=...{...r,edit:+el.dataset.i}`). ACT.msave (:1016) later writes `S.rules[edit]=rule`, and ACT.mdel (:1010) calls `delRule(M.edit)`. Neither checks that the position still holds the rule the window loaded. 2) The dialog is marked aria-modal="true" (modalHTML :888) but does not behave as modal, so S.rules can change underneath it: - #toast has z-index 60 (:339) and #modal has z-index 40 (:276), so the toast's Undo can still be clicked. ACT.undo (:1020) and ACT.impUndo (:980) replace S.rules from a JSON snapshot. - drawModal (:903-906) never moves focus into the dialog, never makes the page behind it inert, and never returns focus to the opener. Tab therefore reaches: - the row trash buttons: ACT.delrule :1009 → delRule :859, which splices S.rules; - 'Show it empty': ACT.wipe :1019, which sets S.rules=[]; - other rows: the Enter/Space handler at :1034 calls ACT.editrule and silently replaces M. - The drop handler (:1060) also reorders the list, and its toast offers Undo. None of these touch or close M, so Save or Delete hits whichever rule now sits at the old position. When that position is past the end, `S.rules[edit]=rule` leaves holes in the array. rulesBand's map skips the holes, but shadowedBy (:653-655) reads S.rules[j] directly, so complete(undefined) → condQs (:650) th

Fixed in the mock by. The rule window now finds its rule by a stable id instead of its list position. Changes: `let RID=0;const rid=()=>"r"+(++RID)` (~579); SEED adds ids; Reset sets RID=0 so the sample ids come back. applyImport gives each row the id of the rule in the same position, and new rows get new ids (~877). ACT.editrule stores `edit:r.id` and ignores a stale row. ACT.msave and ACT.mdel find the rule with `findIndex(x=>x.id===edit)`. If the rule is gone, Save writes nothing and shows 'That rule was removed, so nothing was saved', and Delete shows 'That rule was already removed'. ACT.undo and ACT.impUndo call a new keepM(), which keeps an open window on its rule by id. If an Undo removed that rule (only an import Undo can), keepM closes the window and shows 'Undone. The rule you had open is gone, so its window closed'. drawModal (~942-954) makes .shell, #pitch and .stagewrap inert while the window is open. Focus moves to the selected verb on open and on a new draft, and goes back to the opener on close (drawModal.back plus an actKey selector, falling back to the Create a rule button). shadowedBy now skips empty slots (`!r`/`!e`). Result: Path A Save keeps [dryness,acne,redness,…], and Delete removes redness ('Rule 3 deleted'). Path B: Tab and Shift+Tab never reach the page behind. Drag+Undo+Save keeps dryness. Import-Undo leaves no hole and no crash.

B3Import matches answer text across all questions, so re-importing an unchanged export moves a rule to another questionhighFixed in mock
'Nothing changed', and the rule stays on Q7. The When cell identifies the question for every answer (as scale answers already do with 'Q5 = …

Requirement. 'Nothing changed', and the rule stays on Q7. The When cell identifies the question for every answer (as scale answers already do with 'Q5 = 3'), and import resolves within that question or reports the ambiguity.

Reproduction on the mock. 1) Title ▾ → Filter Results + Rules. '+ Add question' → 'Do you wear SPF every day?' with answers Yes / No → Add. Repeat with 'Do you wear makeup most days?' Yes / No (Q6 and Q7). 2) Create a rule: Q7 'Yes' → sensitive. 3) Table → Export (the file:// mock hides Export; buildWorkbook() writes the identical file). 4) Import that file unedited. Also: a new question with an answer 'Cheeks' moves its rule to Q2 'Cheeks' the same way.

Root cause found in the mock. docs/design/logic-tab/rules-row/index.html (lines 606, 755, 757, 826, 830, 839–840). The export drops which question an answer belongs to, and the import guesses it back by first text match: 1. Line 606, `ansText`: adds the question number only to scale answers ('Q5 = 3'). Every other answer is the bare text. 2. Line 755, `whenParts`: builds the When column with `ans:r.conds[k].map(i=>ansText(q,i))`. So line 757 `whenText` writes 'Yes' to the file, and whenHTML shows 'Yes' in the table, with no question. 3. Line 826, `findAnswer`: the bare-text fallback `for(const q of S.qs){const i=q.answers.findIndex(a=>low(a.t)===low(t));if(i>=0)return{q,i}}` returns the FIRST question whose answer text matches. 'Yes' always goes to Q6 and 'Cheeks' to Q2. 4. Line 830, `parseWhen`: `if(hits.some(h=>h.q.id!==qid)||conds[qid])return null`. 'Yes AND Yes' resolves both parts to q6, hits the duplicate-question check, and the row becomes invalid. 5. Lines 839–840, `applyImport`: - Any invalid row makes `if(bad)skipped+=bad` ignore the whole Rules sheet, so other real edits are dropped. - Otherwise, `key(next[i])!==key(S.rules[i])` counts the silently moved rule as '1 change', and `S.rules=next` commits it.

Fixed in the mock by. Import no longer guesses which question an answer belongs to. findAnswer resolves "Qn = answer" inside that question, and bare text only when exactly one question carries it; anything ambiguous is named ("“Yes” is an answer on Q6 and Q7 — write it as Q7 = Yes") and skipped instead of moved. The export already wrote the machine form (P2); it now also carries a Rule ID column.

B4Import matches Answers-sheet rows to answers by position, so deleting or inserting one row shifts every later answer and rewires rules and mappingshighFixed in mock
The missing row is detected (Q1 reported or skipped). Answers keep their own text and targets, and rules keep their meaning.

Requirement. The missing row is detected (Q1 reported or skipped). Answers keep their own text and targets, and rules keep their meaning.

Reproduction on the mock. Filter Results + Rules, Table. Export, delete the Answers row for Q1 'Shiny all over, pores visible', then Import.

Root cause found in the mock. In index.html, applyImport (line 833) pairs each Answers-sheet row with an answer by position, not by identity. - **Line 841:** `const seen={}`. - **Line 843:** `const ai=seen[q.id]=(seen[q.id]===undefined?0:seen[q.id]+1),a=q.answers[ai]`. The Nth row that carries "Q1" is written onto the Nth Q1 answer. - If a row is deleted, every later row lands one answer early. - Line 851 then overwrites `a.t` and line 853 overwrites `a.targets` (lines 854-857 do the same for filter values and route). - The last answer gets no row and keeps its old text, which creates the duplicate. - Only surplus rows are detected (`if(!a){skipped++;continue}`); a missing row never is. - **Line 835:** sheets are sorted so the Answers sheet is applied before the Rules sheet. - **Line 826:** the Rules sheet resolves answers by text through `findAnswer`, against the answers that were just renamed. "Shiny…" no longer exists, so `parseWhen` returns null. - **Line 840:** Rules import is all-or-nothing (`if(bad)skipped+=bad;else{…}`), so S.rules is left untouched. S.rules stores answer indexes (`conds:{q1:[1]}` and so on), so every rule on a shifted answer now silently means something else. - **The mismatch:** the Answers sheet is matched by position while the Rules sheet is matched by text. The export writes no stable per-answer key, so the importer cannot tell "row deleted or inserted" apart from "answer renamed".

Fixed in the mock by. Answers now carry a stable aid (assigned in A()), exported as a trailing do-not-edit "Answer ID" column. Import resolves each row by id first, then by text inside its own question, and only pairs leftovers one-for-one when the counts line up (a rename). A row that matches nothing is skipped and named; an answer with no row is left alone and reported ("Q1: 1 answer isn't in the file — import never adds or deletes answers").

B5Import reads a missing column as blank: no '#' column deletes every rule, no 'Then' column resets every route, and a row with a blank '#' is dropped silentlyhighFixed in mock
A missing column leaves that field unchanged (the Type column is already guarded with ci('type')>=0), or the sheet is refused with a message…

Requirement. A missing column leaves that field unchanged (the Type column is already guarded with ci('type')>=0), or the sheet is refused with a message. A row with a blank '#' is imported as a new rule, or at least counted and reported as skipped.

Reproduction on the mock. A) Rules only, Table. Export, delete column A '#' from the Rules sheet, Import. B) Export, append a Rules row with '#' blank: Show | sensitive | Stings or itches with most products, Import. C) Filter Results + Rules, Table: set Q1 A's Then to 'Skips to Q4', Export, delete the Then column, Import.

Root cause found in the mock. The bug is in applyImport, in /Users/chase/code/quizocalypse-builder/docs/design/logic-tab/rules-row/index.html at lines 833 to 858. Line 835 finds columns by header name with `ci=k=>head.indexOf(k)`, but every read is `r[ci(k)]` with no check for -1. For a missing column, `r[-1]` is `undefined` and `nrm(undefined)` returns "". So a missing column looks exactly like a blank cell, and a blank cell means "clear this field". (1) Line 837: `const num=nrm(r[ci("#")]);if(!num||num==="—")continue;`. The '#' value is only used as a "this row exists" marker. Rule order comes from row order, and the number itself is never read. With no '#' column, every row hits `continue` and `bad` stays 0. Line 840 then compares `next=[]` with S.rules, finds `d=S.rules.length`, and runs `S.rules=next`, which deletes every rule. (2) Also line 837: when the '#' column exists but a cell in it is blank, a fully filled row still hits `continue` without `bad++`, so it is neither imported nor reported. The Answers branch at line 842 does count a filled row with a blank Q as skipped, so the two sheets behave differently. (3) Line 856: `const th=low(r[ci("then")])` gives "" when the Then column is missing. That sets `route=null`, and line 857 then sets `a.route=null` on every answer that had a custom route. The Type column is guarded (line 845: `if(ci("type")>=0&&...)`), but Then has no guard.

Fixed in the mock by. Every read goes through cell(row,key), which returns undefined when the column is not in the file, and every field is guarded: a missing column leaves that field unchanged. A row counts as a rule when it has content, not when it has a '#', so a filled row with a blank '#' imports as a new rule.

B6Moving 'Picks results' to another question silently wipes the old question's mappings, with no warning, Undo or restorehighFixed in mock
Ruled behaviour (D9, option A; supersedes the review wording). Moving 'Picks results' to another question still clears both questions' answe…

Requirement. Ruled behaviour (D9, option A; supersedes the review wording). Moving 'Picks results' to another question still clears both questions' answer mappings, and there is no confirm dialog. The loss is announced instead: a toast names what was cleared (for example "Q1's 6 recommendations were removed") and its Undo restores the role and every target. One path serves the role menu, the Table and Import.

Reproduction on the mock. 1) Filter Results + Rules (Q1 picks the result, 6 mapped answers). 2) Select Q2 → role button → 'Picks the result' (its description says '· Q1 has it now'), or in Table open Q2's 'What it does ▾' → Picks the result. 3) Set Q2 back to Info only and Q1 back to Picks results. Also: on Q1 itself choose 'Narrows', then 'Picks the result' again. Compare: set Q2 to Narrows, give A 'Face' and B 'Keeps everything', switch Q2 to Info only and back to Narrows.

Root cause found in the mock. The cause is `ACT.setrole` in docs/design/logic-tab/rules-row/index.html:965: `if(k==="decides")S.qs.forEach(x=>{if(x.role==="decides"&&x!==q){x.role="info";x.answers.forEach(a=>a.targets=[])}});if(k!=="decides")q.answers.forEach(a=>a.targets=[]);q.role=k;...render()` - It erases the old decider's targets, and a question's own targets when it leaves decides. It does this with no confirm, no toast and no snapshot. - `ACT.trole` (:974) opens the same `roleMenu` (:918), so the Table path behaves identically. - The `roleMenu` hint "· Q1 has it now" (:918) says who holds the job, not that its mappings will be cleared. - The shared `snap()`/`undo` pair (:657, :1020) covers only `S.rules`, so no Undo is possible for `S.qs`. - `setrole` leaves `values`/`any` untouched, so Narrows data survives a flip while Picks data does not. - `applyImport` (:850) demotes the old decider without clearing its targets. The same role change therefore has two different outcomes depending on the path.

Fixed in the mock by. D9's 'one path' made into one policy: moveRole() now clears a question's values and 'Keeps everything' flags when it leaves Narrows, exactly as it clears mappings when Picks moves, and names both losses in one toast whose single Undo restores the role and everything on the answers. roleLossAny() decides the snapshot; the role menu warns '· clears Q2's values' before the click; Import takes the same path.

B7Type changes delete answers and their mappings with no Undo: Scale '−' says nothing, and Five-point contradicts 'your answers are kept'highFixed in mock
Removing answers is confirmed or offers Undo, and the message names what was lost (answers, mappings, affected rules). The tooltip only prom…

Requirement. Removing answers is confirmed or offers Undo, and the message names what was lost (answers, mappings, affected rules). The tooltip only promises what actually happens.

Reproduction on the mock. A) Filter Results + Rules, Q1 (the deciding question) → 'Single select ▾' → Scale, click '−' beside Max four times (6 → 2 points). B) Reload. Hover 'Single select ▾' (tooltip 'Change the question type — your answers are kept'), click it, choose 'Five-point scale'. C) Create a rule on Q5 with all of 'Vitamin C…' + 'Retinol…', then set Q5 to Five-point scale.

Root cause found in the mock. All line numbers are in docs/design/logic-tab/rules-row/index.html. 1. **setPoints (:607-608)** trims with `q.answers.length=n`. That drops each answer's text, targets, values and route, and quietly filters rule conditions (`r.conds[q.id].filter(i=>i<n)`). It returns nothing, so callers cannot tell the user what was lost. 2. **ACT.tpts (:963)** calls setPoints and then only does `render();drawPop()`. There is no snapshot, no toast and no confirmation. 3. **ACT.settype (:954-960).** - Line 956 builds a count-only message, "Removed N answer(s) to make five points". It does not name the mappings or the rules that were changed. - Line 960 shows that message with plain `toast()` (:914: 2.2 s, textContent only, no Undo). - Line 959, `if(n&&!msg)`, drops the "Rules on Qn now match any of their answers" message whenever a removal message is already set, so an AND→OR change to a rule's meaning goes unreported. 4. **typeBtn (:617)** always says "your answers are kept". That is false for Five-point on a question with more than 5 answers, and for the Scale stepper inside the same popover. 5. **No Undo for question changes.** The mock's Undo, `snap()` (:657) with `undo` (:1020), snapshots only S.rules, so question-shape changes cannot be undone. A pending rule-delete, wipe or drag Undo is also not invalidated when answers are trimmed. Restoring it brings back rule indices that point at answers that no longer exist, and `sentence()`/`ansText()` (:643/:606) crash on `q.answers[i].

Fixed in the mock by. New question-shape Undo slot (QUNDO, index.html:760-768) covering role, type and point changes: qsnap() deep-copies S.qs + S.rules, qLostMsg() names the answers and mappings removed since the snapshot, toastQ() shows it with Undo, ACT.qundo (1146) restores questions and the rule conditions that moved with them. settype (1109) now snapshots before Five-point trims, before a Scale clamp and before it drops all-of flags, and joins the messages instead of suppressing one (the AND→OR change is reported even when a removal message exists). tpts (1130) snapshots on every '−' and says what it took. The type button's tooltip (typeTip, 645) only promises what happens, and the stepper's '−' carries a title naming the point it will remove (ptsTip, 635).

B8Rules that lose all their answers or recommendations are kept with no flag, still count, and don't block ContinuehighFixed in mock
The removal says which rules lost their answers or recommendations, and those rules are flagged in the list and the Table (DECISIONS: dangli…

Requirement. The removal says which rules lost their answers or recommendations, and those rules are flagged in the list and the Table (DECISIONS: dangling references are 'rendered flagged, never silently dropped'; zero-condition rules are blocked at creation). They don't count as coverage, and Continue warns or blocks, the same bar the rule window applies (Save is disabled without an answer or a recommendation).

Reproduction on the mock. 1) Filter Results + Rules. Q1 → type → Scale → Max '−' four times (6 → 2 points). 2) Title ▾ → Rules only; then open Table. Variants: create 'Show sensitive when Q1 = Stings…' and switch Q1 to Five-point scale; tick '10 answers on Q5', create 'Show sensitive when Q5 = Azelaic acid for redness', untick; tick '30 recommendations', create 'Show hydration when Stings or itches…', untick.

Root cause found in the mock. Every removal path edits rule references in place and never reports or checks the result. The "no answers / no recommendation" state is recognised in exactly one place, and nothing that counts coverage or gates Continue uses it. Where the trimming happens (docs/design/logic-tab/rules-row/index.html): - setPoints (:607-608) cuts q.answers down to n and filters r.conds[q.id] to indices below n for every rule and the open draft M. It returns nothing. - ACT.tpts (:963), the Max '−' stepper, calls setPoints with no toast. - ACT.settype, when set to "five" (:956), calls setPoints(q,5). Its toast "Removed N answers to make five points" does not name any rule. - The #stress handler (:1035) does the same trim for Q5 with no toast. - The #stress30 handler (:1055) runs `r.recs=r.recs.filter(...)` with no toast. Where the resulting state is ignored: - complete() (:651) is used only by shadowedBy (:653-654). - ruleCount (:646) counts any rule that lists the recommendation. It feeds the strip "N/6 have a rule" (:718-719), the rule window's own counter (:892-893, :899) and the stripMore/mrecMore lists (:804, :815). - findings() (:667) counts any non-hide rule as covering its recommendation. - In Rules only, findings() (:670) only checks S.rules.length. So blocking() (:674) returns 0 and fbar (:680) renders "Continue →". - rulesBand (:714) flags only shadowed rules, and ruleRows (:703) flags nothing. - sheets() (:762) prints "(none)" and "(no answers)" as plain text, and the Recommendation

Fixed in the mock by. Rules that lose all their answers or recommendations are now flagged, not counted, reported and blocking. deadWhy(i) (index.html ~700) checks completeness first: tag 'never runs · no answers left' / 'no recommendation left' / 'no answers or recommendation left', shown in the Rules-only list, the Filter Rules column and both Tables (rows also get the existing muted class). ruleCount/recCovered go through deadWhy, so the strip reads 2/6 after the repro and the window chip / Table say 'Needs a rule'. findings() adds a crit per incomplete rule in both styles ('Rule 3 has no answers left, so it never runs'), which the check popover renders as a button that opens that rule (Save is disabled there, the same bar). Removals report what they broke: new rkeys()/lossMsg(was,q) compare each rule's conds/recs before and after; ACT.tpts, ACT.settype (appended to its own message), the '10 answers on Q5' untick and the '30 recommendations' untick toast e.g. 'Rule 5 lost an answer on Q1 · it never runs now', 'Rules 3, 4 and 5 lost answers on Q1 · they never run now', 'Rule 6 lost a recommendation · it never runs now'. lossToast() leaves a live delete-Undo toast alone (the rows still carry the flag), so C1's Undo-after-trim path keeps working.

Reset returns the whole mock to its start state (questions, answer targets, both shell checkboxes) and never throws. In the product, an answ…

Requirement. Reset returns the whole mock to its start state (questions, answer targets, both shell checkboxes) and never throws. In the product, an answer cell whose recommendation no longer exists is shown as missing and dropped or flagged, not a crash.

Reproduction on the mock. A) Reload. '+ Add recommendations' → Moisturizers → Add. Title ▾ → Filter Results + Rules, click the tray chip 'Moisturizers', then click Q1 answer A's cell to place it. Click Reset (it switches to Rules only), then title ▾ → Filter Results + Rules. (Same with 'hydration' placed on Q1 A while '30 recommendations' is ticked.) B) Reload. Root cause found in the mock. The cause is `shadowedBy`, index.html:652-656 (the tag is drawn at 713-714). It compares rules word for word, one pair at a time; it does not work out which shoppers each rule catches. - Line 653, `if(!complete(r)||Object.values(r.not).some(Boolean))return null`: any "is not" flag on the later rule turns the check off (case B). This includes a leftover flag on a question with no answers picked (case M, which happens when you pick an answer, toggle "is not", then un-pick the answer). - Line 654, `if(!complete(e)||Object.values(e.not).some(Boolean))continue`: an earlier "is not" rule can never count as catching anyone (C, D). On a single-select question, "is Blotchy" or "is Three to four" already means "is not X". - Line 655, `condQs(e).every(k=>!e.all[k]&&(r.conds[k]||[]).length&&r.conds[k].every(y=>e.conds[k].includes(y)))` has three problems: 1. `!e.all[k]` means an earlier "all of" rule never catches anyone, not even its exact duplicate (K). 2. `(r.conds[k]||[]).length` makes the later rule name every question the earlier rule names. So a catch-all on a question everyone answers (Q1, any of all 6 answers) never catches a rule about Q3 (G). 3. The subset test ignores `r.all[k]`. A later "all of" rule only needs to share one answer with an earlier "any of" rule (A, E). - Lines 654-655: the loop checks one earlier rule at a time and returns a single index j. A rule covered only by several earlier rules together (F) is never found, and the tag at 714 (`rule ${sh+1}`) can

Fixed in the mock by. shadowedBy(i) (index.html ~672) now enumerates what shoppers can answer on the questions the rules name (picksFor: single-select one answer or 'unnamed/skipped'; multi-select every pick set within Min–Max; holds() treats 'is not' as true for skipped/unnamed answers) and walks only the branches rule i allows, keeping the earlier rules still possible on each branch; a branch is caught when its first live rule is fully decided. It returns one earlier rule when one alone covers rule i, else the union that does it together ('never runs · rules 1 and 2 catch them first' via nlist). Earlier is-not, all-of, catch-alls on other questions and unions are all handled; a rule that matches nobody or an enumeration over 200k combinations returns null (no tag). deadWhy is cached per state (DW/dwFp fingerprint over rules + question type/min/max/answer count/routes), since coverage asks every rule's flag for every recommendation.

Root cause found in the mock. The rule window's draft M keeps per-question flags that the sentence never shows, and saving stores M exactly as it is: - index.html:1012 ACT.mnot: sets M.not[q] even when Q has no picked answers. - index.html:1013 ACT.mall: sets M.all[q]. - index.html:1011 ACT.mans: unpicking an answer never clears M.all or M.not, and it leaves empty arrays behind. - index.html:887-888 modalHTML: the join switch is only drawn when picked.length>1, so an "all of" left on one pick is hidden. - index.html:1016 ACT.msave: `const {edit,...rule}=M; S.rules.push(rule)` saves the draft as is, including false flags and empty arrays. sentence() (:643), whenParts() (:755) and whenText() (:757) ignore these flags. They only render questions that have picks, and they print no join for a single answer. So the saved rule differs from the sentence the user sees. shadowedBy() at :653-655 does read the flags: - `Object.values(r.not).some(Boolean)` / `Object.values(e.not).some(Boolean)` skips any rule with a true not flag, including one on a question the rule never tests. - `!e.all[k]` treats any all flag as a real "all of", even on one answer, where "all of" means the same as "any of". The "never runs" tag therefore disappears in both cases. The import's JSON key compare at :840 also sees the leftover flags and empty arrays as differences (B25).

Fixed in the mock by. A new tidy(d) (~958) builds the saved rule. It keeps conds only for questions with picks, in question order. It keeps not[q] only when that question has picks, and all[q] only for 2+ picks on a multi-select. It copies no empty arrays and no false flags. ACT.msave saves tidy(M). ACT.mans drops M.all[q] when picks fall below 2, so a later second pick starts at 'any of'. shadowedBy now reads 'not' flags only on questions the rule tests (neg), and treats a one-pick 'all of' as any-of. Result: case A stays tagged 'never runs · rule 2 catches them first'. In case B the identical Cheeks rule is tagged 'rule 7 catches them first'. A real 'is not' with picks and a real 2-pick 'all of' are still saved. Export then import with no edits reports 0 changes.

Root cause found in the mock. The drop line and the drop position are worked out separately, and they disagree whenever a rule is dragged down. 1. The line always promises "insert above the hovered row." The dragover handler (index.html:1059) always adds .over to the hovered row. The CSS for it (index.html:367, `.rr.over{box-shadow:inset 0 2px 0 var(--accent)}`) always draws the line on that row's top edge. 2. The drop handler (index.html:1060) does `const to=+el.dataset.ri; ... S.rules.splice(to,0,S.rules.splice(dragI,1)[0]); toastU(`Moved to position ${to+1}`)`. It removes the rule first, so when dragI < to every later row moves up one index. Inserting at `to` then puts the dragged rule after the original target row, taking the target's slot at final index `to`. When dragging up (dragI > to) nothing shifts, so the line and the drop agree. That is why only downward drags miss. The toast uses `to+1`, so it matches where the rule lands, not the line.

Fixed in the mock by. One calculation (dropAt) now feeds both the drop line and the drop index: the pointer's half of the row says above or below, and the index allows for the rule being lifted out before it is re-inserted. Added .rr.under for the bottom-edge line, cleaned both classes on drop/dragend, and routed the drop through moveRule so drag, buttons and keyboard share one path and one Undo.

B22One bad Rules row throws away every rule edit in the sheet, and the toast only says '1 skipped'mediumFixed in mock

Requirement. Ruled behaviour (D16, option B; supersedes the review wording). The Rules sheet stays all-or-nothing: one bad row means no rule changed, and the toast says so plainly, naming the spreadsheet row and the reason (for example "Row 3: no recommendation called 'acnee', so no rules were changed"). Per-row application was considered and rejected. The Answers sheet is separate: its valid cells still apply.

Reproduction on the mock. Rules only, Table. Export. In the Rules sheet set row 1 'What happens' to Pin (valid) and row 3 Recommendations to 'acnee' (typo). Import.

Root cause found in the mock. The cause is in the Rules-sheet branch of `applyImport()` (index.html:833–840). Rows are checked one at a time at :839 (`if(!verb||!w||!names.length||ids.some(x=>!x)){bad++;continue}`). A bad row only adds to a counter; its row number and the reason are thrown away. Then :840 (`if(bad)skipped+=bad;else{…if(d){S.rules=next;changes+=d}}`) throws out the whole `next` list if any row was bad. `next` replaces `S.rules` completely, so the author probably added this gate on purpose: dropping one row from `next` would delete that rule and shift the order of the rules after it, and with first-match-wins that order matters. The side effect is that one typo cancels every valid rule edit in the sheet. `importFile()` (:881–883) builds the toast from the bare counts: "Nothing changed · N skipped" or "Imported N changes · N skipped". The Answers sheet uses the same wording (:842–857) for a single skipped cell whose neighbours did apply. So the toast under-reports what was lost (all rule edits, shown as "1 skipped"), gives no row or reason, and in Filter Results + Rules it even reports success.

Fixed in the mock by. Per D16 the Rules sheet stays all-or-nothing, but the toast now names the row and the reason: "No rule changed — Rule 3: there's no recommendation called “acnee”. Fix it and import again" (+N more rows when there are several). Reasons cover the verb, the recommendation, and each parse failure in When they answer.

B23The export writes cells its own import rejects: names containing commas, '(no answers)' and '(none)'mediumFixed in mock
Anything the export writes imports again unchanged: recommendation lists are quoted or use a separator that can't appear in a title, and hal…

Requirement. Anything the export writes imports again unchanged: recommendation lists are quoted or use a separator that can't appear in a title, and half-built rules round-trip (and stay flagged, B8).

Reproduction on the mock. A) Add a recommendation whose title contains a comma (test stand-in 'Daily Moisturizer, 50 ml') via '+ Add recommendations', create a rule for it, Export, change rule 2 to Pin in the sheet, Import. B) Leave a rule with no answers (Q1 'Stings…' rule, then Q1 → Five-point scale) or with no recommendation (the '30 recommendations' toggle), Export, change rule 2 to Pin, Import.

Root cause found in the mock. The export writes three kinds of cell that its own import reads as bad rows. One bad row then throws away the whole Rules sheet. 1. **Comma names and "(none)":** sheets() at index.html:762 writes the recommendations as `r.recs.join(", ")||"(none)"`. The ", " separator can appear inside a name, and "(none)" is a placeholder for an empty list. 2. **"(no answers)":** whenText() at :757 writes "(no answers)" when a rule has no answers left. The rule window won't save such a rule (the ok gate at :894), but they still happen: setPoints() at :607 trims Q1's answers when it becomes Five-point, and the #stress30 handler at :1055 removes recommendations from rules. 3. **parseWhen() at :827:** `if(!t||t==="(no answers)")return null` treats its own placeholder as a parse failure. 4. **applyImport() at :838:** `nrm(cell).split(",").map(nrm).filter(x=>x&&x!=="(none)")` then `names.map(recBy)`. This turns "Daily Moisturizer, 50 ml" into two unknown names and turns "(none)" into an empty list. 5. **Line :839:** `if(!verb||!w||!names.length||ids.some(x=>!x)){bad++;continue}` rejects all three cases. 6. **Line :840:** `if(bad)skipped+=bad;else{...}` drops every row of the sheet (this is B22), so the unrelated edit to rule 2 is lost. importFile() at :883 then toasts "Nothing changed · 1 skipped". Two more places behave the same way: - The compare key at :840 is `JSON.stringify([r.conds,...])`. So even if the placeholders were accepted, {q1:[]} vs {} would count as a change that didn't happen.

Fixed in the mock by. The export writes nothing its own import rejects. List cells are CSV-quoted (nameList/qName) and read back with a quote-aware splitter, so a recommendation called 'Daily Moisturizer, 50 ml' survives. Placeholders are never written as data: an empty recommendation list, an empty When and an unset mapping are empty cells, not '(none)', '(no answers)' or '(not set)'. parseWhen reads an empty When as an empty condition set, so half-built rules round-trip instead of killing the sheet.

B25Import's change count is wrong: an unchanged file reports changes, and one inserted rule counts as sixmediumFixed in mock
A) 'Nothing changed'. B) 'Imported 1 change' (one rule added).

Requirement. A) 'Nothing changed'. B) 'Imported 1 change' (one rule added).

Reproduction on the mock. A) Rules only: create a rule clicking Q4 'Yes, it gets oilier…' before Q1 'Stings…' (→ sensitive), and another where Q3's 'is' was clicked on and off (→ acne). Table → Export → Import the same file. B) Export, insert one new rule row at the top, Import.

Root cause found in the mock. docs/design/logic-tab/rules-row/index.html, applyImport (line 833; the Rules-sheet diff is at line 840). Two problems in that diff: (1) The key is `key=r=>JSON.stringify([r.conds,r.not,r.all,r.verb,r.recs])`. It compares the rule exactly as the rule window stored it with the clean form that parseWhen (lines 827-832) builds. parseWhen puts questions in quiz order (because whenParts, line 755, sorts the export), keeps no empty arrays, and sets not/all only when true (all only for 2+ answers joined with AND). The rule window stores something else: - ACT.mans (line 1011) adds question keys to M.conds in click order and leaves [] when an answer is un-picked. - ACT.mnot (line 1012) and ACT.mall (line 1013) flip flags to false instead of deleting them, and never clear flags on unanswered questions or all-of on a single answer. - ACT.msave (line 1016) saves M as it is (`const {edit,...rule}=M`). So a rule that means the same thing but has a different key order or leftover keys gets a different JSON string. (2) The comparison is by position: `for(let i=0;i<n;i++)if(!next[i]||!S.rules[i]||key(next[i])!==key(S.rules[i]))d++`. Inserting or deleting one rule shifts every later index, and each shifted index counts as a change. importFile (lines 878-883) then shows "Imported d changes" with an Undo, where it should say "Nothing changed" (the check at line 882).

Fixed in the mock by. Rules are compared by canonRule() (questions in quiz order, sorted answers, flags only where they mean something) and counted with an LCS diff: max(old,new) − longest unchanged run. An insert, a delete, an edit or a move each count 1; an untouched file counts 0.

B26A UTF-8 CSV without a byte-order mark is read as Latin-1, overwriting answer text with mojibakemediumFixed in mock
'Nothing changed' (the same file with a BOM gives that).

Requirement. 'Nothing changed' (the same file with a BOM gives that).

Reproduction on the mock. Filter Results + Rules, Table. Edit Q3 answer A to 'Don’t know — keep it simple'. Export the Answers sheet as a UTF-8 CSV without a BOM (what Google Sheets 'Download → CSV' produces) and Import it.

Root cause found in the mock. **Where it starts: index.html:880, `importFile`.** `wb=X.read(await file.arrayBuffer(),{type:"array"})` hands the raw CSV bytes to SheetJS 0.18.5 with no encoding. SheetJS's CSV reader then decodes the bytes as Latin-1, one byte per character. It only decodes UTF-8 when the file starts with a BOM or when codepage 65001 is passed. **What `applyImport` then does with the garbled text.** It compares the garbled strings to the model and treats them as edits: - **:851:** `const at=nrm(r[ci("answer")]);if(at&&at!==a.t){a.t=at;changes++}` overwrites any non-ASCII answer text and counts it as a change. - **:844:** the same thing happens to non-ASCII question text. - **:845-846:** `parseType()` (regexes at :823-824 expect "·" and "–") returns undefined for "Multi-select Â· pick 1â€“N" or "Scale Â· 1â€“N", so `skipped++`. - **:855:** Narrows values such as "Skin type · Dry" match no VALMAP short label, so `skipped++`. Info-only rows are not affected: their "—" cell is ignored. The Rules sheet is not in a single-sheet CSV.

Fixed in the mock by. importFile decodes text files itself: UTF-8 (fatal), falling back to Windows-1252, and only hands raw bytes to SheetJS for the formats it already reads correctly (xlsx ZIP, legacy xls, UTF-16 with a BOM).

Root cause found in the mock. The popover has no lifecycle. It is placed once, never re-placed, and only closed by clicks that hit nothing. 1) index.html:911 openPop stores page coordinates once (top = r.bottom + scrollY + 6, left = r.left or r.right - w) and keeps no link to its anchor. Every render() (:724, which rebuilds #stage) and every drawModal() (:903) replaces the anchor node, and drawPop (:912) keeps re-applying the stale pop.top and pop.left. So nothing re-anchors when layout changes: - C: :970 toggletarget calls render() and then drawPop(). - D: :1029 hint calls render(). - F: the resize handlers at :1036 and :1041 only run markMore and fitRows. - G: nothing listens to .mscroll scrolling. 2) The click dispatcher at :1032 closes the popover only when the click hits no [data-act] element. Any handler that doesn't call closePop() itself leaves the popover open with stale content: - A: :1017 mclose and :1016 msave. - B: :1015 mrec calls drawModal() but not drawPop(). - E: :1020 undo. - D: :1029 hint and :1030 stub. 3) :982 mrecPick dereferences M without a null guard, which is the TypeError in A. The !M branch of drawModal (:903) also doesn't close a popover that belongs to the window. 4) The CSS at :276 makes #modal a fixed scrim that doesn't scroll and has no page scroll lock, so the wheel scrolls the document behind it. #pop (:175) is position:absolute in page coordinates, so it moves with that page scroll (G).

Fixed in the mock by. Popovers now have a lifecycle. openPop stores the anchor as a data-attribute selector (popSel). placePop() (~930) re-reads the live anchor on every render(), drawModal(), window resize and capture-phase scroll. It closes the popover when the anchor is gone, hidden, or scrolled fully out of .mscroll, .twrap or .stagewrap. drawPop builds the content, then calls placePop. The click dispatcher (~1055) closes an open popover on any click outside it, except on its own anchor, which still toggles it; this covers Back, Continue, Paste rules, More, Undo, band chips, Cancel, × and Create rule. mrecPick checks for a null M. CSS html:has(#modal|#aqm|#addrec open){overflow:hidden} (~278) locks the page behind any window. Scrolling inside the windows' own lists still works.

The popover helper in docs/design/logic-tab/rules-row/index.html handles position only, never focus or ARIA state. 1. **Opening does not move focus.** openPop (line 911) stores only `key`, not the trigger, and never moves focus into #pop. 2. **Redraws destroy the focused item.** drawPop (line 912) rewrites #pop.innerHTML on every call. Requirement. Focus stays on the control that was used (or its re-rendered twin), or moves to a sensible neighbour after a delete (the next row, or the toast's Undo).

Reproduction on the mock. Keyboard only, Filter Results + Rules: Tab to rail item Q4 and press Enter; Tab to Q1 answer B's cell, press Enter, Tab into the picker and press Space; press Enter on 'Multi-select' in the type popover; press Enter on Table, More, or a tray chip to arm it. In Add a question press Space on a type card or delete an answer; in Add recommendations activate a tab or press Space on a row; in the rule window press Space on an answer bucket. Root cause found in the mock. Every draw function rebuilds its whole container with innerHTML. That destroys the focused control, and none of them captures focus or puts it back. The only exceptions are drawAQ(focus), drawAR(true), drawVP(true), the search-input `input` handlers and the aqgrip arrow-key handler, which shows that keeping focus was intended. Where focus is lost, in index.html: **Stage:** - renderInner, line 726: `$("#stage").innerHTML=...`. - Reached through render(), line 724, from ACT.sel 944, arm 966, cell placing 967, vw 985, setstyle 1004, hint 1029, delRule 859 and undo 1020. **Popover:** - drawPop, line 912: `el.innerHTML=pop.build()`, used by toggletarget 970 and settype 954-960. - closePop, line 913: hides #pop while it holds focus and never gives focus back to the control that opened it (setstyle and the other menu items). **Rule window:** drawModal, line 905: `el.innerHTML=modalHTML()`, used by mans, mverb and mrec (1011-1015). **Add a question:** drawAQ, line 633, called with no focus argument by aqtype (947) and aqdel (949). **Add recommendations:** drawAR, line 747, called with no focus argument by arTab (1023) and arTog (1024). **Delete and Undo:** - delRule, line 859: never moves focus to a neighbouring rule. - ACT.undo, line 1020: hides the toast that holds focus and re-renders without placing focus. **Dispatchers:** the click dispatcher (line 1032) and the keydown dispatcher (line 1034) call `ACT[...]` with no focus restore.

Fixed in the mock by. The two dispatchers restore focus. The click dispatcher records fkey(el) when the clicked control held focus, runs the action, then refocus(k, popBack) — refocus returns early whenever something visible already has focus, so a handler that placed focus itself (a window opening, the value picker's search) is never fought. The Enter/Space handler for div[data-act] does the same. The Escape branch restores focus after unarming a chip. delRule moves focus to the toast's Undo (the trash it came from is gone) and, when that toast goes, to the rule that took the deleted one's place; ACT.undo focuses the rule it brought back; qundo and impUndo focus the question they restored and the Import button.

B31Dialogs declare aria-modal but don't move focus in, trap Tab, or return focus on closemediumFixed in mock
Focus moves into the dialog on open, Tab and Shift+Tab cycle inside it, the page behind is inert, and closing returns focus to the button th…

Requirement. Focus moves into the dialog on open, Tab and Shift+Tab cycle inside it, the page behind is inert, and closing returns focus to the button that opened it.

Reproduction on the mock. 1) '+ Add question': focus Cancel and press Tab 4 times; focus × and press Shift+Tab; close the dialog. 2) '+ Add recommendations': press Tab repeatedly from the search field; when focus reaches the first rule's trash behind the scrim, press Enter; close with Esc, × or Cancel. 3) Create a rule and press Tab repeatedly.

Root cause found in the mock. In docs/design/logic-tab/rules-row/index.html, the three windows only switch `hidden` on and off and rewrite their host's innerHTML. There is no focus contract at all. 1. **Opening.** drawAQ (l.633), drawAR (l.746-748) and drawModal (l.903-906) never record the element that opened them. None of them makes .shell, #pitch or .stagewrap inert; the attribute `inert` is used nowhere in the file. There is no Tab keydown handler. drawModal never focuses anything, so focus stays on the opener behind the scrim. drawAQ and drawAR only focus on open because ACT.addq and ACT.addRecs pass them a selector or flag. 2. **Closing.** These handlers set the state to null and call draw*(): ACT.aqclose (l.946), aqadd (950), mdel (1010), msave (1016), mclose (1017), reset (1018), arClose (1025), arAdd (1026) and the Esc handler (1033). draw*() then runs `el.innerHTML=""`, which removes the focused element, so focus falls to <body>. Nothing puts focus back on the opener. 3. **Background still works.** The global click dispatcher (l.1032) and the Enter/Space handler for div/tr [data-act] (l.1034) run ACT[...] for any [data-act] without checking whether a window is open. That is why keyboard Enter on 'Delete rule 1' (delrule) works under the Add recommendations scrim, and why editrule, reset and wipe can be triggered under an open rule edit (B2). 4. **In-window updates.** Every change inside a window re-renders it through innerHTML (drawAQ(), drawAR(), drawModal()). This destroys the focused control

Fixed in the mock by. One contract for #modal, #aqm and #addrec. winSync makes .shell, #pitch and .stagewrap inert whenever any window is open, and makes a window under another one inert too (the rule window while Add recommendations is over it) — so a rule's trash behind the scrim can no longer take focus, which is what let Enter delete a rule through the scrim. A capture-phase Tab listener wraps Tab and Shift+Tab inside the topmost window and pulls focus back in if it ever gets out, returning early for #pop so popovers keep their own Tab rules. Each window records the control that opened it and refocuses it on close, after the render that replaced it; the old guard refused to restore while another window was still open, which is exactly the Add-recommendations-over-the-rule-window case, so it now relies on canFocus (an opener that is inert behind a newer window is refused instead).

B32The Undo toast isn't announced and can't be reached from the keyboard before it disappearsmediumFixed in mock
The toast is announced (aria-live / role=status), its Undo is reachable right away (focus moves to it, or a shortcut), and it doesn't expire…

Requirement. The toast is announced (aria-live / role=status), its Undo is reachable right away (focus moves to it, or a shortcut), and it doesn't expire before a keyboard user can get there.

Reproduction on the mock. Rules only, keyboard only. Tab to rule 2's trash, press Enter, then try to reach the toast's Undo.

Root cause found in the mock. There are three causes in index.html: 1. **No live region (:521).** `<div id="toast" hidden></div>` has no role="status" or aria-live. It is also shown and hidden with the `hidden` attribute (display:none), which takes it out of the accessibility tree between toasts, so it cannot reliably be the live region itself. The only live region is #svlive (:522), which the save indicator uses. 2. **Focus is destroyed and never put back (:859, :724/:726).** `delRule(i){snap();S.rules.splice(i,1);closePop();render();toastU(...)}` calls `render()` (:724), whose `renderInner()` (:726) rebuilds `#stage.innerHTML`. That deletes the focused trash button, and nothing moves focus anywhere, so activeElement becomes BODY and Chrome's next Tab starts from the top of #stage. #toast is the last focusable node in the DOM (:521, after #stage and the overlays), so Undo is the last tab stop (the 19th). `ACT.undo` (:1020) has the same problem: it hides the toast and calls `render()` without restoring focus. 3. **A fixed timer with no pause or shortcut (:658, :877, :914).** `toastU` (:658), `toastImp` (:877) and `toast` (:914) each run `clearTimeout(toast.t);toast.t=setTimeout(()=>t.hidden=true, 6000 / 7000 / 2200)`. Nothing pauses the timer on focus or hover. The only keydown handlers (:1033, :1045, :1048) cover Escape, Enter/Space on rows, grips and inline edits, so there is no undo shortcut. The Undo button is the only way to recover a deleted rule, and it expires under keyboard focus.

Fixed in the mock by. A persistent #toastlive (role=status, aria-atomic) carries the message plus ". Press Undo, or Ctrl+Z, to bring it back." whenever the toast has an Undo, and is cleared on hide so the next identical message is announced again. One helper now arms all four toasts (2200/6000/6000/7000 unchanged): it focuses the Undo when the action destroyed whatever had focus, and the timer does not run while the toast holds a visible focus (:focus-visible) or the pointer is on it. Ctrl/Cmd+Z activates whichever Undo is showing (undo, qundo or impUndo) and does nothing once the toast has gone, so it can never roll back a later edit. When the toast hides while holding focus, focus goes to the rule that took the deleted one's place rather than to <body>.

B35Undo only goes back one step: a second delete within 6 s makes the first unrecoverablelowFixed in mock
Both deletions can be undone, or each toast keeps its own Undo.

Requirement. Both deletions can be undone, or each toast keeps its own Undo.

Reproduction on the mock. Filter Results + Rules: delete rule 1 twice within 6 s (hover → trash), then click Undo.

Root cause found in the mock. index.html:657 `let UNDO=null;const snap=()=>{UNDO=JSON.stringify(S.rules)};` is a single undo slot, and every snap() overwrites it no matter what is already there. - delRule (index.html:859) calls snap() even while the previous delete's Undo toast is still on screen. The snapshot from before the first delete is replaced by the one from before the second delete. - toastU (index.html:658) rewrites the single #toast innerHTML, which destroys the first toast's Undo button, and restarts the 6 s timer. - ACT.undo (index.html:1020) restores only that latest snapshot and then sets UNDO to null, so nothing older is left to restore. - The toast text is positional (`Rule ${i+1} deleted`). Deleting the top row renumbers the list, so the second toast is byte-identical to the first and the replacement can't be seen. - wipe (1019) and the drag-reorder drop handler (1060) use the same slot, so a delete followed by a reorder within 6 s also loses the delete.

Fixed in the mock by. Undo now covers a run of actions. While the Undo toast is still up (undoLive: toast visible with [data-act=undo]), further deletes, moves and clears join the same entry; snap(del) starts or joins a run and counts n and dels. One Undo restores the rules from before the run, in their original order. Delete toasts count the run: '2 rules deleted · Undo'. A run that mixes deletes with a move or clear says 'Undo both' or 'Undo all N' on the button, so it is clear what Undo takes back. Any other toast (Rule saved, import, …) ends the run.

It never checks S.style or the answer mappings on the deciding question: - Line 892 counts `done` with ruleCount. - Line 893 sorts `order` with ruleCount, so recommendations without a rule come first. - Line 898 prints "<b>done/N</b> have a rule". In modalHTML the count and sort use recCovered. The header reads 'N/M are covered' in Filter style and still 'have a rule' in Rules only. The chip title reads 'Mapped from an answer · no rule needed', and the dot follows recCovered. mrecMoreHTML sorts by recCovered and labels mapped recommendations 'mapped from an answer'. findings() uses recCovered for 'never recommended', so the band and the check agree.

So "Five-point scale" = old text answers + padded "4","5". 6. ACT.aqadd (:950) seeds "1" to "5", so every point starts as a blank, non-editable numbered point.

Every point is now an editable field: a numbered point shows its end label, or "Add label", as placeholder text and can be named; a text answer on either end of a scale shows that end's label beside it, so q.lo/q.hi are never invisible; an emptied point falls back to its number (input listener); and an answer retyped to its own number stays editable. That leaves 197px per line, so every seeded answer chip lands at a line end and breaks. `.cchip` is the only chip in the file without a no-wrap rule. `.tchip` (line 84) already has `max-width; overflow:hidden; text-overflow:ellipsis; white-space:nowrap`.

Fixed in the mock by. Added white-space:nowrap to .cchip (the one chip class in the file without it) and removed the now-redundant '.msay .cchip' copy. This is the minimal fix B47 verified; I deliberately did not take its optional chip-level ellipsis hardening (see notes).

Nothing clears the highlight when the pointer leaves the page (part B).** - The only way to clear is a later mouseover on something that is not a pill. - Leaving the window fires only `mouseout` (relatedTarget=null), and the page has no mouseout or pointerleave handler. **3. Root cause found in the mock. 1) fitTwoRows, index.html:809-813. The hide loop at :813 skips picked chips (`if(items[i].dataset.on==="1")continue;`), so it can only hide unpicked chips. When the picked chips alone need more than two rows, the loop runs out of unpicked chips and exits with rows()>2, and the band grows. When picked chips fill exactly two rows, the more button itself wraps to row 3. Line :812 unhides the more button and sets its text to "See 0 more" before anything is hidden. Nothing hides it again if n stays 0, which is the case when every chip is picked, so the button reads "See 0 more". 2) Footer. modalHTML (:901) renders `<span class="msay">${sentence(M,true)}</span>`. sentence() (:643-645) adds one chip for every picked recommendation (`r.recs.map`) and every picked answer (`r.conds[k].map`), with no limit. In the CSS, .mfoot (:331) is `flex:none`, and .msay (:332) has no max-height or overflow. The footer grows as tall as the sentence, and all of that height comes out of .mscroll (:282, `flex:1 1 auto;min-height:0`), which holds both the band and the questions. .cchip (:149) has no nowrap, so chips break across lines.

Fixed in the mock by. fitTwoRows (~846) now hides chips in two passes: unpicked chips from the end first, then picked chips only if still needed. The button reads 'See N more' or 'See N more · P picked' and is hidden when nothing is hidden, so 'See 0 more' can't appear. The comment is updated. CSS: .msay gets `max-height:calc(3 * 1.8em + 3px);overflow-y:auto;overscroll-behavior:contain` (3 lines, then it scrolls), and `.msay .cchip{white-space:nowrap}`.

Root cause found in the mock. The cause is in drawModal (index.html:903-906). On every call it reads scrollTop from the existing #modal .mscroll and each .mans scrollLeft (line 904), replaces the whole dialog with innerHTML=modalHTML() (905), then applies those saved values to the new DOM (906). That is intended for redraws of the same draft (mans, mnot, mverb, mrec, arAdd), so the window does not jump. ACT.msave (line 1016) with data-more="1" sets M=blank() and calls drawModal() while the previous draft's DOM is still in #modal. So the old draft's scroll is copied onto the brand-new draft. mclose does not have this problem: M=null makes drawModal clear innerHTML, so the next open reads no .mscroll and uses top=0. The .mans horizontal scrollLeft (keyed by question id) is carried into the new draft the same way. With the seed data at 1280 no answer row overflows, so that part is latent today.

Fixed in the mock by. drawModal takes a new fresh argument. A fresh draft does not carry over the old .mscroll scrollTop or any .mans scrollLeft, and it moves focus into the new draft. ACT.msave calls drawModal(true) after 'Save/Create & add another'. addrule, editrule and createFor also pass true. A redraw of the same draft (picks, not, all, verb, recommendations) still keeps its scroll.

Root cause found in the mock. The document 'input' listener (line 1062) calls drawAR(true) on every input event, including those with isComposing=true. drawAR(true) then refocuses the new input and moves the caret to the end. The consequences: - (a) A new query keeps the old scroll offset, cut down to the new maximum, instead of starting at the top. arTab (line 1023) calls drawAR() and has the same carry-over. - (b) The element holding the IME composition is destroyed mid-composition, so each update starts a new composition after text that was already committed. - (c) The caret position is lost after every keystroke. - (d) AR.q is written back into the HTML without escaping (value="${AR.q}" at line 742, and 'Nothing matches "${AR.q}"' at line 736), so a typed " cuts the value short. Answer keys are built as String.fromCharCode(65+i), which has no wrap or bound, and nothing limits the number of answer rows. 1) docs/design/logic-tab/rules-row/index.html:604: `const akey=(q,i)=>qtype(q)==="scale"?String(i+1):String.fromCharCode(65+i);`. The pane uses this at line 696 (.akey). It takes the last line of the edited text (rs[rs.length-1]) and sets `b.style.left = e.right + 8` with no upper limit. It ignores two things: the pill's own width (about 72px for 'Saving…', 62px for 'Saved') and the right edge of the text's column. That column is ed.parentElement: the h3 in the heading, the .atext grid cell for answers, and the table cell in Table view. #svb is position:fixed with z-index 30 and a solid background (--ground or --ok-wash). So when the text ends within roughly 80px of its column edge, the pill crosses the gap: 20px in the .paneh heading, 10px in the .arow grid, or the table cell border. It then paints over the neighbour: the 'Picks results' role button, the chips or 'Choose a result' in the mapping cell, or the 'What it does' button in the Table view. For the heading this only happens when the last line is beside the top-aligned role button. pointer-events:none means clicks still get through, so the damage is visual only. It lasts about 2.55s: 650ms Saving, then 1500ms Saved, then a 400ms fade.

Fixed in the mock by. svPlace measures the pill unhidden and keeps it inside the edited text's own column (h3 / .atext / table cell): where there is no room beside the last line it drops under the end of it. The choice is made once per save on the wider 'Saving…' label, so it does not jump when it becomes 'Saved'. Final verification round: when the edited line sits at the very top or bottom edge of the window the pill is clamped into view, it sits beside the line rather than falling back onto it, and it re-places itself every 120ms while visible so a re-render cannot leave it stranded. Covered by the smoke section 'R-final D5b'.

B62The Filter Rules column hides extra rules in an unmarked inner scrolllowFixed in mock
A count or an overflow cue (fade or visible scrollbar).

Requirement. A count or an overflow cue (fade or visible scrollbar).

Reproduction on the mock. 1280×720, Filter view with 11 rules, select Q3 (3 answers).

Root cause found in the mock. The inner scroll itself is intentional. The Rules column is pinned to the grid row height, so the list is capped and scrolls instead of growing. What's wrong is that nothing tells the user it overflows, even though the mock uses overflow cues elsewhere: the fade on the rule window's answer rows (.manswrap.more::after at line 298, toggled by markMore() at line 902), the "+N more" and "See N more" chips, and the question count. Where it comes from in docs/design/logic-tab/rules-row/index.html: - **CSS, line 137** `.rcol{position:relative}` and **line 138** `.rcol-in{position:absolute;inset:0;...}` take the column out of the grid's height calculation. The row height comes from `.rail{min-height:480px}` (**line 52**) and the question panel, so the column is about 480px tall no matter the viewport. - **CSS, line 142** `.rlist{flex:0 1 auto;min-height:0;overflow-y:auto;...}` shrinks the list to about 348px and scrolls it, with no fade or mask, no scrollbar styling, and no `.more` toggle. On macOS the default overlay scrollbars are 0px wide and stay invisible until you scroll. - **renderFilter(), line 708** renders `<div class="rcol-h"><h4>Rules</h4>...` with no count. The question list at line 707 renders `<span class="railn">${S.qs.length}</span>`. - **render(), line 724** and renderInner() replace #stage's innerHTML, so the list's scroll position goes back to 0 on every render (switching questions, saving a rule). - **ACT.msave, line 1016** appends the new rule with S.rules.push

Fixed in the mock by. The Rules column heading carries a rule count, the list is wrapped in .rlistw whose .more state paints a bottom fade while there is more below (markRules, also on scroll and resize), render() keeps the list's scroll position across a re-render, and a newly created rule is scrolled into view after msave.

B63Empty Rules column says 'Your 0 switched-on questions are deciding everything'lowFixed in mock
Copy that matches the blocking state, e.g. that no question picks the result yet.

Requirement. Copy that matches the blocking state, e.g. that no question picks the result yet.

Reproduction on the mock. Filter Results + Rules: set Q1 to Info only, then delete every rule.

Root cause found in the mock. `ruleRows()` at `docs/design/logic-tab/rules-row/index.html:702` handles the no-rules case like this: - It counts the questions that are not Info only: `const n=S.qs.filter(q=>roleOf(q)!=="info").length`. - In the Filter style it always prints `Your <b>${n}</b> switched-on question${n===1?" is":"s are"} deciding everything.` It never checks whether any question has `role==="decides"`. That is the same check `findings()` uses at lines 661 and 663 to raise the blocking finding "No question picks the result. Give one question that job.", which `fbar()` turns into "Fix 1 issue to continue". So when no question picks the result, the empty state says the questions decide everything while the step is blocked. With every question Info only, n=0 and the plural branch prints "Your 0 switched-on questions are deciding everything". With only a Narrows question, it prints "Your 1 switched-on question is deciding everything". The copy and `findings()` disagree about the same state. Side note: the `S.style==="rules"` branch inside `ruleRows()` can never run. `ruleRows()` is only called from `renderFilter()` (line 708). Rules only renders its own empty state, `.rempty2` in `rulesBand()` at line 716.

Fixed in the mock by. ruleRows() bases its empty-state copy on whether a question has role 'decides' (the same check findings() uses): with none it reads 'No rules yet. No question picks the result yet, so nothing shows. Set one question to Picks results.'; with one it keeps 'Your N switched-on question(s) … deciding everything.' The unreachable Rules-only branch was dropped (ruleRows is only called by renderFilter).

B65Toast reads 'Added 1 recommendation. Each needs a rule'lowFixed in mock
Singular copy, e.g. 'Added 1 recommendation. It needs a rule'.

Reproduction on the mock. Open '+ Add recommendations', select one item, click 'Add 1 recommendation'.

Root cause found in the mock. In docs/design/logic-tab/rules-row/index.html, ACT.arAdd (lines 1026-1028), line 1028 is: toast(M?`Added and picked for this rule`:`Added ${added.length} recommendation${added.length>1?"s":""}. Each needs a rule`) The first sentence changes with the count, but the second sentence "Each needs a rule" is hard-coded, so adding one item gives "Added 1 recommendation. Each needs a rule".
